# 93 — Feature-Interaction Analysis

> **Status**: Living — the 28 numbered challenges (I-1..I-28) below are
> resolved here as design proposals, but every one of them is cited from a
> normative chapter (00–53) as "decided in 93"; a citing chapter's decision
> stands as decided design regardless of implementation state (see the
> per-chapter "(...unimplemented)" qualifiers). Exploratory status applies
> only to the surrounding pair-classification method and matrix (§1–§3) —
> the un-consumed C(27,2)=351-pair scan this document derives the challenges
> from, not to the challenges' resolutions themselves. See the index below.
> **Sources**: the entire spec (00–53); [91-gap-analysis.md](91-gap-analysis.md)
> **Implementation**: none — analysis document; consuming normative chapters
> carry their own implementation state

This document systematically examines how **every pair** of dataflow-relevant
features in this spec composes. It answers one question per pair: *is the
composed behavior specified, or does it hide a design decision nobody has made
yet?* Unresolved pairs are consolidated into numbered challenges (I-1 … I-28),
each resolved here as a design proposal checked against the design principles
(P1–P10) and the recorded decisions in [91-gap-analysis.md](91-gap-analysis.md).

## 1. Method

The 44 features of the spec were reduced to **27 analysis nodes** (§2); merges
follow the spec's own unifications (e.g. mobility, drain, parking and
traffic-light buffering are "one behavior at two granularities" — 30/33). All
C(27,2) = **351 pairs** were classified by 15 independent scan agents, each
owning a coherent cluster block of the matrix, into exactly one of:

- **SPECIFIED** — the spec states how the two features compose (normative text
  or a recorded resolved decision); every claim cites the section.
- **ORTHOGONAL** — provably independent. Permitted only after three probes came
  back negative: *shared-artifact* (no common runtime artifact), *mid-flight*
  (no interleaving window between the two protocols), *quantified-guarantee*
  (neither guarantee quantifies over conditions the other can break).
- **TENSION** — the features demonstrably interact but the composed semantics
  is unspecified or underspecified. A proposal in 91 is not SPECIFIED.
- **CONFLICT** — two normative statements cannot both hold.

Pairs touching exploratory nodes defaulted to TENSION unless orthogonality
survived all three probes. Result: **120 SPECIFIED, 231 TENSION, 0 ORTHOGONAL,
0 CONFLICT**.

Two classes deserve comment. *No pair was CONFLICT*: the spec does not
contradict itself anywhere in this matrix; every problem found is an absence,
not an inconsistency. *No pair survived the orthogonality probes*: in a
framework where every invocation carries a MessageContext, every connection is
a Link object, and every cell lives behind a host queue, the shared-artifact
probe alone connects nearly every feature pair; the probes are deliberately
biased so that a false independence claim (the expensive error) cannot slip
through. Orthogonality was the hypothesis; the matrix refuted it.

The 231 TENSION pairs were consolidated into **28 challenges** by one rule: two
findings belong to the same challenge iff resolving one mechanism question
would reclassify both pairs. Two pairs are answered directly by existing 91
proposals and carry no interaction-specific residue (§8, marked R in the
matrix). Each challenge was then resolved by a dedicated agent, in dependency
order (substrate challenges first, their adopted resolutions injected into
dependents as fixed decisions), and all 28 resolutions were cross-checked for
mutual consistency and principle compliance.

One deliberate omission: the Cell itself (inventory A1) is not a matrix node —
it is the substrate every node presupposes; its facets are covered by N6
(lifecycle), N7 (hierarchy/membranes), N15 (mutability classes) and N23
(identity).

### Baselines and spec drift

The matrix scan is pinned to spec baseline `36014e1` (M5.7). While the
analysis ran, the spec advanced through M6–M9 in a parallel session
(attention/scheduling, replication, identity, host hierarchy, security
phase 1, evolution). Challenge resolutions were produced against the live
tree and cite the newer text where it existed; §3.1 lists every pair whose
baseline classification the drift affects, judged at head
`a69186a`. Matrix cells in §3 show the scan-baseline
classification.

## 4. Specified interactions

The 120 pairs whose composition the spec already defines, with the defining
section(s). Grouped by the lower-numbered node; each pair appears once.

**N1 — Ports, contracts & port registry**

- **N1 × N2** — Cardinality is a declared property of every port ('a port declares ... a cardinality') encoded directly in the port implementations (FanInlet/FanOutlet/OneToOnePort) that feed the eagerly-populated per-cell PortRegistry. (10/12 §Definition; 10/12 §Cardinality; 10/15 §Port discovery (G-17, resolved))
- **N1 × N4** — Ports optionally declare policies and link-time validation, and the handshake runs on the port with schema/contract mismatch as a named rejection reason, in the fixed order policies → cardinality → onLink. (10/12 §Definition; 10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based); 10/13 §Policies)
- **N1 × N5** — Port interaction is defined as calling methods on the port's contract captured as serializable Invocations, with Serve/Use/Subscribe mapped onto the Inlet/Outlet duality and HostedPortInvocation.Type PORT_API vs PORT_MANAGEMENT mirroring the data/management contract split. (10/14 §The core move (ADR 3); 10/12 §The Inlet/Outlet duality; 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces; 10/14 §Dispatch tiers) *Residual*: G-11 residual: @Contract(management) marks contracts but the push-only lint on data contracts is still open (10/12).
- **N1 × N6** — Cold-phase ports are dormant metadata that register eagerly at construction (so cold cells are enumerable without running logic), serving belongs in onActivate, and hosting-specific port operations are guarded to HOT. (10/15 §Cold phase; 10/15 §Port discovery (G-17, resolved); 10/15 §Normative rules)
- **N1 × N8** — Push propagation is defined as invocations on push-only data-path port contracts (canonically Propagate<D>), which is exactly the contract shape 10/12 mandates, so the composition is the system's core normative path. (10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces; 20/21 §Push (default, implemented)) *Residual*: G-11 residual: @Contract(management) markers exist but the push-only lint on data contracts is still open, so a return-bearing method could slip onto the propagation path unchecked.
- **N1 × N9** — Late-join catch-up flows through ordinary port machinery — the post-install onLinked hook unicasts state-as-delta-from-empty on the outlet, and request/response stays consistent with push-only contracts via the pair-of-push-contracts rule. (20/21 §Pull; 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces) *Residual*: G-18 residual: on-demand pull without relinking is unbuilt, deferred to the state-request protocol on multiplex ports (G-13).
- **N1 × N11** — Every data-path invocation carries MessageContext stamped by the emitting outlet with sourcePort rewritten per hop, while management contracts carry null context and clear stale waves — the data/management port split defines exactly which port traffic is waved. (20/22 §MessageContext (normative, as implemented); 10/14 §Context propagation; 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces) *Residual*: The data/management classification driving null-vs-stamped context rests on @Contract annotation discipline while the G-11 push-only lint remains open.
- **N1 × N12** — Glitch-freedom is an opt-in per-cell wrapper that buffers per-wave inputs at inlets with the frontier drawn from port link sets, while non-declaring ports pass traffic eagerly at zero coordination cost — the port layer is explicitly the buffering locus. (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom (opt-in); 20/22 §The glitch-free frontier (composition)) *Residual*: Upstream frontier discovery ('describe your frontier' as a management invocation) awaits multiplex ports (G-13); today only the static inlet link-set frontier exists, and unwaved traffic passes through.
- **N1 × N14** — Ownership is a property of the port's declared contract: the KSP contract processor scans payload type parameters (recursively) for Owned/Leased and emits an exclusive bit into the generated MethodDescriptor, which port-level enforcement reads at link time instead of reflection. (10/12 §Cardinality; 20/23 §Implementation (G-21, M5.6); 20/23 §The four contracts)
- **N1 × N15** — Data cells are the normative template for port contracts: a semantic command contract (SetOps) on the inlet and a delta contract (Propagate<SetDelta>) on the outlet, declared in the explicit port style with an API interface naming the ports. (20/24 §Established pattern (normative template); 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces; 10/12 §The Inlet/Outlet duality)
- **N1 × N18** — The host's control surface is itself ordinary ports, and the data/management contract split maps directly onto host rules: management contracts may block and preempt at priority 0, data contracts are push-only at priority 20, with the PORT_API/PORT_MANAGEMENT split preserved as the wire-level reflection of that divide. (30/31 §Definition; 30/31 §Normative rules; 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces; 10/14 §Dispatch tiers) *Residual*: G-11 push-only lint on data contracts is still open (10/12 flags it), so the blocking/non-blocking split rests on the @Contract(management) flag plus convention.
- **N1 × N20** — Ports are normatively not mailboxes — buffering is declared a suspension-time behavior owned by 30/33's single Buffering primitive at two granularities — and the eager per-cell PortRegistry exists precisely so a cold cell's ports can be enumerated and moved without running logic. (10/12 §What ports are not; 30/33 §Port-level buffering; 10/15 §Normative rules; 10/15 §Port discovery (G-17, resolved))
- **N1 × N22** — Ports and contracts cross the wire by a recorded design: @Contract interfaces get KSP-generated ContractDescriptor tables (FNV-1a hashed contract/method ids in ContractRegistry), port names resolve through the per-cell PortRegistry whose keys client-side proxies derive from API-interface getters, and the data/management contract split rides onto the wire as HostedPortInvocation.Type with management returns wrapped as Deferred/Future. (10/12 §The Inlet/Outlet duality; 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces; 40/41 §Wire layer; 10/15 §Port discovery; 10/14 §Dispatch tiers) *Residual*: G-11 push-only lint on data contracts is still open, and 40/41's status notes generated boundary proxies remain interim JDK proxies (C-5).
- **N1 × N25** — The DSL's connect resolves ports by name against the per-cell PortRegistry, whose eager-registration rule ('port declaration is discovery') exists precisely so cold cells minted by GraphSpec factories can be enumerated and linked without running logic. (50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 10/15 §Port discovery; 10/15 §Normative rules) *Residual*: KSP generation of port metadata (ownership flags, color, data/management marker G-11) is direction-only, and the G-11 push-only lint on data contracts remains open (50/51 §Code generation; 10/12 §Contracts are push-only interfaces).

**N2 — Cardinality & fan ports**

- **N2 × N4** — Cardinality MUST be enforced at link time (rule 1) and the implemented handshake does exactly that — policies → cardinality → onLink, with capacity violations returning Rejected instead of throwing, and ownership-based fan-out refusal at the FanOutlet funnel on every path. (10/12 §Cardinality; 10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based)) *Residual*: Cross-host handshakes return LinkResult.Deferred (recorded M5.4 decision), so a cardinality rejection surfaces only on the target host's deadLetterOutlet, never synchronously to the initiator (10/13).
- **N2 × N5** — Fan semantics and invocation dispatch compose by construction: FanOutlet emission is broadcast realized by the Broadcast proxy behavior, FanInlet's many callers all resolve to the single served/delegated implementation, and delegation stays intra-cell so it never adds countable links. (10/12 §Cardinality; 10/14 §Standard proxy behaviors; 10/12 §The Inlet/Outlet duality; 10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based))
- **N2 × N8** — The cardinality and delta rules cross-reference explicitly: multi-producer FanInlets are permitted only where the cell declares merge semantics (delta rule 3 restates this from the propagation side), and FanOutlet broadcast is the defined fan-out emission mode for pushed deltas. (10/12 §Cardinality; 20/21 §Incremental vs complete)
- **N2 × N9** — Late-join catch-up composes with fan-out via a targeted per-subscriber unicast (outlet.at(link.to)) on the FanOutlet, recorded as implemented and validated by the 100-seed late-join test with a missed-prefix control. (20/21 §Pull; 10/12 §Cardinality) *Residual*: 10/12 §Cardinality still describes FanOutlet emission as broadcast-only; the per-subscriber at() capability the catch-up relies on is documented only in 20/21.
- **N2 × N11** — MessageContext rule 3 states the composition directly: fan-out duplicates context to every subscriber and fan-in delivers each input's own context, which is precisely what per-wave downstream buffering needs. (20/22 §MessageContext (normative, as implemented); 10/12 §Cardinality)
- **N2 × N12** — Fan-in is the glitch locus and GlitchFreeCell is specified as wrapping a fan-in edge set with per-wave version buffering, fan-out context duplication feeds the diamond, and cross-source fan-in joins are decided to get convergence rather than simultaneity (G-20). (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom (opt-in); 20/22 §Topology versioning; 10/12 §Cardinality)
- **N2 × N13** — A fan-inlet's live link set is normatively part of wave-t input completeness, and the implemented static frontier recomputes the edge set on every completeness check so link/unlink adapts the condition — the spec names this 'the first instance of topology is part of the completeness condition'. (20/22 §Topology versioning; 20/22 §The glitch-free frontier (composition)) *Residual*: Host-stamped topology events (plan step 5, dependent on G-12 Link objects) remain pending, so mid-wave link races rely on live-link recomputation rather than stamped causal order.
- **N2 × N14** — Fan-out MUST be rejected at link time when the contract carries exclusive ownership (rule 2), implemented in M5.6 as the FanOutlet reading the generated exclusive bit and refusing a second subscriber on every attach path, with Broadcast refusal as backstop. (10/12 §Cardinality; 20/23 §The SPSC link rule (normative); 20/23 §Implementation (G-21, M5.6)) *Residual*: The secondary enforcement point — whole-graph validation before/at activation — is stated in 20/23 but not confirmed built anywhere.
- **N2 × N15** — Multi-producer fan-in is permitted only where the cell declares merge semantics (rule 3), and data cells supply exactly that via commutative/associative/idempotent tag-union merges, matching the mutability-class taxonomy of 10/11. (10/12 §Cardinality; 20/24 §Established pattern (normative template); 10/11 §Mutability classes) *Residual*: Rule 3 is not mechanically enforced: no link-time check ties FanInlet acceptance to a declared mergeable mutability class, so single-stream MapCell/ListCell inlets (documented convergence limits) can silently accept concurrent producers.
- **N2 × N18** — Hosts orchestrate links through the same handshake that enforces cardinality — ManagedHost.connect surfaces LinkResult, capacity violations return Rejected rather than throwing, cross-host handshakes return Deferred with rejection dead-lettered on the target host — and per-link FIFO for fan traffic is guaranteed by the (priority, sequence) queue. (10/12 §Cardinality; 10/13 §Two connectivity styles; 30/31 §Normative rules) *Residual*: A proxy-initiated cross-host connect only learns of rejection via the target host's deadLetterOutlet — a recorded M5.4 decision to revisit when a real topology needs it (10/13).
- **N2 × N20** — 30/33 explicitly carries the cardinality/ownership constraint through mobility: parked messages retain exclusivity through migration, exactly-once consumption must survive replay, and per-ref in-order park/replay preserves the single-consumer discipline that was enforced at link time. (30/33 §Constraints from elsewhere; 30/33 §Stale references; 10/12 §Cardinality) *Residual*: Whether relink after migration re-runs cardinality/policy checks — and what happens to parked traffic if a relink is rejected — is not addressed; explicit topology capture is flagged as the remaining work at the wire boundary (30/33 §The drain protocol).
- **N2 × N22** — Cardinality is enforced inside the target-side handshake (policies → cardinality → onLink) and the recorded M5.4 decision extends that contract across the wire: a proxy-initiated linkTo returns LinkResult.Deferred, the authoritative handshake runs on the target's host, and a rejection is emitted to that host's deadLetterOutlet. (10/12 §Cardinality; 10/13 §2. Explicit (handshake-based); 40/41 §Wire layer) *Residual*: The remote initiator never synchronously learns of a cardinality rejection (Deferred + remote dead-letter); the spec defers a synchronous reply channel 'until a real topology needs it'.
- **N2 × N25** — DSL connect routes through the link handshake where cardinality MUST be enforced at link time and returns Rejected instead of throwing, and the builder normatively makes link rejections fail construction loudly at build and replay time. (50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 10/12 §Cardinality; 10/13 §Two connectivity styles) *Residual*: A proxy-initiated cross-host connect returns LinkResult.Deferred with the authoritative rejection dead-lettered on the target host (10/13), so fail-loudly cannot hold for a future multi-host GraphSpec.

**N4 — Links, handshake & link-time policies**

- **N4 × N5** — Links carry invocations through the three dispatch tiers as 'one logical link' regardless of realization, delegation chains are explicitly excluded from topology (intra-cell composition, not links), and per-link FIFO plus the no-message-loss invariant govern the composition. (10/13 §Cross-boundary links; 10/14 §Dispatch tiers; 10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based); 10/13 §Link lifecycle summary) *Residual*: Flow-time policies (deferred to the membrane layer, 10/13 §Policies) will have to reckon with fused/delegated per-message paths that bypass the delegating cell.
- **N4 × N6** — The link lifecycle specifies suspended-target behavior (buffer/fail-fast then re-resolve, never silently drop), and G-16's resolution guarantees deactivation runs only after every accepted invocation has flushed, with in-place re-activation legal — composing links with suspend/resume/despawn normatively. (10/13 §Link lifecycle summary; 10/15 §Normative rules (rule 4, G-16)) *Residual*: Link disposition on despawn (does despawn unlink or orphan retained links?) and whether a handshake may target a still-cold cell's dormant ports are not stated.
- **N4 × N8** — Push propagation is defined as invocations flowing along links, and link operations are governed by the normative no-message-loss and per-link-FIFO invariant, so data in flight across a link op is delivered or explicitly parked. (20/21 §Push (default, implemented); 10/13 §Link lifecycle summary; 10/13 §Cross-boundary links) *Residual*: Flow-time policies that would gate flowing deltas (rate limits) explicitly wait for the membrane layer (10/13 §Policies, G-14 phase 1 note).
- **N4 × N9** — The post-install onLinked hook is explicitly the source-side seam for late-join catch-up: the data cell unicasts state-as-delta-from-empty to just the new subscriber, implemented and validated over 100 seeds with a missed-prefix control. (10/13 §2. Explicit (handshake-based); 20/21 §Pull; 91 G-18/G-22) *Residual*: Catch-up emission is currently unwaved (glitch-free consumers pass it through), and on-demand pull without relinking remains the flagged G-18 residual awaiting G-13 multiplex ports.
- **N4 × N11** — Data invocations crossing links carry outlet-stamped MessageContext while link/management operations carry null context and clear stale waves, and per-link FIFO is what makes per-source wave delivery monotone. (20/22 §MessageContext (normative, as implemented); 20/22 §The glitch-free frontier (composition); 10/13 §Link lifecycle summary) *Residual*: Whether link events themselves receive wave stamps is the separate topology-versioning question (20/22 §Implementation plan item 5, pending) — classified under N4×N13.
- **N4 × N12** — Glitch-freedom rule 4 makes link/unlink events part of the update stream, and the implemented static frontier recomputes the completeness condition from the inlet's live link set on every check, so link operations adapt wave completeness by construction. (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom (opt-in) rule 4; 20/22 §The glitch-free frontier (composition)) *Residual*: Upstream frontier traversal awaits G-13 multiplex ports, and host stamping of topology events (plan item 5) is unbuilt — the spec flags both.
- **N4 × N14** — Link time is the primary SPSC enforcement point: the handshake inspects the contract's payload types and returns Rejected for a second link on an Owned/Leased-carrying outlet, and 10/13 names ownership constraints as one of the things handshakes run (implemented at the FanOutlet.subscribe funnel on every path). (20/23 §The SPSC link rule (normative); 10/13 §Two connectivity styles (normative) / Explicit (handshake-based); 10/12 §Cardinality) *Residual*: Proxy-initiated cross-host links return LinkResult.Deferred with the authoritative handshake on the target host, so an SPSC rejection surfaces only on that host's dead-letter outlet — asynchronous to the remote linker.
- **N4 × N15** — The post-install onLinked hook is the designated source-side seam for late-join catch-up, and every data cell wires it to unicast state-as-delta-from-empty to the new subscriber, with observed-remove tags making catch-up idempotent against duplicated live deltas (G-22 resolved, M4.2). (10/13 §Two connectivity styles (normative) / Explicit (handshake-based); 20/21 §Pull; 20/24 §Required next steps in the family) *Residual*: The catch-up emission is currently unwaved; wave alignment of snapshots waits for the state-request protocol (G-13/G-18).
- **N4 × N18** — Host connect routes through the target-side handshake (policies → cardinality → onLink) and surfaces LinkResult — Deferred plus dead-letter across hosts by recorded M5.4 decision — supervision is explicitly host-management configuration rather than link policy, and the host queue's (priority, sequence) order realizes the per-link FIFO the link invariant requires. (10/13 §Two connectivity styles; 10/13 §Policies; 30/31 §Normative rules) *Residual*: 10/13's status line still flags 'suspension lifecycle and async cross-host results open' — the Deferred path has no completion signal back to the initiator.
- **N4 × N20** — Suspension and migration are defined as link manipulation, unlink() is named load-bearing for exactly this, cross-host links MUST carry the stale-reference fallback, and 30/33's ordering invariant (accepted-before-closure delivered before post-re-resolution sends) discharges 10/13's no-loss invariant end-to-end. (10/13 §Definition; 10/13 §Cross-boundary links; 10/13 §Link lifecycle summary; 30/33 §The drain protocol) *Residual*: The persistent overflow mailbox for indefinitely suspended targets is flagged 'not yet built' (30/33 §Stale references), deferred with G-25.
- **N4 × N22** — A cross-host link is normatively 'one logical link' whose link/unlink/onLink/onUnlink behave identically regardless of realization, composed with the recorded cross-wire handshake contract (Deferred, authoritative handshake on the target host, rejection to dead-letter) and the mandatory stale-reference fallback (fail-fast → re-resolve → park) on cross-host links. Explicit (handshake-based); 40/41 §Wire layer) *Residual*: 10/13's status flags 'async cross-host results open'; remote linkFrom arguments are live objects that cannot cross the wire, so cross-peer linking is restricted to registry proxies + Use.fixed, revisited only when a real topology needs it.

**N5 — Invocations, delegation & fusion**

- **N5 × N6** — Behavior is installed by serve/delegate inside onActivate (eager cells excepted with stated obligations per C-7), serving anew invalidates leases with lazy O(1) re-resolution, and the drain protocol flushes accepted invocations before deactivation with buffered replay running under each invocation's own context. (10/15 §Activation; 10/15 §⚠ CONFLICT (C-7); 10/14 §The Link-and-Lease model; 10/14 §Context propagation (G-4 resolved))
- **N5 × N8** — Push is literally invocations on downstream contracts, dispatched via the three-tier cheapest-path rule, with co-hosted chains fusing to nested direct calls and delegation flattening removing pass-through cells from the per-message path. (20/21 §Push (default, implemented); 20/21 §Fusion and the critical path; 10/14 §Dispatch tiers (normative))
- **N5 × N9** — Pull is deliberately not a new mechanism: late-join catch-up is an ordinary unicast invocation whose state-as-delta-from-empty satisfies the deterministic-application rule, and the proposed state-request is an ordinary invocation traveling upstream. (20/21 §Pull; 10/14 §The core move (ADR 3)) *Residual*: On-demand pull without relinking (G-18 residual) is unbuilt, awaiting the state-request protocol on G-13 multiplex ports.
- **N5 × N11** — Invocation.context carries MessageContext, outlets stamp at emission (fresh when spontaneous, same-wave when reactive), Invocation.invoke is the single restore point so delivery and buffered replay run under the invocation's own context, and every hop including delegated ones rewrites sourcePort (G-4 resolved). (10/14 §Context propagation; 20/22 §MessageContext (normative, as implemented) rules 2 and 4)
- **N5 × N14** — Proxy and dispatch behaviors are ownership-aware by rule: Broadcast refuses Owned/Leased when fanning to more than one target, Buffering MAY hold them (buffering preserves exclusivity, parked Owned stays owned by the link), and bridge egress converts Owned to move-by-serialize while refusing Leased. (20/23 §The SPSC link rule (normative); 20/23 §Implementation (G-21, M5.6); 10/14 §Standard proxy behaviors (implemented)) *Residual*: Supervision RESTART (30/31) restores a spawn-time checkpoint after a failed invocation may have consumed an Owned payload, leaving it neither delivered nor owned — exactly-once under restart is unstated.
- **N5 × N15** — Data-cell traffic is ordinary invocation capture: commands and Propagate(delta) calls are serializable invocations, deltas cross the wire as @SerialName-discriminated polymorphic values in the WireFrame envelope with tags intact, and co-hosted delta chains fuse into nested direct calls per P2. (20/24 §Established pattern (normative template); 10/14 §The core move (ADR 3); 20/21 §Push / §Fusion and the critical path)
- **N5 × N18** — The three dispatch tiers are defined against the host boundary — same-host resolves to a fused zero-cost direct call, cross-host wraps as HostedPortInvocation onto the target's (priority, sequence) queue — and the PORT_API/PORT_MANAGEMENT type split aligns invocations with the host's priority bands and no-result-blocking rule. (10/14 §Dispatch tiers; 30/31 §The host protocol; 30/31 §Normative rules)
- **N5 × N19** — Invocation capture and delivery are defined per color: suspend-aware invokeSuspending with a real continuation, proxied suspend calls captured fire-and-forget (continuation stripped at capture, re-supplied at delivery), wave context riding a coroutine context element, and upstream color coercion is exactly what lets chains fuse to direct calls in one host. (30/32 §How the colors are realized; 30/32 §Compatibility and coercion; 10/14 §Dispatch tiers) *Residual*: Bridge mechanisms at the enqueueHostedInvocation seam are degenerate until bounded intakes exist — 'the safety properties hold vacuously' (30/32 §Bridges).
- **N5 × N20** — Parked traffic IS HostedPortInvocations (already the wire form, contexts riding along), the Buffering/serve/delegate traffic-light idiom is declared the suspension primitive, and stale-location handling is explicitly the Link-and-Lease invalidation story (O(1) invalidate, lazy re-resolution) applied to location. (30/33 §Gaps to close (G-5); 10/14 §The Link-and-Lease model; 30/33 §Stale references; 30/33 §Port-level buffering)
- **N5 × N22** — The three dispatch tiers are the composition: the same captured Invocation is a zero-cost direct call locally, a HostedPortInvocation enqueue cross-host, and a pinned ids-only WireFrame cross-machine (no lambdas or reflect.Method per P9/C-5), with remote sends inheriting the fail-fast + park + re-resolve contract. (10/14 §Dispatch tiers; 40/41 §Wire layer; 10/14 §Reflection budget) *Residual*: Request/response-style management calls over the wire get Deferred/CompletableFuture wrapping with timeouts — a type-safety cost the spec itself notes (40/41 point 5); cross-wire propagation of Invalidating lease re-resolution events is not spelled out.
- **N5 × N25** — 'No new semantics in the DSL layer, ever' — everything the builder does must be expressible as management invocations, and the codegen direction (stable method-id tables, reflection-free proxies) is the recorded C-5 resolution in 10/14. (50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 50/51 §Code generation; 10/14 §Reflection budget) *Residual*: GraphSpec spawn steps carry Serializable lambda CellFactories while P9/10/14 forbid lambdas and classloader-dependent artifacts in serialized wire form — cross-process GraphSpec replay is unevaluated (00/02 §P9 — Serialization-friendly everywhere; 10/14 §The core move).

**N6 — Cell lifecycle**

- **N6 × N8** — Cold ports are dormant metadata and hosting operations on cold cells are guarded errors, push requires HOT, the drain protocol flushes every accepted invocation before deactivation, and suspended targets buffer/park per policy without loss. (10/15 §Normative rules (rules 3-4); 10/13 §Link lifecycle summary; 30/33 §The drain protocol (per host)) *Residual*: Eager cells (C-7) may push unhosted, with the stated obligation to tolerate onActivate never being called.
- **N6 × N9** — onLinked fires 'once the counterpart is reachable', and traffic to a suspended target — including a catch-up delta — parks and replays in order under the drain ordering invariant, so lifecycle transitions preserve catch-up delivery. (10/13 §2. Explicit (handshake-based); 20/21 §Pull; 30/33 §The drain protocol (ordering invariant)) *Residual*: 'Reachable' is not pinned for cold/not-yet-spawned counterparts — whether catch-up fires at link time or at activation is loose; cross-host handshakes return Deferred with rejection to dead-letter.
- **N6 × N11** — Lifecycle/management invocations carry null context, parked invocations carry their MessageContext and replay under the single restore point, and migration was validated to preserve monotonic wave order and state continuity over 100 seeds. (20/22 §MessageContext (normative, as implemented); 30/33 §Constraints from elsewhere; 30/33 §Exit criterion (M3)) *Residual*: Persistence of a source outlet's wave-mint counter across a wire-boundary respawn (cold cell + Stateful snapshot) is unstated — in-process the object moves whole, but a reset counter would re-mint used (sourceId, counter) pairs.
- **N6 × N12** — The spec states the composition directly: parked invocations carry their MessageContext and 'version buffers are cell state, so they capture/restore with the cell', so partially-buffered waves survive suspension and migration. (30/33 §Constraints from elsewhere; 20/22 §Interaction with other parts) *Residual*: This implies GlitchFreeCell must implement Stateful for its per-wave buffer; the obligation is asserted, not spelled out per cell.
- **N6 × N15** — The constructor-serving data cells are the resolved C-7 case: they are legitimate 'eager cells' usable unhosted provided they never assume a host context and tolerate onActivate never being called, while hosted semantics apply only to spawned cells and data cells implement Stateful for drain/migrate survival. (10/15 §⚠ CONFLICT (C-7); 20/24 §Required next steps in the family (G-22)) *Residual*: Default guidance remains onActivate; the per-cell obligation to document which mode each data cell supports is unverified in the spec.
- **N6 × N17** — The implemented durability half is anchored to lifecycle normatively: the drain protocol guarantees onDeactivate runs only after every accepted invocation flushes and captures Stateful snapshots at exactly that point, with restore on in-place resume or migration re-activation (G-16 resolved, M3.3). (10/15 §Normative rules (rule 4, G-16); 20/24 §Durability spectrum (G-25, M3.3 state-capture half)) *Residual*: The journal remainder is undesigned: ordering of journal replay relative to re-activation (before or after onActivate, against which snapshot) is open with G-25.
- **N6 × N18** — Hosts own every lifecycle transition — spawn registers then runs onActivate on the host's execution context, despawn mirrors it, re-spawning a live ref is rejected — and supervision is defined directly in lifecycle terms (RESTART = deactivate → activate → restore spawn-time checkpoint; SUSPEND parks per-cell until resume replays). (10/15 §Activation; 10/15 §Normative rules; 30/31 §Normative rules) *Residual*: Eager cells (C-7) sit outside hosted semantics; how supervision RESTART interacts with a constructor-serving cell rests on the per-cell documentation obligation (10/15 §⚠ CONFLICT C-7).
- **N6 × N19** — Lifecycle and color meet at one specified point: spawn validates BlockingCell/SuspendingCell markers against the host scheduler's color and rejects wrong-color spawns, pure cells are coerced by placement with no adapter classes, and migration re-applies the same validation at the target host. (30/32 §Compatibility and coercion; 30/31 §Colors of hosts; 30/33 §The drain protocol) *Residual*: Whether onActivate/onDeactivate themselves may block or suspend (they are plain funs on Cell) is not addressed per host color.
- **N6 × N20** — The SUSPENDED lifecycle state is realized by the drain protocol — deactivation guaranteed to run only after the accepted queue flushes (phase-2 task below data priority), Stateful snapshots captured at that point, reactivation-in-place legal — and rule 1 (no logic in constructors) exists explicitly so cold cells are safe to create anywhere for mobility. (10/15 §Normative rules; 30/33 §The drain protocol)
- **N6 × N22** — Cold cells are normatively safe to create on machines that will never run them, activation runs on the hosting side's execution context, and remote senders compose with target lifecycle transitions through the specified closable/fail-fast + park + re-resolve contract, so a proxy survives its target suspending, despawning, or relocating. (10/15 §Normative rules; 40/41 §What exists (in-process); 40/41 §Wire layer) *Residual*: Cold-cell serialization is marked '(future)' (10/15 §Cold phase) and reconnection beyond park-and-replay is explicitly out of scope (M5.5).
- **N6 × N25** — The cold phase exists precisely so factories can mint cells anywhere ('safe to create anywhere, including on machines that will never run it — codegen'), GraphSpec spawn steps mint fresh cold cells, and host spawn drives onActivate on the host's execution context — cold-on-build, hot-on-apply is the stated DSL semantics. (10/15 §Normative rules; 10/15 §Hot phase; 50/51 §Graph construction DSL) *Residual*: Eager cells serving in constructors remain a documented exception with stated obligations (10/15 §⚠ CONFLICT C-7); operator combinators on cold handles stay unbuilt (50/51 §Graph construction DSL).
- **N6 × N26** — The generative harness composes the two directly: seeded GraphSpec pipelines are driven with mid-stream late-join and host-migration lifecycle events while the invariant suite is asserted on every graph, and the drain protocol guarantees deactivation only after accepted invocations flush. (50/52 §Invariant testing; 10/15 §Normative rules) *Residual*: Lifecycle of a shadow subgraph (suspending or evicting a NoOp'd candidate) falls under unbuilt G-32 (50/52 §Live invariants).

**N8 — Push propagation & delta algebra**

- **N8 × N9** — Late-join catch-up is defined as push's own mechanism: a state-as-delta-from-empty unicast from the post-install onLinked hook satisfies the deterministic-application rule, after which the live push stream follows. (20/21 §Pull; 20/21 §Incremental vs complete) *Residual*: On-demand pull without relinking is the G-18 residual awaiting the state-request protocol on multiplex ports (G-13); the catch-up emission is currently unwaved.
- **N8 × N11** — Every push emission is stamped by the framework: origination mints a fresh per-source Timestamp from the emitting outlet's monotonic counter, response emissions carry the same timestamp with sourcePort rewritten, fan-out duplicates and fan-in delivers per-input context. (20/22 §MessageContext)
- **N8 × N13** — Structural changes are normatively part of the same causal stream as pushed value updates: link/unlink events are stamped into the wave time domain and the edge set feeding wave t is part of wave t. (20/22 §Topology versioning) *Residual*: Host stamping of topology events is unimplemented (20/22 §Implementation plan item 5, depends on G-12).
- **N8 × N14** — Delta push and ownership compose by construction: exclusive (Owned/Leased) payload contracts force unary links, push fan-out is Rejected at the FanOutlet.subscribe funnel and refused by Broadcast, and Owned→freeze→Frozen is the sanctioned fan-out route. (20/23 §The SPSC link rule; 20/23 §Implementation)
- **N8 × N15** — Data cells are the normative instantiation of the delta rules — command contracts in, effective-only delta emission out — and the requirement that concurrent-producer deltas declare merge semantics is met by commutative/associative/idempotent tag-set union. (20/21 §Incremental vs complete; 20/24 §Established pattern) *Residual*: MapDelta/ListDelta carry documented arrival-order convergence limits until replication pressure (G-23 remainder).
- **N8 × N20** — The drain protocol's ordering invariant — messages accepted before closure delivered before post-re-resolution sends, per-link FIFO end-to-end, parked traffic being HostedPortInvocations replayed in order — states exactly how a live delta stream survives suspension and migration, validated zero-loss/exactly-once over 100 seeds. (30/33 §The drain protocol; 30/33 §Stale references; 30/33 §Exit criterion (M3)) *Residual*: The persistent overflow mailbox for indefinitely suspended targets is spec-flagged 'not yet built' (30/33 §Stale references), so pushes to a long-suspended subgraph park in memory only.
- **N8 × N22** — Delta push over a remote link is the stated third dispatch tier: 41 requires linking to behave identically with only cost differing, and the pinned WireFrame carries delta arguments as @SerialName-pinned polymorphic values (SetDelta named explicitly) with P9 forbidding non-serializable payloads on the wire. (40/41 §Requirement; 40/41 §Wire layer; 20/21 §Push; 00/02 §P9) *Residual*: Spec-flagged corners: corrupt frames dead-letter while traffic continues (40/41 §Wire layer, M5.3) and reconnection beyond park-and-replay is out of scope (M5.5) — a downstream cell sees either as a silently missing prefix of the delta stream.
- **N8 × N25** — The DSL is normatively a thin veneer ('no new semantics in the DSL layer, ever' — every op lowers to spawn/connect management invocations), so push/delta propagation over DSL-built or GraphSpec-replayed links is identical to hand-wired propagation, and the generative harness validates delta pipelines built as GraphSpecs (incremental == batch recompute, cross-view convergence). (50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 20/21 §Push; 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic))
- **N8 × N26** — An invariant is a cell that subscribes to the delta flows it constrains (attaching = linking) and folds effective-only deltas like any subscriber, validated by the generative suite's convergence / incremental==batch / zero-dead-letter assertions. (50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic); 20/21 §Incremental vs complete; 50/52 §Live invariants) *Residual*: Shadow mode is a spec-flagged gap (G-32): NoOp-serving effectful sinks while upstream deltas still fan into the shadow subgraph lacks the effect-classification marker (G-11).

**N9 — Pull, late-join & catch-up**

- **N9 × N13** — A late-join is a topology change whose composition is stated: onLinked fires once the subscriber is reachable, catch-up unicasts then the live stream follows, and the glitch-free completeness condition recomputes its edge set from live links so the new edge joins the condition. (20/21 §Pull; 20/22 §Local glitch-freedom; 20/22 §Topology versioning) *Residual*: Because catch-up is unwaved, the wave at which the new edge starts counting toward completeness is defined only operationally by frontier recompute, not by a stamped topology event.
- **N9 × N14** — Late-join catch-up cannot violate exclusivity because every attach path — including a late subscriber's link — converges on FanOutlet.subscribe, where a second subscriber on an exclusive contract is Rejected before onLinked (and hence catch-up) could ever fire. (20/23 §Implementation; 20/21 §Pull) *Residual*: Catch-up after a legal consumer swap (unlink then relink) on an Owned-carrying contract is unaddressed, though data-cell deltas are not ownership-wrapped today.
- **N9 × N15** — G-22 is resolved: every data cell wires onLinked to unicast state-as-delta-from-empty, and observed-remove tags make the catch-up idempotent against replayed or duplicated live deltas (100-seed validated with a missed-prefix control). (20/21 §Pull; 20/24 §Required next steps) *Residual*: Idempotence rests on the tag algebra, so the map/list families inherit their documented arrival-order limits at catch-up.
- **N9 × N18** — Late-join catch-up runs through ordinary host delivery — the post-install onLinked hook unicasts state-as-delta-from-empty via outlet.at(link.to) and the host's (priority, sequence) per-link FIFO guarantees the snapshot precedes subsequent live deltas, validated cross-host over 100 seeds with a missed-prefix control. (20/21 §Pull; 30/31 §Normative rules) *Residual*: Spec-flagged G-18 residual: on-demand pull without relinking is unbuilt; also RESTART re-activation never refires onLinked, so subscribers get no re-catch-up after a producer's state reverts (unflagged).
- **N9 × N20** — Catch-up traffic is ordinary link traffic, so the drain protocol's park/replay and the per-link ordering invariant carry a mid-flight catch-up across suspension and migration unchanged, and late-join combined with migration events is exercised by the generative harness (G-31). (30/33 §The drain protocol; 20/21 §Pull; 90/91 §Gaps — process (G-31)) *Residual*: onLinked firing while the producer host is mid-drain (snapshot emitted from a state being captured) is not explicitly addressed.
- **N9 × N25** — A DSL/GraphSpec connect is the same management connect whose post-install onLinked hook fires the state-as-delta-from-empty catch-up unicast, and the generative harness's mid-stream late joiner over GraphSpec-built graphs validates late joiner == early joiner (100 seeds with missed-prefix control). (20/21 §Pull; 50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic))
- **N9 × N26** — Stated directly: 'a late-linked invariant receives catch-up like any subscriber (21)', so attaching an invariant mid-run folds the state-as-delta-from-empty snapshot and then the live stream, with observed-remove tags making the baseline idempotent against duplicated live deltas. (50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic); 20/21 §Pull) *Residual*: Catch-up emission is currently unwaved (spec-flagged in 20/21 §Pull), so a late-linked invariant cannot wave-align its baseline until the state-request protocol on multiplex ports lands (G-18 residual, G-13).

**N11 — MessageContext & per-source waves**

- **N11 × N12** — Glitch-freedom is built directly on MessageContext: cells buffer per (sourceId, counter), waves flush in per-source counter order with per-link FIFO making completion monotone per source, and cross-source joins are defined to get convergence rather than simultaneity (G-20 decided). (20/22 §MessageContext; 20/22 §Local glitch-freedom; 20/22 §Topology versioning) *Residual*: Cycles remain open; upstream frontier traversal awaits multiplex ports (G-13).
- **N11 × N14** — The one point where context handling and ownership meet — fan-out duplicating an invocation's context along with its payload — is closed by construction because SPSC rejects a second consumer on exclusive contracts at link time, and buffered replay delivers a parked Owned invocation once under its own restored context. (20/22 §MessageContext; 20/23 §The SPSC link rule)
- **N11 × N15** — The spec explicitly separates the two uses of the Timestamp shape: OR-set tags are minted cell-locally per add instance while the wave context rides delta invocations unchanged, precisely because a wave id repeats across every cell it touches and cannot serve as a unique tag. (20/22 §Interaction with other parts; 20/24 §Established pattern)
- **N11 × N18** — Context transport through hosts is normatively pinned: outlets stamp at emission, the cross-host proxy captures context into invocations, Invocation.invoke is the single restore point so both queue delivery and parked/supervision replay run under the invocation's own context, management invocations carry null context, and per-link FIFO makes wave completion monotone per source. (20/22 §MessageContext; 30/31 §Normative rules)
- **N11 × N19** — 30/32 states the composition directly: the wave context rides a coroutine context element across suspension points, proxied suspend calls are captured fire-and-forget with the continuation stripped and re-supplied at delivery, and any-color cross-host send is one enqueue of an invocation already carrying its context. (30/32 §How the colors are realized; 20/22 §MessageContext)
- **N11 × N20** — Both sides state it and cross-reference each other — buffered waves survive suspension/migration because Buffering parks invocations in order with their contexts and context rides inside invocations — and the M3 exit criterion validated monotonic wave order through mid-stream migration with a serialization round-trip. (20/22 §Interaction with other parts; 30/33 §Constraints from elsewhere; 30/33 §Exit criterion (M3))
- **N11 × N22** — MessageContext crosses the wire by construction: the pinned WireFrame envelope carries a context field with Timestamp under a stable @SerialName discriminator, G-4's resolution records context capture at the cross-host proxy, and 41 explicitly sequenced the wire layer after G-4 precisely so context need not be retrofitted into a shipped format. (40/41 §Wire layer; 40/41 §Ordering of work; 20/22 §MessageContext)
- **N11 × N25** — DSL operations are management invocations, which normatively carry null MessageContext and clear any stale wave, and GraphSpec replay mints fresh cells whose outlets mint fresh per-source Timestamps only at origination — construction never fabricates or perturbs wave context. (20/22 §MessageContext; 50/51 §Graph construction DSL)
- **N11 × N26** — An invariant cell receives context-stamped data invocations through ordinary transparent flow and fan-out duplication (framework stamps at outlets; cell logic never touches context), and violations it emits in response to an input carry the triggering wave's timestamp per rule 2. (20/22 §MessageContext; 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic)) *Residual*: A late-linked invariant's catch-up baseline arrives unwaved (20/21 §Pull), so its first fold input has no wave id.

**N12 — Glitch-freedom & the frontier**

- **N12 × N13** — Rule 4 of glitch-freedom makes topology consistency part of the contract — the set of edges feeding wave t is part of wave t's input completeness condition — implemented as frontier recompute from the inlet's live link set on every completeness check. (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom; 20/22 §Topology versioning) *Residual*: Upstream frontier traversal beyond the static inlet link set awaits multiplex ports (G-13); host stamping of topology events pending.
- **N12 × N15** — Glitch-free buffering and the tag algebra compose as designed: wave context rides delta invocations unchanged while tags stay cell-local, and derived cells like UnionSetCell additionally dedup duplicate deliveries across diamond fan-ins. (20/22 §Interaction with other parts; 20/24 §Established pattern) *Residual*: Operator cells that absorb tag churn without flipping membership (effective-only) leave the absorbed-wave completeness question of 20/22 open.
- **N12 × N20** — The two sections mutually specify the composition: 20/22 states buffered waves survive suspension/migration because buffering happens at ports and context rides in invocations, and 30/33 lists glitch-freedom as a constraint — parked invocations carry their MessageContext and version buffers are cell state that captures/restores with the cell through the drain snapshot. (20/22 §Interaction with other parts; 30/33 §Constraints from elsewhere)
- **N12 × N22** — Glitch-free buffering needs only per-link FIFO plus context-on-invocations, and both are normative across boundaries: per-link ordering is required end-to-end for cross-boundary links including re-resolution, parked remote traffic replays in order (M5.4), and context rides inside the WireFrame. (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom; 10/13 §Cross-boundary links; 10/13 §Link lifecycle summary; 40/41 §Wire layer) *Residual*: Corrupt frames dead-letter while traffic continues (40/41 §Wire layer, M5.3), which can leave a wave permanently incomplete in a glitch-free version buffer — unaddressed; upstream frontier traversal (needed to discover a frontier across the bridge) is spec-flagged as awaiting G-13.
- **N12 × N25** — The implemented static frontier is the inlet's current link set recomputed on every completeness check, so links added by DSL or GraphSpec replay — ordinary management connects under the 'no new semantics' rule — adapt a glitch-free cell's completeness condition exactly like hand-built links. (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom; 50/51 §Graph construction DSL) *Residual*: Upstream frontier traversal beyond the immediate link set awaits multiplex ports (G-13); this is a spec-flagged N12 limitation independent of the construction path.

**N13 — Topology versioning**

- **N13 × N14** — The interaction point is the link operation itself and both sides define it: the handshake inspects payload contracts and rejects a violating second link, while a parked Owned message remains owned by the link across drain and relink so consumer swaps preserve exactly-once. (20/23 §The SPSC link rule; 20/22 §Topology versioning)
- **N13 × N15** — Commutative/associative/idempotent tag merge makes set/counter convergence independent of arrival order and therefore of topology churn, while map/list deltas carry documented single-stream limits that multi-path topologies would break. (20/24 §Established pattern; 20/22 §Topology versioning) *Residual*: Map/list arrival-order semantics assume single-stream delivery, so topology-induced rerouting or diamond duplication falls outside their documented guarantee.
- **N13 × N25** — DSL/GraphSpec steps lower to host-applied link operations, and topology versioning normatively requires each host-applied link/unlink to be stamped into the same logical-time domain as data waves — the DSL introduces no structural semantics of its own to version. (20/22 §Topology versioning; 50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 20/22 §Implementation plan) *Residual*: Host stamping of topology events is pending (implementation plan item 5; the static-frontier live-link recompute is the interim), and GraphSpec replay claims no atomicity, so intermediate topologies during a replay onto a live graph are wave-visible per-link.
- **N13 × N26** — Attaching an invariant is itself a link event under the topology-versioning discipline, the late-linked invariant receives catch-up like any subscriber, and the generative harness asserts the invariant suite across mid-stream topology changes (late joiner, host migration) with an order-bias control. (50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic); 20/22 §Topology versioning; 20/21 §Pull) *Residual*: Catch-up is unwaved (spec-flagged, 20/21 §Pull), so an invariant attached mid-wave cannot align its baseline with the wave/topology version at which it joined.

**N14 — Ownership contracts & SPSC**

- **N14 × N15** — Data-cell delta contracts compose with ownership through the generic enforcement funnel: the KSP processor scans payload types for Owned/Leased and delta types are plain @Serializable values with no markers, so they are non-exclusive and FanOutlet broadcast plus late-join catch-up are permitted by construction, while any exclusive payload on a contract would be Rejected at link/subscribe time. (20/23 §Implementation (G-21, M5.6); 20/23 §The SPSC link rule; 20/24 §Established pattern) *Residual*: 20/24 never assigns an ownership class to deltas — hot-path Owned/Leased delta variants (in-place delta mutation per P2) are unexplored; deltas are only implicitly Borrowed/Frozen-like by their fan-out usage.
- **N14 × N20** — Both documents state the composition rule in matching terms: a parked Owned message is still owned by the link through suspension/migration, Buffering preserves exclusivity, and exactly-once consumption must survive replay. (20/23 §The SPSC link rule; 30/33 §Constraints from elsewhere; 30/33 §Port-level buffering) *Residual*: Cross-machine migrate of a host holding parked Leased invocations collides latently with 'Leased MUST NOT cross machine boundaries' — drain step 5 transfers parked invocations but bridge egress refuses Leased, and already-captured parked payloads cannot be frozen or copied first.
- **N14 × N22** — The boundary corollaries of the SPSC rule are normative and implemented at BridgeEgressCell: Owned crosses the machine boundary as move-by-serialize (the sender's wrapper is consumed as the frame is encoded) and Leased is refused at the boundary as a send-time check, with Owned/Frozen/Borrowed wire-registered payloads. (20/23 §The SPSC link rule (normative); 20/23 §Implementation (G-21, M5.6); 40/41 §Wire layer) *Residual*: Reconnect beyond park-and-replay is explicitly out of scope (G-15 residual, 40/41 §Wire layer M5.5), so an Owned payload whose wrapper was consumed at encode but whose frame is lost on a dropped connection has no stated recovery story.
- **N14 × N25** — The KSP contract processor emits the exclusive bit into generated MethodDescriptors so enforcement reads metadata, and the DSL's spawn/connect apply real management invocations whose link rejections 'fail construction loudly', so an SPSC-violating graph{} is rejected at build time by the same link-time funnel. (20/23 §Implementation (G-21, M5.6); 20/23 §The SPSC link rule (normative); 50/51 §Graph construction DSL (G-30, implemented M4.5)) *Residual*: The secondary whole-graph validation pass (20/23 enforcement point 2, before/at activation) is named but absent from the implemented funnel list.

**N15 — Data cells, mutability classes & merge tags**

- **N15 × N17** — Every data cell implements Stateful so tag state is captured at drain and round-trips real serialization on migrate (G-22 resolved and test-verified), which is precisely the implemented state-capture half of the durability spectrum. (20/24 §Required next steps in the family; 20/24 §Durability spectrum) *Residual*: The spec-flagged journal remainder (G-25): whether replayed command invocations re-mint identical Timestamp tags (is the per-cell counter part of the snapshot?) is unstated — nondeterministic re-minting would desynchronize downstream tag state.
- **N15 × N20** — Data cells are Stateful with drain/migrate round-trips verified, parked invocations replay in per-link order, and onLinked catch-up is idempotent thanks to tags, so migration mid-stream composes with the delta algebra by design and is covered by the M3 exit test over 100 seeds. (20/24 §Required next steps in the family; 30/33 §The drain protocol; 30/33 §Exit criterion (M3))
- **N15 × N22** — Every delta type is @Serializable with a stable @SerialName and crosses the wire tags-included as polymorphic values in the WireFrame envelope, so causal merge semantics hold across processes, validated by the M5.3 bridged generative harness (100 seeds with drop/corrupt controls). (20/24 §Established pattern (normative template) (M5.2 note); 40/41 §Wire layer)
- **N15 × N25** — Data cells are the DSL's demonstrated vocabulary — graph{} spawns SetCell/UnionSetCell, GraphSpec replay mints fresh cells with the same topology, and the generative harness emits seeded data-cell pipelines as GraphSpecs built on one host and replayed verbatim onto another (G-30 resolved, serialization round-trip verified). (50/51 §Graph construction DSL (G-30, implemented M4.5); 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic) (M4.6); 20/24 §Required next steps in the family)
- **N15 × N26** — G-23 convergence is validated invariant-style (200-seed tag-union interleaving test plus an order-biased control) and the M4.6 generative harness asserts cross-view convergence, incremental == batch recompute, late-joiner equivalence, a non-negative count InvariantCell, and zero dead letters over seeded data-cell pipelines. (20/24 §Established pattern (normative template) (G-23); 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic) (M4.6)) *Residual*: MapDelta/ListDelta's documented single-stream convergence limits bound what convergence invariants can assert for multi-writer map/list flows.

**N17 — Durability & journal replay**

- **N17 × N20** — The implemented halves are one mechanism by explicit cross-reference: Stateful.snapshot()/restore() is captured by the drain protocol and forced through a real serialization round-trip on migrate, with 30/33 G-5 item 3 tying state capture to the 24 durability snapshots. (20/24 §Durability spectrum; 30/33 §The drain protocol; 30/33 §Gaps to close (G-5)) *Residual*: Spec-flagged corners remain: the persistent overflow mailbox for indefinitely suspended targets (30/33 §Stale references, 'not yet built') and the invocation journal (G-25) — including whether a journal travels with a migrating host.

**N18 — Hosts: queues, priorities, supervision, hierarchy**

- **N18 × N19** — Host-color composition is normative: one ManagedHost carries its color on the injected HostScheduler, spawn validates BlockingCell/SuspendingCell markers against it, and cross-host sends of any color pair reduce to a single non-blocking offer onto the unbounded (priority, sequence) intake, so the bridge table is explicitly degenerate. (30/31 §Colors of hosts; 30/32 §Compatibility and coercion; 30/32 §Bridges) *Residual*: Spec-flagged corner: bounded intakes/backpressure are deferred with no milestone; when intakes can refuse, the four ADR 2 bridges become real code at enqueueHostedInvocation and their interplay with the priority bands and supervision SUSPEND parking is unevaluated — the safety properties currently hold vacuously (30/32 §Bridges).
- **N18 × N20** — The drain protocol is expressed in the host's own queue machinery (management task at priority 0 closes the intake, completion task at 30 below data's 20 flushes accepted traffic before deactivation) and the supervision-mobility interaction is normative: supervision is per-host, does not migrate, and a suspended cell leaving the host dead-letters its parked traffic. (30/33 §The drain protocol; 30/31 §Normative rules; 30/31 §The host protocol) *Residual*: Spec-flagged: host hierarchy G-28 (resource limits, shutdown cascade, spawn placement) is undesigned yet named as needed for mobility (30/31 §Hierarchy of hosts).
- **N18 × N22** — Boundary crossing is normative — a port used across hosts wraps calls as HostedPortInvocation and enqueues on the target host, the host's management surface is ordinary ports so hosts are administrable remotely with no special mechanism, and corrupt wire frames dead-letter on the receiving host while traffic continues. (30/31 §The host protocol; 30/31 §Definition; 40/41 §Wire layer) *Residual*: G-15's recorded remaining interims: reconnection beyond park-and-replay out of scope, in-process JDK dynamic proxies still interim (40/41 §Wire layer; 90/91 §Gaps — distribution (40)).
- **N18 × N25** — The DSL is normatively a thin veneer over HostManagementApi — every builder operation lowers to spawn/connect management invocations on the host's management inlet (priority 0, never starved by data), with 'no new semantics in the DSL layer, ever' as the recorded composition rule. (50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 30/31 §The host protocol) *Residual*: GraphSpec targets a single management inlet and has no vocabulary for host-level configuration (supervise steps) or spawn placement across a host hierarchy (G-28 undesigned, 30/31 §Hierarchy of hosts).
- **N18 × N26** — Both sides state the composition: per-cell ErrorReporting outlets emit CellError under every supervision policy for consumption by invariant cells, the harness asserts zero dead letters, and the C-2 resolution names the SimulationController-configured ManagedHost as the deterministic test host of 50/52. (30/31 §Normative rules; 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic); 30/31 §Host vs Runner duplication (C-2, resolved)) *Residual*: Invariant fold continuity across a supervised RESTART is unaddressed — RESTART restores the spawn-time Stateful checkpoint, so a downstream InvariantCell's fold may have observed emissions the restored cell no longer accounts for.

**N19 — Colors, coercion, bridges & backpressure**

- **N19 × N20** — Color and mobility compose by stated rules: color validation applies at the migration target (marked cells crossing colors is a caller error, pure cells cross freely) and on a coroutine host a task suspended mid-message completes before drain deactivation (actor semantics). (30/33 §The drain protocol; 30/32 §Compatibility and coercion) *Residual*: Because bounded intakes are deferred (30/32 §Bridges), park/replay has never contended with intake refusal — backpressure-during-drain composition is unevaluated.
- **N19 × N26** — The deterministic SimulationController issues schedulers of either color with suspend-aware stepping (a task runs undispatched until it completes or genuinely suspends), and 52 names this simulated configuration as the substrate the invariant/generative harness runs on. (30/32 §How the colors are realized; 50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic); 30/31 §Host vs Runner duplication (C-2, resolved)) *Residual*: The bounded-intake/backpressure gap has no milestone and its bridge safety properties 'hold vacuously' (30/32 §Bridges), so there is nothing the invariant harness can exercise for that half of the node until intakes can refuse.

**N20 — Mobility & parking**

- **N20 × N22** — The spec records one unified mechanism: Location = Local(host) | Remote(bridge sink) in the same LocationRegistry, with park/replay applying identically to closure, migration, and the wire, and remote sends inheriting the fail-fast + re-resolve + park contract — validated by 50-seed mid-stream migration over remote addressing. (30/33 §Gaps to close (G-5); 40/41 §Wire layer; 41 §What exists (in-process)) *Residual*: Spec-flagged edges: reconnection beyond park-and-replay is out of scope (40/41 §Wire layer, M5.5) and the persistent overflow mailbox for indefinite suspension is not yet built (30/33 §Stale references).

(50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 30/33 §Stale references: closable queues (normative); 30/31 §The host protocol) *Residual*: Behavior of spawn/connect landing inside the drain window (after intake close, before respawn/republish) is not pinned — e.g. whether a mid-drain spawn joins the migration batch or is deactivated without ever activating.

(50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic); 30/33 §Exit criterion (M3) — met; 90/91 §Gaps — process (50)) *Residual*: Whether InvariantCell's own fold state is Stateful (surviving its own host's drain/migration) is not stated — a migrated invariant may silently restart its fold.

**N22 — Location transparency & wire**

- **N22 × N26** — The wire's correctness story is explicitly the invariant machinery: the full wire format runs under the 100-seed generative harness across two registries with drop/corrupt control runs (corrupt frames dead-letter, traffic continues) as 'the wire's P1 proof', capped by the M5 exit DistributedCollaborativeAppTest. - **N23 × N24** — The glossary records the composing decision — replicas are co-existing Instances of one logical cell (G-8's logicalId, decided for M6), 'incarnation' is explicitly reserved for the evolution track — and 42 adds the normative constraint that nothing in layers 10–30 may assume one live instance except declared single-writer. ## 6. Challenges

Each challenge below is one mechanism question consolidated from the TENSION
pairs listed in its restatement, resolved as a **design proposal** (candidate
mechanisms, recommendation, principle check, spec impact). Substrate
challenges were resolved first; their recommendations were injected into every
dependent challenge as fixed decisions, so the resolutions form one mutually
consistent design, verified by a final cross-check (§8 records the verdicts).

### I-1 — Multiplex sub-port model: unit of contract, cardinality, ordering, policy, and addressing (G-13)

> Member pairs: N1×N3, N2×N3, N3×N4, N3×N5, N3×N8, N3×N11, N3×N14, N3×N18, N3×N19, N3×N20, N3×N22, N3×N25
> Existing gaps touched: G-13, G-11, G-14 · Confidence: high · Substrate: yes
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 11/12 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — Everything the resolution adds beyond M6.1: the PORT_PROTOCOL third dispatch class, ProtocolDescriptor/ProtocolRegistry generation, Link.protocolCapabilities negotiation at handshake, the seven normative rules (especially the explicit rejection of data sub-…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

G-13 (10/12 §Multiplexed ports and generic protocols) requires ports that carry **several protocols at once** — "generic protocols (attention propagation 30/34, time/consistency requests 20/22, link management 10/13) stacked beside the cell-specific contract, with composable handlers." The minimal form shipped in M6.1: `cell.protocol.ProtocolSupport` gives any port sub-channels keyed by well-known `ProtocolId`s "sharing the port's existing links … one map lookup per delivery," and attention (34) plus suspension notices ride it. The spec explicitly leaves open: "full multiplex *data* sub-ports (several data protocols on one link/queue slot), the state-request protocol (21, G-18 residual), and wire transport for generic protocols."

**The single mechanism question**: when several protocols share one physical link, is the *sub-port* (ProtocolId-keyed) or the *shared physical link* the unit of — contract identity, cardinality, ownership exclusivity, handshake/policy, ordering/priority, closable-intake parking, and wire addressing?

**Member pairs** pull in different directions on exactly this axis:
- Toward *sub-port as unit*: N2×N3 wants fan-shaped attention aggregation beside a OneToOne exclusive data protocol on the same link (10/12 §Cardinality); N3×N14 asks whether one `Owned`/`Leased` sub-contract forces unary cardinality on all co-resident protocols (20/23 §The SPSC link rule).
- Toward *link as unit*: N3×N4 notes sub-ports "sharing one link and one queue slot" collide with per-link handshake, policy, and FIFO (10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based)); N3×N8 and N3×N18 note data deltas ride data band 20 while management rides band 0, and "one queue slot" leaves the relative ordering of mixed traffic unevaluated (30/31 §The host protocol).
- Orthogonal but co-dependent: N3×N5 (contractId/methodId dispatch vs ProtocolId dispatch, 10/14 §Dispatch tiers); N3×N11 (what PortRef/wave a sub-port stamps, 20/22 §MessageContext); N3×N19 (counter-directional protocols crossing unidirectional color bridges, 30/32 §Bridges); N3×N20 (do generic protocols park with data or bypass like management, 30/33 §The drain protocol); N3×N22 (the shipped `WireFrame` addresses one contract via contractId/methodId + portName with no ProtocolId slot, 40/41 §Wire layer); N3×N25 (GraphSpec connect steps address (cell, portName) with no ProtocolId slot, 50/51 §Graph construction DSL).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: G-13 is a *proposal* whose only concrete text is "sharing one link and one queue slot." Every specified surface — PortRegistry naming, `@Contract` classification, dispatch tables, handshake/policy scoping, priority bands, closable parking, the SPSC exclusive bit, WireFrame addressing, and GraphSpec connect steps — was designed for **one contract per link** and has no defined slot for sub-port traffic. The M6.1 minimal form answered the metadata case (attention, suspension) in-process; the residual is precisely the unit-of-X decision for everything else.

#### 2. Why this is hard

The principles and prior decisions pull against each other:

- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path)** vs sub-port generality. If every ProtocolId is a first-class port with its own cardinality/ownership/policy/FIFO, dispatch becomes *link lookup + protocol lookup + per-protocol machinery* on paths that P2 budgets at "a volatile read + an enqueue." The recorded "one table lookup" reflection budget (10/14, C-5) assumes one dispatch key.
- **P5 (correctness by construction)** vs shared-link ambiguity. The SPSC exclusive bit (20/23) and cardinality (10/12) are enforced *per link* at link time. A shared link with one exclusive data sub-contract and one fan-in metadata sub-contract has no single answer to "what is this link's cardinality?" unless we decide whether ownership is a link property or a sub-port property.
- **P4 / decided null-context management** vs waves on sub-ports. The recorded decision "management invocations carry null MessageContext" and G-20 per-source waves assume each *data* hop presents one emitting PortRef. A ProtocolId sub-port sharing the link has no obvious wave identity.
- **Decided drain ordering invariant** ("invocations accepted before intake closure are delivered before anything sent after re-resolution; per-link FIFO end-to-end", 30/33) vs the fact that the very protocols catch-up depends on (state-request, frontier discovery, link management, resume) would, if parked *with* data, stall exactly the traffic that is supposed to unpark the data — a deadlock.
- **Decided wire form** ("ids-only, version byte reserved; no class/method names", 40/41) vs a new ProtocolId addressing dimension — the retrofit cost 40/41 explicitly warns against.
- **P10 / P6 (niche first, interest drives resources)** counsel *against* building general multiplexing "just in case." The niche needs attention, suspension, state-request, frontier discovery, link management — a *bounded, known* set of framework metadata protocols — not an open user-facing sub-port framework.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Full sub-port symmetry (sub-port = unit)

*Semantics*: every ProtocolId is a first-class port sharing the physical link: its own contract, cardinality (FanInlet/FanOutlet/OneToOnePort), ownership regime, LinkPolicy set, per-protocol FIFO, and handshake accept/reject. The link is a passive bundle; PortRegistry gains sub-entries; WireFrame gains a ProtocolId dimension.

*Fast-path cost*: two lookups per delivery (which sub-port, then dispatch) plus per-sub-port state; the data path pays for machinery only metadata needs.

*Failure modes*: cardinality/ownership conflict on the shared link has no single answer (N2×N3, N3×N14); handshake bootstrap paradox (link management riding the substrate that link management must first establish, N3×N4); wave identity per sub-port undefined (N3×N11); wire retrofit is a genuine new addressing dimension (N3×N22).

*Tradeoffs*: maximally general; violates P2, P5, P10. Rejected.

##### Candidate B — Pure link-as-unit, protocols as reserved method ranges

*Semantics*: the link has exactly one contract; "protocols" are reserved method-id ranges on that one contract. No sub-channels at all; attention/suspension become methods the data contract must declare.

*Fast-path cost*: minimal — one dispatch, as today.

*Failure modes*: cannot express counter-directional flow (attention travels *upstream* against data, N3×N19); cannot give a protocol its own cardinality (fan-in attention on a OneToOne data link, N2×N3); conflates metadata lifecycle with data lifecycle — protocols would park with data and deadlock (N3×N20); forces every data contract to declare framework methods, violating composability (P4) and the clean `@Contract` model.

*Tradeoffs*: cheapest, but structurally cannot carry the generic-protocol requirement G-13 exists to satisfy. Rejected.

##### Candidate C — Metadata plane / third dispatch class (recommended)

*Semantics*: the **link is the unit for all data concerns** (identity, cardinality, ownership/SPSC, handshake, policy, data-FIFO, waves). Generic protocols are a **bounded, framework-owned metadata plane** — a *third dispatch class* `PORT_PROTOCOL` parallel to the existing `PORT_MANAGEMENT`/`PORT_API` split — that rides an already-established link, keyed by ProtocolId, with a static per-protocol descriptor (direction, band, ordering lane, protocol-intrinsic cardinality). Protocols are management-class (null context, bypass parking), never carry `Owned`/`Leased`, and are never user *data* sub-ports. Arbitrary data sub-ports are rejected: a second data contract between the same two cells is a second link.

*Fast-path cost*: the data path is untouched — `PORT_API` branches straight to the data path as today. Only `PORT_PROTOCOL` messages pay the `ProtocolSupport` map lookup, exactly the M6.1 minimal form, and off the data hot path.

*Failure modes*: none of the member-pair conflicts survive (see §4); residual risk is confined to protocol capability negotiation across peers and the reverse-channel wire realization (§8), both bounded.

*Tradeoffs*: gives up general user-facing multiplexing (the niche does not need it, P10) in exchange for a model where every existing surface — dispatch, cardinality, ownership, waves, parking, wire — keeps its single-contract meaning and gains one clearly-scoped enum variant.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt the **metadata-plane** model: the physical link is the unit of contract identity, cardinality, ownership/SPSC, handshake, policy, and data-FIFO; generic protocols are a bounded, framework-owned metadata plane — a third dispatch class parallel to `PORT_MANAGEMENT`/`PORT_API` — that rides an already-established link but never becomes a data sub-port.

**Data shapes**
- `ProtocolId(name)` stays as today, but each well-known protocol also has a generated `ProtocolDescriptor { protocolId; contractId (= the `@Contract`-generated id of the protocol interface); direction: Upstream | Downstream; band: Int (host priority band); lane: OrderingLane (its own per-link FIFO, independent of the data lane); cardinality: FanInMerge | FanOutBroadcast (protocol-intrinsic, NOT the link's) }`, collected into a `ProtocolRegistry` beside `ContractRegistry`.
- `HostedPortInvocation.Type` gains a third variant `PORT_PROTOCOL` (today it is exactly `{PORT_MANAGEMENT, PORT_API}`). This is the single dispatch key: `PORT_API` → the data path (unchanged), `PORT_MANAGEMENT` → the port's management API, `PORT_PROTOCOL` → `ProtocolSupport.deliver(protocolId, link, msg)` (one map lookup, as the M6.1 minimal form already does in-process).
- `Link` records a negotiated `protocolCapabilities: Set<ProtocolId>` (the intersection of what both ports' `ProtocolSupport` declares), established once at the ordinary 10/13 handshake. Unsupported protocols drop silently, as today.
- `WireFrame` is unchanged structurally: `PORT_PROTOCOL` joins the existing `type` field and the protocol interface's `contractId`/`methodId` already identify the message. Bump the reserved version byte only if the enum's wire encoding is not additively compatible.

**Rules the model introduces (normative)**
1. A link carries exactly ONE primary data contract. That contract alone owns the link's cardinality (FanInlet/FanOutlet/OneToOnePort), its SPSC/ownership exclusivity (the KSP exclusive bit, enforced at `FanOutlet.subscribe`), its MessageContext waves, and its data FIFO lane. Need a second data contract between the same two cells? Add a second link (a second port pair). There are no data sub-ports.
2. Generic protocols are management-class: their invocations carry NULL MessageContext (they never mint, carry, or clear waves), and they ride the always-open inlet — they BYPASS data-path parking on a closed/draining host, exactly as the management inlet does (30/33). This is mandatory, not optional: the protocols that catch-up and re-resolution depend on (state-request, frontier-discovery, link-management, attention/resume) would deadlock if parked behind the data they are meant to unpark.
3. Because they bypass the data FIFO/drain ordering, every generic protocol MUST be idempotent and tolerant of reordering/duplication relative to the data stream (attention = idempotent max/band-change; suspension resume replays as late-join catch-up; state-request idempotent). Each protocol occupies its OWN ordering lane and priority band per its descriptor; they do not interleave in the data lane — refining G-13's "one queue slot" phrasing to "one link, separate lanes."
4. Generic protocol contracts MUST NOT declare `Owned`/`Leased` payloads (enforced by the same KSP scan that emits the exclusive bit). Thus a co-resident exclusive data contract constrains only its own link's cardinality, never the fan-shaped attention channel beside it; the SPSC-vs-multiplex tension dissolves.
5. Protocol cardinality is protocol-intrinsic and independent of link cardinality: attention is FanInMerge (aggregate-by-max across links, M6), suspension notices are FanOutBroadcast. This composes on any link cardinality because protocols carry no ownership and are commutative metadata.
6. Directionality lives on the descriptor. Upstream protocols travel producer-ward, downstream protocols consumer-ward. Cross-host: the bridge cell pair becomes protocol-aware — a `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame is emitted by the egress on the sending side and delivered to `ProtocolSupport` on the receiving side; a counter-directional (upstream) protocol simply uses the reverse bridge path that the link already maintains for re-resolution. No new bridge type; a protocol message is an ordinary frame tagged with direction, closing the "generic protocols have null endpoints on bridged links" gap.
7. Delegation/fusion rebind the DATA contract only; protocol capabilities are link-scoped and cheaply re-negotiated on relink. The DSL/GraphSpec keeps addressing links by (cell, portName) with no ProtocolId slot — protocol capabilities are auto-negotiated port metadata (emitted by codegen alongside ownership flags and color), never a connect-step argument.
