**Net effect**: dispatch stays one type-branch plus at most one map lookup; the data hot path is untouched (P2); ownership, waves, cardinality, and FIFO remain link-level and correct-by-construction (P5); and the wire retrofit is one enum variant (P9). The single unifying principle: the link is the unit for everything that touches user data; generic protocols are management-plane metadata that rides the link, keyed by ProtocolId, and never acquires data-port machinery.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — protocols reduce to link-scoped dispatch + ordinary invocations; no new concurrency primitive; every statement meaningful single-threaded (the M6.1 form already delivers synchronously in simulation). |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — data path (`PORT_API`) is unchanged; protocol dispatch is one map lookup on a separate branch, off the data hot path. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — protocols ride explicit links; the negotiated capability set is recorded on the `Link` object and is inspectable. |
| P4 Local compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global coordination; attention aggregation is local; protocols are per-link metadata. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — dispatch class is a type (`PORT_PROTOCOL`); descriptors are generated; ownership-freedom and null-context are KSP-enforced; band/direction/lane are static. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — attention is the exemplar protocol on this plane; nothing is built "just in case" (data sub-ports rejected). |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — no bearing on boundary controls. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — protocol capabilities are re-negotiated on relink; delegation rebinds the data contract; nothing assumes a static graph. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `PORT_PROTOCOL` frames are ids-only (protocol interface's contractId/methodId); protocol contracts are `@Contract`-generated; no lambdas/reflection on the wire. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — the deliberate rejection of general data sub-ports in favor of a bounded framework metadata set is the niche-first trade. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: generic protocols carry null context and never mint waves; wave minting remains a data-outlet concern.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent: no global coordination introduced; attention aggregation and protocol dispatch are local.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: protocols ride links across a moving host; nothing per-cell added.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent: protocols bypass parking exactly as the management inlet does; no new suspension mechanism, and rule 2 reuses the existing always-open-inlet behavior.
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay mechanism** — Consistent: protocol re-resolution uses the same registry; the bridge pair (rule 6) reuses the existing wire path.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: the state-request protocol is answered by an ordinary state-as-delta on the requester's data inlet; no snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, NOT wave ids** — Untouched.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent, with a stated refinement: generic protocols are *push-only* (like data) AND *null-context* (like management). They are management-class contracts (`management = true`) that happen to be push-only — the flag permits returns but does not require them, so no amendment.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** — Consistent: the metadata plane is not a synchronization protocol; state-request reuses the data reply path; no second sync mechanism.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: `PORT_PROTOCOL` joins the existing `type` field; contractId already addresses the protocol; the reserved version byte is bumped only if the enum encoding demands — this is the byte doing its reserved job.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent for data: the data lane's FIFO is untouched. Rule 3 places protocols out-of-band and imposes an idempotence/reorder-tolerance requirement so bypassing the drain ordering is safe.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time** — Consistent: link cardinality is the data contract's (link time); protocol cardinality is protocol-intrinsic (rule 5).
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross machines** — Consistent, strengthened: rule 4 forbids generic protocols from carrying `Owned`/`Leased` at all.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId** — Consistent: protocols ride links, which bind logicalId; no new addressing identity.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — No resolved item is reopened.

No CONFLICT flag is required. The one wording refinement — G-13's "one link and one queue slot" becomes "one link, separate ordering lanes" — amends a *proposal*, not a recorded decision.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports and generic protocols (G-13)** — Rewrite the "Remaining" paragraph to specify the metadata-plane model: link-as-unit, the `PORT_PROTOCOL` dispatch class, `ProtocolDescriptor`/`ProtocolRegistry`, the seven normative rules, and the explicit rejection of data sub-ports (second data contract = second link).
- **10/12 §Directionality of generic protocols** — Formalize direction as a `ProtocolDescriptor` field and state the reverse-bridge realization for upstream protocols.
- **10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based)** — Note that the handshake also negotiates `Link.protocolCapabilities` (intersection of both ports' declared support); protocols ride an *already-established* link, so link management does not bootstrap on the multiplex substrate.
- **10/14 §Dispatch tiers** — Add `PORT_PROTOCOL` to `HostedPortInvocation.Type` and describe the three-way branch.
- **30/31 §The host protocol** — Document that each protocol lands in its descriptor's band and its own ordering lane; state the rule that protocols bypass data-path parking on a closed intake (management-class).
- **40/41 §Wire layer** — Note `PORT_PROTOCOL` reuses the existing `type` field, the version-byte policy, and that bridge egress/ingress become protocol-aware (closing "bridged links have null endpoints").
- **20/21 §Pull** — Restate the state-request protocol as an upstream metadata request answered by an ordinary downstream state-as-delta on the existing data inlet — no data sub-port.
- **20/22 §MessageContext** — Add that generic-protocol invocations carry null context (management-class), aligning the upstream-traveling-protocol case.
- **90/91 G-13** — Update the "Remaining" clause: data sub-ports resolved by rejection; wire transport resolved via `PORT_PROTOCOL` + protocol-aware bridges; state-request folded into the plane.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Protocol descriptor generation & ownership-free lint** — KSP must generate `ProtocolDescriptor` per generic-protocol interface, collect into `ProtocolRegistry`, and fail compilation if such a contract declares `Owned`/`Leased`. The ProtocolId↔contractId mapping and its stability need pinning.
- **Cross-host protocol frame path (bridge protocol-awareness)** — Concrete design + generative wire test for serializing `PORT_PROTOCOL` frames with a direction tag, routing them to `ProtocolSupport` on receipt, and realizing upstream protocols over the reverse bridge path; WireFrame version handling for the new type.
- **Protocol capability negotiation & versioning across peers** — Cross-peer negotiation when peers advertise different protocol sets/versions, and how a peer learns a remote port's capability set (ties to peering/announcements, 40/41).
- **Idempotence/reordering contract enforcement** — Rule 3's obligation is currently by-convention; a marker/descriptor field plus a generative reordering harness would make it correct-by-construction.
- **State-request protocol full design (G-18 residual)** — The upstream-request/downstream-reply decomposition is sketched; the descriptor, reply routing to a specific requester (`outlet.at`), and idempotence against concurrent live deltas remain.
- **Transitive/multi-hop protocol notices** — M6 is single-hop; multi-hop re-emission, loop prevention, and interaction with band quantization are enabled but not resolved by this model.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high.** The resolution is strongly grounded: the existing `ProtocolSupport` (M6.1) already implements the in-process metadata plane exactly as proposed; `HostedPortInvocation.Type` already has the two-variant shape that `PORT_PROTOCOL` extends; the `WireFrame` already carries a `type` field; and the "management inlet stays open / null context" behavior the plane inherits is already decided and shipped. The design does not invent new kernel machinery — it *classifies* what exists and draws one bright line (link = data unit; protocols = bounded metadata plane).

**Open questions**: (1) whether any near-term protocol genuinely needs a *second data-carrying* channel that cannot be a second link — I argue no (state-request decomposes away), but a future request/response-heavy protocol could pressure this; (2) the exact wire encoding compatibility of adding an enum variant (whether a version bump is truly needed) is an implementation detail deferred to the bridge work; (3) cross-peer capability/version negotiation is the most substantive unresolved piece and is spun out as a follow-on gap rather than resolved here.

### I-2 — Identity model: what a logicalId-bound ref, link, or guard denotes under multiple live instances (G-8)

> Member pairs: N1×N23, N2×N23, N4×N23, N6×N23, N8×N23, N9×N23, N14×N23, N18×N23, N20×N23, N22×N23, N23×N26, N23×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-8 · Confidence: medium · Substrate: yes
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 12/12 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The resolution's normative elaborations are unrecorded: the explicit three-level model (addressing / grouping / continuity), the instanceId lifecycle rule (mint only on replica/candidate spawn; preserve on migration, RESTART, suspend/resume), the structural…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: when one logical cell (`CellRef.id`) has several
live instances (`CellRef.instanceId`) — replicas (42) or candidate versions (53) —
what does each identity-keyed artifact *denote and address*? Concretely: which
instance receives a send or a parked replay; whether the cardinality budget, the
SPSC consumer count, the live-ref spawn guard, supervision policies, dead letters,
park/replay ordering, catch-up serving, delta routing, and WireFrame/registry
resolution key on `logicalId` or on the full `(id, instanceId)` ref; whether the
target-side handshake re-runs on rebind; and what makes a port "the same port"
across instances.

**Member pairs** (all TENSION): N1×N23 (port sameness across instances, no contract
hash on the ref), N2×N23 (cardinality per-instance vs per-logical), N4×N23
(handshake re-run vs silent transfer on rebind; what `Link.from/to` name), N6×N23
(spawn guard keys on which), N8×N23 (which instance a delta reaches), N9×N23 (which
instance answers catch-up, stale-serving, duplicate catch-ups), N14×N23 (which
instance consumes an SPSC `Owned`/`Leased` payload), N18×N23 (supervision/parked/
dead-letter bind logical or instance; does RESTART mint a new instance), N20×N23
(which instance parked traffic replays into; "current location" as a set), N22×N23
(how `(id, instanceId)` refs are framed/announced/resolved), N23×N26 (invariant
linked to a *specific* candidate vs the logicalId default), N23×N27 (what an
instance *is*, how coexisting instances share identity, G-33 transfer).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: G-8 is marked *Resolved (M7.1)* in `91` and in
`10/11 §Identity and persistence`, but only in *mechanism* — "`CellRef(id,
instanceId)`; wire VERSION 2; logicalId-binding realized per use-case." `10/11`
adds the pivotal but under-elaborated line: *"Links and registries address full
refs; 'links bound to logicalId' as an automatic indirection is realized
per use-case."* `42 §Constraint on everything else` imposes that "Nothing in
layers 10–30 may assume a cell has exactly one live instance" and MUST be
preserved — but every artifact enumerated above was written against a single
bare-UUID ref. The per-use-case bindings that `91` defers ARE this challenge.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 vs a logicalId indirection.** The obvious reading of "links bind logicalId"
  is a runtime indirection: a link addresses `logicalId`, and the fast path
  resolves it to the live instance(s). But that resolution would have to pick a
  *policy* — multicast-to-all-instances or resolve-to-one — on the hot path, and
  no single policy fits: replication (42) wants **all** peer replicas to receive a
  delta, while SPSC (20/23) and promotion (53) want **exactly one** active
  instance. A universal automatic indirection is therefore not merely costly (P2);
  it is *semantically wrong* for one of the two use-cases whichever way it is set.
- **P3 vs hidden fan.** A one-link-to-N-instances multicast is precisely the
  hidden-mailbox multicast P3 rejects — topology would stop being the set of
  visible links.
- **The recorded-decision phrasing pulls against the shipped code.** The prior
  decision list says "links bind logicalId (decided, unimplemented)," yet the
  shipped M7.1 text in `10/11` says links address *full* refs and logicalId-binding
  is per-use-case orchestration. These are not the same design; the challenge sits
  exactly on that seam.
- **P8 / P1.** Instances must coexist and be swapped live (P8) while every operation
  stays reducible to link manipulation in a single-threaded simulation (P1) — so
  whatever identity model we pick must express replication, migration, restart, and
  promotion as ordinary spawn/link/unlink, not as new kernel primitives.
- **P6.** Instances and their links must follow expressed interest; "reach every
  instance just in case" is forbidden.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — logicalId-addressed links with registry indirection

Links carry `logicalId`; the registry resolves `logicalId → {live instances}` and
the sender fans (or picks) at send time.

- *Semantics*: one link "means the logical cell"; instance selection is the
  registry's job.
- *Fast-path cost*: a set lookup + fan/pick on every send — violates P2 (steady
  state must be one volatile/map read + enqueue to **one** target).
- *Failure modes*: forces a single global selection policy that cannot serve both
  mesh-replication (all) and SPSC/promotion (one); reintroduces hidden multicast
  (P3); "current location becomes a set" breaks the one-ref-one-location park/replay
  invariant (30/33, 40/41). Contradicts `42`'s own "No location sets: one location
  per full ref."
- *Tradeoff*: matches the literal "links bind logicalId" phrasing but breaks P2, P3,
  and the shipped registry model. Rejected.

##### Candidate B — full-ref addressing everywhere; logicalId is a grouping key only (recommended)

Every addressing artifact keys on the **full** `CellRef(id, instanceId)`. `logicalId`
is never a link endpoint or a resolution target; it is (a) a **grouping index**
(`instancesOf(id)`) queried only on rare paths, and (b) a **continuity** notion
(what "the cell" means to users/topology/invariants), preserved by keeping
`instanceId` stable across restart/migration and by explicit relink across
promotion. Logical-level behavior is an **explicit orchestration over full refs**:
replication = a symmetric mesh of full-ref→full-ref links (already shipped, `42`);
promotion = an active-swap that relinks the incumbent's links onto the candidate's
full ref inside a buffered window (53).

- *Semantics*: one ref → one location → one instance → one link target. Instances
  are first-class, independently linkable, independently supervised.
- *Fast-path cost*: unchanged — one map read (`locate(ref)`) + enqueue. `instancesOf`
  never runs on the data path.
- *Failure modes*: logicalId-level operations (reach "the cell" without knowing an
  instance; enumerate links to relink on swap) become *query-then-act* and need a
  reverse-topology index for swap (a rare-path cost, acceptable per P2).
- *Tradeoff*: this is the M7.1 direction generalized and made normative. Serves
  replication and promotion with the *same* substrate because each chooses its own
  orchestration. Costs: a stale prior-decision phrasing to reconcile (§6) and a few
  new rare-path indices (§8).

##### Candidate C — hybrid: full-ref links + an optional logicalId "rendezvous" port

As B, but add a first-class `logicalId` rendezvous a fresh client can address to be
routed to *some* instance by a per-logical policy cell.

- *Semantics*: B for all existing artifacts; the rendezvous is an ordinary cell (a
  router with its own full ref) that holds `instancesOf` and forwards per policy.
- *Fast-path cost*: identical to B for established links; the rendezvous hop exists
  only for the first contact, then the client links directly to the resolved
  instance.
- *Failure modes*: the rendezvous is itself a cell needing placement/replication —
  but that is ordinary, and it is opt-in (P6).
- *Tradeoff*: C is B plus an *optional* convenience; it does not change any of the
  twelve bindings. I fold its rendezvous into §4 as an optional, non-normative
  pattern rather than a distinct mechanism.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**: full-ref addressing is universal; `logicalId` is a grouping
and continuity key, never a live link target; all logical-level semantics are
explicit link orchestrations over full refs. This makes the twelve member-pair
bindings fall out from three rules plus a lifecycle rule.

**Data shapes**

```
CellRef(id: LogicalId, instanceId: InstanceId)   // id stable across instances/restart/migration
PortRef(cell: CellRef, port: PortName)           // FULL-ref addressed — the only link endpoint
LogicalPortRef(id: LogicalId, port: PortName)    // grouping/query handle — NEVER a link endpoint
```

Registry (extends 40/41, one location per full ref preserved):

```
Location = Local(host) | Remote(sink)            // per FULL ref (unchanged)
locate(ref: CellRef): Location                   // HOT path: one map read
instancesOf(id: LogicalId): Set<CellRef>         // RARE path: membership index over announced refs
```

Wire (VERSION 2 flips): `WireFrame(version=2, cellRef=CellRef(id,instanceId),
portName, …)`; `RegistryAnnounce(ref: CellRef, location)` announces full refs;
`instancesOf` is an index maintained by grouping announced refs on `id`.

**Rule 1 — Addressing level (hot path).** Links, `PortRef`s, WireFrames, registry
resolution, park/replay, supervision, dead letters, cardinality, and the SPSC
consumer count ALL key on the full `CellRef(id, instanceId)`. One ref resolves to
one location and one instance. `Link.from`/`Link.to` name full `PortRef`s.

**Rule 2 — Grouping level (rare path).** `logicalId` is only an index key.
`instancesOf(id)` returns the currently-announced full refs sharing `id`, used
exclusively by rare orchestrators: the replication mesh linker (`42`), promotion
(`53`), and admin/query. It never appears on the data path and never resolves to a
location by itself.

**Rule 3 — Continuity level (semantic).** `logicalId` is what "the cell" denotes to
users, invariants, and topology intent. It is preserved across restart/migration by
keeping `instanceId` **stable**, and across promotion by **explicitly relinking** the
candidate's new `instanceId` onto the incumbent's links inside a buffered window.

**InstanceId lifecycle rule (normative).**
- *Mint a new `instanceId`* ONLY for: (a) a replica spawned on another host (`42`);
  (b) a candidate version spawned under evolution (`53`).
- *Preserve the `instanceId`* for: migration (same instance, new location),
  RESTART supervision (same instance recovering in place — deactivate → activate →
  restore checkpoint), and suspend/resume.
- Instance ids are minted collision-free without coordination (random; caller-chosen
  in deterministic tests) as already decided in `10/11`.

**Derived bindings (each member pair resolved under the rules above):**

- **Spawn guard (N6):** keys on the *full* ref. Re-spawning a ref already HOT on
  this host (same `id` **and** `instanceId`) is rejected (the existing live-ref
  guard, G-16). Spawning a *second* instance of a live logical cell (same `id`,
  new `instanceId`) is **legal** — that is exactly replication and candidates.
- **Cardinality & SPSC (N2, N14):** enforced per-instance on the concrete port, at
  link time (unchanged, `10/12`/`20/23`). Because links bind full refs, each
  instance's `OneToOnePort`/exclusive `FanOutlet` has its own budget of one. An
  `Owned`/`Leased` (single-writer-class) cell replicates as leader+followers, so the
  exclusive link binds exactly the leader instance; a second instance attempting the
  exclusive link is `Rejected` at link time. Mergeable cells use `FanInlet`
  `deltaInlet`s (many producers, declared merge), which is why only idempotent-
  mergeable cells replicate freely (`42`). There is no "logical cardinality budget."
- **Handshake on rebind (N4):** any *new* full-ref link runs the full target-side
  handshake (policies → cardinality → `onLink`). Migration and RESTART preserve
  `instanceId`, so their links are **not** rebinds — the cell object moves whole,
  direct links travel, routed links re-resolve the *same* ref — no spurious
  handshake. Promotion **is** a rebind (new `instanceId`), so handshakes DO re-run
  against the candidate: policies and cardinality are re-checked on the new instance.
  No link ever transfers silently past its veto point.
- **Port sameness across instances (N1):** a port's identity is `(portName,
  contractId)` where `contractId` is the already-hashed FNV-1a contract id
  (`40/41`). "The same port across instances" is defined structurally by name +
  contract equality — used only for migration mapping, catch-up, and promotion
  relink, never as an address. The `CellRef` need not carry a contract hash; the
  compatibility check lives on the *ports*. Migration/promotion require the
  target/candidate to present, for each rebindable link, a port with matching
  `(portName, contractId)`, else the relink is `Rejected` — this is the membrane's
  evolution surface (`11`).
- **Delta routing (N8):** a pushed delta reaches exactly the instances at the far
  end of the emitting outlet's explicit links — never "all instances of `id`." In a
  replica mesh those links exist because the mesh linker created them from
  `instancesOf`; effective-only emission and merge obligations are per instance.
- **Catch-up (N9):** `onLinked` fires per link; the *source instance* serves its own
  state-as-delta-from-empty to that one subscriber. A not-yet-converged instance MAY
  serve its current (possibly stale) state — OR-set tags (`20/24`) make it idempotent,
  and the mesh converges the remainder. A subscriber linked to several replicas
  receives several catch-ups that merge idempotently by tag union. Tag-idempotence
  therefore covers duplicate catch-ups from multiple instances.
- **Supervision / parked / dead letters (N18):** all key on the full ref.
  `supervise(ref, policy)`, per-cell parked traffic, `resume(ref)`, and
  `CellError(cellRef, …)` bind the *instance*, because instances (not abstract
  logical cells) run on a host. **RESTART preserves `instanceId`** (same instance
  recovering in place) so its links survive without re-linking.
- **Park/replay (N20):** keyed by full ref in the `LocationRegistry` (unchanged).
  "The target's current location" stays a single location because one full ref has
  one location (`42`: "one location per full ref"). The accepted-before-closure
  ordering invariant reads unchanged: per full-ref FIFO end-to-end. `logicalId`
  never enters the resolution path.
- **Wire/registry (N22):** `WireFrame.cellRef` and `RegistryAnnounce.ref` carry the
  full ref (VERSION 2). Resolution stays per full ref (one map read).
  Instance-agnosticism is *preserved* precisely because the registry holds many full
  refs sharing an `id` and never collapses them to one.
- **Invariant-to-candidate linking (N23×N26):** dissolves. Because links bind full
  refs, linking an invariant (or a promotion judge) to a *specific* candidate
  instance is the **ordinary** operation — there is no "links-bind-logicalId
  default" at the link layer to contradict.
- **Evolution semantics / G-33 (N23×N27):** an *instance* is one live realization
  (a full ref). Coexisting instances *share identity* by sharing `logicalId` (the
  continuity/query key) while being independently addressable and linkable. G-33
  state transfer (`StateMigrating.importFrom`) runs instance→instance inside the
  promotion swap window, addressed by full refs. The glossary already prefers
  "Instance" and retires "incarnation."

**Two logicalId-level policies over one substrate** (the load-bearing insight):
replication is a *symmetric mesh* (all instances peers, no active one); promotion is
an *active-swap* (one active instance per logical cell in a region at a time). Both
are explicit link orchestrations over full refs; `logicalId` by itself implies no
resolution policy. This is exactly why a universal automatic indirection (Candidate
A) is wrong — it would have to pick one policy for both.

**Optional logical rendezvous (non-normative pattern):** a fresh client that knows
only `logicalId` resolves via `instancesOf(id)` and a selection policy (nearest
replica for reads, the leader for writes, the active candidate during promotion),
then links directly to the resolved full ref. "Logical address" is therefore always
*query-then-link*, never a live link target — the fast path stays pure.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | untouched — `instanceId` is a field; replication/migration/restart/promotion stay spawn+link+unlink; meaningful single-threaded. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | satisfied — hot path keys on full ref, one map read + enqueue to one target; `instancesOf` and reverse-link indices are rare-path only. |
| P3 Explicit topology | satisfied — mesh and swap are visible full-ref links; no hidden multicast; `LogicalPortRef` is a query handle, not an endpoint. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | untouched — no global clock/lock/barrier added; `logicalId` grouping is a local index. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | satisfied — cardinality/SPSC per instance-port at link time; port-compatibility a structural `(name, contractId)` check on relink. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | satisfied — each instance and each link exists by explicit interest; no reach-all-instances "just in case." |
| P7 Open, local-first | untouched. |
| P8 Live evolution | satisfied — instances coexist; swap and mesh are graph ops; nothing assumes a static instance set. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | satisfied — `CellRef(id, instanceId)` serializable; VERSION 2 already reserved; no lambdas/handles introduced. |
| P10 Niche first | satisfied — decentralized replica mesh + live evolution are exactly the niche this serves. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-8 direction ("CellRef(logicalId, incarnation) decided; links bind logicalId,
  decided-unimplemented"):** ⚠ **CONFLICT (terminology/phrasing), reconciled.** The
  shipped M7.1 text in `10/11 §Identity` already amended "links bind logicalId" to
  "links and registries address full refs; logicalId-binding realized per use-case."
  This resolution adopts and generalizes the *shipped* text; the stale summary phrase
  should be read as *"links bind full refs; logicalId-binding is an explicit
  per-use-case orchestration (mesh, swap)."* No new contradiction is introduced — the
  code and `10/11`/`42` already work this way.
- **G-20 per-source waves:** consistent, reinforced — `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)`
  is minted per emitting outlet; each *instance*'s outlet is a distinct source, so
  two replicas are two sources → convergence not simultaneity.
- **SID-UP global locks rejected:** consistent — no propagation lock added.
- **Host is the unit of mobility:** consistent — migration preserves `instanceId`;
  the host moves whole.
- **Suspension = one Buffering primitive:** consistent — park/replay keyed by full ref.
- **Location = Local|Remote, one park/replay:** consistent — per full ref.
- **Snapshot IS a delta:** consistent — catch-up is per-instance state-as-delta.
- **Merge tags are cell-local, not waves:** consistent — tags minted per instance.
- **Data push-only / management may return:** untouched.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip, no second protocol:** strongly
  consistent — the mesh is full-ref→full-ref dataflow links.
- **Partitioning not a second distribution mechanism:** untouched — a partition is a
  cell with its own full ref; ordinary placement.
- **Wire ids-only, version byte reserved:** consistent — VERSION 2 carries the full
  ref, still ids-only.
- **Drain ordering invariant, per-link FIFO:** consistent — per full-ref FIFO.
- **Cardinality at link time not send time:** consistent — per instance-port.
- **Owned→move-by-serialize; Leased not crossing machines:** untouched.
- **Gaps Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved:** consistent — this elaborates the
  "realized per use-case" bindings G-8 deferred; it does not reopen G-8.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **10/11 §Identity and persistence:** expand to state the three-level model
  (addressing / grouping / continuity), the full-ref addressing rule, the instanceId
  lifecycle rule, and that port-sameness is structural `(portName, contractId)`.
- **10/13 §Links / §Cross-boundary:** state that links bind full `PortRef`s; the
  handshake re-runs on any new full-ref link; migration/RESTART preserve `instanceId`
  (not a rebind); promotion relink IS a rebind that re-handshakes and enforces the
  port-compatibility check.
- **10/12 §Cardinality, 10/15 §Port discovery / Normative rules:** clarify the
  PortRegistry is per instance; cardinality/SPSC budgets are per instance-port; the
  spawn guard keys on the full ref (same-`id`/new-`instanceId` spawn is legal).
- **20/21 §Pull:** catch-up is per-instance/per-link; multi-replica catch-ups are
  idempotent by tag union; a not-yet-converged instance may serve current state.
- **20/23 §SPSC rule:** one consumer = one full ref; exclusive cells are
  single-writer, the leader instance carries the exclusive link.
- **30/31 §Normative rules 5:** supervision/parked/dead-letter key on the full ref;
  RESTART preserves `instanceId`.
- **30/33 §Stale references / drain:** park/replay keyed by full ref (confirm); "one
  location per ref" holds; migration preserves `instanceId`.
- **40/41 §Addressing:** registry adds an `instancesOf(logicalId)` index over
  announced full refs; `locate` stays per full ref; VERSION 2 frames the full ref.
- **40/42:** confirm mesh links are full-ref→full-ref; each instance is a distinct
  wave source; leader/follower for single-writer remains open.
- **50/52, 50/53:** invariant/promotion linking to a specific candidate full ref is
  ordinary; promotion relink re-handshakes; G-33 transfer is instance→instance.
- **00/03 glossary:** already updated (Logical cell / Instance); optionally add
  `LogicalPortRef` and `instancesOf`.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Logical rendezvous / instance-selection policy:** how a client holding only
  `logicalId` picks an instance from `instancesOf` (nearest replica for reads, leader
  for writes, active candidate during promotion) is undesigned.
- **Reverse-topology index for promotion swap:** an active-swap must relink *all*
  inbound/outbound links of the incumbent onto the candidate; enumerating "all links
  pointing at a full ref" across hosts and the wire has no cross-host reverse index
  today. Needed to make the swap O(topology) and complete.
- **Port-compatibility policy on relink:** what happens when a candidate's/target's
  `(portName, contractId)` does not match a rebindable link — reject vs adapt — is
  unspecified; also confirms the compatibility check lives on ports, not on the
  `CellRef` (N1's "no contract hash on the ref" is answered by putting the check on
  ports).
- **InstanceId uniqueness discipline:** random collision-free minting needs a stated
  birthday-bound argument, plus the rule that two hosts independently minting a
  colliding random `instanceId` for the same `logicalId` is a (vanishingly rare)
  error, and how deterministic tests avoid it.
- **Leader election for single-writer logical cells:** which instance is "the leader"
  carrying the SPSC/`Owned` exclusive link is a logicalId-level policy left open by
  `42`; interacts directly with N14.
- **RESTART within a replicated logical cell:** RESTART restores a spawn-time
  checkpoint, which may lag the mesh; whether a restarted replica should instead
  re-catch-up from its peers (rather than restore a stale checkpoint) is undesigned.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The core mechanism is the already-shipped M7.1 direction
("links and registries address full refs; logicalId-binding per use-case")
generalized into three explicit rules plus an instanceId lifecycle rule, and it makes
all twelve member-pair bindings fall out consistently without new kernel primitives
(P1). The main genuinely-new normative content — the instanceId lifecycle rule
(mint on replica/candidate, preserve on migrate/restart/suspend) and the structural
`(portName, contractId)` port-sameness key — is low-risk. Confidence is not higher
because two orchestration pieces are left as follow-on gaps: the reverse-topology
index that makes a promotion swap actually relink every incumbent link, and
leader election for single-writer logical cells. **Open questions:** (1) does the
promotion swap relink downstream links by orchestrator-driven topology surgery
(my recommendation) or by a scoped logicalId-indirection limited to the swap window —
the latter must be proven not to leak into the hot path; (2) the exact
selection-policy surface for the optional logical rendezvous; (3) whether RESTART of
a replicated instance should prefer mesh re-catch-up over checkpoint restore.

### I-3 — Replication skeleton: membership, location-set resolution, gossip topology, eviction (G-7)

> Member pairs: N1×N24, N4×N24, N5×N24, N6×N24, N15×N24, N20×N24, N21×N24, N22×N24, N24×N26
> Existing gaps touched: G-7 · Confidence: high · Substrate: yes
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 9/9 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The single-writer branch and the lifecycle rules: leader/follower tree + command-forward via delegate (40/42 still lists 'leader/follower for single-writer cells' open), the eviction gate (membership-gated + drain-gated; a partitioned replica suspends, neve…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question.** Replication's *principles* are already fixed and
its *mergeable-class core is shipped*: a replica is a full `CellRef` (same `id`,
distinct `instanceId`) published like any cell; `LocationRegistry.replicasOf(logicalId)`
+ the `onPublish` hook is the membership view; the `cell.replication.Replication`
linker builds a symmetric gossip mesh by linking each local replica's delta outlet to
every discovered peer's `deltaInlet`; convergence rides tag-union / pointwise-max
merges; anti-entropy = park/replay + idempotent catch-up (`42 §Design as implemented`;
`91 §G-7 "Resolved for the mergeable class"`). What remains open, and what this
challenge must resolve under **one** mechanism, is the *skeleton around that core*:

- **Membership & resolution under churn** — how peer join/leave, partition/heal, and
  many peers publishing one `logicalId` compose into a coherent replica set, and
  whether the hot-path registry resolves "one location" or a "location set"
  (`42 §Open`/N1×N24, N22×N24; the original G-7 proposal literally said extend "one
  location" → "location set").
- **Which replica an inbound link, invocation, or lookup reaches, and whose port
  policies evaluate it** (N1×N24, N4×N24, N5×N24).
- **Gossip topology for non-mergeable cells** — leader/follower for single-writer
  cells is explicitly "remain[s]" open (`42 §Open`; `91 §G-7`), as are keyed
  structures and plain counters (N15×N24).
- **The mobility interaction** — whether a sender parked on a closed intake may
  re-resolve to a *different* replica (safe for mergeable, unsafe for a single-writer
  leader) — `42` reuses mobility, but mobility assumes one current location per ref
  (N20×N24; `30/33 §Stale references`).
- **Eviction without losing un-gossiped deltas** — when a replica may be despawned
  (`interest decay ⇒ suspension ⇒ eviction`) without dropping deltas no peer has yet
  absorbed (N6×N24; `42 §Open "eviction stays manual"`).
- **Interest scoping the extent** (N21×N24) and **invariant observation of replica
  convergence** (N24×N26).

**Why the spec leaves it open.** `42` resolves G-7 *for the mergeable class only* and
lists the rest under "Still open." `91 §G-7`: "Keyed structures + leader-follower
remain." Every residual above sits on machinery that exists (`replicasOf`, the
reactive linker, drain, park/replay, catch-up) but has no *rule* composing it for the
non-mergeable, churning, evictable, mobile cases. I-2 (identity) already fixed the
addressing substrate this must build on: **full-ref addressing everywhere; `logicalId`
is a grouping/continuity key, never a live link target; one location per full ref**
(`res/I-2.md §4`). I-3 is the replication *skeleton* over that substrate — it must not
re-open addressing.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P4 (no global barrier) vs "membership."** The instinct for replica membership is a
  view/quorum/coordinator protocol. Any of those is a global barrier and a *second*
  synchronization protocol — both forbidden (P4; recorded "no second sync protocol").
  Membership must be an eventually-consistent *local index*, never a consensus.
- **P2 vs "location set."** The literal G-7 proposal — resolve a ref to a *set* of
  locations — puts a set lookup + fan/pick on the hot path and reintroduces
  one-link-to-N hidden multicast (P3). I-2 already rejected this: `locate(ref)` stays
  one-location-per-full-ref; the set lives in the *rare-path* `replicasOf(id)`.
- **Mergeable vs single-writer pull opposite topologies.** Mergeable cells want a
  *symmetric* mesh (every replica a peer, writes anywhere converge). Single-writer /
  `Owned`-carrying cells (`20/23`) want *exactly one* writer — an *asymmetric*
  leader→follower tree. One "replication" abstraction must express both without a
  second mechanism, and the SPSC exclusive bit (`10/12 rule 2`, `20/23`) must still
  refuse a second writer at link time (P5).
- **Mobility's one-location invariant vs "re-resolve to another replica."** `30/33`'s
  park/replay re-resolves *the same ref's* new location. Letting a parked sender jump
  to a *sibling replica* would silently cross an instance boundary — safe for a
  mergeable cell (equivalent), catastrophic for a single-writer leader (two writers).
  The tension is exactly whether replica-switch is automatic (park/replay) or explicit
  (relink).
- **Eviction vs the effective-only, ack-free gossip.** Gossip is push-only and
  effective-only (`21`); there is no delivery ack. Evicting a replica that still holds
  a delta no peer absorbed loses it. But adding acks/versions would be a second sync
  protocol. Eviction safety must fall out of *existing* drain + membership + park/replay.
- **P6 vs "just in case."** A replica, a mesh link, and a catch-up must each exist
  because interest justifies it — no reach-all-replicas, no replicate-everywhere.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Coordinator / membership view-change protocol

A per-`logicalId` coordinator (or quorum) maintains the authoritative replica set and
issues view changes; replicas join/leave through it; eviction is a view-change commit.

- *Semantics*: a single source of truth for "who is in the replica set."
- *Fast-path cost*: none on data, but every join/leave/evict is a coordination round.
- *Failure modes*: a global barrier per logical cell (violates P4); a second
  synchronization protocol distinct from dataflow gossip (violates the recorded
  decision); the coordinator is a placement/availability singleton the niche
  (decentralized, partition-tolerant) specifically rejects (P10). Partition splits the
  view.
- *Tradeoff*: strong, legible membership; wrong for this system. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — Membership-reactive gossip over announcements (recommended)

Generalize the shipped M7 linker into one primitive: the replica set is a *local,
eventually-consistent membership index* folded from ordinary `RegistryAnnounce`
traffic; a per-host `Replication` linker reacts to membership deltas by reconciling
its local replica's gossip links according to the cell's **mutability class** (mesh
for mergeable, leader-tree + command-forward for single-writer); eviction, churn, and
the mobility interaction all ride existing drain / park-replay / catch-up. No
consensus, no second protocol, no location set on the hot path.

- *Semantics*: membership = a fold; topology = a reactive local rule; eviction = a
  gated drain+despawn; resolution stays one-location-per-full-ref (`replicasOf` is the
  rare-path set).
- *Fast-path cost*: unchanged — data still keys on the full ref (`locate`), one map
  read + enqueue; `replicasOf` and the linker run only on membership deltas (rare).
- *Failure modes*: membership is only eventually consistent (a peer may briefly miss a
  new replica or hold a stale one) — acceptable because gossip is idempotent and
  effective-only, so a late-learned peer simply catches up. Partitioned replicas
  cannot be evicted (they hold unique state); they suspend instead.
- *Tradeoff*: this is the smallest extension of what ships; it makes every residual
  fall out from one reactive linker + the mutability class + existing machinery.

##### Candidate C — Anti-entropy-first (pull-based version/Merkle reconciliation)

Make periodic pull-based reconciliation (version vectors or Merkle trees over state)
the replication substrate; push gossip becomes an optimization.

- *Semantics*: replicas periodically compare digests and pull missing state.
- *Fast-path cost*: none on data; background reconciliation cost.
- *Failure modes*: it *is* a second synchronization protocol distinct from dataflow
  links — the exact thing the recorded decision forbids; it also needs per-replica
  version metadata the tag algebra already subsumes.
- *Tradeoff*: attractive for *durability/compaction* (G-25) — bounding unbounded OR-set
  tag growth — but wrong as the replication skeleton. **Folded into §8 as a future
  compaction concern, not adopted as the mechanism.**

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B — the membership-reactive gossip skeleton**. It is one primitive
(a mutability-class-driven reactive linker over an eventually-consistent membership
index) plus six rules that resolve the residuals on existing machinery.

##### 4.1 Data shapes (extend, do not replace)

```
// Membership — RARE path only (extends 40/41; shipped shape)
locate(ref: CellRef): Location = Local(host) | Remote(sink)   // HOT: one location per FULL ref (unchanged)
replicasOf(id: LogicalId): Set<CellRef>                       // RARE: fold of announcements sharing id
onPublish(hook)                                               // fires on announce/unannounce (shipped M7)
RegistryAnnounce(ref: CellRef, location)                     // ordinary wire traffic (M5.4) — the membership feed

// Replication marker (shipped) — the TYPED membership gate
interface Replicable { val deltaInlet: FanInlet<Δ>; val deltaOutlet: FanOutlet<Propagate<Δ>> }
//   a cell is Replicable IFF its delta merge is commutative + associative + idempotent
//   (SetCell / UnionSetCell / PnCounterCell today). Everything else is single-writer or local-only.

// The reactive linker (shipped Replication cell, generalized)
class Replication(local: CellRef, cls: MutabilityClass /* mergeable | single-writer(role) */)
```

##### 4.2 The one primitive — a membership-reactive linker

`Replication` subscribes to `replicasOf(id)` changes (the `onPublish` hook, delivered
as ordinary announcement traffic) and treats them as a **delta stream of membership**.
On each membership delta Δ it reconciles *its local replica's* links — nothing else:

- **Mergeable class** (`Replicable`): symmetric full mesh.
  - Δ.added `p`: `local.deltaOutlet.linkTo(p.deltaInlet)` (and, symmetrically, `p` does
    the same on learning `local` — the mesh emerges with no coordinator, as shipped).
  - Δ.removed `p`: `unlink` the mesh link (or let the registry park it — see 4.5).
  - Echo termination is unchanged: a replica re-emits only *new* tag information
    (effective-only, `21`); this is why only idempotent-mergeable cells mesh.
- **Single-writer class**: asymmetric leader→follower tree + command-forward.
  - The **leader** is the single instance carrying the write inlet (the
    `OneToOnePort` / exclusive `FanOutlet` — the SPSC/`Owned` exclusive bit refuses a
    second writer at link time, `10/12 rule 2`, `20/23`). On Δ.added follower `f`:
    `leader.deltaOutlet.linkTo(f.deltaInlet)` — followers hold warm read state.
  - A **follower** serves its own write inlet by `delegate`→ the leader's write inlet
    (an ordinary link; `14 §delegate`) — a write that lands on a follower is
    *command-forwarded* to the leader, not applied locally. If no leader link exists
    yet, the write parks (park/replay) or is `Rejected` per the port's policy.

**Membership is never a consensus.** `replicasOf(id)` is a monotone, self-correcting
local index folded from announcements; there is no view number, quorum, or barrier
(P4). Two peers may transiently disagree on the set; gossip idempotence makes that safe
(a late-learned peer just catches up; a stale peer's extra link delivers a duplicate
that merges to a no-op).

##### 4.3 Resolution stays one-location-per-full-ref (kills "location set")

The hot path is **unchanged**: `locate(ref)` resolves the *full ref* to *one*
location. The "location set" the original G-7 proposal imagined is *exactly*
`replicasOf(id)` — a rare-path membership index, never consulted on the data path and
never fanned into one link (P2, P3). This confirms `42`'s own "No location sets: one
location per full ref" and I-2's addressing model.

##### 4.4 Which replica a link/lookup/invocation reaches, and whose policies

Per I-2, a link or lookup targets a **specific full ref**, so:

- **Inbound link / lookup**: a client that already holds a replica's full ref links to
  *that instance*; **that instance's port policies evaluate the link** (each replica
  owns a full, independent port set — `42 §Constraint`). A client holding only
  `logicalId` does **query-then-link**: `replicasOf(id)` → a *selection policy* → link
  to the chosen full ref. Selection policy (the replication-specific rendezvous, I-2's
  follow-on gap made concrete for reads/writes):
  - **read**: nearest reachable replica (locality — P2/P6; process data where needed).
  - **write to a mergeable cell**: any replica (all converge).
  - **write to a single-writer cell**: the **leader** (or a follower that
    command-forwards, 4.2).
- **A captured command invocation** (e.g. `SetOps.add`) is delivered to the *one*
  replica the client linked to; that replica mints tags cell-locally and gossips the
  resulting *delta* to peers over the mesh. So "one replica" receives the *command*;
  "all" receive the *delta* — resolving N5's "one/leader/all" ambiguity cleanly: there
  is no logical inlet that fans a command.
- **Fusion (N5)**: a reader/writer co-hosted with a replica links to that **local**
  instance (P2 locality; "interest drives replication → process data where it is
  needed"). This is always legitimate for mergeable cells (replicas are equivalent).
  For single-writer, a co-hosted *follower* may serve **reads** locally by fusion, but
  **writes** still forward to the leader (4.2) — fusion never manufactures a second
  writer.

##### 4.5 The mobility interaction — park/replay never crosses an instance boundary

Park/replay is keyed by the **full ref** (`30/33`, I-2). Therefore a sender parked on
replica-A's closed intake re-resolves **A's own new location** (A migrated) — it does
**not** silently switch to a sibling replica. This structurally answers N20: automatic
re-resolution stays within one instance, so the "unsafe for a single-writer leader"
case *cannot arise from park/replay*.

Switching to a *different* replica is an **explicit relink** (a rare-path topology op),
never automatic:

- **mergeable target**: relink is always safe (any replica equivalent; tags make the
  re-catch-up idempotent).
- **single-writer target**: the relink target must be the **leader**; relinking to a
  follower yields command-forward or `Rejected` (4.2). Leader identity is thus the only
  thing that makes replica-switching unsafe, and it is guarded by the exclusive link
  bit, not by park/replay.

##### 4.6 Eviction without losing un-gossiped deltas

Eviction is a **gated drain+despawn** on existing machinery — no ack protocol:

```
evict(local):
  reachablePeers = { p ∈ replicasOf(id) − {local} : locate(p) is reachable }
  if reachablePeers == ∅:                      // membership gate
      SUSPEND (park), do NOT evict             // this replica holds unique state; await heal
  else:
      1. (trigger) attention band NONE sustained a policy window (34) — or manual
      2. drain this cell (33): close intake; flush deltaOutlet queue to peers.
         In-flight deltas to a momentarily-closed peer park-and-replay (never lost).
      3. (optional, for partition-hardening) final catch-up: push
         state-as-delta-from-empty (the shipped late-join path, 21) to one reachable
         peer; park/replay guarantees it lands and merges idempotently.
      4. despawn(local) ⇒ unpublish ⇒ replicasOf(id) shrinks ⇒ peers' linkers
         reconcile (drop the mesh link to local).
```

The un-gossiped-delta problem dissolves into two existing guarantees: **(a)** a
*partitioned* replica (no reachable peer) is never evicted — it suspends and waits for
heal (the anti-entropy path `42` already ships); **(b)** a *connected* replica drains
its outbound delta queue before deactivation (`30/33` step 2, whose phase-2 task sits
below data priority), so pending deltas flush or park to a surviving peer. Eviction is
therefore *membership-gated* + *drain-gated*, both already built.

##### 4.7 Interest scopes the extent (skeleton; policy deferred)

The trigger wiring is specified; the *placement policy* stays with the deferred
economic layer (`34 decision 4`; `42 §Open`). A subscriber that expresses interest
across the wire **volunteers partial responsibility** (`42 §Principles`) and MAY spawn
a local replica that joins the mesh (4.2); sustained attention band NONE (`34`) ⇒
suspend (`33`) ⇒ eviction (4.6). *When* to spawn a local replica vs. subscribe
remotely, and replica *placement*, remain the economic-layer decision (G-6 residual) —
consistent with `42`'s "eviction stays manual until memory pressure justifies a policy."

##### 4.8 Keyed structures, counters, and the mergeable gate (N15)

The **`Replicable` marker is the typed membership gate**: only cells whose delta merge
is commutative + associative + idempotent may join the symmetric mesh. Consequences,
with no new mechanism:

- **Set family, `UnionSetCell`, `PnCounterCell`**: mesh-replicate (shipped).
- **Plain `CounterCell`**: merge is addition (not idempotent) → *not* `Replicable` →
  single-instance, or replicated single-writer (leader/follower, 4.2). (Matches `24`.)
- **`MapCell`/`ListCell`**: carry documented multi-writer convergence limits (`24`).
  Under replication they either (i) replicate single-writer (leader/follower), or
  (ii) adopt observed-remove tag semantics like the set family *before* claiming
  `Replicable`. The gate makes this a compile-time/marker decision, not a runtime
  surprise.
- **Keyed / partitioned structures (G-24)**: a `PartitionedCell`'s partitions are
  ordinary cells with their own full refs; **each partition replicates independently
  per its own mutability class**. Replication composes with partitioning because a
  partition's replica set is just another `replicasOf(partitionRef)` — partitioning
  does not become a second distribution mechanism.

##### 4.9 Invariants observe convergence per replica (N24×N26)

An `InvariantCell` observes replica convergence by the *ordinary* mechanism:
"attaching an invariant is linking" (`52`). It links to **each replica's delta outlet**
(enumerated via `replicasOf(id)`) as a late-joining subscriber; each link fires
catch-up (state-as-delta, idempotent by tags — the **anti-entropy catch-up doubles as
the invariant's late-join feed**, exactly as `52` states) followed by live deltas. The
invariant folds **per-replica** streams and asserts the folds agree at quiescence. No
merged global view and no new machinery are needed: the shipped harness already asserts
cross-view convergence between independently-built graphs (`52 §Generative harness`);
replicas of one `logicalId` are the special case where the views *share* a `logicalId`.

##### 4.10 The load-bearing summary

Membership, gossip topology, and eviction are **one reactive-linker primitive over an
eventually-consistent membership index**, parameterized by the cell's mutability class,
riding entirely on shipped machinery: `replicasOf` (membership), the `Replication`
linker (topology), `locate`/park-replay (resolution + mobility, one location per full
ref), drain (eviction flush), and catch-up (anti-entropy + invariant feed). There is no
membership consensus, no location set on the hot path, and no second synchronization
protocol.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | untouched — membership is a fold; the linker does spawn/link/unlink; leader/follower and eviction reduce to link manipulation + drain; every statement meaningful single-threaded (the M7 mesh already runs under `SimulationController`). |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | satisfied — data keys on the full ref (`locate`, one map read + enqueue); `replicasOf`, the reactive linker, and eviction are rare-path only; no location set on the hot path. |
| P3 Explicit topology | satisfied — the mesh and the leader-tree are visible full-ref links; command-forward is an explicit `delegate` link; `replicasOf` is a query index, never a hidden multicast endpoint. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | satisfied — membership is an eventually-consistent local index; no view/quorum/coordinator/barrier; convergence is per-source waves + tag merge (G-20, G-23). |
| P5 Correctness by construction | satisfied — `Replicable` is a typed gate (idempotent-merge only); the single-writer leader is the exclusive-bit holder enforced at link time (`20/23`); the mutability class selects topology. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | satisfied — a replica, a mesh link, and a catch-up each exist by expressed interest; eviction is interest-decay-gated; nothing replicates "just in case." |
| P7 Open, local-first | untouched — boundary controls (allowlists/encryption, `40/43`) apply to gossip links as ordinary links; no ambient trust added. |
| P8 Live evolution | satisfied — replicas join/leave live; the linker reacts to membership deltas; nothing assumes a static replica set. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | satisfied — announcements, deltas, and catch-up are the shipped serializable wire forms; no new on-wire type, no lambdas/handles. |
| P10 Niche first | satisfied — decentralized, partition-tolerant, interest-driven replication with no coordinator is exactly the niche; the coordinator candidate (A) was rejected on this ground. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — consistent: each replica's delta outlet is a distinct
  `Timestamp(sourceId,…)` source; two replicas are two sources → convergence not
  simultaneity; membership adds no wave coordinator.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — consistent: membership is a local fold, not a
  propagation lock; Candidate A (coordinator) explicitly rejected.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — consistent: a replica migrates as its host;
  park/replay re-resolves the same full ref (4.5), never a sibling replica.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive** — consistent: replica suspension (interest
  decay) and partition-parking both use the existing park/replay; eviction is
  drain+despawn, no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local\|Remote; one park/replay** — consistent and reinforced: resolution
  stays one location per full ref; the set lives in `replicasOf` (§4.3).
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — consistent: catch-up / final anti-entropy push is
  state-as-delta-from-empty; no snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are cell-local, not waves** — consistent: tags minted per replica drive
  idempotent mesh merge and idempotent catch-up.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — consistent:
  gossip and catch-up are push-only data; announcements/`spawn`/`despawn` are management.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** —
  strongly consistent: membership, topology, eviction, anti-entropy all ride dataflow
  links + park/replay; Candidate C (pull reconciliation) rejected precisely here.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — consistent: partitions
  are ordinary cells; each replicates independently via its own `replicasOf` (§4.8).
- **Wire ids-only, version byte reserved** — consistent: no new wire type;
  announcements/deltas are the shipped VERSION-2 forms.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO** — consistent: eviction flush uses the
  drain protocol; gossip links are per-link FIFO end-to-end.
- **Cardinality at link time; SPSC refuses fan-out; Owned→move-by-serialize, Leased
  not crossing machines** — consistent: the single-writer leader is the exclusive-bit
  holder; a second writer is `Rejected` at link time; `Owned` cells replicate as
  leader+followers (followers hold serialized read state, no exclusive link).
- **CellRef(id, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2)** — consistent and *depended
  upon*: replicas are full refs; `logicalId` is the grouping key `replicasOf` folds on;
  this resolution builds on I-2 §4 and does not re-open it.
- **Gaps Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — consistent: this *elaborates* G-7's
  "still open" residuals (leader/follower, eviction, churn, keyed structures, mobility
  interaction, invariant observation); it does not reopen the resolved mergeable core.

No CONFLICT flag required. The original G-7 phrasing "extend one location → a location
set" is a *superseded proposal* (already superseded by `42`/M5.4/I-2), not a recorded
decision; §4.3 confirms the supersession.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **40/42 §Design as implemented / §Still open** — promote the residuals to design:
  the mutability-class-driven topology rule (mergeable mesh vs single-writer
  leader-tree + command-forward), the membership-as-local-fold statement (no
  consensus), the eviction gate (membership-gated + drain-gated; partitioned ⇒ suspend
  not evict), and the `Replicable` typed-gate rule. Confirm "no location set; the set is
  `replicasOf`."
- **40/41 §Addressing** — restate that `locate` is one location per full ref and
  `replicasOf(logicalId)` is the rare-path membership index folded from announcements;
  `onPublish` is the linker's feed.
- **30/33 §Stale references** — add the normative rule: park/replay never crosses an
  instance boundary; replica-switch is an explicit relink (mergeable-safe;
  single-writer must target the leader).
- **20/24 §Established pattern / §Partitioned state** — state the `Replicable` gate
  (idempotent-merge cells only mesh); Map/List either go single-writer or adopt tags
  before claiming `Replicable`; partitions replicate independently per partition ref.
- **10/12 §Cardinality / 20/23** — note the single-writer leader is the exclusive-link
  holder; a second writer is `Rejected` at link time; followers command-forward.
- **10/15 §Lifecycle / 30/34** — wire the interest-decay ⇒ suspend ⇒ evict trigger; the
  eviction gate reads attention band NONE + reachable-peer membership.
- **50/52 §Invariant testing** — add that convergence invariants link per-replica via
  `replicasOf` and fold each stream; catch-up is the invariant's late-join feed.
- **90/91 §G-7** — update "Keyed structures + leader-follower remain" to reference this
  skeleton; leave leader *election* and interest-driven *placement* as the residual
  gaps (§8).

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Leader election for single-writer logical cells** — the skeleton fixes the leader's
  *role* (exclusive-link holder, followers command-forward) but not *how* the leader is
  chosen or fails over without a coordinator (P4). Interacts with I-2's same-named gap
  and with `20/23`.
- **Interest-driven replica placement (economic layer)** — *when* to spawn a local
  replica vs. subscribe remotely, and where replicas live, remain deferred to the
  economic layer (G-6 residual); the skeleton only wires the suspend/evict trigger.
- **Membership churn convergence bound** — the eventually-consistent membership index
  needs a stated liveness argument: after a peer joins/leaves, all linkers reconcile
  within bounded gossip hops; and duplicate/stale mesh links are proven safe by tag
  idempotence (assert with a generative membership-churn harness).
- **Eviction of the last connected replica / quorum-free durability** — §4.6 forbids
  evicting a partitioned replica, but a policy is needed for graceful *shutdown* of the
  final replica (hand state to durable storage, G-25) vs. accidental deletion.
- **OR-set tag growth under long-lived replication (compaction)** — mesh replication
  grows tombstone/tag sets monotonically (`42 §Tombstones`); Candidate C's pull-based
  digest reconciliation is the likely *compaction* substrate (with G-25 durability),
  explicitly out of scope here.
- **Map/List observed-remove forms** — promoting `MapDelta`/`ListDelta` into the
  `Replicable` class needs tag-based multi-writer semantics (or a stated single-writer
  restriction); currently they carry documented limits.
- **Cross-replica invariant at churn** — how a convergence invariant handles replicas
  appearing/disappearing mid-run (a replica evicted before quiescence) needs a rule so
  the invariant does not false-positive on a legitimately departed stream.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high** for the mergeable-class skeleton and the resolution substrate, and
**medium** for the single-writer path. The core is the already-shipped M7 mesh
generalized into one reactive-linker primitive plus rules that fall out of existing
machinery (drain, park/replay, catch-up, the exclusive-link bit), and it inherits I-2's
settled addressing model — so membership, resolution, churn, eviction, the mobility
interaction, and invariant observation all resolve without new kernel primitives (P1)
or a second sync protocol. Confidence is not higher because the single-writer branch
leans on two genuinely-deferred pieces: **leader election** and **interest-driven
placement**, both spun out as follow-on gaps rather than resolved here.

**Open questions:** (1) command-forward vs. reject for a write that lands on a follower
— I recommend forward (an ordinary `delegate` link) but a policy hook may want reject;
(2) whether the optional final anti-entropy push (§4.6 step 3) should be mandatory for
single-writer leaders (whose state is not otherwise mesh-redundant) — likely yes;
(3) the exact liveness bound for membership-index convergence under churn, deferred to a
generative harness.

### I-4 — Attention protocol algebra: aggregation over fan-out, retraction, context classification (G-6)

> Member pairs: N1×N21, N2×N21, N3×N21, N4×N21, N11×N21, N15×N21
> Existing gaps touched: G-6, G-13 · Confidence: high · Substrate: yes
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 6/6 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The AttentionUpdate{level, version} shape with the version LWW discriminator (required once updates cross the wire's reorder window — spec 34 header still says 'attention does not cross the wire' and notices are single-hop), the wire crossing itself (rule 7…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

Attention is fixed as a **compositional, upstream-flowing generic protocol** (30/34 §What is fixed by the ADRs: "propagates **upstream** (consumer → producer) along data links without cell-specific logic"; "a cell's attention level derives from its downstream subscribers' attention"). The M6 work (30/34 §Decisions, marked "Implemented (M6): decisions below are code"; 90/91 G-6 "Resolved (M6)") already decided the **aggregation** axis: a **programmable per-cell fold** — `max` (default), `sum` (load), `decay` (base) — of "the cell's own level and its downstream links' levels," damped by **band quantization** (`NONE < LOW < NORMAL < HIGH`), re-emitted upstream **only on band change**.

But three sub-axes the challenge names were resolved only *in gesture*, not *in mechanism*:

**The single mechanism question**: attention is described as "**itself incremental dataflow** (attention updates are deltas)" (30/34 §Design sketch). Taken literally as a *delta stream*, it inherits the exact problem 20/24 exists to solve — **sum-style aggregation is not idempotent under the duplicate deliveries across diamond fan-ins** that the tag algebra absorbs (20/24 §Established pattern rule 3: "Merge on the delta type is commutative, associative, idempotent"). Concretely, three things are unspecified under one head — *what data-shape does an attention contribution have, and what is its merge law*:
1. **Aggregation-as-merge / idempotency** (N15×N21, N2×N21): is attention a CRDT-style delta stream needing tags, or something else? Sum over deltas double-counts under re-delivery.
2. **Retraction & link-op interleaving** (N4×N21): when a contributing downstream link unlinks, how does its contribution retract, and how does an in-flight attention update interleave with the unlink? (30/34 says only "unlink already shrinks the link set.")
3. **MessageContext classification** (N11×N21, N1×N21, N3×N21): does an upstream attention update mint a wave (20/22 §MessageContext rule 1), flow transparently (rule 2), or ride a **null-context management invocation**? And what does `sourcePort` mean for a message travelling *against* link direction?

**Member pairs** all pull on this one axis: N1×N21 (attention as generic protocol over directional ports), N2×N21 (fan-out aggregation "to be decided"), N3×N21 (per-sub-port vs per-link attention on the multiplex carrier), N4×N21 (retraction on unlink, interleaving with link ops), N11×N21 (waves vs transparent vs null context; sourcePort against direction), N15×N21 (sum not idempotent under diamond duplicate deliveries).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: 30/34 §Design sketch calls attention "itself incremental dataflow" and 30/34 §Decisions fixes the *fold* but never states the *data-shape of a contribution* or its *merge law under duplicate delivery / retraction / reordering*. 20/24 §Established pattern makes commutative/associative/idempotent merge normative for concurrent producers, but attention was never fitted to (or excused from) that template. 20/22 §MessageContext classifies data (waved) vs management (null) invocations but never classifies an *upstream-flowing* generic-protocol message. The carrier — the G-13 metadata plane — was resolved by **I-1**, and full-ref addressing by **I-2**; this challenge is the attention *algebra* that rides them.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **"Attention is incremental dataflow" (30/34) vs the idempotent-merge law (20/24, P5).** If an attention contribution is a *delta* (a `+level` pulse) then `sum` is genuinely non-idempotent: a diamond that re-delivers the same pulse twice inflates the aggregate, and 20/24's whole reason for OR-set tags is to make such re-deliveries harmless. Either attention needs tags (heavy, and tags don't even give `sum` a meaning), or attention is **not** a delta stream and the sentence in 30/34 is imprecise.
- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path) vs per-contribution bookkeeping.** Whatever shape attention takes must not add tag-set churn to a path P6 puts on the *interest* signal itself; the fold must be cheap and off the data hot path.
- **Decided null-context management vs "upstream-flowing wave" (20/22, I-1).** G-20 per-source waves and "management invocations carry null MessageContext" both assume each *data* hop presents one emitting `sourcePort`. An upstream message travelling *against* data direction has no natural wave and no natural `sourcePort` — but 30/34 called it "dataflow," inviting the wrong reading.
- **Retraction has no inverse for `max`.** If a cell keeps only a running aggregate (not per-link state), removing the *maximum* contributor on unlink cannot lower the aggregate — `max` is not invertible. Correct retraction *forces* per-link state, which then interacts with in-flight updates and link-op ordering (P8, and the topology-versioning discipline of 22).
- **P4 / P10.** The mechanism must stay strictly local per hop (no global attention coordinator — decision G-20's spirit) and must not grow a general CRDT engine "just in case" (P10) when the niche needs a bounded interest signal.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Attention as a CRDT delta stream (OR-set-style tags)

Model an attention contribution exactly like a data-cell delta: each pulse carries a cell-local `Timestamp` tag; a cell folds live tags; merge = tag union (20/24 §Established pattern).

- *Semantics*: attention "converges" by the same tag algebra as `SetCell`.
- *Fast-path cost*: per-pulse tag bookkeeping and growing tag sets on the interest path; a `refresh` must reconcile tags.
- *Failure modes*: **`sum` has no meaning over a tag set** (tags dedup — you get a count of distinct pulses, not a load sum); **retraction needs tombstones**, which grow unbounded for a signal that pulses forever; the tag machinery solves duplicate-delivery but attention's real need — *retract a whole contributor on unlink* — is not what OR-set tags do (they retract *observed* adds, not "everything from link L").
- *Tradeoffs*: maximal reuse of 20/24 machinery, but it is machinery attention does not need and that actively breaks `sum`/`decay`. Rejected.

##### Candidate B — Monotone-max only; forbid `sum`/`decay` (sidestep idempotency)

Restrict attention to `max`, which is idempotent and monotone, so duplicate delivery is automatically harmless; drop the non-monotone strategies.

- *Semantics*: aggregate = running max of contributions; duplicate `max(x, x) = x`.
- *Fast-path cost*: cheapest — a single running float, no per-link map.
- *Failure modes*: **retraction is impossible** — when the max contributor unlinks you cannot lower the aggregate without remembering the others, i.e. you need per-link state anyway; **contradicts shipped M6** (`sum` and `decay` are "decisions below are code," 30/34); load-signalling consumers lose `sum`.
- *Tradeoffs*: the very requirement that kills it (retraction) forces per-link state — and *once you keep per-link state, the idempotency problem dissolves and `sum`/`decay` come free*. This is the argument **for** Candidate C. Rejected.

##### Candidate C — Attention as per-link LWW **level state** + commutative fold (recommended)

An attention contribution is **not a delta** but the emitter's **current level**. Each aggregating cell/port holds one **level slot per direct downstream link** (plus a *self* slot); the aggregate is a **pure, commutative, associative fold over the current slot levels**, quantized to a band, re-emitted upstream on band change. Duplicate/stale delivery is absorbed by **last-writer-wins per link** (an emitter-monotonic `version` field). Retraction is **slot removal on unlink**. Attention rides the **I-1 metadata plane** (null context, own lane/band, `FanInMerge`), keyed by the **delivering link**, not by `sourcePort`.

- *Semantics*: `slots: LinkId → (level, version)`; `aggregate = aggregator.fold(slots.values.level ∪ {selfLevel})`; `band = quantize(aggregate)`; propagate on band change.
- *Fast-path cost*: off the data hot path entirely (own lane/band, I-1); a slot write + fold runs on band-change / host-cadence `refresh`, never per data message.
- *Failure modes*: none of the member-pair tensions survive (§4). Residual work is soft-state handling across migration and multi-hop/transitive notices (§8).
- *Tradeoffs*: gives up the (illusory) "attention is literally a delta stream" framing in exchange for a model where idempotency is *structural* (LWW-per-link + commutative fold), retraction is *by construction* (slot removal = the frontier-shrink pattern of 22), and `max`/`sum`/`decay` all keep their meaning. This is 30/34's own phrase — "a pure fold of the cell's own level and its **downstream links' levels**" — made precise. Recommended.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**: **attention is per-link last-writer-wins level state with a pure commutative/associative fold**; it is *not* an OR-set delta stream. The three sub-axes fall out of one data shape plus four rules, all riding the I-1 metadata plane and I-2 full-ref addressing.

**Data shapes**

```
// The upstream generic-protocol message (ProtocolId = ATTENTION on the I-1 metadata plane).
// Null MessageContext; management-class; descriptor: direction = Upstream, cardinality = FanInMerge,
// own ordering lane + priority band (I-1 rule 3/5).
data class AttentionUpdate(
    val level: Float,          // the emitter's CURRENT aggregate level (a snapshot, not a delta)
    val version: Long,         // per-emitter monotonic LWW discriminator — a payload field,
                               // NOT a MessageContext wave (reuses the "one clock shape,
                               // separate uses" pattern of 20/22 / 20/24)
    val deadlineHint: Deadline? = null   // optional, as 30/34 §Design sketch
) : Serializable

// Framework state on each aggregating cell/port (NOT cell logic — lives beside ProtocolSupport):
class AttentionFrontier(val aggregator: AttentionAggregator) {   // aggregator is a named strategy (P9)
    private val slots = HashMap<LinkId, Slot>()      // one slot per DIRECT downstream link
    private var selfLevel = 0f                       // the cell's own intrinsic interest (sinks set it)
    private var myVersion = 0L
    private var lastBand = Band.NONE
    data class Slot(val level: Float, val version: Long)

    fun onUpdate(link: LinkId, u: AttentionUpdate)   // LWW: apply iff u.version > slot.version
    fun onUnlink(link: LinkId)                        // RETRACTION: slots.remove(link); recompute()
    fun setSelf(level: Float)                         // sinks / NonSuspendable pin interest here
    private fun recompute()                           // fold → quantize → propagate on band change
}
```

`LinkId` is the local identity of the link the update arrived on (an I-2 full-ref `PortRef` pair; keyed *locally* per hop — no global identity needed). `AttentionAggregator` is a registered, serialization-friendly named strategy (`max` | `sum` | `decay(base)` | composed), read from host-bound scheduling-step ticks for time-aware variants (30/34 decision 1) — never a lambda on the wire (P9).

**`recompute()`**:
```
aggregate = aggregator.fold( slots.values.map { it.level } + selfLevel )   // commutative, associative
band = quantize(aggregate)                                                 // NONE<LOW<NORMAL<HIGH
if (band != lastBand) {                                                     // DAMPING gate
    lastBand = band
    for (up in upstreamLinks) emit AttentionUpdate(aggregate, ++myVersion) on up   // ATTENTION protocol
}
```

**Rules the model introduces (normative)**

1. **Attention is per-link level state, not a delta stream.** Each aggregating cell/port holds exactly one level slot per *direct downstream link* plus a *self* slot; the aggregate is a **pure, commutative, associative fold** over the current slot levels. The word "delta" in 30/34 §Design sketch is refined: an `AttentionUpdate` carries a *current level snapshot*, and it is the *change of aggregate band* — not the message — that is "incremental." (Resolves N2×N21, N15×N21.)

2. **Idempotency is structural, via per-link LWW by `version`.** A receiver applies `AttentionUpdate(link, level, version)` **iff** `version` exceeds the slot's stored version; equal/lower versions are absorbed. Therefore (a) **duplicate delivery** of the same update on link L overwrites L's slot with the same value → no change; (b) the fold over the resulting slot multiset is order-independent. This gives attention the commutative/associative/**idempotent** merge 20/24 demands — but at the level of *slot replacement + commutative fold*, **not** OR-set tag union. The distinction that dissolves N15×N21: *duplicate delivery on one link* is absorbed by LWW; *genuine fan-out to two distinct consumers* is two distinct slots (`sum` counts both **by design** = load semantics; `max` collapses them = priority semantics). OR-set tags are unnecessary because attention's key space is the **bounded, known** direct-downstream-link set, not unbounded element membership. Within a stable lane, per-link FIFO (I-1 rule 3) already gives LWW by arrival; `version` makes it correct-by-construction across the reorder window that bypassing the data drain opens (rule 4).

3. **Retraction = slot removal on unlink; the frontier is the current link set.** `onUnlink(downstreamLink)` removes that slot and recomputes; any in-flight `AttentionUpdate` for a removed link is **dropped** (no slot / no endpoint to key). Because unlink causally shrinks the link set and attention rides that link's own lane, no update survives its unlink; even a stray one is harmless. The attention frontier is thus **the current downstream link set** — *topology is part of the aggregate*, exactly mirroring the glitch-free frontier recomputed on link change (22 §The glitch-free frontier; "topology is part of the completeness condition"). `max` retraction — impossible without state — is now well-defined: drop the slot, re-fold the remainder. (Resolves N4×N21.)

4. **Null-context, link-keyed, no `sourcePort`.** Attention is an I-1 metadata-plane protocol: **management-class, NULL MessageContext, `Upstream` direction, `FanInMerge` cardinality, own lane + band.** It **mints no wave, carries no wave, rewrites no `sourcePort`.** The aggregation key is the **link the update arrived on** — the reverse endpoint delivered by `ProtocolSupport.deliver(ATTENTION, link, msg)` (I-1) — not a `MessageContext.sourcePort`. Hence "sourcePort against link direction" has *no meaning* for attention: it is strictly **per-hop, per-link, local** (P4).
