The `version` field is a payload discriminator, explicitly analogous to how merge tags "reuse the `Timestamp` type but are minted cell-locally, not taken from the current wave" (20/22 §Interaction / 20/24) — one clock shape, a separate use. (Resolves N11×N21, N1×N21, N3×N21.)

5. **Band-gated propagation is the damping (carried from 30/34).** A cell re-emits its aggregate level upstream **only when its quantized band changes**; intra-band jitter is structurally incapable of propagating. This is magnitude-throttling (21, G-19) applied to attention itself and is what keeps non-monotone folds (`sum`, `decay`) from re-exciting cycles. The value propagated is the aggregate **level (float)** — preserving `sum`'s load information — gated on **band** change. (Carries 30/34 decision 1 unchanged.)

6. **Park preserves the slot; only unlink retracts.** Suspension/migration **parks** (interest survives; latency, not interest, is lost — 30/34 decision 2, "park-not-drop"): the attention slot is **retained** across park and wire re-resolution. Only a genuine `unlink` removes a slot. This keeps attention consistent with "suspension = one Buffering primitive; a quiesced subgraph loses latency, never messages." On a full re-resolution that *does* lose soft state, each downstream re-announces its current level on relink — reusing the `onLinked` late-join catch-up seam (13, 21, G-22): a re-announce *is* the attention analogue of state-as-delta-from-empty. (Reconciles retraction with suspension.)

7. **Cross-host via I-1 protocol-aware bridges.** An upstream `AttentionUpdate` crossing hosts is a `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame on the **reverse bridge path** the link already maintains for re-resolution (I-1 rule 6): egress serializes it, ingress delivers it to the remote `ProtocolSupport`, keyed by the bridge link. This closes 30/34's remaining item ("attention does not cross the wire — bridged links carry no protocol endpoints") using the I-1 mechanism, with no new bridge type. Per-instance frontiers (I-2): each replica instance aggregates its **own** downstream links; there is no logical-level attention aggregation across replicas.

**Net effect**: one data shape (per-link level + version), one fold (commutative/associative), one gate (band change), one retraction (slot removal). Idempotency and retraction are correct-by-construction (P5); the interest path never touches the data hot path (P2); every hop is local (P4); `max`/`sum`/`decay` all keep their meaning; and the "attention is a CRDT delta stream" reading — which would have broken `sum` — is explicitly rejected in favour of *bounded per-link LWW state*, which is what the niche needs (P10).

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — the frontier is a per-port map + a pure fold; `onUpdate`/`onUnlink`/`recompute` are ordinary synchronous operations, meaningful single-threaded (the M6 code already delivers attention synchronously in simulation). No new concurrency primitive. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — attention rides its own lane/band off the data path (I-1); a slot write + fold runs on band-change / host-cadence `refresh`, not per data message; `recompute` propagates only on band change. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — attention rides explicit links; the frontier *is* the current downstream link set, inspectable; retraction is an unlink event, not hidden decay. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — every hop aggregates only its own direct downstream slots and re-emits locally; no global attention coordinator, clock, or barrier. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — idempotency = LWW-by-`version` + commutative fold (a typed pure strategy); retraction = `onUnlink` slot removal; band/direction/cardinality/lane are static descriptor fields (I-1). |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — attention *is* the interest signal; level 0 sustained → suspend; renewed level → resume (30/34). The exemplar of P6. |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — no bearing on boundary controls. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — the frontier is recomputed on every link/unlink; nothing assumes a static downstream set; per-instance frontiers coexist under evolution (I-2). |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `AttentionUpdate` is ids-only (`Float` level + `Long` version); aggregators are *named registered strategies*, never lambdas on the wire; rides the I-1 `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — a bounded per-link interest signal, deliberately *not* a general CRDT engine; the rejection of OR-set-tagged attention is the niche-first trade. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: attention carries **null** MessageContext, mints/carries no wave; `version` is a payload field, not a wave id.
- **SID-UP global propagation locks REJECTED** — Consistent: aggregation is strictly local per hop; no global attention lock/clock/coordinator.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: park preserves the frontier across a moving host (rule 6); attention crosses via the link's existing bridge path.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent: attention *drives* suspend/resume; park-not-drop preserves the slot; no new suspension mechanism (reuses 30/34 decisions 2–3).
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay mechanism** — Consistent: attention re-resolves with its link; a lost-soft-state re-resolution triggers `onLinked` re-announce (rule 6).
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: attention re-announce on relink is state-as-current-level, the attention analogue of state-as-delta-from-empty; no snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps minted cell-locally, NOT wave ids; tags and waves stay separate uses of one clock shape** — Consistent, reinforced: the attention `version` is a *third* use of the "monotonic counter" shape, explicitly not a wave and not an OR-set tag.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent: `AttentionUpdate` is push-only AND null-context; attention is a management-class generic protocol (per I-1) that happens to be push-only. No amendment.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second synchronization protocol** — Consistent: attention is local per-hop metadata, **not** replicated state and **not** a sync protocol; per-instance frontiers (I-2) mean no cross-replica attention convergence to synchronize.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: `AttentionUpdate` crosses as an I-1 `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame, ids-only; the message-level `version` field is payload, distinct from the wire version byte.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent: attention **bypasses** the data drain (management-class, I-1 rules 2–3) on its own lane; rule 2's LWW-by-`version` supplies the idempotence/reorder-tolerance I-1 rule 3 requires of any bypassing protocol.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time** — Consistent: attention cardinality is protocol-intrinsic `FanInMerge` (I-1 rule 5), independent of the data link's cardinality; nothing is enforced at attention send time.
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross machines** — Consistent: the attention contract carries no `Owned`/`Leased` (I-1 rule 4); `AttentionUpdate` is a plain value.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId (per I-2: full-ref addressing)** — Consistent: `LinkId` slots key on full-ref `PortRef`s; each *instance* has its own frontier; there is no logicalId-level attention aggregation.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — G-6 is "Resolved (M6)"; this **elaborates** the residual (retraction/merge/context) that 30/34 itself flagged conceptually, preserving all four M6 decisions. No M6 decision is reversed → **no CONFLICT flag**. The only refinement is a wording precision: 30/34's "attention updates are deltas" becomes "attention updates carry current-level snapshots; the *band change* is what is incremental."

#### 7. Spec impact

- **30/34 §Decisions, decision 1** — Add the per-link **LWW level-slot** formulation, the `AttentionUpdate{level, version}` shape, the explicit **idempotency law** (LWW-by-version + commutative fold), and the distinction between duplicate-delivery absorption (LWW) and genuine-fan-out counting (`sum` semantics). Refine "attention updates are deltas" → "current-level snapshots; band change is the increment."
- **30/34 §Decisions — new decision (retraction)** — State retraction = slot removal on `onUnlink`; the frontier is the current downstream link set (topology-as-aggregate, cross-ref 22); in-flight updates for removed links are dropped; interleaving is resolved by the link's own lane + `version`.
- **30/34 §header "Remaining"** — Update: wire crossing **resolved** via I-1 protocol-aware bridges (rule 7); note the `version` LWW field; single-hop→multi-hop notices remain open (§8).
- **10/12 §Directionality of generic protocols / §Multiplex** — Record the attention `ProtocolDescriptor`: `Upstream`, `FanInMerge`, own lane/band; attention is keyed by the **delivering link**, not `sourcePort` (cross-ref I-1).
- **20/22 §MessageContext** — Add that generic protocols (attention exemplar) carry **null** context — no wave minted, no `sourcePort` rewritten for upstream traffic; and that per-link attention state reuses the "clock shape, separate use" pattern with a `version` field (cross-ref 20/24).
- **20/24 §Established pattern** — Add a note: attention is **not** an OR-set delta stream; it is **per-link LWW level state** whose merge is slot-replacement + commutative fold; OR-set tags are unnecessary because attention's key space (direct downstream links) is bounded. Distinguish duplicate-delivery idempotency from genuine-fan-out counting.
- **90/91 G-6** — Update "Remaining": retraction/merge/context **specified** (this resolution); wire crossing via I-1; transitive/multi-hop notices still open.
- **40/42 / I-1 cross-ref** — Confirm per-instance frontiers; cross-host `AttentionUpdate` as reverse-bridge `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Attention frontier as migratable soft state vs re-announce-on-relink.** Rule 6 offers both (park preserves; full re-resolution re-announces via `onLinked`); the precise trigger boundary, and whether the frontier is captured by `Stateful.snapshot` on migrate or always rebuilt, needs pinning.
- **Transitive / multi-hop notices.** 30/34 notes notices are single-hop ("a join sees only direct upstream parks, not transitive ones"). Attention itself is multi-hop by re-emission, but the interaction of *transitive retraction* with band-gating (a retraction that must cross several damped hops to quiesce a deep subgraph) and loop-prevention is unresolved.
- **`deadlineHint` aggregation.** 30/34 carries an optional deadline hint, but its fold across links (min? earliest?) is unspecified; it needs its own aggregation rule distinct from the level fold.
- **`version` minting discipline & wraparound.** Per-emitter monotonic `Long`; the minting rule (per-frontier vs per-upstream-link), collision-freedom across migration, and wraparound handling need stating.
- **Cross-host attention convergence harness.** A generative test that reorders/duplicates `AttentionUpdate` frames across the wire and asserts band convergence under LWW-by-`version` — the wire analogue of `AttentionGenerativeTest`.
- **Retraction × suspension-region atomicity.** Interaction of a retraction that would quiesce a member of a glitch-free **suspension region** (30/34 decision 3) mid-wave — does the region's atomic-park resolution race the retraction, or does the veto/NonSuspendable contagion settle it?

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high.** The resolution is strongly grounded: 30/34 *already* frames the fold as "a pure fold of the cell's own level and its **downstream links' levels**," which is per-link state — this challenge only makes the *data shape* (LWW level + version), the *idempotency law*, the *retraction rule*, and the *context classification* explicit, all of which fall out of I-1's already-adopted metadata-plane model and I-2's full-ref addressing. The load-bearing insight — that **retraction forces per-link state, and per-link state dissolves the sum-idempotency tension** — turns the headline conflict (N15×N21) into a non-problem by distinguishing duplicate-delivery (LWW-absorbed) from genuine fan-out (counted by design). No M6 decision is reversed; the only change is a wording precision in 30/34.

**Open questions**: (1) whether the attention frontier is captured on migration or always rebuilt by re-announce — I lean rebuild-by-`onLinked` (soft state, catch-up parallel) but a large deep subgraph may want capture; (2) `deadlineHint` fold semantics, spun out as a follow-on; (3) the transitive-notice / deep-retraction behaviour, which M6 explicitly left single-hop and this resolution enables but does not fully specify.

### I-5 — Wave semantics in cycles: same-wave re-entry detection and per-iteration topology version

> Member pairs: N10×N11, N10×N12, N10×N13, N10×N23
> Existing gaps touched: G-19, G-20, G-8 · Confidence: medium · Substrate: yes
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 1/4 member pairs findings need re-wording while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The whole design: CycleHead re-origination (iteration = wave), the distinct absorbing feedbackInput, the wave-uniqueness theorem replacing re-entry detection, per-iteration topology versioning falling out of per-wave rules, per-instance loop identity, the l…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: transparent flow preserves a wave id on every
response emission (`20/22 §MessageContext` rule 2: "when a cell emits in response
to an inlet invocation, the outlet invocation carries the *same* timestamp"), so a
delta circulating a cycle `A→B→C→A` re-presents its original `Timestamp(sourceId,
counter)` forever. This defeats the glitch-free invariant "evaluate exactly once
per wave" (`20/22 §Local glitch-freedom` steps 2–3: version buffering + a local
evaluation barrier per wave) and leaves four coupled sub-questions the spec flags
as open:

1. **Re-entry detection** — `20/22 §Interaction with other parts → Cycles`: "a
   cycle re-entering a glitch-free cell with the same wave id must be detected —
   candidate: wave id + hop count, or explicit cycle-breaker cells. Open."
2. **Glitch-free behaviour on re-entry** — what a per-wave version buffer does when
   a wave it already flushed arrives again.
3. **Per-iteration topology version** — `20/22 §Topology versioning` gives each wave
   "a definite edge set," but a loop iterating under *one* wave id across a
   mid-iteration link change has no defined topology version per iteration.
4. **Identity of "the same cell"** — `20/21 §Cycles` (G-19) re-entry presumes
   recognising the same cell, but under G-8 (`10/11 §Identity and persistence`,
   `CellRef(id, instanceId)`) the loop can route through a *different instance* of
   the same `logicalId`; neither G-19 nor the open re-entry note says whether
   detection keys on logical or instance identity.

**Member pairs**: N10×N11 (transparent flow re-presents the wave id forever; wave-id
+ hop-count only a candidate), N10×N12 (same-wave re-entry defeats per-wave
buffering; fixpoint×glitch-freedom declared open research), N10×N13 (no topology
version per iteration under one wave id across a mid-iteration link change),
N10×N23 (re-entry detection must recognise "the same cell" but G-8 lets a loop
re-enter a different instance).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: `20/21 §Cycles` specifies only magnitude-based
throttling for *divergence* (G-19) and explicitly defers "Fixpoint semantics (and
interaction with glitch-freedom timestamps in cycles)" as "an open research item —
flagged, not resolved, by this spec." `20/22` names two candidates and picks
neither. The wave machinery (`Timestamp`, transparent flow, per-wave buffering,
topology versioning) was designed and validated on a DAG (the diamond test, 200
seeds); the cyclic case is the one traversal shape none of those rules was written
against.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **Transparent flow is *right* for DAGs and *wrong* for loops.** Preserving the
  wave id lets a glitch-free join recognise "these two inputs belong to wave *t*"
  (`20/22 §Local glitch-freedom`, the diamond). The identical rule, applied where an
  edge feeds back, means the wave never terminates as an identity. One rule cannot
  be both preserved and self-terminating; the resolution must locate *where*
  preservation is deliberately broken.
- **P4 forbids the obvious fix.** A global superstep/BSP coordinator that advances
  the whole loop in lockstep would give clean per-iteration waves — but it is a
  global barrier (P4) and a global coordinator (P1), and "SID-UP-style global
  propagation locks are REJECTED" (recorded decision, `20/22 §Local glitch-freedom`).
- **P2 vs per-message loop bookkeeping.** Any "detect re-entry" scheme that keeps
  per-cell per-wave memory, or puts a hop/epoch field into the *join key*, taxes the
  fast path (a volatile read + enqueue) and pollutes the join semantics that the
  diamond test validates.
- **P6/P10 vs "just in case."** Most graphs are acyclic; the niche does not want
  every message to carry loop machinery on the off chance a cycle exists.
- **G-8 / I-2 pull the identity question sideways.** "Recognise the same cell on
  re-entry" assumes a stable per-cell wave memory, but I-2 fixed that links bind
  **full refs** and "each instance's outlet is a distinct source" (I-2 §6). Under
  replication (`42`) a loop can traverse two instances of one `logicalId`; a
  detection scheme keyed on `logicalId` would conflate two independent sources.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Wave-id + hop-count re-entry detection (the spec's first candidate)

Keep transparent flow; add a `hop: Int` to `MessageContext` that increments per
hop; a glitch-free cell remembers, per wave, the highest hop it processed and
treats a same-`(sourceId, counter)` arrival with a higher hop as a re-entry to
re-evaluate (or drop).

- *Semantics*: detection = "same wave id seen again"; the cell holds per-wave hop
  state.
- *Fast-path cost*: an extra field (cheap) **plus** unbounded per-wave memory in
  every glitch-free cell on a loop, and a decision point on every delivery.
- *Failure modes*: `hop` **cannot** enter the join key — an asymmetric diamond
  (`A→B→D`, `A→X→Y→D`) delivers one legitimate wave over paths of different length,
  so different hops must still join as one wave. But then `hop` no longer
  *distinguishes* a re-entry from a slow diamond arm; detection is ambiguous
  precisely where it matters. It never defines a per-iteration topology version
  (question 3) and never yields fixpoint semantics — it is a divergence guard
  wearing the costume of an identity.
- *Tradeoff*: a detection patch, not a semantics. **Rejected** as the primary
  mechanism; its bounded-`hop` idea survives only as a liveness guard (§4).

##### Candidate B — Re-origination at declared cycle heads (recommended)

Every cycle contains at least one cell declared a **CycleHead**. A CycleHead
*absorbs* incoming feedback into loop state and, if the change is still significant
(G-19 magnitude), **mints a fresh wave** (its own instance `sourceId`, incremented
counter) for the next iteration instead of transparently preserving the incoming
one. Transparent flow is unchanged for every other cell.

- *Semantics*: an iteration *is* a wave. Because the head never forwards an incoming
  wave id, no `(sourceId, counter)` traverses any cell twice — so there is nothing to
  "detect." Every per-wave rule (buffering, evaluate-once, topology versioning,
  drain FIFO) applies to loops **unchanged**.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero for non-head cells (transparent flow untouched). The head
  pays a magnitude compare and a counter bump per iteration — off the steady-state
  ideal only at the one declared point, exactly where G-19 already puts a compare.
- *Failure modes*: a cycle with **no** declared head recirculates one wave id
  forever; must be caught (link-time structural check for local cycles; a bounded
  hop guard for cross-host cycles no single host can see).
- *Tradeoff*: reduces to the *existing* origination rule (P1), correct-by-construction
  (P5), pays only where a cycle is declared (P6). Requires one declaration per cycle
  — but G-19 *already* requires a quiescence-threshold declaration per cycle, so the
  head role is folded into a declaration the cycle needs anyway.

##### Candidate C — Epoch-tagged waves (re-origination with lineage)

As B, but instead of a wholly fresh mint the head bumps an `epoch` sub-field on the
inherited `Timestamp`, and joins key on `(sourceId, counter, epoch)`. Iteration *N*
is `(…, epoch=N)`, traceable to the external event that seeded the loop.

- *Semantics*: re-origination that preserves provenance — a wave carries its loop
  lineage.
- *Fast-path cost*: widens the decided `Timestamp` shape (G-20) and the join key on
  every glitch-free cell, even acyclic ones.
- *Failure modes*: still needs a breaker to bump the epoch (so it does not avoid B's
  declaration); it taxes the DAG join key for a provenance feature the niche may not
  need yet.
- *Tradeoff*: strictly richer than B (provenance) at a real DAG cost. **Fold in as a
  future extension of B**, not the base mechanism: B can grow an `epoch` later
  without changing the head model.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B — re-origination at declared cycle heads.** The single move:
**turn each loop iteration into a fresh wave at one declared point, so "iteration"
becomes "wave" and every existing per-wave rule covers cycles with no new
machinery.** Same-wave re-entry is not *detected*, it is *structurally prevented*.

##### Data shapes

```kotlin
// A cell participating in a cycle declares itself a head and a quiescence threshold.
// This is the SAME declaration G-19 already requires of a cycle participant.
interface CycleHead {
    val quiescence: Double        // G-19: below this magnitude, absorb instead of emit
}

// Feedback inlets are declared DISTINCTLY from ordinary (wave-joining) inlets.
val feedback by feedbackInput<Propagate<D>>()   // absorbs into loop state; NOT a wave join input

// Delta types on cycle edges carry magnitude (G-19, unchanged).
interface Magnitude { fun size(): Double }

// MessageContext gains a divergence guard — a guard, NOT part of wave identity.
data class MessageContext(
    val timestamp: Timestamp,     // (sourceId, counter) — join key, UNCHANGED
    val sourcePort: PortRef,
    val hop: Int = 0              // increments per transparent-flow hop; NEVER in the join key
)
```

`Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` is **unchanged** (G-20 shape preserved); the head
mints a fresh one exactly as a source does.

##### Protocol / rules the model introduces (normative)

**Rule 1 — Re-origination at the head.** On a `CycleHead`, the transition
*(feedback delivered → derived emission)* mints a **fresh** `Timestamp(headSourceId,
++counter)` on the emitting outlet, rather than preserving the incoming timestamp.
`headSourceId` is the head **instance's** outlet source (per I-2 §6, "each instance's
outlet is a distinct source"). This is the one, precisely-located exception to
transparent flow (`20/22 §MessageContext` rule 2); every non-head cell preserves the
timestamp as before.

**Rule 2 — Feedback is absorbed, not joined.** A `feedbackInput` delivers into the
head's loop state and triggers a magnitude check; it does **not** enter the head's
glitch-free completeness condition as a wave input. Consequently the incoming wave
*terminates* at the head (absorbed into state) and a new wave *originates* for the
next iteration. A head is a wave **sink** for the loop edge and a wave **source** for
the iteration — ordinary origination (`20/22 §MessageContext` rule 1). The head MAY
still be glitch-free on its *external* (non-feedback) inlets: those are ordinary DAG
joins.

**Rule 3 — Quiescence terminates the wave sequence.** If the absorbed feedback's
`size()` is below `quiescence`, the head absorbs without emitting (G-19). The
iteration sequence `t_1, t_2, …` halts; the fixpoint is the state after the last
emitted wave settles. This is the base I-6 (cycle fixpoint) rests on: fixpoint =
the terminating sequence of head-minted waves.

**Rule 4 — Wave-uniqueness theorem (why re-entry detection is unnecessary).** Every
cycle contains ≥1 `CycleHead`, and a head never forwards an incoming wave id. Therefore
no `(sourceId, counter)` traverses any cell more than once. A glitch-free cell inside
a loop sees a stream of **distinct** waves and applies "evaluate exactly once per
wave" (`20/22 §Local glitch-freedom`) verbatim — no re-entry state, no special case.
This answers questions 1 and 2 by dissolving them.

**Rule 5 — Topology version per iteration falls out.** Because an iteration is a wave,
"the topology version iteration *N* sees" *is* "the edge set feeding wave `t_N`," which
`20/22 §Topology versioning` already defines: link/unlink events are stamped into the
same logical-time domain and are part of a wave's completeness condition. A
mid-iteration link change is an event causally ordered against the waves: at each cell
it lands either before `t_N` (that cell evaluates `t_N` over the new topology) or after
(over the old); the *next* iteration `t_{N+1}`, minted after the change, sees the new
topology uniformly from the head onward. No cycle-specific topology rule is needed —
this answers question 3.

**Rule 6 — Identity is per instance (G-8 / I-2).** The head mints on its **instance
(full-ref) sourceId**. If the loop reroutes through a different instance of the same
`logicalId` (migration, or a replica in the path), that is a **topology change** (a new
edge set, causally stamped) and the new instance is simply a new source minting its own
waves. There is no cross-instance "same cell" to recognise; "the same cell" for the
(now-vacated) detection question would have been the **instance**, consistent with I-2's
full-ref addressing. This answers question 4.

##### Safety nets for undeclared cycles (a cycle with no head is an error)

**Rule 7 — Link-time structural check (locally-visible cycles).** Because topology is
explicit and inspectable (P3), when a `connect` would close a cycle wholly visible to
one host, the host walks the new cycle; if it contains no `CycleHead`, the link is
`Rejected` with a `CycleWithoutHead` `LinkResult`. This is a rare-path check (P2
permits expensive linking) and correct-by-construction (P5).

**Rule 8 — Runtime hop guard (cross-host cycles).** A cycle closed jointly by links on
different hosts/peers is not locally visible (P8, decentralisation). `MessageContext.hop`
increments per transparent-flow hop and is reset by a head's re-origination (a head mints
`hop=0`). If `hop` exceeds a host-configured bound at any cell, that cell dead-letters the
invocation as a `CycleError` (via the existing `deadLetterOutlet`, G-26) instead of
re-emitting. In a correctly-headed graph `hop` never approaches the bound (it resets each
iteration); the guard only fires on an unbroken loop. `hop` is explicitly **not** part of
the wave join key (Rule 4 keeps the join key `(sourceId, counter)`), so it cannot perturb
diamond joins — it is purely a liveness backstop, and Candidate A's one salvageable idea.

##### Net effect

Transparent flow, per-wave buffering, topology versioning, and drain FIFO are all
**reused unchanged**; the only additions are a `CycleHead` declaration (folded into the
G-19 threshold a cycle already needs), a distinct `feedbackInput`, one re-origination
exception at the head, and a hop guard that fires only on malformed graphs. Fixpoint
semantics (I-6) now have a foundation: a terminating sequence of well-defined,
well-versioned waves.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — re-origination is ordinary origination; no coordinator, no barrier; every rule meaningful in single-threaded simulation (a head is a cell that mints a wave when it emits). |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — non-head cells unchanged; the head pays a magnitude compare + counter bump (rare, at one point). *Tension, disclosed*: `hop` adds one int to every context; it is a single increment beside the timestamp write already on the path, and never enters the join key. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — cycles are explicit link paths; the link-time head check is a graph walk over inspectable topology; no hidden loop mechanism. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global clock/lock/barrier; each head is a local source; cross-source loop iterations get convergence, not simultaneity (G-20). |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — the head role and feedback inlet are declared in types; wave-uniqueness is structural (Rule 4), not runtime discipline; unheaded local cycles rejected at link time. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — loop machinery exists only where a cycle is declared; the head declaration is one a cycle already needs for G-19. |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched.** |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — mid-iteration link changes are ordinary causally-stamped events; rerouting through a new instance is a topology change; nothing assumes a static loop. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `MessageContext` gains a serializable int; `CycleHead`/`feedbackInput` are ordinary declarations; nothing new on the wire but one field. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — decentralized feedback loops (UI↔model, learning) resolve with re-origination + local throttling, no global iteration protocol. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent, reinforced: a head is a source; re-origination *is* origination; the `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` shape is unchanged.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent: no coordinator, no barrier; the superstep/BSP alternative is explicitly rejected (§2).
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: a migrated head keeps its instance `sourceId` (I-2); its wave sequence continues; the loop path re-resolves.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive** — Consistent: head-minted waves buffer/park like any wave; no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local|Remote; one park/replay** — Consistent: cross-host loop edges re-resolve through the same registry; the hop guard is a dead-letter, not a new park path.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Untouched.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, NOT wave ids** — Consistent, reinforced: waves (including head-minted ones) stay separate from cell-local OR-set tags.
- **Data push-only / management null context** — Consistent: cycle edges are data (push `Propagate<D>`); the magnitude/quiescence throttle is the head's own logic, not a management call.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** — Consistent: magnitude throttling and re-origination add no synchronization protocol; per I-1 the throttle is a *data* property, not a metadata-plane protocol.
- **Partitioning not a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched.
- **Wire ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: `hop` is an additive int on `MessageContext`; bump the reserved version byte only if the encoding is not additively compatible.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent: per-link FIFO of head-minted waves is unchanged; the head absorbs feedback in arrival order.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time** — Consistent: `feedbackInput` is an ordinary inlet with ordinary cardinality; nothing send-time added.
- **CellRef(id, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2)** — Consistent, load-bearing: the head mints per instance; loop identity is per full ref; no cross-instance recognition.
- **I-1 metadata-plane model** — Consistent: magnitude is a data-delta property (`Magnitude` on the delta), not a `PORT_PROTOCOL`; the head throttle is cell logic, keeping the plane bounded.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — No resolved item reopened. G-19 (cycle throttling) and the `20/22` cycles note remain *open* items this resolution now closes with a concrete design.

No CONFLICT flag required. The one refinement — `20/22`'s two candidates resolve to
"explicit cycle heads that re-originate" (candidate 2), with wave-id+hop-count
(candidate 1) retained only as a liveness guard — amends open *proposals*, not a
recorded decision.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/21 §Cycles (G-19)** — Replace the "fixpoint semantics … open research item"
  clause: specify `CycleHead` (folding the quiescence threshold), `feedbackInput` as a
  distinct absorbing inlet, re-origination at the head, and that fixpoint = the
  terminating head-minted wave sequence. State the requirement "every cycle MUST contain
  a CycleHead" and the two safety nets.
- **20/22 §MessageContext** — Add the head re-origination rule as the single stated
  exception to transparent flow (rule 2); add the `hop` guard field with the explicit
  note that it is never part of the join key.
- **20/22 §Local glitch-freedom / §Topology versioning** — Add the wave-uniqueness
  theorem (Rule 4) and state that "iteration = wave" makes per-iteration topology
  versioning a special case of the existing per-wave rule (Rule 5); no cycle-specific
  buffering.
- **20/22 §Interaction with other parts → Cycles** — Rewrite the "unresolved / candidate"
  bullet to point at this resolution: re-origination prevents re-entry; hop is a guard.
- **10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based) / cardinality** — Note the link-time structural
  cycle-without-head check (`CycleWithoutHead` `LinkResult`).
- **10/11 §Identity** — Cross-reference that loop identity is per full-ref instance
  (I-2); a loop rerouting through a new instance is a topology change.
- **30/31 §host / G-26** — Note the `hop`-bound guard dead-letters as `CycleError`.
- **90/91 G-19** — Update: throttling + fixpoint resolved via CycleHead re-origination;
  "fixpoint semantics open" clause removed, deferring only the multi-head and
  convergence-rate questions (§8).

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Multi-head cycles and nested loops** — a cycle may declare several heads, or loops may
  nest; the interaction of multiple independent wave sequences on overlapping edges (each
  head a distinct source → convergence, not simultaneity) needs a stated well-formedness
  rule ("≥1 head per elementary cycle") and a detection algorithm over the cycle basis.
- **Convergence-rate / fixpoint existence (I-6 core)** — magnitude monotonic-decrease is
  assumed but not guaranteed; whether a head's `quiescence` threshold plus `Magnitude`
  guarantees termination, and what "fixpoint" means for non-contractive maps, is the
  substance handed to I-6.
- **Cross-host cycle detection** — Rule 7 only catches locally-visible cycles; a
  distributed cycle-detection protocol (or accepting the hop guard as the sole backstop)
  is undesigned. Ties to peering/announcements (`40/41`).
- **`hop` bound calibration** — the host-configured hop bound is a magic number; relating
  it to graph diameter, or making it adaptive, is open.
- **Feedback join semantics** — Rule 2 forbids joining feedback as a wave input; a use-case
  needing a consistent snapshot of *external input × current loop state* (a glitch-free
  head over both) needs the convergence-vs-simultaneity boundary spelled out.
- **Epoch/provenance extension (Candidate C)** — if loop-iteration provenance (tracing a
  delta to the external event that seeded the loop) becomes required, the `epoch`-tagged
  wave is the additive extension; its DAG join-key cost must be justified when adopted.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The mechanism reduces the four open sub-questions to one
structural move (re-origination at a declared head makes "iteration" = "wave"), and that
move reuses the *existing, validated* wave machinery rather than adding kernel primitives
(P1, P5) — it is the spec's own second candidate ("explicit cycle-breaker cells") made
precise and fused with the G-19 declaration a cycle already requires. It is
decisively consistent with G-20 (head = source) and I-2 (per-instance sourceId).
Confidence is not higher because: (1) the "≥1 head per elementary cycle" well-formedness
obligation needs a real cycle-basis algorithm and a cross-host detection story (only the
local link-time check and the runtime hop guard are concrete here); (2) whether
re-origination actually *converges* — the fixpoint-existence question — is deliberately
handed to I-6 and not proven here; (3) the `hop` guard is a pragmatic backstop whose bound
is uncalibrated. **Open questions**: does a multi-head cycle need any coordination beyond
"each head is an independent source" (I believe not — convergence, not simultaneity,
suffices); and is the disclosed P2 tension of carrying `hop` on every message acceptable,
or should `hop` be host-enabled only for regions known to contain cycles?

### I-6 — Cycle divergence guard: Magnitude declaration, quiescence thresholds, throttling granularity (G-19)

> Member pairs: N1×N10, N2×N10, N4×N10, N5×N10, N6×N10, N7×N10, N8×N10, N9×N10, N10×N14, N10×N15, N10×N16, N10×N17, N10×N18, N10×N20, N10×N21, N10×N22, N10×N24, N10×N25, N10×N26
> Existing gaps touched: G-19 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 3/19 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — All normative content: the magnitude/idempotentMerge KSP descriptor bits beside the M5.6 exclusive bit, the per-feedbackInput quiescence threshold gating re-origination on the inbound returning lap (never the outbound broadcast), link-time cycle admission (…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: `20/21 §Cycles` allows feedback loops and names
exactly one divergence guard — "magnitude-based throttling: a cycle continues only while
deltas remain significant" — but flags the entire machinery as unbuilt (`⚠ GAP G-19`;
`90/91 §Gaps — semantics` lists G-19 as the only gap with *no* phase-1 resolution). The
open sub-questions all live on one axis — *what is the data-and-declaration shape of the
throttle, where does its threshold live, at what granularity does it fire, and what does
it therefore guarantee*:

1. **Declaration/verification surface** (N1×N10) — there is no contract-level way to
   declare or verify that a delta type is throttle-capable. `20/21` *proposes* a
   `Magnitude { fun size(): Double }` interface but gives it no home; `10/12 §Contracts`
   has no descriptor bit analogous to the M5.6 KSP exclusive-ownership bit
   (`20/23 §Implementation`), and no home for a threshold declaration.
2. **Throttling granularity** (N2×N10) — the G-19 sketch has a cycle-participating cell
   "absorb instead of emitting" below threshold, but `FanOutlet` emission is *broadcast*
   to every subscriber (`10/12 §Cardinality`), so absorbing to quiesce a cycle edge would
   silence non-cycle subscribers too. Per-cell vs per-link throttling is unspecified.
3. **Link-time cycle admission** (N4×N10) — topology is mutable at runtime
   (`10/13 §Definition`), so any `connect` may close a cycle, but nothing checks at link
   time that the payload type carries `Magnitude`, and the fate of deltas circulating when
   an `unlink` severs a live loop is undefined.
4. **Exclusive-payload absorption** (N10×N14) — "absorb instead of emit" collides with
   `Owned` consume-once semantics and mandatory `Leased` release (`20/23 §The four
   contracts`); the sketch says nothing about exclusive payloads circulating a loop.
5. **The quiescence guarantee itself** (N6×N10, N8×N10, N10×N15, N10×N17, N10×N26, …) —
   `20/21 §Cycles` states outright "no guarantee cycles quiesce," yet a dozen composed
   mechanisms *presuppose* termination: host drain phase-2 flushes "after every accepted
   invocation" (`30/33 §The drain protocol`); `runToIdle` verification diverges on a
   non-quiescing loop (`50/52`, which defers virtual time "until something is
   timer-driven, e.g. G-19 throttling"); journals grow per lap (`30/33`/`20/24
   §Durability`); gossip meshes lean on merge idempotence (`40/42`); a co-hosted cycle
   recurses on the call stack (`20/21 §Fusion`).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: G-19 is a one-paragraph *proposal* whose only concrete
content is the `Magnitude` interface name and the phrase "declares a quiescence
threshold; below it, it absorbs instead of emitting." It explicitly defers fixpoint
semantics as "an open research item — flagged, not resolved." **I-5** has since resolved
the *wave/identity* half of cycles — a declared `CycleHead` absorbs feedback on a distinct
`feedbackInput` and **re-originates** a fresh wave per iteration, so "iteration = wave,"
with a link-time `CycleWithoutHead` check and a runtime `hop` guard (I-5 §4 Rules 1–8).
I-5 §8 hands the *magnitude/quiescence* half — "convergence-rate / fixpoint existence" —
explicitly to I-6. This challenge is that half: the throttle's declaration surface,
granularity, exclusive-payload handling, and the termination guarantee dependent
features may assume. It builds on I-5's head/feedback structure and does **not**
re-litigate it.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P5 (correctness by construction) vs an unverifiable runtime marker.** The obvious
  reading — "cycle cells check `delta.size()` at runtime" — is pure runtime discipline: a
  cycle can be built whose delta type has no `Magnitude` at all, and nothing catches it
  until the loop diverges in production. P5 demands the throttle-capability be a
  *compile-time, metadata-read* fact, like the M5.6 exclusive bit — but G-19 gives it no
  such surface.
- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path) vs per-message granularity.** A per-subscriber emission
  gate on `FanOutlet` (so a cycle edge is throttled but a fan-out sibling is not) would put
  a branch on the broadcast hot path and break the uniform enqueue P2 budgets. Yet a
  per-cell "absorb everything below threshold" gate silences non-cycle subscribers
  (N2×N10). Neither obvious granularity is both cheap and correct.
- **"No guarantee cycles quiesce" (20/21) vs a dozen features that need one.** Drain,
  `runToIdle`, journaling, and mobility replay are all written against DAGs that reach
  idle; each *presupposes* termination that G-19 disclaims. The resolution must state an
  *honest* guarantee — strong enough for these features, not overclaimed — and P4 forbids
  buying it with a global barrier / superstep coordinator (also rejected by the SID-UP
  decision and I-5 §2).
- **`Owned`/`Leased` consume-once vs "absorb / drop" (P5, 20/23).** The throttle's core
  move is *dropping* a sub-threshold delta. For a `Leased` payload that means a lease
  silently un-released (a pool leak); for `Owned`, "drop" and "consume" must be reconciled.
- **P6/P10 (interest / niche-first) vs "just in case."** Most graphs are acyclic; the
  divergence guard must cost nothing on non-cycle edges and must not grow a general
  fixpoint-solver "just in case." The niche needs a *bounded, declared* guard on the rare
  loop, not a numeric-analysis engine everywhere.
- **Two genuinely different quiescence physics.** Set-family / `PnCounter` cycles quiesce
  *structurally* — effective-only emission over idempotent merge means a re-circulated
  delta carrying no new tags is *empty* and is never emitted (`20/21 rule 2`, `20/24 rule
  3`). Numeric feedback (a `CounterDelta`, a control loop) has no such property; it needs a
  real threshold and may never contract. One declaration surface must serve both without
  pretending they carry the same guarantee.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Runtime `Magnitude` marker, per-cell outlet throttle (the literal G-19 sketch)

Every cycle-participating cell checks `delta.size()` against a per-cell threshold at its
*outlet*; below threshold it absorbs instead of emitting. `Magnitude` is a plain interface
checked by `is Magnitude` at runtime.

- *Semantics*: any cell on a loop damps its own emissions.
- *Fast-path cost*: an `is`-check and a compare on an emission path; per-cell threshold
  state.
- *Failure modes*: **silences fan-out** — an outlet feeding both the loop and non-cycle
  subscribers cannot absorb for the loop without dropping the broadcast (N2×N10);
  **unverifiable** — a cycle over a non-`Magnitude` delta compiles and diverges (violates
  P5); **per-cell granularity is wrong** — the throttle belongs to the *loop edge*, not to
  every cell that happens to sit on one; conflicts with I-5, which localizes the
  absorb/re-originate decision to the declared head, not every cell.
- *Tradeoff*: cheapest to describe, but breaks P5 and N2×N10. **Rejected**; its
  `Magnitude` interface survives, relocated.

##### Candidate B — Magnitude descriptor bit + inbound feedback-edge throttle + two-tier quiescence (recommended)

`Magnitude` is detected by the **same KSP scan** that emits the exclusive bit and recorded
as a `magnitude` bit on the generated `MethodDescriptor`; the throttle threshold lives on
the **`feedbackInput`** (per-edge, refining I-5); the absorb/re-originate decision is made
on the *inbound* returning-feedback delta at the head, **never** on any outbound
broadcast; and quiescence is a **two-tier** guarantee — *structural* for idempotent-merge
(`Replicable`) cycles, *best-effort threshold + hard hop-guard backstop* for numeric ones.

- *Semantics*: throttle-capability is compile-time metadata; the throttle is a per-loop-
  edge inbound gate; termination is guaranteed (quiescence or hop-guard), convergence-to-
  fixpoint is guaranteed only for the idempotent/contracting tier.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero on non-cycle edges and on all fan-out broadcast; the head pays one
  `size()` compare per returning lap — exactly where I-5 already puts a compare and a
  counter bump.
- *Failure modes*: none of the member-pair tensions survive (§4); residual is
  convergence-rate proof for non-contracting numeric loops (handed to the hop-guard as a
  hard bound; §8).
- *Tradeoff*: reuses the M5.6 KSP machinery and I-5's head/feedback structure wholesale;
  gives up a *universal* fixpoint guarantee (impossible without contractivity) in exchange
  for an *honest, tiered* one that every dependent feature can rely on. **Recommended.**

##### Candidate C — Magnitude + a fused `FixpointCell` operator (run-to-convergence inside one cell)

A loop is collapsed into a single `FixpointCell` that iterates the loop body internally
until `size() < threshold`, emitting only the converged result.

- *Semantics*: the cycle is an implementation detail *inside* one cell; the graph sees a
  DAG.
- *Fast-path cost*: the internal iteration is a tight local loop (cheap when co-hosted).
- *Failure modes*: **destroys explicit topology** (P3) — the loop is no longer inspectable
  links; **cannot distribute** the loop across hosts (the body must be co-hosted and
  fused); collides with I-5's whole "iteration = wave" model and with `20/21`'s allowance
  of *distributed* feedback loops (UI↔model across a wire bridge).
- *Tradeoff*: a legitimate *optimization* for a small, fully-co-hosted, numeric loop, but
  wrong as the general mechanism. **Folded into §8** as an opt-in fusion for co-hosted
  numeric loops, not the base model.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. The single unifying move: **make throttle-capability a declared,
KSP-verified property of the delta contract, put the threshold on the feedback edge, and
gate the head's re-origination on the *inbound* returning lap — so the FanOutlet broadcast
is never touched and quiescence is a two-tier guarantee (structural for idempotent merges,
threshold+hop-guard for numeric).** Everything reuses I-5's head/feedback structure and
M5.6's KSP exclusive-bit machinery.

##### 4.1 Data shapes

```kotlin
// The throttle interface (I-5 named it; I-6 fixes its contract).
interface Magnitude {
    fun size(): Double        // MUST be ≥ 0; size() == 0.0  ⇔  "no effective change"
}                             // (aligns with effective-only emission, 20/21 rule 2)

// KSP-emitted metadata, read at link time — NEVER reflection (mirrors the M5.6 exclusive bit).
class MethodDescriptor(
    /* … existing … */
    val exclusive: Boolean,        // Owned/Leased present in a param type      (M5.6, 20/23)
    val magnitude: Boolean,        // a delta param type implements Magnitude    ← NEW (I-6)
    val idempotentMerge: Boolean,  // the delta type is Replicable (tag-union / pointwise-max, 40/42)
)

// The threshold lives on the feedback inlet (per-edge), refining I-5's per-head `quiescence`.
val feedback by feedbackInput<Propagate<D>>(quiescence = 0.0)
//   quiescence default 0.0  →  re-originate iff a returning lap has size() > 0
//                              (the idempotent / "strong" tier: quiesce exactly on an empty lap)
//   numeric loops set quiescence > 0  →  stop when returning laps get small (the "weak" tier)
```

`quiescence` on the inlet (not the head) is the one refinement of I-5: a head may close
several cycles through several feedback inlets, each with its own convergence character; a
per-inlet threshold is strictly more general, and I-5's single per-head `quiescence` is the
one-feedback-inlet special case.

##### 4.2 Rules the model introduces (normative)

**Rule 1 — Magnitude is a KSP-verified descriptor bit (declaration/verification surface).**
The M5.6 contract processor already recursively scans a contract method's parameter types
for `Owned`/`Leased` to emit the `exclusive` bit. Extend the *same* scan to detect whether
a delta parameter type implements `Magnitude` (emit `magnitude`) and whether it is
`Replicable` with an idempotent tag-union / pointwise-max merge (emit `idempotentMerge`).
Enforcement reads generated metadata, never reflection (P5, P9). This gives N1×N10 its
missing surface: "is this contract throttle-capable?" is a compile-time boolean on the
`MethodDescriptor`, exactly analogous to the exclusive bit. *(Resolves N1×N10.)*

**Rule 2 — Two-tier quiescence.** A cycle edge's delta type falls in one of two tiers, and
each tier carries a *different, honestly-stated* guarantee:

- **Strong (structural) tier — `idempotentMerge` deltas** (`SetDelta` tag-union,
  `PnCounterDelta` pointwise-max, and derived operators over them, `20/24`). These quiesce
  **by construction, threshold-free**: effective-only emission (`20/21 rule 2`) means a
  re-circulated delta carrying no *new* tag information derives an **empty** delta, which is
  never emitted, so the loop stops. Laps are bounded by the number of distinct tags a
  single external event introduces. A strong-tier feedback inlet keeps `quiescence = 0.0`;
  the guard essentially never fires because the loop is already empty when it converges.
  *This is the rigorous form of the N10×N15 observation ("set-family cycles quiesce
  naturally") and the mechanism gossip meshes already rely on (N10×N24).*
- **Weak (best-effort) tier — `magnitude` but not `idempotentMerge`** (`CounterDelta`,
  numeric control feedback, `MapDelta`). These carry **no structural termination**; the
  `quiescence` threshold is a divergence *damper* (below it, stop re-originating), not a
  proof. Termination for this tier is guaranteed **only** by the I-5 **hop guard** (Rule 6
  below) — a hard, always-firing backstop.

**Rule 3 — Throttle on the inbound feedback edge, gating re-origination (granularity).**
The absorb/re-originate decision is made **at the head's `feedbackInput` on the returning
lap**, never at any outbound `FanOutlet`. On a returning delta `d`:

```
head.feedbackInput.onDelta(d):
    fold d into loop state
    if d.size() > this.quiescence:  re-originate  (mint fresh wave, emit derived delta — I-5 Rule 1)
    else:                           absorb only    (loop stops here; no re-origination)
```

Because the gate is on an *inbound* edge, the head's ordinary outlet broadcast is **never
gated**: every effective derived delta reaches all subscribers (loop and non-loop) through
the normal uniform enqueue. A sub-threshold lap simply does not *spin the loop again* — and
there is no new information that lap to withhold from external subscribers anyway (they
already received the last significant delta). **No cell ever "absorbs on its outlet," so no
fan-out subscriber is ever silenced by cycle throttling.** This dissolves N2×N10 — the
granularity is *per-feedback-edge, inbound*, and I-5 Rule 3's "absorb without emitting" is
refined to "absorb without **re-originating**." *(Resolves N2×N10; refines the "feedback
join semantics" I-5 §8 left open.)*

**Rule 4 — Link-time cycle admission (extends I-5 Rule 7).** When a `connect` closes a
cycle wholly visible to one host (P3), the host walks the new cycle and, in addition to
I-5's `CycleWithoutHead` check, verifies every data edge on the cycle:

- every edge's contract carries `magnitude || idempotentMerge` — else `Rejected` with
  `CycleRequiresMagnitude`;
- no edge's contract carries `Leased` (i.e. `exclusive` with a `Leased` param) — else
  `Rejected` with `CycleRejectsLeased` (Rule 5);
- an `Owned`-carrying edge is unary (`OneToOnePort` / exclusive `FanOutlet`, already
  enforced by M5.6) — which means an `Owned` loop edge has *no* fan-out siblings, so N2×N10
  cannot even arise for it.

This is a rare-path graph walk (P2 permits expensive linking) over inspectable topology
(P3), correct-by-construction (P5). Cross-host cycles no host can see fall back to the
runtime hop guard (Rule 6), exactly as in I-5. *(Resolves N4×N10.)*

**Rule 5 — Exclusive payloads on cycle edges.** *(Resolves N10×N14.)*
- **`Leased` is forbidden** on any cycle edge (Rule 4). A lease circulating a loop has
  ambiguous release responsibility, and the throttle's core move (drop a sub-threshold lap)
  would silently leak the lease. This is consistent with the existing posture that `Leased`
  is pool-scoped and "MUST NOT cross machine boundaries" (`20/23`); to feed mutable-buffer
  state around a loop, `freeze()` first — `Frozen` fans out safely and needs no release.
- **`Owned` is permitted** and its consume-once semantics are *satisfied, not violated*, by
  absorption: "absorb" = `Owned.take()` into loop state (consumed exactly once);
  "re-originate" = `take()` + derive a fresh `Owned`/`Frozen` delta for the next lap. The
  `size()` read is a `Borrowed`-style read that does not consume. An `Owned` loop edge is
  unary (Rule 4), so the head needs a *separate* non-exclusive outlet (`Frozen` or plain)
  for any external subscribers — the same structure the SPSC rule already imposes.

**Rule 6 — `CycleHead` is a fusion barrier; the hop guard is the hard termination bound.**
*(Resolves N5×N10.)* Within a host, a chain fuses into nested direct calls (`20/21
§Fusion`), so a fully co-hosted cycle would recurse on the call stack. Therefore a
**`CycleHead`'s re-origination MUST break the call stack**: the head *enqueues* its
re-originated wave on the host queue rather than direct-calling downstream, even
co-hosted. Re-origination is a fresh wave (like a source event), so entering via the queue
is natural. This bounds stack depth to O(1) per lap and serializes laps through the queue.
Combined with I-5's `hop` guard (a lap that exceeds a host-configured bound dead-letters as
`CycleError`), **every cycle terminates in bounded laps** — by quiescence if contracting
(Rule 2), by the hop guard always. A co-hosted cycle round-trips the queue once per lap and
cannot blow the stack.

**Rule 7 — The quiescence guarantee contract (what dependent features may assume).** From
Rules 2 + 6, the single guarantee downstream features get is:

> **Bounded-lap termination is guaranteed for every admitted cycle** (quiescence for the
> contracting/idempotent tier; the hop-guard dead-letter as a hard backstop for the weak
> tier). **Convergence to a *meaningful* fixpoint is guaranteed only for the strong tier**;
> the weak tier converges only if its loop map is contractive w.r.t. `size()`, which the
> framework does not verify.

Applied:
- **Host drain (N6×N10, N10×N20)** — phase-2 completion (priority 30, "after every accepted
  invocation," `30/33`) terminates because an intra-host cycle emits *finitely many* laps
  after intake closure (bounded by quiescence or the hop guard). Intra-host re-emissions
  *are* accepted-after-closure work, but a bounded amount; the drain flush drains it and
  quiesces. Parked cross-host feedback replayed on resume/migrate re-enters at the head's
  feedbackInput and is re-thresholded like any lap — a captured snapshot plus replayed
  feedback re-converges (strong tier) or is hop-bounded (weak tier); it does not re-ignite
  unboundedly.
- **`runToIdle` / verification (N10×N26)** — idle (no pending invocations) is *reachable*
  because laps are bounded; the harness does not diverge. Quiescence is **lap-based, not
  time-based**, so `runToIdle` needs **no virtual time** — the `50/52` deferral ("add
  virtual time when something is timer-driven, e.g. G-19 throttling") is *not* triggered by
  this design; the throttle is a magnitude compare, not a timer.
- **Journals (N10×N17)** — a journal records bounded laps per external event → bounded
  growth. Replay re-drives the deterministic head-minted counter sequence and re-quiesces
  at the *same* fixpoint for the strong tier (idempotent merge is replay-stable); the weak
  tier re-quiesces identically under the same seed because re-origination is deterministic.
- **Gossip meshes (N10×N24)** — replica gossip cycles are the **strong tier**: echoes
  terminate on effective-only emission over idempotent merge (`40/42`; I-3). Magnitude
  throttling and merge-idempotence are therefore **not two competing guards** — gossip
  quiescence is the *structural* special case of Rule 2's strong tier. Gossip cells need
  **no** explicit `quiescence` threshold (default 0.0). *(Resolves N10×N24.)*
- **Wire laps (N10×N22)** — bounded laps ⇒ bounded serialization cost and bounded parking.
  A sender parking on disconnect stalls the loop (park/replay resumes it at the same
  feedbackInput); a corrupt-frame dead-letter simply drops a lap — which for a loop means
  "do not spin again," a *safe* failure (the loop stops rather than diverges). The hop guard
  is the same backstop across the wire as in-host.
- **Host-rate defense (N10×N18)** — magnitude throttling bounds *one external event's*
  laps, **not** the aggregate arrival rate. A high-frequency external driver of a cycle is
  an ordinary load problem handled by the host's priority bands / subtree quotas
  (`30/31`, G-28) and attention band-gating (I-4), *not* by this guard. This resolution
  explicitly delegates rate/fairness to the scheduling layer and does not duplicate it.

**Rule 8 — Unlink fate & late-join into cycles.** *(Resolves the N4×N10 residual, N9×N10.)*
When an `unlink` severs a live loop edge, in-flight loop deltas on that edge follow ordinary
unlink semantics (`30/33`): they are parked/dropped with the link. The severed cell rests at
its last-emitted state, which is safe — external subscribers already received the last
effective delta, and the loop simply stops. No cycle-specific "in-flight fate" is needed. A
late joiner linking *into* a cycle receives ordinary catch-up (state-as-delta-from-empty,
`20/21`); if the join lands on a loop edge, the catch-up delta arrives at a feedbackInput
and is thresholded like any lap — for the strong tier it carries existing tags, so the
returning lap is empty (size 0) and absorbed; for the weak tier it is one hop-bounded lap.
Catch-up is unwaved, but if it triggers re-origination the head mints a proper fresh wave
(I-5), so the joiner is glitch-free from its first real iteration.

##### 4.3 Net effect

One declared property (the `magnitude`/`idempotentMerge` KSP bits), one threshold home (the
`feedbackInput`), one gate (inbound returning-lap `size()` compare that governs
re-origination, never fan-out), one exclusive-payload rule (`Owned` absorbs = consumes,
`Leased` refused at link time), one stack bound (`CycleHead` = fusion barrier), and one
honest guarantee (bounded-lap termination always; fixpoint convergence for the strong
tier). The data hot path and every fan-out broadcast are untouched (P2); throttle-capability
is correct-by-construction (P5); and the mergeable gossip mesh's structural quiescence is
recognized as the strong-tier special case rather than a second mechanism.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — the throttle is a `size()` compare in a cell's feedbackInput handler; the fusion-barrier enqueue is ordinary host-queue behavior; every rule meaningful single-threaded (the compare and the counter bump run in `SimulationController`). No coordinator, no barrier. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — non-cycle edges and *all* fan-out broadcast are untouched; only the head pays one `size()` compare per returning lap (rare, at one declared point). The fusion barrier costs one enqueue per lap — a bounded, rare-op cost, not a steady-state tax. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — cycles stay explicit link paths (Candidate C's cell-internal loop rejected precisely for hiding them); the link-time admission check walks inspectable topology. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — the throttle decision is strictly local to one head/feedbackInput; no global clock/lock/barrier; convergence across sources is per-source waves (G-20), not simultaneity. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — throttle-capability is a KSP descriptor bit; the two tiers are typed (`idempotentMerge`); `Leased`-on-cycle and non-`Magnitude`-on-cycle are rejected at link time; `Owned` absorption is `take()`-into-state. Not runtime discipline. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — throttle machinery exists only on declared cycle edges; the threshold declaration is one a cycle already needs; nothing on acyclic edges. |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — a cycle crossing a membrane keeps its head as quiescence owner; the membrane is a boundary control, not a quiescence authority (defer membrane-specific policy to G-10). |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — a link that closes a cycle is admitted (or rejected) at link time; an unlink that severs one is ordinary; nothing assumes a static loop. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `Magnitude`/`idempotentMerge` are descriptor bits (ids-only metadata); `size()` is ordinary code, never on the wire; deltas cross as the existing serializable forms. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — a bounded, declared per-loop guard with an honest tiered guarantee, deliberately *not* a general fixpoint solver; the strong tier is exactly the decentralized incremental-dataflow case the niche centers on. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: the head re-originates a fresh per-source wave per
  lap (I-5); the throttle only decides *whether* to re-originate. No wave coordinator.
- **SID-UP global propagation locks REJECTED** — Consistent: no superstep/BSP/barrier; the
  guard is a local per-edge compare (Candidate C's global-ish fusion also rejected).
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: a migrated head keeps its instance
  sourceId (I-2); parked feedback replays into the same feedbackInput and is re-thresholded.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive** — Consistent: cycle laps park/replay like any
  invocation; no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local\|Remote; one park/replay** — Consistent: cross-host laps re-resolve
  through the registry; the hop-guard dead-letter reuses the existing `deadLetterOutlet`,
  not a new park path.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: late-join into a cycle uses state-as-delta
  catch-up; no snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps minted cell-locally, NOT wave ids** — Consistent, reinforced:
  the strong tier's structural quiescence *is* the tag algebra (idempotent union) doing its
  job; tags and waves stay separate.
- **Data push-only; management null context** — Consistent: cycle edges are data (push
  `Propagate<D>`); the throttle is the head's own cell logic, not a management call.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** —
  Consistent, load-bearing: gossip quiescence is the *strong tier*, not a competing guard
  (Rule 7); no second protocol.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Consistent: a loop through
  a key-routing proxy has per-partition heads/thresholds; each partition is an ordinary cell
  (N10×N16), placement is ordinary placement.
- **Wire ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: `magnitude`/`idempotentMerge` are
  generated metadata bits like the exclusive bit; nothing new on the wire but the deltas
  that already cross.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent: per-link FIFO of laps
  is unchanged; the head absorbs feedback in arrival order; Rule 7 shows drain terminates.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time** — Consistent, reinforced: the cycle-admission check
  (Rule 4) is a link-time check; `Owned` loop edges stay unary; `Leased` refused at link
  time.
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross machines** — Consistent,
  strengthened: `Leased` is refused on cycle edges outright (Rule 5); `Owned` absorption is
  consume-once-honoring.
- **CellRef(id, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2)** — Consistent: the head throttles
  per instance; a loop rerouting through a new instance is a topology change (I-5 Rule 6).
- **I-5 (wave-reentry-in-cycles)** — **Built upon, one refinement flagged.** I-6 adopts I-5's
  `CycleHead`/`feedbackInput`/re-origination/`hop` guard/`CycleWithoutHead` check wholesale.
  The one refinement: I-5 placed `quiescence` on the `CycleHead` (per-head); I-6 relocates it
  to the `feedbackInput` (per-edge) to answer the granularity question I-5 explicitly left
  open ("feedback join semantics"). I-5's per-head threshold is the one-feedback-inlet
  special case, so this is a *compatible generalization*, **not a CONFLICT**.
- **I-1 (metadata plane), I-4 (attention algebra)** — Consistent: attention oscillation in
  cyclic topologies is damped by I-4's band-gating (magnitude throttling applied to
  attention), on the I-1 metadata plane — a *separate* application of the same "band change
  is the increment" idea, needing no `CycleHead` (attention is not a data cycle). (N10×N21.)
- **I-2 / I-3 (identity, replication skeleton)** — Consistent and depended-upon: gossip
  cycles are the strong tier over full-ref replica meshes.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — No resolved item reopened.
  G-19 (the only phase-1-unresolved gap) is closed here with a concrete tiered design;
  I-5 closed its wave half.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/21 §Cycles (G-19)** — Replace the "magnitude/throttling unspecified … fixpoint
  semantics open" paragraph with: the `Magnitude` contract (`size() ≥ 0`, `0 ⇔ no change`),
  the two-tier quiescence model (strong idempotent / weak numeric), the inbound
  feedback-edge throttle gating re-origination, and the bounded-lap termination guarantee
  (quiescence or hop guard). State plainly that fixpoint convergence is guaranteed only for
  the strong tier.
- **10/12 §Cardinality / §Contracts** — Note the `magnitude` and `idempotentMerge`
  descriptor bits emitted by the KSP scan (beside the M5.6 exclusive bit); note the FanOutlet
  broadcast is never throttled.
- **20/23 §The SPSC link rule** — Add: `Leased` refused on cycle edges (`CycleRejectsLeased`);
  `Owned` absorption on a cycle head = `take()`-into-state (consume-once honored); `Owned`
  loop edges are unary and need a separate non-exclusive outlet for external subscribers.
- **10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based)** — Add the link-time cycle-admission check extending
  I-5's `CycleWithoutHead`: every cycle edge `magnitude || idempotentMerge`, no `Leased`,
  `Owned` unary; `CycleRequiresMagnitude` / `CycleRejectsLeased` `LinkResult`s.
- **20/24 §Established pattern** — State that idempotent-merge (`Replicable`) cycles quiesce
  structurally (effective-only + tag idempotence) and are the strong tier; no explicit
  threshold needed.
- **30/33 §The drain protocol** — Note that bounded-lap termination makes phase-2 flush
  terminate on a host containing a cycle; replayed feedback re-thresholds at the head.
- **30/31 §host / §Fusion (20/21)** — State the `CycleHead` fusion barrier (re-origination
  enqueues, bounding co-hosted stack depth) and that the hop guard dead-letters as
  `CycleError`; note magnitude throttling is per-event, not rate-limiting (bands/quotas own
  rate).
- **50/52 §Invariant testing** — Note `runToIdle` terminates on admitted cycles without
  virtual time (throttle is lap-based, not timer-based); add a generative cyclic-graph
  harness (strong-tier convergence + weak-tier hop-guard termination + a divergence control).
- **40/42 §Design as implemented** — Cross-reference that gossip quiescence is the strong
  tier of the G-19 model, not a separate guard.
- **90/91 G-19** — Update from "unspecified" to resolved: `Magnitude` descriptor bit +
  two-tier quiescence + inbound feedback-edge throttle; residual = weak-tier convergence-rate
  and cross-host cycle detection (§8).

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Weak-tier convergence-rate / fixpoint existence.** The framework guarantees *termination*
  (hop guard) but not *convergence* for non-idempotent numeric loops; a contractivity marker
  or a static/dynamic check that a loop map is `size()`-contracting (so quiescence, not the
  hop guard, terminates it) is undesigned — this is the residual of the "fixpoint semantics
  open" research item.
- **`size()` well-formedness.** The `Magnitude` contract requires `size() ≥ 0` and `0 ⇔ no
  effective change`; enforcing/asserting the "0 ⇔ empty" coupling with effective-only
  emission (a lint or a generative property test) is unspecified.
- **Cross-host cycle detection.** Rule 4 catches only locally-visible cycles; a distributed
  cycle whose magnitude/idempotence admission cannot be checked at link time relies wholly on
  the hop guard. A distributed cycle-detection protocol (ties to peering/announcements,
  `40/41`, and I-5's same gap) is undesigned.
- **`hop`-bound calibration for the weak tier.** The hop guard is the weak tier's only hard
  bound; relating the bound to loop diameter, or making it adaptive to observed
  contraction, is open (shared with I-5 §8).
- **Fused `FixpointCell` (Candidate C) as an opt-in optimization.** For a small,
  fully-co-hosted, numeric loop, collapsing it into one run-to-convergence cell avoids
  per-lap queue hops; when and how to lower a declared co-hosted cycle into a fused fixpoint
  operator (without losing distributability) is a future optimization.
- **Multi-tier cycles.** A cycle mixing an idempotent edge and a numeric edge takes the weak
  tier overall (the numeric edge governs); whether such mixes should be discouraged, or
  whether the idempotent segment can be proven to bound the numeric one, is open.
- **Membrane-crossing cycle quiescence ownership** (N7×N10) — the head owns quiescence, but a
  membrane claiming stronger consistency inside than across may want to *scope* a cycle's
  laps to the membrane; the interaction with G-10 membrane form is unevaluated.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The mechanism is strongly grounded: it reuses the *shipped*
M5.6 KSP exclusive-bit scan (adding two sibling bits), the *adopted* I-5 head/feedback
structure (adding only a per-edge threshold home and the inbound-gate refinement), and the
*shipped* effective-only + tag-idempotence machinery (recognized as the strong tier). The
load-bearing insight — **throttle the inbound returning lap, not the outbound broadcast** —
turns the headline granularity tension (N2×N10) into a non-problem and requires no fan-out
hot-path change. The honest two-tier guarantee (structural quiescence for idempotent merges;
termination-by-hop-guard, not convergence, for numeric loops) is defensible and gives every
dependent feature (drain, `runToIdle`, journals, gossip) a rule it can rely on without
overclaiming. Confidence is not higher because: (1) the weak tier's *convergence* (as opposed
to mere termination) is genuinely unsolved and handed to a follow-on — a numeric control loop
that oscillates just above threshold is terminated only by the hop-guard dead-letter, which
is a blunt instrument; (2) cross-host cycle admission cannot be link-time-checked and leans
entirely on the hop guard; (3) the `CycleHead`-as-fusion-barrier rule, while necessary to
bound co-hosted stack depth, trades one queue hop per lap against P2's fusion ideal — an
acceptable but real cost. **Open questions**: is a contractivity marker worth adding to lift
the weak tier toward a real convergence guarantee, or is the hop-guard backstop sufficient in
the niche; and should a mixed idempotent/numeric cycle be rejected at link time rather than
silently taking the weak tier.

### I-7 — Invocation journal: what is journaled, what replay means downstream, and where the journal lives (G-25)

> Member pairs: N1×N17, N2×N17, N3×N17, N5×N17, N7×N17, N8×N17, N9×N17, N12×N17, N13×N17, N14×N17, N16×N17, N17×N18, N17×N22, N17×N23, N17×N24, N17×N25, N17×N26
> Existing gaps touched: G-25, G-26, G-32 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 12/17 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — Topology journaling and the GraphSpec preserve-refs replay mode (recovery currently depends on out-of-band graph rebuild); output-side journaling for spontaneously-emitting sources; the Effectful processed-frontier so effectful sinks do not re-act on replay…
> ⚠ Divergence with landed code: R4, the resolution's linchpin — replay with outlets NoOp-served (G-32 suppression) so recovery never re-transmits — is contradicted by the landed M10 design: recoverFrom replays frames through the ordinary decode path with UN-suppressed emission (the recove…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question.** `20/24 §Durability spectrum` proposes the entire
durability story in three sentences: *"durability as a host concern (30/31): a durable
host journals applied invocations (they are serializable — P9 pays off) alongside those
snapshots. Replay = recovery. Cells stay oblivious."* That leaves three things
undefined, and this challenge must fix all three under **one** mechanism:

1. **Event classification — what is journaled.** "Applied invocations" is ambiguous
   across every dispatch shape:
   - Tier-1 fused and delegated intra-host chains materialize *no* `Invocation` object —
     they are "zero-cost direct method calls" (`10/14 §Dispatch tiers`), so a fused
     `A→B→C` has nothing to journal at B or C (N5×N17).
   - Management-contract invocations may return values and block (`spawn(): CellRef`,
     `10/12 §Contracts are push-only`, `30/31 Normative rule 4`); replaying a blocking
     spawn is nothing like replaying a push-only delta (N1×N17).
   - Multiplexed generic-protocol traffic (attention, state-request, link-management)
     rides links beside data (`10/12 §Multiplexed ports`, G-13); replaying it re-executes
     topology/scheduling actions (N3×N17).
   - Null-context link/unlink events are stamped into the same logical-time domain as
     data waves (`20/22 §Topology versioning`); their journal ordering against data is
     unstated (N13×N17).

2. **Replay/dedup contract — what replay means downstream.** "Replay = recovery, cells
   oblivious" re-drives transitions that already produced downstream emissions:
   - a `FanOutlet` re-broadcasts to subscribers that already saw the delta (N2×N17);
   - `CounterDelta` merge-is-addition double-counts (`20/24 Established pattern`), while
     tag-set merges are idempotent (N8×N17);
   - `Owned`/`Leased` exactly-once (`20/23 §SPSC`) collides with re-delivery (N14×N17);
   - remote consumers get duplicate wire delivery (`40/41 §Failure semantics`, N17×N22);
   - restored links re-fire `onLinked` catch-up, interleaving with replayed emissions
     (`20/21 §Pull`, N9×N17);
   - effectful sinks re-act on the world, and the only suppression named — G-32 shadow
     NoOp-serving (`50/52 §Live invariants`) — is unconnected to recovery (N26×N17);
   - glitch-free per-wave version buffers are cell state whose reconstruction under replay
     is unspecified (`20/22 §Local glitch-freedom`, N12×N17).

3. **Locus.** Membranes define "tracing and replay at crossings" (`10/11 §Membranes`)
   while G-25 puts the journal in the host with "replay = recovery"; which one governs
   organelle-internal traffic under the host hierarchy (G-28) is unreconciled (N7×N17).

And it must **compose** with the host's two existing replay regimes — RESTART's
spawn-time checkpoint and SUSPEND's parked-traffic replay (`30/31 Normative rule 5`),
three regimes on one queue with no stated precedence (N17×N18) — with GraphSpec replay,
which deliberately mints *fresh* refs (`50/51`, N17×N25), with replication anti-entropy
(`40/42`, N17×N24), with partitioned composites (`20/24`, N16×N17), and with the split
identity `CellRef(id, instanceId)` (I-2, N17×N23).

Why the spec leaves it open: G-25 is a *proposal sketch*; the state-capture half exists
(`Stateful.snapshot()/restore()`, M3.3) but the journal half was never designed. Every
surface it touches was written before durability existed.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 vs journaling every message.** Steady-state flow is "a volatile read and an
  enqueue" (`00/02 P2`). Journaling every accepted invocation adds a serialize+append per
  message — genuinely on the hot path *if* durability were global.
- **Exactly-once (P5, `20/23`) vs "replay = recovery."** The naive reading — re-run
  journaled invocations and let emissions flow — violates the SPSC/`Owned` consume-once
  guarantee and double-counts non-idempotent deltas. The member-pair cluster (N2, N8,
  N14, N22, N26) is one recurring symptom of this single collision.
- **P4 (no global barrier) vs a consistent recovery point.** Classic durable systems take
  a coordinated snapshot (a consistent cut). `00/02 P4` forbids a global barrier, and G-20
  gives "convergence, not simultaneity, across sources." Recovery must be *per-cell/
  per-host local* and reconcile by convergence — not a distributed snapshot.
- **"Snapshot IS a delta" + "no second sync protocol" (recorded decisions) vs a bespoke
  recovery path.** Anti-entropy already recovers a partitioned replica by snapshot + delta
  replay = the *late-join catch-up path* (`40/42 §Anti-entropy`: "the late-join path (21)
  doubles as recovery"). Durability must not invent a *second* recovery protocol.
- **Determinism of replay vs sources and effects.** Command-replay reconstructs state only
  for deterministic transitions. Spontaneously-emitting source cells (external input) and
  `Effectful` sinks (external world) are not inbound-deterministic.
- **Three replay regimes on one queue.** RESTART, SUSPEND, and journal-recovery all "replay
  into a cell" but mean different things; without an ordering they conflict.
