#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Command journal, replay re-emits (the naive G-25 reading)

Journal every accepted invocation; on recovery re-run them and let outlets emit normally.

- *Semantics*: cells re-drive their transitions; downstream sees the emissions again.
- *Fast-path cost*: serialize+append per accepted invocation on a durable host.
- *Failure modes*: **the entire member-pair cluster.** Re-broadcast to live `FanOutlet`
  subscribers (N2), double-counted `CounterDelta` (N8), re-delivered `Owned` violating
  consume-once (N14), duplicate wire delivery (N22), re-fired effectful sinks (N26). It
  turns recovery into an uncontrolled replay of history against a live world.
- *Tradeoff*: matches the literal "applied invocations / replay = recovery" wording and is
  general, but is semantically wrong wherever an emission is non-idempotent or effectful.
  **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — Pure state-delta journal (output-side; anti-entropy everywhere)

Journal periodic `Stateful` snapshots + the cell's own *emitted* effective deltas.
Recovery applies deltas directly to rebuild state; cell logic never re-runs.

- *Semantics*: recovery = "replay my own output into my own state," exactly the
  late-join/anti-entropy shape (`40/42`).
- *Fast-path cost*: append emitted deltas (already effective-only, small).
- *Failure modes*: does **not** capture *accepted-but-not-yet-applied* inbound (the host
  queue contents at crash) unless every upstream producer is itself durable; and it
  presumes a cell's recoverable state is fully reconstructible from its own emitted delta
  stream — true for the data-cell vocabulary, awkward for cells with hidden internal state
  not mirrored in output.
- *Tradeoff*: elegant, reuses catch-up, no re-emission problem — but incomplete for
  in-flight inbound and for cells whose output underdetermines their state. Good as the
  *source/effect* case, not as the whole answer.

##### Candidate C — Input-side WAL + snapshots, replay with **suppressed emission**, rejoin via catch-up (recommended)

The durable host write-ahead-logs accepted `PORT_API` invocations and topology events in
host-sequence order, plus periodic per-cell `Stateful` snapshots. Recovery replays the log
**with outlets NoOp-served** (G-32 suppression) so state is reconstructed but nothing is
re-transmitted; the cell then rejoins live and downstream reconciles by ordinary idempotent
catch-up. Sources and `Effectful` sinks journal output-side (Candidate B) since they are
not inbound-deterministic.

- *Semantics*: recovery is **state reconstruction, not re-transmission**. Suppression is
  the linchpin that dissolves the whole downstream cluster; catch-up is the single
  reconciliation path.
- *Fast-path cost*: append per accepted invocation *only on a durable host* (opt-in, P6);
  log append can be batched/async so the critical path pays an enqueue-to-log, not an
  fsync.
- *Failure modes*: requires deterministic transitions for input-mode cells (sources/effects
  fall back to output-mode); log compaction and non-deterministic cell logic become
  follow-on gaps.
- *Tradeoff*: combines B's "no re-emission, reuse catch-up" with A's "captures accepted
  inbound, works for any deterministic cell," using already-shipped machinery (Stateful
  snapshot/restore, G-32 NoOp-serve, catch-up, GraphSpec replay, host-sequence ordering).
  **Recommended.**

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**. Durability is a per-host opt-in; a durable host keeps one
host-sequence-ordered write-ahead log plus per-cell snapshots; recovery replays that log
with emission suppressed and reconciles downstream by the existing catch-up path. Every
member pair falls out of one rule set.

##### Data shapes

```
// One ordered log per durable host, ordered by the existing monotonic HostSeq (C-8, 30/31)
sealed interface JournalEntry { val seq: HostSeq }
  Accepted(seq, target: CellRef, portName, invocation: Invocation)   // PORT_API only
  Topology(seq, event: TopoEvent)                                    // spawn/despawn/connect/unlink/supervise
  SnapshotMark(seq, ref: CellRef, snapshotId)                        // "a snapshot for ref was cut at this seq"

Snapshot(ref: CellRef, seq: HostSeq, state: Delta)   // state-as-delta-from-empty = Stateful.snapshot()

// TopoEvent carries the CONCRETE full ref + CellFactory so replay REBINDS existing refs
TopoEvent = Spawn(ref: CellRef, factory: CellFactory) | Connect(from,to,ports) | Unlink(...) | Supervise(ref,policy)
```

`Invocation` is the same serializable object already defined for the wire
(`contractId`/`methodId` + polymorphic args + `MessageContext`, `10/14`, `40/41`) — "P9
pays off" as `20/24` promised. `HostSeq` is the host's existing per-cell-invocation
sequence number that already makes `(priority, sequence)` order inviolable (C-8, `30/31`).

##### Recovery protocol (four phases, total order)

1. **Restore snapshots.** For each cell load the newest *complete* `Snapshot` (atomic
   write-then-swap; torn snapshots ignored). Empty for a cell with no snapshot.
2. **Replay the log suffix in `seq` order** (entries with `seq >` the cell's snapshot seq):
   - `Topology` entries reconstruct the graph — spawn with the **pinned** full ref +
     factory, connect/unlink, re-apply supervision. This is `GraphSpec.applyTo` (`50/51`) in
     **preserve-refs mode** (rebind existing `(id, instanceId)`), not construction mode
     (which mints fresh). Cells activate in **REPLAY MODE**.
   - `Accepted` entries route to their target cell, which applies them with **every outlet
     NoOp-served** (the `Shadow.spawn` mechanism of G-32, `50/52`). State advances; nothing
     is broadcast, no effect fires, no `Owned` is re-transferred, no frame hits the wire.
3. **Exit replay mode.** Restore real outlets; re-announce this host's refs to the location
   registry (`40/41 §Addressing`); each restored link's `onLinked` fires ordinary
   **idempotent catch-up** (state-as-delta-from-empty, `20/21`), reconciling any downstream
   that lagged. Tag idempotence (`20/24`) absorbs duplicates.
4. **Drain parked (SUSPEND) traffic live** — un-suppressed — since parked traffic is
   post-recovery live delivery, not already-applied history.

##### Rules the model introduces (normative)

- **R1 — Durability is a host property, opt-in.** A durable host journals at its intake;
  non-durable hosts are byte-for-byte unchanged (P2/P6). This is the "durable" point on
  ADR 1 §3's in-memory/durable/hybrid spectrum.
- **R2 — Journal classification.** Journal **only** (a) accepted `PORT_API` data
  invocations and (b) topology/management events that change the durable cell/link set.
  **Never** journal `PORT_PROTOCOL` generic-protocol metadata (I-1: it is null-context,
  management-class, idempotent, reorder-tolerant — re-negotiated/re-requested live on
  recovery, never a state transition). **Never** separately journal fused/delegated
  *intra-host* inner calls: journal the invocation that crosses the host **intake** (the
  head of the fused chain); the fused tail re-derives deterministically on replay. This is
  the direct answer to N5 — the durability boundary is the host intake, where an
  `Invocation` already exists, not the fused interior where it deliberately does not.
- **R3 — One host-sequence-ordered log; replay in exactly that order.** Because replay
  follows the same `(priority, seq)` order the live host enforced (C-8), it is
  deterministic and automatically preserves: per-link FIFO; topology-before-the-data-that-
  flows-over-it (N13 — a link event and a wave-t delta over it keep their recorded order);
  and glitch-free frontier reconstruction (N12 — the same inbound order rebuilds the same
  per-wave version buffers; suppression means a completed wave becomes restored state
  rather than an emission, so buffers need no special snapshot handling).
- **R4 — Replay suppresses emission.** During phase 2, outlets are NoOp-served (G-32).
  Recovery reconstructs state; it never re-transmits. This single rule dissolves N2
  (no re-broadcast), N8 (a `CounterDelta` is applied to the counter's state exactly once,
  never re-emitted — so non-idempotent merge is a non-issue), N14 (no `Owned`/`Leased`
  re-delivery — the *result* of consuming an owned payload is captured as state, the owned
  command is not re-run), N22 (no duplicate wire delivery), and N26 (no effectful re-fire
  for interior effectful cells; sinks handled by R8).
- **R5 — One reconciliation path.** After replay, downstream lag is closed by the ordinary
  idempotent catch-up of `20/21`, identical to late-join and to `40/42` anti-entropy.
  There is **no second recovery protocol** (recorded decision honored). Replayed emissions
  do not re-gossip because they do not happen; live re-convergence gossips normally and
  dedups by tag.
- **R6 — Keying and identity.** Snapshots and journal entries key on the **full**
  `CellRef(id, instanceId)` (I-2, full-ref addressing). Recovery **preserves `instanceId`**
  (I-2's RESTART lifecycle rule): the recovered cell is the *same* instance, so its links
  survive without re-handshaking. Topology replay in preserve-refs mode is exactly what
  distinguishes recovery (rebind existing refs) from GraphSpec construction (mint fresh) —
  answering N25 and N23 with one flag on one replay machine.
- **R7 — Uncoordinated per-cell snapshots (no global barrier).** Each cell snapshots
  independently at an inter-invocation boundary (the host is single-consumer, so this is
  always a clean boundary). No consistent cut across cells or hosts. Within a host the WAL
  gives a total order; across hosts each host recovers to its own frontier and catch-up
  reconciles (convergence not simultaneity, G-20; P4). This is the same stance `40/42`
  already takes for partitions.
- **R8 — Output-side journaling for sources and effectful sinks.** A spontaneously-emitting
  **source/ingress** cell has no inbound to replay; it journals its **emitted effective
  deltas** (its own state-as-delta) — Candidate B for exactly the cells that need it. This
  is also where the deferred **disk-overflow mailbox** for indefinitely-parked wire traffic
  (`30/33`, deferred to G-25) lives: parked frames spill into the journal. An **`Effectful`
  sink** (`50/52` marker) journals a **processed-frontier** — the set of tags/waves it has
  already acted on — so that post-recovery live re-delivery is *deduped* (dropped as
  already-processed) rather than re-acted. This connects G-32 to recovery for the external-
  effect case (N26): shadow-mode suppresses effects during replay; the processed-frontier
  suppresses them against live re-delivery after replay.
- **R9 — Composition with the two existing regimes (precedence fixed).** Durability
  *subsumes* RESTART: a durable cell's RESTART restores its latest snapshot + WAL suffix
  (suppressed) instead of the spawn-time checkpoint — same mechanism, richer checkpoint
  source; a non-durable cell's RESTART is the degenerate case (spawn snapshot, empty WAL).
  SUSPEND's parked replay stays **live/un-suppressed** and runs in phase 4, strictly after
  suppressed recovery. Total precedence: **snapshot → suppressed WAL replay → re-announce +
  catch-up → parked live drain.** Three regimes, one ordered pipeline (N18 resolved).

##### Locus (N7)

The journal lives **at the durable host, at its intake** — the same boundary that already
owns the closable intake, park/replay, and drain machinery (`30/33`, `40/41`). The
membrane's "tracing and replay at crossings" (`10/11`) is the *conceptual* framing; the
*mechanical* crossing for durability **is** the host intake (the point where a cross-host
`Invocation` materializes). Under the host hierarchy (G-28), durability is declared on a
host and cascades like drain (children-first): a durable parent journals its own intake,
and its recovery reconstructs child hosts from the topology log. Organelle-internal fused
traffic below the intake is not separately journaled (R2).

##### Partitioned composites (N16)

Each partition organelle is an ordinary cell with its own full ref, placed and journaled on
its own (possibly durable, possibly not) host — partition placement is ordinary placement
(recorded decision). Each partition recovers independently from its own journal; the merging
outlet reconstructs by re-catching-up from each recovered child (R5). Convergence — not a
distributed snapshot — is the consistency story, consistent with P4 and "partitioning must
not become a second distribution mechanism."

##### Net effect

Recovery is *local state reconstruction with suppressed emission, reconciled by the one
catch-up path*. The classification question is answered by "journal at the intake:
`PORT_API` data + topology, never protocol metadata, never fused interiors." The downstream
question is answered by one rule (R4: suppress on replay) plus tag idempotence. The locus is
the host intake. And it reuses five already-shipped mechanisms rather than inventing any.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Untouched** — journal/replay is a host concern; every step is meaningful single-threaded (replay is a deterministic re-drive of the recorded order). No kernel primitive added. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied (with a stated opt-in cost)** — non-durable hosts are unchanged; a durable host pays a batched log append per accepted invocation, a configured durability cost, not a change to the non-durable steady state. Replay/snapshot are rare operations (P2 budget). |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — the topology log is the GraphSpec (visible, serializable); recovery rebinds visible refs; no hidden reconstruction. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — per-cell uncoordinated snapshots, per-host ordered WAL, cross-host reconciliation by convergence; no global barrier/clock/cut. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — suppression (NoOp-served outlets) is a structural mechanism (G-32), not runtime discipline; exactly-once is preserved because owned/effect/non-idempotent emissions simply do not re-occur. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — durability is opt-in per host; nothing is journaled "just in case"; protocol metadata and fused interiors are excluded. |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — durability is orthogonal to boundary security (the journal is a bridge/host configuration, like encryption). |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — recovery preserves `instanceId` so links survive; topology replay is ordinary spawn/connect; a durable graph is still fully mutable at runtime. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied, load-bearing** — the journal *is* serializable `Invocation`s/`Snapshot`s/`TopoEvent`s (the wire form); no lambdas/handles (CellFactory is already a `Serializable` fun interface, `50/51`). |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — the trade (state reconstruction + convergent catch-up over general command-replay-with-re-emission) resolves in favor of decentralized, idempotent, long-lived, interest-driven recovery. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-25 "durable host journals applied invocations; replay = recovery; cells oblivious":**
  consistent, refined. Cells stay oblivious (they re-drive transitions unaware). "Applied
  invocations" is sharpened to "accepted `PORT_API` invocations + topology events at the
  host intake"; "replay = recovery" is sharpened to "replay **with emission suppressed**,
  reconciled by catch-up." No CONFLICT — this fills the sketch, it does not contradict it.
- **A snapshot IS a delta (state-as-delta-from-empty):** strongly consistent — `Snapshot`
  is `Stateful.snapshot()` = a delta; recovery applies it; catch-up serves it.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol:** strongly
  consistent — R5 makes recovery reconcile through the *same* catch-up/anti-entropy path
  `40/42` already uses; no second recovery protocol.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive; park/replay by full ref:** consistent — parked
  (SUSPEND) replay is live and distinct from suppressed journal replay; R9 orders them.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end:** consistent — the WAL is the
  "accepted" set; replay in `HostSeq` order preserves accepted-before-closure and per-link
  FIFO exactly.
- **Cardinality/SPSC; Owned→move-by-serialize, Leased not crossing machines:** consistent —
  R4 means owned payloads are never re-delivered on recovery; the state resulting from their
  consumption is captured, the transfer is not re-run.
- **CellRef(id, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2):** consistent — R6 keys on full
  refs and preserves `instanceId`; recovery is the same instance.
- **Generic protocols are a bounded metadata plane (I-1):** consistent — R2 excludes
  `PORT_PROTOCOL` from the journal precisely because I-1 made them idempotent/null-context/
  reorder-tolerant.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved:** consistent — the journal reuses the
  `WireFrame`/`Invocation` serialization; no new wire dimension.
- **G-20 per-source waves; no global barrier:** consistent — R7 recovers per host to its own
  frontier; convergence not simultaneity.
- **G-32 shadow / `Effectful` marker; G-30 GraphSpec replay:** consistent, newly connected —
  G-32 NoOp-serve is the suppression mechanism (R4); GraphSpec replay gains a preserve-refs
  mode for recovery (R6). No decision reopened.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **`20/24 §Durability spectrum`** — replace the three-sentence sketch with the Candidate-C
  mechanism: durable-host opt-in, the `JournalEntry`/`Snapshot` shapes, the four-phase
  recovery protocol, R1–R9, and the input-mode/output-mode split.
- **`30/31 §Normative rules`** — add durability as a host property; state that a durable
  host journals accepted `PORT_API` + topology events in `HostSeq` order; state the
  precedence (R9) subsuming RESTART and ordering SUSPEND drain after recovery; note
  children-first cascade for durable host hierarchies (G-28).
- **`50/52 §Live invariants`** — record that G-32's NoOp-serve suppression is *also* the
  replay-suppression mechanism, and that `Effectful` sinks hold a durable processed-frontier
  for post-recovery dedup.
- **`50/51 §Graph construction DSL`** — add a preserve-refs replay mode (rebind existing
  `(id, instanceId)`) distinct from construction (mint fresh); the topology log is a
  GraphSpec replayed in that mode.
- **`20/21 §Pull`** — note that recovery reuses the `onLinked` catch-up path verbatim; a
  recovered cell is reconciled exactly like a late joiner.
- **`40/42 §Anti-entropy`** — cross-reference: durable recovery and replica anti-entropy are
  the same reconciliation path; a durable replica restores its journal then rejoins the mesh
  (does not re-gossip replayed deltas).
- **`30/33` (drain/park)** — the deferred disk-overflow mailbox for parked wire traffic is
  realized as output-side journaling on a durable host (R8).
- **`10/11 §Membranes`** — clarify that "replay at crossings" is realized mechanically at
  the durable host intake.
- **`90/91` G-25** — update to Partial→(recovery designed): snapshot half shipped, journal
  design fixed here, disk-overflow mailbox homed.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Non-deterministic cell logic** — input-mode replay reconstructs state only for
  deterministic transitions; a cell reading wall-clock/random inside its logic breaks it.
  Needs a determinism marker/lint that forces such cells to output-mode (R8), or a captured-
  entropy record in the WAL.
- **Output-side journaling design (sources / `Effectful` sinks)** — the emitted-delta log
  format, the processed-frontier data shape, and its dedup contract against live re-delivery
  need full design and a generative recovery-dedup test.
- **Log compaction & snapshot cadence** — when to cut a snapshot vs grow the WAL; interacts
  with OR-set tombstone/tag-set growth (`40/42`, `20/24`) and the disk-overflow mailbox.
- **External-effect idempotency ceiling** — R8 dedups re-delivery only if the sink holds a
  durable processed-frontier *and* the external world accepts idempotent re-delivery; sinks
  to external systems without idempotency keys remain unsolved (a documented limit).
- **Cross-host recovery-frontier divergence** — how far apart two hosts' independent
  recovery frontiers may drift before catch-up cost blows up; an *opt-in* coordinated
  checkpoint for tightly-coupled subgraphs (never global) may be warranted.
- **Owned/Leased at-most-once under crash** — an owned payload parked-but-not-yet-snapshotted
  at crash is lost; confirm the sender-durability contract that makes this at-most-once
  acceptable (or requires the producing host to be durable too).
- **Glitch-free partial-wave buffers** — confirm deterministic replay reconstruction (R3)
  suffices in all frontier shapes, or require `GlitchFreeCell` to include partial buffers in
  `Stateful.snapshot()`.
- **RESTART within a replicated logical cell** (carried from I-2) — whether a durable replica
  should prefer local journal restore or mesh re-catch-up when its journal lags the mesh.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The mechanism reuses five already-shipped pieces — `Stateful`
snapshot/restore (M3.3), G-32 NoOp-serve suppression (M9.2), `onLinked` catch-up (M4.2),
GraphSpec replay (M4.5), and the host's `(priority, seq)` ordering (C-8) — and the single
load-bearing idea (replay with **suppressed** emission, reconcile by catch-up) collapses the
entire downstream member-pair cluster (N2/N8/N14/N22/N26) into one rule while honoring "no
second sync protocol" and "snapshot is a delta." The classification and locus questions
resolve cleanly by placing the journal at the host intake. Confidence is not higher because
three pieces are genuinely new design rather than reclassification: the output-side journal
for sources/effectful sinks (R8), the determinism requirement for input-mode replay, and log
compaction — all spun out as follow-on gaps.

**Open questions:** (1) whether input-mode (command WAL) should be the default with
output-mode as fallback, or whether a durable host should choose per cell by a determinism
marker; (2) the exact processed-frontier shape that makes effectful-sink recovery dedup
correct against concurrent live deltas; (3) whether any tightly-coupled subgraph genuinely
needs an opt-in coordinated checkpoint, or whether per-host frontiers + catch-up always
suffice within the niche.

### I-8 — PartitionedCell composite design: routing, merging, lifecycle, identity, and wave semantics (G-24)

> Member pairs: N1×N16, N2×N16, N3×N16, N4×N16, N5×N16, N6×N16, N8×N16, N9×N16, N11×N16, N12×N16, N13×N16, N14×N16, N15×N16, N16×N23, N16×N25, N16×N26
> Existing gaps touched: G-24 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 2/16 member pairs findings need re-wording while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The entire composite: the @Key/keyIndex descriptor slot + broadcast-not-exclusive lint, the served router proxy (P2-budgeted branching node), the two membrane ports, demux-preserves-SPSC, the wave-transparent merge with disjointness as the correctness proof…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: what *is* a `PartitionedCell` as a concrete
cell — how does one composite whose organelles each own a disjoint key range
(a) route keyed commands to the owning organelle, (b) merge per-organelle delta
streams into one outlet, (c) register its ports, (d) run its lifecycle and
rebalance, (e) present identity and waves to the outside, (f) get declared in
GraphSpec and observed by invariants — such that every kernel-facing surface is
defined and the whole thing reconciles per-message routing with the P2 fast
path?

The G-24 text is a *proposal sketch only*: "a **PartitionedCell** is a composite
cell whose organelles each own a key range; its inlet routes commands by key (a
routing proxy — same mechanism as `HostRoutingApi`); its outlet merges child
delta streams. Placement of partitions across hosts is then ordinary cell
placement … partitioning must not become a second distribution mechanism"
(20/24 §Partitioned state). `91` marks G-24 **Deferred with trigger**. Nothing
is built; the M4 exit app "never sharded" (20/24 §Partitioned state; 52
§Invariant testing notes the harness has never exercised sharding).

**Member pairs** all pull on this one composite design, each on a different
kernel surface:
- *Ports & registration* (N1×N16): how the command contract exposes the routing
  key and how the two composite ports register in the `PortRegistry`
  (10/12 §Definition, §Cardinality; 10/15 §Port discovery).
- *Cardinality & SPSC* (N2×N16, N14×N16): which cardinality classes the internal
  ports use; whether the router is a single SPSC consumer or a fan-out; where
  the exclusive bit fires on the routed `Owned`/`Leased` path (10/12
  §Cardinality; 20/23 §The SPSC link rule).
- *Fast path* (N5×N16): a key-router is intrinsically per-message dispatch and
  cannot delegate-flatten to any single organelle, against 10/14 §The
  Link-and-Lease model / 00/02 §P2.
- *Lifecycle* (N6×N16): activation order of router vs partitions, cold-phase
  construction of the partition set, rebalancing as spawn/despawn (10/15
  §Activation, §Normative rules).
- *Merge, waves, frontier* (N8, N11, N12, N15 × N16): ordering and effective-only
  emission across partitions; whether the merging outlet re-mints waves or leaks
  per-organelle sources; whether the composite is one frontier node; and
  `MapDelta`/`ListDelta`'s documented single-stream convergence limit under
  multi-child merge (20/21 §Push, §Pull; 20/22 §MessageContext, §The glitch-free
  frontier; 20/24 §Established pattern).
- *Late-join* (N9×N16): whether each organelle unicasts its own catch-up or the
  composite coordinates one cross-partition snapshot (20/21 §Pull).
- *Repartition ordering* (N13×N16): stamping/sequencing a key-range move against
  in-flight keyed commands (20/22 §Topology versioning).
- *Protocol stacking* (N3×N16): ordering of ProtocolId demux vs key-range
  routing; which organelle answers a generic-protocol request at the composite
  port (10/12 §Multiplexed ports).
- *Handshake* (N4×N16): whether `onLink`/`onLinked` (incl. cross-range catch-up)
  runs on the composite or per organelle; whether rebalancing is external
  unlink/relink (10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based)).
- *Identity* (N16×N23): which unit carries the logicalId links bind to; how
  repartitioning preserves link-bound identity (10/11 §Identity; 40/42
  §Constraint on everything else).
- *GraphSpec* (N16×N25): how partitioned datasets are declared in `graph{}`,
  recorded, and replayed with placement (50/51 §Graph construction DSL).
- *Invariants* (N16×N26): whether an invariant observes the merging outlet or
  per-partition streams, and what cross-partition completeness means (50/52
  §Invariant testing).

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 vs intrinsic per-message dispatch.** Delegation (10/14) exists so
  behavior-change cost is proportional to *redefinitions, not messages*, and
  chains flatten to remove pass-through cells. A key-router is the opposite: it
  *branches per message* by inspecting the payload key, so it can never
  delegate-flatten onto one downstream. The naive reading is "the router
  violates P2." The reconciliation must show the router is P2-*budgeted*, not
  P2-*violating*.
- **P4 vs a merged multi-source stream.** One merging outlet fanning in N
  organelle sources looks like it needs a cross-partition coordinator to give
  the composite a single wave identity — but any such coordinator is a global
  barrier over the partition set, exactly what P4 (no global barrier) and G-20
  (per-source waves, convergence not simultaneity) forbid.
- **P5 vs `MapDelta`/`ListDelta` convergence limits.** 20/24 documents that
  map/list deltas are single-stream (arrival-order) convergent. A composite that
  *by definition* merges several children's map streams appears to inherit an
  unspecified multi-writer convergence problem for exactly the keyed data the
  feature targets.
- **P3/P8 vs identity under churn.** The composite must look like one stable
  logical cell to external links (P3 explicit topology; location transparency)
  while its organelle set changes at runtime (P8), and repartitioning must not
  break the link-bound identity that I-2 pins to the full ref.
- **The decided "partitioning is not a second distribution mechanism"**
  (20/24; recorded decision) forbids inventing new placement/sync machinery:
  organelles must be ordinary cells under ordinary placement, and rebalancing
  must reuse the existing suspension/drain and topology-versioning primitives.

The load-bearing observations that make it tractable: **key ranges are
disjoint**, and **the composite is a membrane**. Disjointness turns the
multi-source merge into a conflict-free union; the membrane keeps external
identity stable across internal churn.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Router-as-hosted-cell (a proxy cell in front of organelle cells)

The router is its own cell with its own ref, holding the routing table, and
re-dispatches via a keyed variant of `HostRoutingApi.route(target, inlet,
invocation)`. A separate merger cell fans in the organelle outlets.

- *Semantics*: the sketch read literally — "same mechanism as `HostRoutingApi`"
  = an actual routing cell.
- *Fast-path cost*: **two hops** per keyed command (enqueue to router, then
  enqueue to organelle) even when router and organelle are co-hosted; plus a
  third hop through the merger. The router cell is an async boundary that a
  co-hosted call should not need.
- *Failure modes*: the extra hops violate P2's "a direct method call in-host";
  the router and merger become identity/placement units of their own, competing
  with the organelles' identity (muddies N23); repartitioning must relink around
  three cells.
- *Tradeoff*: conceptually simplest, matches the sketch's words, but pays hops
  P2 forbids. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — Composite with a served router-proxy + wave-transparent fan-in merge (recommended)

The composite is one cell exposing exactly two external ports. The router is a
**serve-time `Proxy`** installed on the composite's inlet (like the
Traffic-Light cell serves a `Buffering`/`delegate` proxy, 10/14) — *not* a
separate hosted cell, so it adds **no queue hop**: it reads the key from the
invocation, looks up the owning organelle in a versioned routing table, and
forwards by direct call (co-host) or one enqueue (cross-host). The merging
outlet is an internal fan-in that forwards each organelle's delta **carrying the
organelle's own `MessageContext` unchanged** — the composite is wave-transparent.
Because key ranges are disjoint, the merge is a conflict-free union and needs no
cross-partition coordination.

- *Fast-path cost*: one descriptor lookup (methodId → key-arg index) + one key
  hash + one volatile read of the routing table + a direct call or single
  enqueue — exactly P2's "a volatile read + an enqueue cross-host, a direct
  method call in-host." Merge forwarding is a direct fan-in (co-host) or one
  enqueue (cross-host), the cost the cross-host organelle would pay anyway.
- *Failure modes*: none of the member-pair conflicts survive (§4). Residual
  risk is confined to repartition-window buffering correctness and cross-host
  routing-table propagation (§8), both reusing existing primitives.
- *Tradeoff*: gives up positional-list partitioning (out of scope; §4 rule 0)
  and requires one KSP descriptor slot (`@Key`), in exchange for a design where
  every existing surface keeps its single-cell meaning. **Recommended.**

##### Candidate C — Flat partitioning (no composite; organelles are top-level cells + client-side routing)

Expose N organelle cells directly; a shared routing table lets clients pick the
partition and link straight to it.

- *Semantics*: no membrane; partitioning is a client convention.
- *Fast-path cost*: excellent (clients link directly), but…
- *Failure modes*: breaks location transparency — external links must know the
  partition scheme (against P3's spirit and the "composite cell" requirement);
  repartitioning changes which organelle owns a key, so a client's link to
  organelle A becomes wrong — link-bound identity breaks (N23, against I-2
  continuity); invariants and late joiners must re-implement cross-partition
  fan-in themselves.
- *Tradeoff*: cheapest fast path but abandons the composite/membrane the feature
  is defined around. **Rejected** (folded in only as the *optional* direct-link
  shortcut a client MAY take once it holds a specific organelle's full ref, §4).

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. A `PartitionedCell` is one composite cell (one membrane,
one logicalId) that owns a set of organelle cells, each an ordinary data cell
holding a **disjoint key range**. Routing is a served proxy on its inlet;
merging is a wave-transparent fan-in on its outlet; the disjointness of ranges
is the correctness argument that dissolves the merge/wave/frontier tensions.

##### Data shapes

```
// Descriptor slot, parallel to the G-21 `exclusive` bit (gen/wire/ContractDescriptor.kt):
data class MethodDescriptor(
    val methodId: Long, val name: String, val jvmDescriptor: String,
    val exclusive: Boolean = false,
    val keyIndex: Int = -1,      // NEW: index of the @Key parameter, -1 = key-less (broadcast)
)

// KSP: a @Key annotation on ONE parameter of a data-contract method emits keyIndex.
//   interface MapOps<K,V> { fun put(@Key k: K, v: V); fun remove(@Key k: K); fun clear() }
//   interface SetOps<E>   { fun add(@Key e: E);      fun remove(@Key e: E) }   // element IS the key

// The composite:
class PartitionedCell<K, Cmd, Delta>(
    override val ref: CellRef,
    val partitioner: Partitioner<K>,        // Serializable: key -> partitionId; a total function
    val organelleFactory: (partitionId) -> Cell,   // Serializable CellFactory (51)
    val placement: (partitionId) -> HostHint,      // Serializable; default = local host
) : Cell { /* two external ports below */ }

// Versioned routing table, held by the served router proxy:
data class RoutingTable(
    val epoch: Long,                            // topology version, bumped on any rebalance
    val ranges: Map<PartitionId, Use<Cmd>>,     // partitionId -> the organelle's inlet Use
    val owner: (K) -> PartitionId,              // = partitioner
)
```

##### The two external ports (N1)

1. **Routing inlet** — contract = the *same* command contract as the organelles
   (`FanInlet.create<MapOps<K,V>>()`), registered in the composite's
   `PortRegistry` by name (`"inlet"`), exactly like any data cell's inlet
   (10/15 §Port discovery). From outside, the composite is indistinguishable
   from a single `MapApi` cell — location transparency (P3, 40/41).
2. **Merging outlet** — contract = the delta contract
   (`FanOutlet.create<Propagate<MapDelta<K,V>>>()`), registered as `"outlet"`.

Organelles carry their *own* inlets/outlets internally; they are never
externally addressed by name.

##### Rule 0 — Scope: keyed structures only

`PartitionedCell` targets **hashable-keyed** structures (Set = element-keyed,
Map = key-keyed, keyed collections). Positionally-indexed `ListCell` is **out of
scope**: a global position index across shards is ill-defined, and `ListDelta`'s
index-addressed convergence limit (20/24) is *not* dissolved by disjointness.
This matches ADR 1 §5 as quoted in 20/24 ("large **keyed** datasets shard by
key"). Partition a list by keying its entries on a stable id, never on position.

##### Rule 1 — Routing is a served proxy, key from the descriptor (N1, N5)

At activation the composite installs a `Proxy` on its routing inlet (the same
serve/delegate seam the Traffic-Light cell uses, 10/14). On each data
invocation the proxy:
1. reads `keyIndex` from the method's `MethodDescriptor` (one map lookup, the
   descriptor already rides `ContractRegistry`);
2. if `keyIndex >= 0`: extracts `key = invocation.args[keyIndex]`, computes
   `partitionId = partitioner(key)` (a **total function**, so every key maps to
   exactly one organelle), reads the routing table (volatile), forwards the
   invocation to that organelle's inlet `Use` — **direct call co-host, one
   enqueue cross-host**;
3. if `keyIndex < 0` (key-less, e.g. `clear()`): **broadcasts** to all
   organelles (permitted only for non-exclusive contracts — Rule 4).

This is P2-conformant: routing is O(1) table read + hash, not a chain of
forwarders. **The reconciliation with delegation (N5):** delegate-flatten
removes *pass-through* (non-branching) indirection; a key-router is a *branching*
node, the one place per-message dispatch is *intrinsic to the feature* and
therefore P2-budgeted rather than P2-violated — the same status the sketch's
"routing proxy — same mechanism as `HostRoutingApi`" already implies
(`HostRoutingApi.route` is per-message target dispatch and is accepted). Within
each partition, downstream derived chains still delegate-flatten normally.

##### Rule 2 — The router is a demultiplexer, so it preserves SPSC (N2, N14)

A partition function maps each key to **exactly one** organelle, so a keyed
command reaches exactly one consumer even though the composite has N organelles.
Therefore:
- The **exclusive bit** (G-21) is honored end-to-end: the external inlet link has
  one consumer (the router); the router **moves** an `Owned` payload
  (`Owned.take()`, 20/23) exactly once into exactly one organelle; each internal
  router→organelle edge is `OneToOnePort` for exclusive contracts. Demux is
  exclusivity-preserving; **fan-out is not demux**. The exclusive-bit check fires
  where it already fires — `FanOutlet.subscribe` on each internal edge (20/23
  §Implementation) — and at the external inlet.
- **Key-less broadcast of an exclusive payload is refused** (you cannot move one
  `Owned` to N organelles) — Rule 4.
- The merging **outlet** is an ordinary `FanOutlet` (many subscribers, broadcast
  emission); rule-3 merge-declaration obligations (10/12 §Cardinality rule 3)
  attach to it exactly as to any multi-producer-fed outlet — satisfied because
  the organelles already declare merge semantics (Set/Map deltas, 20/24) and the
  streams are key-disjoint (Rule 5).

##### Rule 3 — Lifecycle: composite spawns organelles in onActivate; rebalance = spawn/despawn (N6)

- **Cold**: the constructor declares the two external ports as dormant metadata
  and stores config (partitioner, factory, placement). No organelles yet
  (10/15 §Cold phase).
- **Activation** (ordered): (1) spawn each organelle via the host —
  organelles are ordinary child cells, hierarchy is the same mechanism (11
  §Organelles), placed by ordinary placement per `placement(partitionId)` (30/33,
  40/42); (2) link each organelle's delta outlet into the merging outlet
  (internal fan-in); (3) build the `RoutingTable` (epoch 0); (4) **serve the
  router proxy on the inlet**. Between (1) and (4) the inlet holds a `Buffering`
  proxy so early commands park and replay — the ordinary suspension primitive
  (10/14, 30/33), no new machinery.
- **Runtime rebalance** = spawn a new organelle / despawn an old one + a routing
  table flip (Rule 6). Ordinary lifecycle ops, not a new protocol.

##### Rule 4 — Broadcast vs demux is a per-method property (N2)

A method with a `@Key` parameter is **demux** (one organelle). A key-less method
is **broadcast** (all organelles) and MUST be non-exclusive (KSP lint: a method
that is both `keyIndex < 0` and `exclusive` fails compilation — you cannot move
one `Owned` to N). This covers `clear()` and range-less resets without a second
mechanism.

##### Rule 5 — Wave-transparent merge; disjointness dissolves convergence, waves, frontier (N8, N11, N12, N15)

The merging outlet **forwards** each organelle's delta preserving its
`MessageContext` — it neither re-mints a wave nor coalesces sources. Each
organelle outlet is its own wave source (`Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` minted
per emitting outlet, G-20 / 20/22). Consequences:
- **N15 dissolves.** `MapDelta`/`ListDelta`'s single-stream convergence limit is
  a *per-key/per-index* limit (two writers racing the same key). Partitions are
  **key-disjoint**, so a `MapDelta` from organelle A only ever mentions A's keys;
  merging disjoint-key streams is a conflict-free union with no additional
  convergence obligation. **The partition function is the merge-safety proof.**
- **N11 dissolves.** The composite does not re-mint (which would break
  transparent flow, 20/22 rule 2) and does not need one logical source. It
  **leaks N per-organelle sources behind one membrane by design** — which is
  exactly G-20's "convergence not simultaneity across sources." Because ranges
  are disjoint, no downstream diamond ever joins two partitions on the *same*
  key, so cross-source glitches are impossible without any coordination.
- **N12 dissolves.** The composite is **not** a single frontier node. Downstream
  glitch-free frontier discovery (20/22 §The glitch-free frontier) reaches the
  organelle outlets as the nearest upstream sources; the membrane is transparent.
  Multiplying (source, counter) streams behind the membrane is safe precisely
  because of disjointness.
- **N8**: emission is effective-only per organelle (20/21 §Incremental rule 2);
  the merge introduces no ordering constraint across partitions because there is
  no cross-partition key dependency.

##### Rule 6 — Repartitioning: per-range TrafficLight + versioned routing table (N13)

Moving key range R from organelle A to B while commands are in flight reuses the
suspension/drain primitive at sub-cell granularity:
1. **Close R on A**: the router sets range R to `Buffering` (TrafficLight red for
   that range — the ONE Buffering primitive at port granularity, 10/14, 30/33).
   New commands for R park; commands for other ranges flow untouched.
2. **Transfer R's state**: A serves its R-range **state-as-delta-from-empty**
   (Stateful snapshot scoped to R, 20/24 §Durability spectrum; a snapshot IS a
   delta) to B, which applies it. Idempotent OR-set tags (20/24) make this safe
   against any concurrent live delta.
3. **Flip atomically + bump epoch**: the routing table entry for R points at B;
   `epoch` increments. The flip is a topology change stamped into the same
   logical-time domain as data waves (20/22 §Topology versioning).
4. **Replay** the buffered R commands into B in order — per-key FIFO preserved
   (the decided drain-ordering invariant: accepted-before-close delivered before
   anything after re-resolution, 30/33).
5. **Stale-epoch guard**: a command that a downstream organelle receives for a
   key it no longer owns (epoch mismatch) is re-routed by the router — the same
   placement-blind park/replay used for migration (30/33, and I-1's re-resolution
   pattern). External links never see any of this (Rule 7).

##### Rule 7 — Handshake and identity live on the composite membrane (N4, N23)

- **Identity**: the **composite** carries the logicalId that external links bind
  to (full-ref addressing per I-2: external `PortRef` = composite's full ref +
  `"inlet"`/`"outlet"`). Each organelle is its own cell with its own full ref,
  addressed only internally. Repartitioning changes the organelle *set* but not
  the composite's logicalId or its external ports — **link-bound identity is
  preserved because links bind the composite's ports and only the routing table
  behind them changes** (11 §Membrane as evolution surface; I-2 rule 3
  continuity).
- **Handshake**: `onLink`/`onUnlink`/`onLinked` run on the **composite's**
  external ports (the membrane surface, 10/13). Rebalancing is expressed as
  *internal* organelle unlink/relink + table flip, **never** as external
  unlink/relink — so external counterparts never re-handshake on a rebalance.
- **Composition with replication**: an organelle (mergeable class) may itself be
  replicated by the ordinary gossip mesh (each organelle a `Replicable` full ref
  linked organelle-to-organelle by its own logicalId, 40/42). Partitioning (shard
  by key, composite) and replication (replicate a shard, mesh) compose — this is
  the "keyed structures + upstream responsibility" 40/42 left open — with **no
  second distribution mechanism**: the composite routes, ordinary placement +
  the existing mesh distribute.

##### Rule 8 — Late-join = per-organelle catch-up; disjoint union is the coherent snapshot (N9)

When a subscriber links to the composite's merging outlet, the composite fans
that new downstream link to each organelle's outlet; each organelle unicasts its
own **key-range state-as-delta-from-empty** (`outlet.at(link.to)`, the shipped
G-22 mechanism, 20/21 §Pull). The **union of disjoint-key catch-ups IS the
coherent cross-partition snapshot** — no key appears twice, no ordering
constraint across partitions, so no composite-level coordination is needed.
OR-set tag idempotence covers overlap with live deltas per organelle.

##### Rule 9 — Generic protocols demux first, then key-routing (N3)

Per I-1, generic protocols are a bounded metadata plane (`PORT_PROTOCOL` dispatch
class) riding the link, orthogonal to `PORT_API` data. So on the composite's
inlet the branch order is: **dispatch class first** (`PORT_PROTOCOL` →
`ProtocolSupport`; `PORT_API` → the router), **then** within `PORT_API` the
key-routing of Rule 1. They never compete on one layer. Which organelle answers a
generic-protocol request at the composite:
- **state-request** (RequestState, 20/21 / I-1) → the composite fans it to all
  organelles; each replies its range's state-as-delta (same as Rule 8).
- **attention** (30/34) → forwarded to all organelles (interest in the composite
  = interest in its partitions), or key-scoped if the notice carries a key.
- Protocols carry null context and bypass data-path parking (I-1 rules 2–3), so
  they are never subject to the router's per-range Buffering.

##### Rule 10 — GraphSpec records the composite as one spawn; organelles regenerate (N16×N25)

The composite is **one** `spawn` step in `graph{}`
(`spawn("userStore") { PartitionedMapCell(partitioner, factory, placement) }`),
with its config as the `Serializable` `CellFactory` arguments (50/51). External
`connect` steps address the composite's ports. Organelles are spawned by the
composite's own `onActivate` (internal logic), so replay re-runs `onActivate` and
**deterministically regenerates the partition set** from config — GraphSpec's
"spawn/connect replays fresh cells" invariant is preserved with no new DSL
semantics (50/51: "anything the DSL does must be expressible as management
invocations"; internal spawns are the composite's logic, not DSL steps). Explicit
cross-host partition placement is a `placement` config parameter, not a separate
recorded step — keeping partition placement "ordinary cell placement."

##### Rule 11 — Invariants: merging outlet = whole-dataset; disjointness gives completeness (N16×N26)

An invariant subscribed to the **merging outlet** observes the complete keyed
dataset — every key exactly once, from its owning partition — so **cross-partition
completeness is exactly "subscribe to the merging outlet"**; disjointness
guarantees no double-count and no gap (a cross-partition `CountCell` sums
disjoint per-partition deltas soundly). A late-linked invariant receives catch-up
from every organelle (Rule 8), so it too sees the whole dataset (52 §Invariant
testing: "a late-linked invariant receives catch-up like any subscriber"). An
invariant needing per-partition scope links to a specific organelle's outlet by
full ref — the ordinary operation (I-2 N26).

##### Optional direct-link shortcut (non-normative)

A client that already holds a specific organelle's full ref (e.g. it only ever
touches one key range and wants to skip the router hop) MAY link directly to that
organelle — but then it forfeits repartition transparency and must tolerate
stale-epoch re-routing. Default and recommended path is always through the
composite membrane.

**Net effect**: two composite ports, one served router proxy (O(1), P2-budgeted),
a wave-transparent fan-in merge whose correctness is the disjointness of ranges,
repartition and catch-up built entirely from the existing Buffering/drain/
state-as-delta primitives, identity on the membrane, and one KSP descriptor slot
(`@Key`). No kernel primitive is added (P1).

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — composite, organelles, router-proxy, merge are ordinary cells/ports/links/invocations; rebalance/catch-up reduce to link manipulation + Buffering; meaningful single-threaded. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — routing = descriptor lookup + hash + volatile table read + direct call (co-host) / one enqueue (cross-host); merge = direct fan-in / one enqueue. The per-message branch is intrinsic and budgeted, not a forwarder chain. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — external links bind the composite's named ports; the routing table and organelle links are inspectable; no hidden mailbox. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no cross-partition barrier/clock/lock; each organelle is an independent source; convergence not simultaneity (G-20). |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — `@Key`/`keyIndex` and the broadcast-not-exclusive lint are KSP-enforced; demux preserves the exclusive bit at the existing funnel; disjointness is a structural merge-safety property. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — organelles and their links follow subscriptions; catch-up on link; replication of a shard is opt-in per organelle. |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Untouched** — boundary controls unchanged; the membrane is where policies already attach. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — rebalance is runtime spawn/despawn + table flip; the composite's external identity is stable across organelle churn. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — partitioner/factory/placement are `Serializable`; deltas already cross the wire with tags (20/24); `keyIndex` is a wire-registered descriptor field; no lambdas/reflection on the wire. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — keyed, incremental, decentralized sharding that composes with replication; positional lists deliberately excluded as off-niche. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent, reinforced: each organelle outlet is a
  distinct source; the merge leaks sources rather than minting one (Rule 5).
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent: no cross-partition barrier; merge
  needs no coordination (disjointness).
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: organelles are placed/moved as
  ordinary cells on hosts; no per-partition mobility protocol.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent:
  activation window and repartition-window both use TrafficLight/Buffering at
  port (sub-range) granularity; no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local|Remote; one park/replay** — Consistent: cross-host routing
  and stale-epoch re-routing reuse the registry park/replay (Rule 6).
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: repartition transfer and late-join both
  use state-as-delta-from-empty (Rules 6, 8).
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, NOT wave ids** — Consistent: organelles keep
  cell-local OR-set tags; the composite forwards wave context unchanged.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent:
  command/delta contracts stay push-only; generic protocols at the composite are
  null-context management-plane (Rule 9).
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** —
  Consistent: a shard replicates via the existing mesh; the composite only routes.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT become a second distribution mechanism** — Consistent
  and central: the composite is a routing/membrane structure; organelles are
  ordinary cells under ordinary placement (Rules 3, 7).
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: `keyIndex` is a
  descriptor field (like `exclusive`), not new wire addressing; the routed
  invocation is the ordinary `WireFrame`.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent: repartition
  buffers-then-replays in order per range (Rule 6).
- **Cardinality enforced at link time, not send time** — Consistent: internal
  edges' cardinality/exclusive checks fire at link time at `FanOutlet.subscribe`
  (Rule 2).
- **Exclusive ownership refuses fan-out** — Consistent, sharpened: demux is not
  fan-out; broadcast of an exclusive payload is refused by lint (Rule 4).
- **Owned crossing machines = move-by-serialize; Leased not across machines** —
  Consistent: a routed `Owned` to a remote organelle degenerates to
  move-by-serialize at the bridge (20/23); `Leased` to a remote partition is
  refused there.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId (per I-2: full-ref
  addressing, logicalId is grouping/continuity)** — Consistent: the composite
  carries the externally-bound logicalId; organelles have their own full refs;
  repartition preserves the composite's identity (Rule 7).
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — No resolved item
  reopened; this fills G-24 (deferred) and touches the open 40/42 "keyed
  structures" remainder without reopening G-7.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/24 §Partitioned state (G-24)** — Replace the proposal sketch with the
  concrete composite design: two ports, the served router proxy + `@Key`/
  `keyIndex`, the demux-preserves-SPSC rule, the disjointness merge-safety
  argument, wave-transparent fan-in, per-range repartition via
  Buffering + state-as-delta, per-organelle catch-up, Rule 0 scope (keyed only).
- **20/24 §Established pattern** — Note that `MapDelta`/`ListDelta`'s single-stream
  limit is *per-key*, hence dissolved by disjoint partitioning (but not for
  positional lists).
- **10/12 §Cardinality** — Add: a demultiplexing router preserves the exclusive
  bit (demux ≠ fan-out); the merging outlet is a `FanOutlet` fed by
  merge-declaring organelles.
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports** / cross-ref I-1 — Note protocol-demux-then-key-route
  ordering at composite ports (Rule 9).
- **10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based)** — Note that composite handshakes run on
  the membrane; rebalancing is internal relink, not external unlink/relink.
- **10/14 §Dispatch tiers / §Standard proxy behaviors** — Document the router as a
  served proxy (a branching, non-flattening but P2-budgeted node) and the
  per-range Buffering reuse.
- **10/15 §Activation** — Add the composite activation order (organelles → merge
  links → routing table → serve router; inlet buffers meanwhile).
- **20/22 §The glitch-free frontier / §Topology versioning** — Note the composite
  is wave-transparent (not a frontier node) and repartition flips are epoch-stamped
  topology changes.
- **20/21 §Pull** — Note per-organelle catch-up on the composite outlet; disjoint
  union is the cross-partition snapshot.
- **40/42 §Still open** — Mark "keyed structures" addressed: shard-by-composite +
  replicate-per-organelle compose; leader/follower still open.
- **50/51 §Graph construction DSL** — Note a `PartitionedCell` is one recorded
  spawn whose organelles regenerate on replay from `Serializable` config.
- **50/52 §Invariant testing** — Note the merging outlet as the whole-dataset
  observation point; cross-partition completeness = subscribe-to-outlet.
- **gen (ContractDescriptor/ContractProcessor)** — Add the `keyIndex` slot and
  `@Key` scan, parallel to the `exclusive` bit; add the broadcast-not-exclusive
  lint.
- **91 G-24** — Move to Resolved (design) with the composite mechanism; note
  build trigger unchanged (first keyed dataset under placement pressure).

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **`@Key` descriptor generation & multi-key/composite-key routing** — KSP
  emission of `keyIndex`, the broadcast-not-exclusive lint, and the case of a
  method whose key spans several arguments (composite key) or whose key is a
  derived function of the payload rather than a single argument.
- **Partitioner evolution / resharding policy** — changing the partition function
  (split/merge ranges, grow N) is a bulk multi-range Rule-6 rebalance; the
  triggering policy (load, size, attention) and its atomicity across many ranges
  is undesigned.
- **Cross-host routing-table propagation & epoch consistency** — the routing table
  behind the served proxy must stay coherent when organelles live on many hosts;
  how an epoch flip and the stale-epoch re-route behave under a concurrent host
  migration of an organelle needs a generative wire test.
- **Repartition-window buffering bounds** — a long state transfer parks a range's
  commands; interaction with backpressure, quotas (30/31, G-28), and overflow
  (G-25) under sustained load is unspecified.
- **Partition × replication interaction (leader/follower keyed)** — when each shard
  is also replicated, which replica the router targets and how leader/follower
  (still open in 40/42) applies per shard.
- **Range-query / multi-key read protocol** — reads spanning several partitions
  (scatter-gather over ranges) beyond single-key demux and key-less broadcast are
  not designed; interacts with the state-request protocol (I-1, G-18 residual).
- **Positional partitioned collections** — explicitly out of scope here; if ever
  needed, requires an order-preserving cross-shard index design that
  disjointness does not provide.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The design adds no kernel primitive (P1): the router
is the already-shipped served-proxy seam (Traffic-Light idiom, 10/14), the merge
is an ordinary fan-in `FanOutlet`, repartition and catch-up reuse the shipped
Buffering/drain/state-as-delta machinery (30/33, G-22), identity follows I-2's
full-ref/membrane model, and the one new artifact — the `@Key`/`keyIndex`
descriptor slot — is a direct parallel to the shipped G-21 `exclusive` bit. The
two load-bearing ideas are simple and checkable: *disjointness makes the
multi-source merge conflict-free* (dissolving N8/N11/N12/N15 at once), and *demux
preserves exclusivity* (dissolving N14). Confidence is not higher because nothing
is built (the harness has never sharded, 52) and three interactions are genuinely
unproven: cross-host routing-table/epoch consistency under concurrent organelle
migration, bulk resharding atomicity, and partition×replication leader routing —
all spun out as follow-on gaps rather than resolved here.

**Open questions**: (1) whether the router should be a served proxy (my choice,
P2-optimal, no hop) or a thin hosted organelle in cases where cross-host routing
tables are hard to keep coherent behind a proxy — the proxy wins on the fast path
but pushes table-coherence work onto the composite; (2) the exact `@Key` surface
for composite/derived keys; (3) whether key-less broadcast should be permitted at
all for large N, or replaced by a scatter-gather read protocol.

### I-9 — Attention as the resource lever: suspension triggers, priority mapping, fairness, and edge cases (G-6)

> Member pairs: N5×N21, N6×N21, N8×N21, N14×N21, N16×N21, N17×N21, N18×N21, N19×N21, N20×N21, N21×N23, N21×N25, N21×N26, N21×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-6 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 13/13 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The lattice itself as a recorded precedence (management > admission > suspension-gate > banding > FIFO) with the advisory/authority split; the veto vocabulary (HELD_LEASE, CONSTRUCTION_LEASE, MGMT_ACTIVITY); the edge-triggered window with mid-window-cancel …

#### 1. Challenge restatement

I-4 fixed the attention **algebra** — how a level is aggregated, retracted, and
carried (per-link LWW level + commutative fold, band-quantized `NONE<LOW<NORMAL<HIGH`,
riding the I-1 metadata plane, per-instance frontiers, `setSelf` for sinks). I-9 is the
companion: given a band, **how does it enforce a resource decision?** 30/34 §Principle
names the suspension machinery "the enforcement arm" and 30/34 §Design sketch maps
"relative levels → queue priority bands" and "0 for longer than a policy window →
suspend," but the *composition* rules are open at every seam.

**The single mechanism question**: attention is a *demand signal*; the host is the *sole
scheduler* (30/31 §Definition: "hosts define *when and where* invocations execute"). What
is the precedence discipline by which a band drives the host's three levers —
**suspend/resume**, **queue banding**, **migration** — while composing correctly with
every authority already at that seam (explicit management drains, the
`management(0)>router(10)>data(20)` order and `(priority,sequence)` FIFO of 30/31, the
`NonSuspendable` veto and glitch-free region of 30/34 decision 3, future bounded-intake
backpressure of 30/32, the SPSC/`Owned`/`Leased` rule of 20/23, catch-up of 20/21, and
the identity model of I-2)?

**Member pairs** all press on this one enforcement seam:
- **N5×N21**: fused/delegated chains never enqueue, so banding cannot see them; a
  delegated-away cell's attention-aggregation role is undesigned (10/14 §Dispatch tiers,
  §Link-and-Lease).
- **N6×N21 / N20×N21**: the policy window, its precedence against explicit drains, and
  mid-drain renewal are open (30/34 §Principle, §Design sketch; 30/33 §Constraints).
- **N8×N21**: does disinterest propagate upstream, or do parked buffers grow unbounded
  (20/21 §Push; 30/34 §Principle)?
- **N14×N21**: a suspended sole consumer strands parked `Owned` and un-released `Leased`
  (20/23 §The four contracts, §Implementation).
- **N16×N21**: a `PartitionedCell`'s single merging outlet has no per-key interest
  (20/24 §Partitioned state).
- **N17×N21 / N20×N21**: indefinite suspension leans on the unbuilt disk overflow mailbox
  (30/33 §Stale references; 20/24 §Durability; 90/91 G-25).
- **N18×N21**: how bands compose with the implemented `(priority,sequence)` FIFO and
  management-preempts-data (30/31 §The host protocol; 30/34 §Decisions decision 2).
- **N19×N21**: attention (demand) vs backpressure (supply) meet at
  `enqueueHostedInvocation` with no stated precedence (30/32 §Bridges; 30/34).
- **N21×N23**: does a promoted instance inherit attention or start suspend-eligible at
  zero (10/11 §Identity; I-2)?
- **N21×N25**: a graph mid-construction has no sinks → no attention → immediate quiescence
  (50/51 §Graph construction DSL; 00/02 P6).
- **N21×N26**: a live invariant pins its subgraph awake forever; the wall-clock window is
  untestable in a harness with no virtual time (50/52 §Live invariants, §Invariant testing).
- **N21×N27**: does a shadow subscription mint *real* upstream interest — inflating
  production, or being suspended mid-evaluation (50/53 §Model; 30/34 §Principle)?

**Why the spec leaves it open**: 90/91 G-6 marks the *machinery* Resolved (M6) —
`AttentionPolicy` band dispatch, the stride floor, NONE-window park/replay — but 30/34
§Decisions gives only two floors (decision 2) and the region-atomic veto (decision 3).
Every list above is a *composition* of that machinery with another subsystem, and 30/34
itself flags the residuals ("attention does not cross the wire … notices are single-hop").
A resolution must state the precedence rules *on top of* the shipped enforcement arm.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P6 vs P4/P2 authority conflicts.** Attention *is* the interest signal (P6, the
  exemplar), so the naive move is to let a band directly set priority and directly
  trigger suspend. But that lets demand override authorities that must win regardless of
  interest: management reconfiguration (must never be starved, 30/31), backpressure (a
  full intake must refuse the *most*-wanted task too), exclusivity (a lease must be
  released even by a cell no one is watching, 20/23), and correctness of a half-built or
  under-evaluation subgraph. A single "attention = priority" rule is *semantically wrong*
  at each of those seams.
- **The policy window is a state machine, not a threshold.** "0 for a window → suspend"
  hides three transitions: born-at-zero (construction, N25), fell-to-zero-then-renewed
  (mid-window and mid-drain, N6/N20), and stayed-zero-indefinitely (N17). Level-triggering
  on NONE-ness conflates all three and quiesces graphs that were never meant to sleep.
- **Fusion makes the message path and the attention topology diverge (P2).** Banding is a
  property of *queued* tasks, but a fused chain and a delegated-away cell have attention
  presence with no queue presence (N5). The enforcement model must not assume they
  coincide.
- **Two unbuilt mechanisms are load-bearing.** Indefinite suspension (N17/N20) leans on
  the disk overflow mailbox (G-25) and backpressure (N19) leans on bounded intakes
  (30/32, no milestone). The resolution must give a *bounded* story that does not *require*
  either to be built first.
- **P10/P6 forbid bespoke patches.** Twelve edge cases invite twelve flags
  (construction-flag, shadow-flag, invariant-flag, lease-flag …). That proliferation is
  the anti-pattern; the precedence *between* patches would then be the new gap.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Attention as direct scheduler control (level ⇒ priority ⇒ suspend)

A cell's band directly sets its queue priority and NONE directly triggers suspend, with
no interposed authority.

- *Semantics*: the M6 sketch read literally; attention *is* the schedule.
- *Fast-path cost*: cheap — a band read at enqueue.
- *Failure modes*: attention can lift data above management (violates the
  management-preempts-data invariant, 30/31); a full bounded intake could be forced to
  admit a HIGH task (violates backpressure safety, 30/32); a suspended lease-holder
  strands the pool (20/23); a never-attended under-construction subgraph is quiesced
  mid-build (N25); a shadow that mints real demand inflates production (N27). No precedence
  handling at all.
- *Tradeoff*: matches the naive reading of 30/34; breaks P5 composition at every seam.
  **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — Per-concern patches (one rule per edge case)

Give each seam its own escape: a `UnderConstruction` flag, a `Shadow` flag, an
`Invariant` flag, a `LeaseHeld` flag, a mid-drain-abort path, a per-partition attention
field, etc.

- *Semantics*: each member pair gets a targeted fix.
- *Fast-path cost*: acceptable individually.
- *Failure modes*: the *precedence between* flags is undefined (does `Shadow` beat the
  window? does a lease beat an explicit migrate?) — which is exactly the gap restated;
  marker proliferation violates P10; nothing composes (a new edge case needs a new flag).
- *Tradeoff*: locally plausible, globally the anti-pattern the task forbids. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate C — Advisory attention + a fixed enforcement precedence lattice (recommended)

Attention is **advisory** — it proposes bands and suspend-eligibility; the host is the
**sole authority** and enforces through **one fixed precedence lattice at one seam**
(`enqueueHostedInvocation` + the per-step suspension check). Every "keep awake" duty is
expressed as either `setSelf` attention (I-4) or a `NonSuspendable` veto (30/34 decision
3) — never a bespoke exception. Suspension and backpressure unify as *intake-closure +
park/replay* at two triggers; disinterest propagates upstream (I-4) to bound parked
buffers; per-instance frontiers + relink-reannounce (I-2/I-4) handle promotion;
partitions-as-cells + an attention-routing proxy handle per-key interest.

- *Semantics*: `management > admission(backpressure) > suspension-gate(+vetoes) >
  attention-banding > (priority,sequence) FIFO`. Each layer acts only within what the
  layer above admits.
- *Fast-path cost*: unchanged from M6 — the data enqueue reads a band and a closed-intake
  volatile; the suspension check runs on the host `refresh` cadence, off the hot path
  (30/34 decision 1).
- *Failure modes*: none of the twelve tensions survive (§4); residual work is the two
  genuinely-deferred substrates (overflow mailbox, bounded intakes) and cross-host region
  quiescence, all bounded (§8).
- *Tradeoff*: gives up the illusion that a band is a schedule, in exchange for one
  lattice that makes every seam a placement in the order rather than a special case. This
  is 30/34's "the suspension machinery is the enforcement arm" made into an authority
  discipline. **Recommended.**

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**. Attention is advisory; the host enforces one precedence lattice;
"keep awake" is always `setSelf` or a veto. Twelve member pairs fall out of one authority
order plus ten rules, all riding shipped M6 machinery (`AttentionPolicy`, stride floor,
NONE-window park/replay) and the mobility park/replay of 30/33.

##### Data shapes (extend the shipped `ManagedHost` + `AttentionPolicy`)

```
// Bands (I-4 / M6, unchanged)
enum class Band { NONE, LOW, NORMAL, HIGH }

// Host queue key (shipped C-8): (priority, sequence). Base regions (30/31):
//   MANAGEMENT = 0, ROUTER = 10, DATA = 20, DRAIN_DONE = 30
// Attention refines ONLY the DATA region into sub-priorities:
fun dataPriority(band: Band): Int = 20 + (Band.HIGH.ordinal - band.ordinal)
//   HIGH→20, NORMAL→21, LOW→22 ; NONE is never enqueued as data (it is suspended)

// Per-region suspension gate (a region = 30/34 decision 3's glitch-free unit)
class SuspensionGate(val region: Region, val policyWindowSteps: Int /* host policy, default e.g. 64 */) {
    var band: Band                 // folded from members' AttentionFrontiers (I-4)
    var noneSince: Step? = null    // scheduling-step at which band last EDGE-fell to NONE
    fun vetoes(): Set<Veto>        // any non-empty set blocks AUTOMATIC suspension
}
enum class Veto {
    NON_SUSPENDABLE,      // 30/34 decision 3 marker (contagious across the region)
    ATTENDED,            // a member's band > NONE
    HELD_LEASE,          // a member holds un-released Leased payloads (20/23)
    CONSTRUCTION_LEASE,  // held by the graph builder / GraphSpec application (50/51)
    MGMT_ACTIVITY        // drain / migrate / promotion swap window in progress (30/33, 53)
}
```

##### The authority order (the lattice)

Enforcement precedence at the intake seam, **highest wins**:

1. **Explicit management operations** — `drainHost`/`migrate`/`resume`/`despawn`/
   `supervise` (30/31), and the promotion swap (53). Band 0, always-open inlet
   (30/33 §Stale references), **unconditional**. Attention and every `Veto` are about
   *automatic* suspension only; they never block or override an explicit operation.
2. **Admission / backpressure** — whether a data enqueue is *accepted at all*. A closed
   or full data intake refuses regardless of band; the sender parks and re-resolves
   (30/33). (Bounded intakes are future, 30/32; suspension is the one live trigger today.)
3. **Suspension gate** — attention NONE sustained for the window, *unless vetoed*.
4. **Attention banding** — among admitted, non-suspended data tasks, `dataPriority(band)`
   sets sub-priority within the DATA region, refined by the stride floor.
5. **`(priority, sequence)` FIFO** — the shipped base order, always preserved within a band.

**Advisory/authority split (the load-bearing move):** attention *proposes* (a band, a
suspend-eligibility); the host *disposes* (actual scheduling, honoring 1–2 first). This
keeps enforcement strictly local per host (P4): a host reads its own local attention
state and makes its own scheduling decision; attention never *forces* anything across a
host boundary (cross-host regions fall back to WAIT/DEGRADE — 30/34 decision 3, unchanged).

##### Enforcement algorithm

```
// data enqueue for cell C (hot path; management/router bypass this)
if C.dataIntakeClosed:                        // (2) admission: suspended or backpressured
    LocationRegistry.park(C, invocation)      //     park/replay, exactly as 30/33
else enqueue(dataPriority(C.band), nextSeq)   // (4) banding within DATA region

// per-step suspension check (off the hot path; host refresh cadence, 30/34 decision 1)
for region R local to this host:              // 30/34 decision 3 resolves the region
    if R.vetoes().isNotEmpty(): R.noneSince = null; continue     // (3) veto wins
    if R.band != Band.NONE:     R.noneSince = null; continue     //     attended
    if R.noneSince == null:     R.noneSince = currentStep        //     EDGE to NONE: start window
    else if currentStep - R.noneSince >= R.policyWindowSteps:
        drainRegion(R)                                           //     COMMIT: atomic per-region suspend
```

##### Rules the model introduces (normative)

**Rule A — Bands refine the data region only; management/router are inviolate.**
`dataPriority(band)` maps bands to sub-priorities *inside* region 20; attention can never
lift a data task to or above router(10)/management(0). The **stride floor** (shipped,
default 16, `∞` disables) services the oldest lower-band task by *sequence* every `stride`
higher-band dequeues, bounding starvation at `stride × task-time` without timers. `(priority,
sequence)` FIFO within a band is preserved. This is 30/34 decision 2 restated as a
composition rule answering N18×N21.

**Rule B — Fusion inherits the band of the entry task; delegated cells are attention-only.**
Banding is a property of *queued* tasks (30/31). A synchronous fused/delegated chain
(10/14, 20/21 §Fusion) runs entirely within the servicing of one dequeued task and
inherits that task's band — fused cells have **no independent queue presence** and need
none. A **delegated-away cell** (removed from the message path, 10/14 §delegate) remains
on the *attention topology*: its `AttentionFrontier` (I-4) still folds its downstream
links and re-emits upstream, so its producers see correct interest — it is an **attention
relay, not a data relay**. Scheduler-invisible + attention-visible is correct by P6 (no
message, no resource). Answers N5×N21.

**Rule C — Suspension and backpressure unify as intake-closure + park/replay.** A
suspended cell (Rule G, NONE sustained) and a backpressured cell (bounded intake full,
future 30/32) both close their *data* intake; senders park and re-resolve identically to a
moved host (30/33 §Stale references — one park/replay mechanism). **Admission is evaluated
before banding**: a HIGH-attention task is *not* exempt from a closed/full intake (supply
safety wins over demand preference, authority 2 > 4). The management inlet stays open under
both, so a suspended/backpressured cell remains administrable. This is "suspension = ONE
Buffering primitive" (30/33) extended to two triggers — demand-side and supply-side — with
one enforcement arm. Answers N19×N21 and gives N17/N20 their bounded seam.

**Rule D — Edge-triggered window + construction lease (the born-at-zero fix).** The
suspension window is **edge-triggered on the NONE transition**: a region that has *never*
been attended starts no window (`noneSince` stays null until a band actually falls to
NONE). A subgraph under construction is held `CONSTRUCTION_LEASE`-veto by the graph builder
/ `GraphSpec` application (50/51 — the builder already "applies immediately and records");
the lease releases when the block / spec completes, after which the standard NONE-window
applies to any still-unattended member. The window is counted in **host scheduling steps**
(30/34 decision 2), so it is fully deterministic in `SimulationController` — answering
N21×N26's "virtual time is omitted, the window is untestable": it is testable by *step
count*, not wall time. Answers N21×N25.

**Rule E — "Keep awake" is always `setSelf` attention or a veto — never a bespoke
exception.** Every subsystem that must hold a subgraph awake plugs into one of I-4's two
existing hooks:
- **Invariant monitors** emit via `setSelf` (I-4): a *passive* monitor emits NONE (default
  — it observes only while the subgraph is independently awake and catches up on resume via
  late-join, 20/21, tolerating observation gaps); an *active* monitor (liveness/security)
  emits **LOW**, pinning at LOW so it yields to real HIGH work under the stride floor. A
  monitor **never** pins at HIGH. Answers N21×N26 (aggregation = `max` over `setSelf`;
  damping = band quantization; fairness = stride floor — all inherited from I-4/M6).
- **A cell holding un-released `Leased` payloads** carries the `HELD_LEASE` veto (it is
  `NonSuspendable`) until phase-3 release-on-drain exists (20/23). When phase 3 lands,
  suspension releases leases in `onDeactivate` (the drain hook, 10/15) and the veto is
  dropped. Answers N14×N21 (interim: exclusive-lease consumers do not auto-suspend; the
  correctness-by-construction default).
- **Management activity** (drain/migrate/promotion swap window) carries `MGMT_ACTIVITY`
  against *automatic* suspension (the explicit op itself is authority 1). Answers the
  mid-drain fraction of N6/N20 and the swap window of N21×N23.

**Rule F — Mid-window renewal cancels; mid-drain renewal resumes (the fell-to-zero fix).**
Renewed attention *during the window* (before `drainRegion`) resets `noneSince` — the
suspend is cancelled (hysteresis). Renewed attention *after the drain commits* does not tear
the drain (drains run to completion, 30/33): the region parks, then **resumes emergently** —
30/34 decision 3's "renewed interest at any member propagates upstream … every member's own
band listener unparks it." So there is no torn state and no lost interest: window→cancelable,
commit→emergent-resume. An **explicit** management drain (authority 1) proceeds regardless of
attention; `resume` is then a separate management decision. Answers N6×N21, N20×N21.

**Rule G — Disinterest propagates upstream to bound parked buffers.** When a region
suspends, its frontier emits **NONE upstream** (I-4). Its producers, folding NONE downstream
attention, become suspend-eligible / stop emitting to the dead link — so parked traffic for
an indefinitely-suspended subgraph does **not** grow without bound in steady state, because
the *source* is quiesced by the same signal (answers N8×N21: producers stop, they do not
emit "just in case"). For the transient residual (in-flight at suspension, or from a
`NonSuspendable`/external producer): **mergeable/idempotent data cells MAY drop parked deltas
and re-catch-up on resume** — G-22 state-as-delta-from-empty + effective-only + OR-set tags
(20/21, 20/24) make this **lossless in effect**, so park-not-drop (30/34 decision 2) is
satisfied at the *effect* level without unbounded retention (see §6 for the disclosed
refinement; dropping is opt-in per the `Replicable` marker, default retains). **Exactly-once
payloads** (`Owned`/`Leased`) MUST be retained (30/33 constraint: "a parked `Owned` message
is still owned by the link"), bounded by host memory and spilling to the future disk overflow
mailbox as **move-by-serialize** (20/23 — the same degeneration as a cross-machine `Owned`).
This is the bounded story the overflow-mailbox gap was standing in for; it needs the mailbox
only for the exactly-once residual, not the common case. Answers N17×N21, N20×N21, and the
`Owned` half of N14×N21.

**Rule H — Promotion inherits attention by relink-reannounce; per-instance frontiers.** Each
instance has its own `AttentionFrontier` (I-4 rule 7; I-2 per-instance). A promoted candidate
does **not** copy a number: the swap relinks downstream subscribers onto the candidate's full
ref (I-2/53), each relink fires `onLinked`, and each subscriber **re-announces its current
