The single mechanism question: **when a host intake can refuse or delay an enqueue, what does that refusal mean, and who owns the traffic that is refused or parked?** Every host intake today is an unbounded `(priority, sequence)` queue, so a cross-host send is "one non-blocking offer" (30/32 §Bridges) and the four ADR-2 color bridges "degenerate" — "the asymmetry only appears when an intake can exert backpressure" and "the safety properties hold vacuously" (30/32 §Bridges). The spec defers bounded intakes / backpressure explicitly and **with no milestone** (30/32 §Bridges ⚠ GAP).

The gap is load-bearing because eleven other mechanisms quantify over exactly the refusal/delay condition it introduces:

- The link invariant demands accepted-before-unlink messages be "delivered or explicitly parked in a durable/inspectable place" (10/13 §Link lifecycle summary), but a bounded intake's refusal "is neither closure nor acceptance" — a third state the invariant does not name.
- Push grows a slow consumer's queue without bound (20/21 §Push); catch-up unicasts a snapshot-sized burst into that queue (20/21 §Pull); glitch-free version buffers hold per-wave inputs "with no stated bound" (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom); delta streams ride the same intakes (20/24 §Established pattern).
- Ownership transfer assumes "the cross-host send is one always-succeeding non-blocking offer" (20/23 §The four contracts) — a refused `Owned`/`Leased` enqueue has no owner-of-record rule.
- Membranes are specified "antiport-like: ingress/egress tied by backpressure" (10/11 §Membranes) with no substrate on either side (G-10).
- Cycles are absorbed only by unbounded intakes today; bounding them risks each host blocked on the other's full queue (20/21 §Cycles, G-19).
- Parked traffic is in-memory only — the disk overflow mailbox "remains with G-25" (20/24 §Durability spectrum) — so a host crash already breaks the parking half of the invariant (10/13 §Link lifecycle summary; G-25).

Current spec text leaves it open because 30/32 names the seam (`enqueueHostedInvocation`) and the mechanism (four bridges) but says nothing about *policy* — block, drop, park, or coalesce — and defers the whole question without deciding.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 vs bounded queues.** The steady-state fast path must stay "a volatile read and an enqueue" (P2). Any per-message backpressure check that is not fused into an already-paid read breaks the near-zero-cost guarantee.
- **P4 vs blocking.** ADR-2's literal bridge mechanisms are `BlockingQueue.put` / `Channel.send` — they *block the sender*. But a host has exactly one consumer thread (30/31 rule 1); blocking it is a local propagation lock over that host's whole cell set, which is precisely the SID-UP-style global-lock family that P4 and the recorded decision reject. Blocking is also the circular-wait that deadlocks a cycle spanning two bounded intakes (N10).
- **The no-loss invariant vs G-25.** 10/13 promises "delivered or explicitly parked in a durable/inspectable place," but durability is the unbuilt remainder of G-25 — parking is in-memory. Backpressure that grows the park re-creates unbounded memory somewhere else and worsens the crash-loss window.
- **Exactly-once vs retry/drop.** 20/23 makes `Owned` consume-once and forbids fan-out; a refused enqueue that is retried, parked, or dropped each interacts differently with `take()`.
- **Effective-only + convergent merge is an opportunity, not just a constraint.** 20/24 already requires delta merges to be commutative, associative, idempotent, and 21 requires effective-only emission. That is exactly the algebra that lets a queue *coalesce* instead of grow — the niche-first (P10) move — but it only applies to mergeable payloads, not to `Owned`/`Leased` or management calls.
- **Wave/topology causality.** Management preempts data (20/22 §Topology versioning; 30/31 priorities); under delay, data can be overtaken by link ops. The existing wave machinery tolerates this only if backpressure stays per-source-FIFO.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Block the sender (ADR-2 bridges made literal)

*Semantics.* At high-water the enqueue blocks: 🔵 sender `put`s, 🟣 sender `suspend`s in `suspendCancellableCoroutine`, exactly the ADR-2 table.

*Fast-path cost.* One volatile read of a saturation flag (fusable with the closure read). Zero cost when not full.

*Failure modes.* The blocking happens on the *sender host's single consumer thread*, so host A stops draining its own queue while waiting on host B — head-of-line blocking for all of A's cells (a local propagation lock, P4). Two hosts sending to each other's full intakes deadlock (N10). A 🟣 sender suspends the *whole* host (actor semantics, 32).

*Tradeoffs.* Faithful to ADR-2's letter; classic, well-understood; but violates P4 and re-introduces the cycle deadlock the challenge asks to avoid. Unusable as a default.

##### Candidate B — Refusal = temporary closure (park-and-re-resolve reuse)

*Semantics.* A saturated intake fails fast like a closed one (`IntakeSaturatedException`); the sender catches, parks in-order in its `LocationRegistry`, and replays at low-water. Refusal is "the intake is momentarily closed to this band."

*Fast-path cost.* The same volatile read as closure; the send *returns immediately* after parking — no consumer thread blocks.

*Failure modes.* Relocates the unbounded queue to the sender's park (still in-memory, still G-25). Bound must eventually bite at the sender.

*Tradeoffs.* Reuses an existing, proven mechanism verbatim; preserves P2/P4; no cycle deadlock (no blocking). But alone it just moves the memory hazard upstream — needs a termination story.

##### Candidate C — Coalesce via declared merge (delta-aware backpressure)

*Semantics.* For a contract whose delta declares merge (20/24), a saturated intake folds queued deltas into a per-source pending slot instead of appending. The queue is bounded by the number of sources, by construction.

*Fast-path cost.* Enqueue becomes a merge into the pending slot — O(1) amortized, a volatile read + a merge; only on the saturated path.

*Failure modes.* Only works for mergeable payloads — not `Owned`/`Leased` (can't merge exclusivity), not management (must not be reordered/lost), not value-complete streams where every intermediate matters. Cross-wave coalescing would collapse wave identity (breaks glitch-freedom) unless keyed by wave counter.

*Tradeoffs.* Niche-optimal (P10): the incremental-dataflow layer's whole point is that deltas merge, so a slow consumer simply sees fewer, larger, observationally-identical deltas. Provably loss-free and convergence-preserving for the set/counter family (associative merge + observed-remove tags). But it is a *partial* answer — it needs B for the non-mergeable remainder.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

A bounded intake carries a three-state lifecycle — `OPEN | SATURATED | CLOSED` — collapsed into the single volatile word the send path already reads for closure (30/33), so the steady-state fast path stays one volatile read + enqueue (P2). Bounding is opt-in per intake (`IntakeBound(highWater, lowWater, policy)`, default UNBOUNDED), except that any intake carrying a contract whose delta declares a merge (20/24) gets an implicit coalescing bound for free, giving the incremental-dataflow layer safety-by-default without configuration.

At high-water the intake flips to SATURATED and emits a `SaturationSignal` upstream on the attention/generic-protocol sub-channel (G-6/G-13) — a retractable notice, retracted when the queue drains below low-water. This is how backpressure PROPAGATES without any thread blocking: it is an interest-throttle (P6), the same shape as an attention notice, not a new protocol.

What a SATURATED send does is dispatched by the payload's contract class (read from the exclusive bit / merge metadata already in the generated `MethodDescriptor`), under ONE mechanism:

1. Mergeable delta (contract declares commutative/associative/idempotent merge, 20/24): the send FOLDS into a per-source pending slot instead of appending. The queue is bounded by the number of sources, never by traffic. Because merge is associative and emission is effective-only (21), `coalesce(d1,d2)` delivered once is observationally identical to `d1` then `d2` for any convergent consumer, and observed-remove tags dedup replays — so coalescing is loss-free and convergence-preserving. For waved/glitch-free traffic the coalescing key is `(source, wave counter)`, so distinct waves stay distinct (wave identity preserved) and only same-wave deltas merge — exactly what a glitch-free version buffer already does.

2. Exclusive (`Owned`/`Leased`) or non-mergeable payload: the send FAILS FAST with a distinct `IntakeSaturatedException` (a re-resolution signal, not a dead letter — mirroring closure), and the sender parks the invocation in-order in its own `LocationRegistry` park slot for that link, registering a low-water callback to replay. Owner-of-record for a refused exclusive payload is the SENDER's link: ownership has NOT transferred, `Owned.take()` on the receiver fires exactly once at eventual replay-delivery, and because the SPSC rule (20/23) guarantees one consumer there is exactly one park slot and no fan-out ambiguity. Drop is forbidden for exclusive payloads; cross-machine move-by-serialize happens at replay time (the wrapper is consumed once when the frame is built), `Leased` still refused at the boundary.

3. If the sender's own park exceeds its bound, the sender's intake saturates in turn — backpressure propagates as a chain of `SaturationSignal`s toward a throttleable source (attention, 34). Only if it reaches a boundary that can neither throttle nor park does it degrade to a visible dead-letter (never silent loss).

Management invocations (null context, priority 0, 20/22) are EXEMPT: the management band is never saturated and always accepted, exactly as the management inlet stays open on a CLOSED host (30/33). Consequently a management-triggered `onLinked` catch-up (21, M4.2) never blocks — the trigger runs on the management band and returns immediately, while its state-as-delta-from-empty EMISSION rides the data band and, being a mergeable delta, coalesces into at most one pending slot against any live deltas (idempotent tags keep the merged result correct). A snapshot-sized burst degrades to a single coalesced delta under backpressure rather than blocking or overflowing.

Block-the-sender (ADR-2's literal `BlockingQueue.put` / `Channel.send`) is REJECTED as the default: a blocked single-consumer host thread is a local propagation lock over that host's whole cell set (P4) and is the circular-wait that would deadlock a cycle spanning two bounded intakes. It survives only as an opt-in membrane policy (`Block(timeout)`) for explicit lock-step exchange, bounded by a timeout that degrades to Park. The ADR-2 bridges "become real" at `enqueueHostedInvocation` as the color-correct saturation handlers (park/coalesce always run on the sender's own color context, never crossing a blocking call into a coroutine or a suspension into a blocking thread) — the bridges' actual job (no color starves another) is honored, while the specific blocking-put mechanism is reinterpreted as non-blocking park/coalesce.

Cycles therefore never deadlock: the default (coalesce) is bounded and non-blocking, and the fallback (park-at-sender) returns immediately, so no consumer thread ever blocks on a full downstream — the circular-wait precondition is structurally absent. Coalescing additionally IS a magnitude-reducing operation, so a saturated cycle couples directly to G-19 quiescence: the merged pending delta shrinks below the magnitude threshold and the cycle stops emitting.

Causal/topology consistency (20/22) is preserved unchanged: backpressure is per-band (management preempts data as today) and per-source-FIFO-preserving (park replays in order; coalesce is per-source associative and carries each delta's `MessageContext`), so the existing wave-stamping + version buffering still see monotone per-source wave completion. Membrane antiport coupling (11, 43) is realized as a membrane object reading two ports' `SaturationSignal` flags and applying a cross-port rule (egress on A only while ingress B is below high-water) — no new substrate beyond the saturation signal.

Data shapes introduced: `IntakeState = OPEN | SATURATED | CLOSED` (one volatile word per intake); `IntakeBound(highWater, lowWater, policy)`; `SaturationPolicy = Coalesce | Park | Block(timeout) | Shed`, constrained by payload contract (exclusive forbids Coalesce and Shed; management exempt); `SaturationSignal(portRef, asserted: Boolean)` as a retractable management-band notice; a per-source (or per-source-per-wave) pending slot on coalescing intakes; the existing `LocationRegistry` park slot reused verbatim for the Park policy.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | Satisfied — saturation state lives on the host intake, coalescing is delta merge (a data-cell concern, 20/24), parking reuses the host `LocationRegistry`; kernel (cells/ports/links/invocations) untouched and expressible in the single-threaded `SimulationController` as a queue-length check + merge. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | Satisfied — the saturation check is fused into the volatile read already paid for closure; coalesce/park are the rare (saturated) path only. |
| P3 Explicit topology | Satisfied/strengthened — `SaturationSignal` is an observable signal on named ports; no hidden mailbox; membrane antiport reads it. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | Satisfied — coalesce and park-at-sender are local to a port/host and never block a consumer thread; block-the-sender is rejected as default *because* it is a local propagation lock. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | Satisfied — `SaturationPolicy` is constrained by the payload's exclusive/merge metadata (already in `MethodDescriptor`), so illegal combinations (coalesce an `Owned`) are rejected structurally. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | Satisfied/core — `SaturationSignal` is an upstream interest-throttle; bounding is opt-in; coalescing is bounded resource use. |
| P7 Open, local-first | Untouched — membrane backpressure remains a boundary control. |
| P8 Live evolution | Satisfied — bounds/policies are runtime-configurable per intake; topology events still wave-stamped. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | Satisfied — parked invocations are already wire-form; `SaturationSignal` and coalesced deltas are serializable. |
| P10 Niche first | Satisfied/core — coalescing-by-default for the incremental layer is the decentralized/incremental-optimal choice. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: coalesce and park are per-source; the coalescing key includes the wave counter so `(source, counter)` identity is preserved.
- **SID-UP global locks rejected** — Consistent/reinforced: block-the-sender-as-default is rejected for the same P4 reason.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: park-at-sender reuses the location-level `LocationRegistry`; no per-cell mobility protocol.
- **ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent (must state clearly): Park reuses that primitive verbatim; *coalescing is delta merge (20/24), not suspension/buffering*, so it adds no third suspension primitive.
- **Location = Local|Remote, one park/replay** — Consistent: refusal degenerates to "momentarily closed to this band," handled by the existing park/replay.
- **Snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: the catch-up burst coalesces precisely because it is a delta.
- **Merge tags are not wave ids** — Consistent: coalescing uses the merge tags for dedup; the wave counter is the coalescing key — the two clock uses stay separate.
- **Data push-only; management returns/null-context** — Consistent/load-bearing: the management band is exempt from data backpressure.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; no second sync protocol** — Consistent: backpressure rides the same links; `SaturationSignal` reuses the attention/generic-protocol band (G-6/G-13), not a new protocol.
- **Drain ordering invariant / per-link FIFO** — Consistent/extended: park replays in order and coalesce is per-source associative, so per-link FIFO holds; the invariant is extended to name the SATURATED state.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time; exclusive refuses fan-out** — Consistent: SPSC still guarantees one consumer, so one park slot, no fan-out ambiguity.
- **Owned cross-machine = move-by-serialize; Leased not cross** — Consistent: serialize happens at replay; `Leased` still refused at the boundary.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation)** — Untouched.

*No CONFLICT flags.* The only reinterpretation is of ADR-2's bridge *mechanism* (blocking put → non-blocking color-correct park/coalesce); this honors the bridges' stated purpose (no color starves another) and the recorded decisions do not lock blocking semantics, so it is a refinement rather than a contradiction — flagged here for visibility.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **30/32 §Bridges (degenerate…)** — Replace the "degenerate/vacuous" text with the saturation-signal mechanism; describe the four ADR-2 bridges as the color-correct saturation handlers at `enqueueHostedInvocation`, and record block-as-opt-in with the P4 rationale.
- **10/13 §Link lifecycle summary** — Add SATURATED alongside the suspended/closed states; broaden the no-loss invariant wording to "delivered, coalesced, or parked in a bounded inspectable place; a visible dead-letter on park overflow; crash-durability of the park awaits G-25 — never silent loss."
- **30/33** — Add the SATURATED intake state next to CLOSED; note refusal reuses the re-resolution/park path and that coalesce is merge (20/24), not the Buffering primitive.
- **30/31** — Introduce the `{OPEN, SATURATED, CLOSED}` intake state enum, per-band saturation, and the management-exempt rule; note the fast-path read is unchanged.
- **20/21 §Push / §Cycles** — Document coalescing under backpressure as effective-only-preserving, and the coupling of coalescing to G-19 magnitude/quiescence.
- **20/24 §Established pattern / §Durability** — State that the declared delta merge doubles as the coalescing operation via a per-source(-per-wave) pending slot; note coalescing bounds memory but does not close G-25.
- **20/23 §The four contracts** — Add the owner-of-record rule for a refused exclusive enqueue (sender's link retains ownership; `take()` once at replay; drop forbidden).
- **20/22 §Topology versioning** — Note that backpressure is per-band and per-source-FIFO-preserving, so wave-stamping/version-buffering are unaffected.
- **10/11 §Membranes / 43 §Authority** — Realize antiport coupling as a membrane reading two ports' `SaturationSignal` flags (a concrete first membrane cross-port rule for G-10).
- **90/91** — Give the un-IDed N19 backpressure gap a real ID marked "resolved-in-design"; keep G-25 (park durability) and G-19 (cycle quiescence formalization) open.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Park-overflow policy at an unthrottleable sender** — When backpressure reaches no throttleable source, the sender's park overflows; the terminal behavior (visible dead-letter vs Shed vs opt-in Block) and its tie-in to subtree quotas (G-28) need a concrete default.
- **Crash-durability of parked and coalesced-pending state** — Coalescing bounds memory but parked invocations and pending slots remain in-memory; the "durably parked" clause of the 10/13 invariant is satisfied only as "inspectable in memory" until the G-25 journal.
- **Coalescing under Map/List arrival-order convergence limits** — Must show aggressive coalescing of `MapDelta`/`ListDelta` is no worse than live streaming and does not widen the divergence window; likely resolved only under replication pressure (42).
- **SaturationSignal band** — Whether it reuses the attention band (G-6) max-aggregation/quantization or needs a distinct retractable-notice channel, and how a retraction races a late attention notice, is undesigned.
- **Cross-machine application backpressure vs transport flow control** — The wire bridge (40/41) has no flow-control frame; framing a remote `SaturationSignal` and reconciling it with TCP/WebSocket backpressure is unspecified.
- **Opt-in Block policy vs glitch-free waves** — `Block(timeout)` semantics and whether a timeout can strand a partially-complete wave at a glitch-free frontier need definition.
- **Formal quiescence of a coalescing cycle (G-19 coupling)** — Proving fixpoint/termination for a cycle of coalescing bounded intakes (merge idempotence + wave ids in cycles + magnitude threshold) remains the open G-19 research item.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

Confidence: **medium**. The mechanism composes cleanly from parts the spec already commits to (the closed-intake re-resolution/park path, delta merge with observed-remove tags, the management/data band split, the attention sub-channel), and it resolves all ten member pairs under one saturation-signal mechanism dispatched by payload class rather than per-pair patches. The cycle-deadlock and owner-of-record answers are structural and I hold them with high confidence.

Open questions lowering confidence to medium: (1) the reinterpretation of ADR-2's blocking bridges as non-blocking handlers is defensible but is a genuine softening of the original ADR mechanism and deserves an explicit ADR amendment rather than a quiet refinement; (2) durability (G-25) is not closed — the honest position is that backpressure reduces but does not eliminate the crash-loss window, and the invariant wording must say so; (3) the formal quiescence of coalescing cycles ties into G-19, which the spec itself flags as unresolved research, so I inherit that uncertainty; (4) whether `SaturationSignal` should literally reuse the attention band or be a sibling channel is a wiring decision I have proposed but not proven.

### I-13 — Stamping topology events into the wave domain: null-context management ops vs edge-set completeness

> Member pairs: N1×N13, N3×N13, N4×N13, N5×N13, N6×N13, N11×N13, N13×N18, N13×N20, N13×N22, N13×N24
> Existing gaps touched: G-20, G-12 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 2/10 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The whole mechanism: in-band EdgeOpen/EdgeClose markers on the link's own FIFO channel, the consumer-computed per-source floor completeness rule (prospective floors, pre-join discard, EdgeClose unblocking waiting waves), the rule that migration/re-resolutio…
> Reconciled after cross-check: swap invisibility qualified by the epoch guard: preserved-epoch relocations invariant; fresh-epoch successions wave-observable via the ReBaseline notice.

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The single mechanism question: **how does a host-applied link/unlink acquire a place in the wave-time domain, when the invocation that carries it is defined to have none?**

20/22 §Topology versioning requires that "Each link/unlink applied by a host is stamped into the same logical-time domain as data waves," and that "A glitch-free cell treats 'the set of edges feeding wave *t*' as part of wave *t*'s input completeness condition." But three implemented facts collide with this:

- Link/unlink travel as **management invocations**, which by the implemented rule "have null context and clear any stale wave" (20/22 §MessageContext rule 2; 10/14 §Context propagation; `HostedPortInvocation.Type.PORT_MANAGEMENT`, 10/14 §Dispatch tiers). The invocation machinery has *no carrier* for the stamp topology versioning demands.
- G-20 **abolished any global time domain**: wave ids are `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` minted by an *emitting outlet* (20/22 §MessageContext; §Topology versioning). A host-applied link event is not an emission from any wave-minting source, so **no `(sourceId, counter)` is defined for it**.
- The reconciling step is **unbuilt plan item 5** ("Topology events stamped by hosts (depends on Link objects, G-12)", 20/22 §Implementation plan). The static-frontier `GlitchFreeCell` dodges it by recomputing its edge set from *live* links on every completeness check (20/22 §The glitch-free frontier) — a read of *current* topology, not topology-as-of-wave-*t*.

Member pairs pulling on this one mechanism: N1/N5/N11/N13 (null-context management op must yet acquire a wave stamp), N3×N13 (link management is slated to ride multiplex ports as a stacked protocol — does a protocol-carried link event get wave-domain order?), N13×N18 (the management band preempts queued data — which wave's edge set does a preempting link op join?), N6×N13 and N13×N20 (drain step 4 "needs no code in-process"; are drain/resume stamped topology events?), N13×N22 (remote link/unlink has no defined causal order against data frames on the same bridge), N13×N24 (replication makes edge churn routine — gossip links appearing, evicted replicas' edges vanishing mid-wave).

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P4 (no global clock/barrier) vs the demand for a total order.** The intuitive fix — give topology events a global sequence so every consumer agrees which wave they precede — is exactly the SID-UP global lock that is REJECTED (20/22; recorded decision). G-20's per-source waves mean there is no clock to hang a topology event on.
- **The null-context rule (P5, correctness-by-construction) vs the stamping requirement.** Management invocations are null-context *by design* — they must not be mistaken for data waves, and they clear stale waves. Minting a wave id for them would re-pollute the context they were deliberately kept out of (10/12 data/management split; decided: "management invocations carry null context").
- **P2/P6 (near-zero-cost, interest-driven) vs universal stamping.** Most cells are not glitch-free and process eagerly with zero coordination (20/22 §The glitch-free frontier). A stamping mechanism that taxes every outlet emission or every link op regardless of downstream interest violates the fast path.
- **P1 (concurrency-free kernel) vs distributed reconfiguration.** "Which wave's completeness contains the pre- vs post-migration edge set" must be meaningful in single-threaded simulation, yet migration bursts, bridge frames, and gossip churn are inherently multi-host.
- **The management band preempts data (30/31).** Preemption is desirable (reconfiguration is never starved) but means a link op is *out of band* with respect to the data whose edge set it changes — the very ordering topology versioning needs is the ordering preemption removes.
- **Convergence, not simultaneity, across sources (G-20).** A topology event that is "its own source" cannot be aligned per-wave with data sources without an explicit coordinator — the coordinator the challenge notes is unspecified ("the unspecified coordinator of seed 12").

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Topology as its own wave source (synthetic wave lane)

Mint, per host (or per outlet), a dedicated source id and stamp each link op as a wave `Timestamp(topologySourceId, counter)`. Topology events become first-class waves; glitch-free cells treat the topology lane as another input.

- *Semantics*: link ops re-enter the wave domain literally; downstream cells join the topology lane with their data lanes.
- *Fast-path cost*: one counter bump per link op (cheap; link ops are rare, P2-compatible).
- *Failure modes*: the topology lane is a **different source** from the data sources, so by G-20 a glitch-free cell gets only *convergence* between "topology wave" and "data wave" — it cannot know *which* data wave a topology change precedes without an explicit coordinator. This reintroduces the exact alignment problem it set out to solve. It also violates the null-context rule (management ops would now carry context) and taxes cross-source joins everywhere.
- *Tradeoff*: conceptually uniform, but pushes the hard part (cross-source alignment) into every join and breaks a recorded decision. Rejected as the primary mechanism.

##### Candidate B — In-band per-link structural markers with a consumer-computed per-source floor *(recommended)*

The management invocation stays null-context; its **effect** injects a structural marker (`EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`) into the affected link's own FIFO data channel. The marker carries no wave id; its "logical time" is a **per-source floor** the consumer computes from its own flushed high-water when it processes the marker. Per-link FIFO (30/31, 30/33) plus the consumer's single-host serialization (management preempts data) supply the ordering.

- *Semantics*: a link, once opened for source *s*, carries every subsequent *s*-wave; the marker tells the consumer *from which counter* to start expecting it, prospectively. Migration/re-resolution/instance-swap are not markers (logical edge set invariant). Mergeable consumers ignore the floor.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero for non-glitch-free consumers (emission gated on downstream topology-order interest, P6); one map read + enqueue unchanged for data; markers are rare (link-time only).
- *Failure modes*: a newly-added link whose upstream path does not actually disseminate a source can leave a glitch-free consumer waiting for a contribution that never comes (liveness gap — see §8); needs downstream source-set propagation for multi-hop changes.
- *Tradeoff*: satisfies the letter of "same logical-time domain" (floors are per-source counters) without minting wave ids for non-emissions; keeps null-context intact; localises the hard case to explicit coordinators. Best fit to the principles.

##### Candidate C — Local topology-epoch drain (quiesce-then-reconfigure)

Each topology change bumps a per-consumer epoch; the consumer *drains* (flushes all in-flight waves under the old frontier) before admitting data under the new frontier.

- *Semantics*: a purely **local** barrier — no global lock — that separates waves into pre-change and post-change epochs.
- *Fast-path cost*: none in steady state; on change, a local drain.
- *Failure modes*: the drain waits for in-flight waves, so a slow upstream stalls reconfiguration; it cannot represent overlapping frontiers (a wave that legitimately spans the change is forced to one side); coarser than needed.
- *Tradeoff*: simplest and robust for the local single-consumer case; a good **fallback** when a floor cannot be determined, but too coarse as the general mechanism.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Reconcile the null-context management rule with topology versioning by relocating the "stamp" from the invocation to its structural effect. The link/unlink management invocation stays null-context (unchanged, 20/22 §MessageContext); its effect emits an in-band per-link structural marker.

**Data shapes.** Introduce a downstream-directional generic protocol (a multiplex-port sub-channel, G-13) carrying:

```
sealed interface EdgeEvent { val link: LinkId }   // LinkId = stable (outletPortRef, inletPortRef) identity
data class EdgeOpen(link)  : EdgeEvent
data class EdgeClose(link) : EdgeEvent
```

EdgeEvents ride the **same link and the same per-link FIFO channel** as the data waves of that link. They carry no `(sourceId, counter)` of their own — the "logical time" of a topology change is expressed by the **per-source floor** the *consumer* computes when it processes the marker (below), drawn from the existing per-source wave counters. Topology events thereby sit in the same logical-time domain as waves (20/22 §Topology versioning) without a wave id being minted for a non-emitting event, closing the G-20 gap.

**Stamp identity & ordering.**
1. The stamp identity of a link op is `(LinkId, kind, per-source floor)`, where `floor(s)` = the downstream glitch-free consumer's flushed high-water counter for source *s* at the instant it processes `EdgeOpen(link)`.
2. Ordering vs data is **per-link FIFO end-to-end** (30/31 rule 3; 30/33 drain invariant): `EdgeOpen` is the first event on a new link, ahead of any data; `EdgeClose` is the last, after the final data.
3. The consumer applies the marker under its host's single-consumer serialization where **management preempts data** (priority 0 < 20, 30/31), so the frontier update lands strictly before any data enqueued after the topology op.

**Consumer (glitch-free) completeness rule.** A glitch-free fan-in cell maintains, per inlink, an OPEN/CLOSED state and, for OPEN links, the floor established at `EdgeOpen`. For wave `(s, t)` the expected-contributor set = every inlink *L* that is OPEN with `floor_L(s) < t`. Rules:
- On `EdgeOpen(L)`: set `floor_L(s)` = the cell's current flushed high-water for each source *s*; add *L* to the pending frontier of every in-flight wave with counter `> floor_L(s)`.
- Any arrival on *L* with counter `<= floor_L(s)` is a **pre-join** arrival and is discarded (idempotent; the wave closed before *L* joined — a legitimate linearization of "*L* joined at this point"). This makes consumer-computed floors safe even against a **lagging** upstream outlet.
- On `EdgeClose(L)`: drop *L* from the pending frontier of all in-flight waves (its contributions up to its last delivered wave already counted), **unblocking** any wave that was waiting on *L* — this resolves the wait-forever deadlock on unlink.
- Non-glitch-free (eager) and mergeable (CRDT) consumers ignore EdgeEvents entirely — zero fast-path cost (P2/P6). Emission of EdgeEvents is **gated on a downstream having expressed the topology-order protocol interest**, so outlets without glitch-free subscribers pay nothing.

**Migration / re-resolution / instance-swap are NOT stamped.** Topology versioning operates on the **logical edge set** — links bind `logicalId` (`CellRef(logicalId, incarnation)`). Host migration, wire re-resolution, and promotion instance-swaps (G-33) leave the logical link intact, so they emit **no** EdgeEvent. Per-link FIFO across the drain (messages accepted before closure delivered before those after re-resolution, 30/33) preserves the wave stream over the logical link; version buffers migrate as cell state (20/22 §Interaction). A glitch-free consumer's logical frontier is invariant across physical relocation. Only a genuine logical link/unlink is an edge event.

> **Reconciled** (post-consistency-check): this invisibility is qualified by the epoch guard of I-14 Rule S1. It holds as stated for **preserved-epoch** relocations (suspend/resume, migration, T0/T1 promotion adoption per I-11/I-27). A **fresh-epoch succession** of a live lane (T2 promotion, RESTART) still emits no `EdgeEvent` — the logical edge set is intact — but it **is** wave-observable: the `ReBaseline` supersession notice (I-22) is the event by which a glitch-free consumer recomputes its per-source completeness set (I-14 Rule S5).

**Replication.** Gossip links between replicas *are* logical edges and do emit `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`, but replicated inputs are the mergeable class, whose consumers converge regardless of edge set and therefore ignore the floor — so gossip edge churn is **invisible** to wave completeness (answers the replication-churn concern, N13×N24). No second protocol: EdgeEvents ride existing dataflow links (40/42, decided).

**Cross-source joins & the coordinator.** Per G-20, distinct sources give convergence, not simultaneity; a topology change concurrent with in-flight waves from an *independent* source path likewise gives convergence, not per-wave glitch-freedom. Where strong per-wave ordering across a topology change is required, insert an **explicit coordinator cell** at the join: it serializes the reconfiguration stream with the data streams by routing both through its single host queue (management-preempts-data), converting convergence into simultaneity for that join. This is the previously-unspecified "seed-12 coordinator": a topology-serializing *JoinBarrier* cell, not a global mechanism.

**Bridged links.** For a cross-host/wire link, `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` are ordinary frames on the link's bridge channel (a new `WireFrame` event type), inheriting per-link FIFO over the wire against data frames; on disconnect, `unpublishRemotes` parks senders (40/41) and reconnect replays in order — no synchronous handshake reply is required (consistent with the deferred cross-host handshake decision, 10/13).

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — EdgeEvents are ordinary in-band invocations on links; the completeness rule is a per-cell fold, meaningful in single-threaded simulation. Kernel untouched (fold lives in the `GlitchFreeCell` decorator, per plan item 3). |
| P2 near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — no per-emission bookkeeping; markers are link-time only; emission gated on downstream interest; data path unchanged (map read + enqueue). |
| P3 explicit topology | **Satisfied** — topology changes become first-class, inspectable events flowing on the very links they concern. |
| P4 local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global clock/lock; ordering derives from per-link FIFO + per-consumer host serialization; coordinator is a local, opt-in cell. |
| P5 correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — stamp is structural (marker on the link), not runtime discipline; null-context stays a type-level invariant. |
| P6 interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — EdgeEvents materialise only where a glitch-free/topology-interested downstream exists. |
| P7 open/local-first | **Untouched.** |
| P8 live evolution | **Satisfied** — mechanism exists precisely to keep completeness correct under runtime topology change. |
| P9 serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` are plain serializable values (LinkId = port-ref pair); a new `WireFrame` event type carries them ids-only. |
| P10 niche first | **Satisfied** — resolves in favour of incremental, long-lived, decentralized reconfiguration over global-order simplicity. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 (per-source waves; convergence not simultaneity; no coordinator):** consistent — floors live in the per-source counter domain; cross-source strong ordering is the *explicit coordinator cell*, exactly G-20's escape hatch.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED:** consistent — no global order introduced.
- **Host is the unit of mobility:** consistent — migration is not an edge event; logical frontier invariant.
- **Suspension = one Buffering primitive:** consistent — version buffers migrate as cell state, unchanged.
- **Location = Local|Remote; one park/replay:** consistent — bridged EdgeEvents inherit park/replay, no new re-resolution path.
- **Snapshot IS a delta:** consistent — late-join catch-up is floored at `EdgeOpen`, delivered as a pre-wave baseline (partially aligns 21's currently-unwaved catch-up).
- **Management contracts null context:** **consistent — this is the crux**: the invocation stays null-context; the stamp is on the derived marker, not the invocation.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links; no second sync protocol:** consistent — EdgeEvents ride existing links/multiplex protocol.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved:** consistent — EdgeEvents are a new ids-only frame type under the reserved version byte.
- **Drain ordering invariant / per-link FIFO end-to-end:** consistent — reused as the ordering foundation.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time:** consistent — EdgeOpen fires only for links that passed the handshake.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId:** consistent — the mechanism *depends* on this: topology versioning is over logical links, so instance swaps are transparent.
- No CONFLICT flags.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/22 §Topology versioning & §Implementation plan (item 5):** rewrite item 5 from "topology events stamped by hosts (mint a wave id)" to "topology events emitted as in-band per-link `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` markers; the stamp is a consumer-computed per-source floor." Add the completeness rule (prospective floor, pre-join discard, EdgeClose unblocking) to §Local glitch-freedom rule 4 and §The glitch-free frontier (replacing "recomputes its edge set from live links" with "folds EdgeEvents into the frontier").
- **20/22 §MessageContext:** add a note that management ops stay null-context and that their *effect* carries the topology stamp — closing the apparent conflict in-document.
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports:** register the downstream-directional **topology-order** generic protocol alongside attention (upstream) and link-management; note directionality (travels *with* data).
- **10/13 §Links:** state that a successful `onLink`/`onUnlink` on a topology-interested edge emits `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`; migration/instance-swap re-resolution do not.
- **30/33 §The drain protocol (step 4):** clarify that step 4 emits **no** EdgeEvent — the logical edge set is invariant; the wire-boundary "real work" is physical re-resolution, not a topology-version event.
- **40/41 §Wire layer:** add an `EdgeEvent` `WireFrame` type and its per-link-FIFO ordering vs data frames and behaviour across park/replay.
- **40/42 §What replication must mean:** note gossip edges emit EdgeEvents but mergeable consumers ignore the floor.
- **91 gap-analysis:** mark G-12/G-20 plan-item-5 dependency addressed by this mechanism; add the new gaps below.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Per-source floor representation and source-horizon retention** — bound the floor map size; compaction/horizon rule for idle sources; behaviour when a link reopens a long-idle source.
- **Downstream propagation of source-set changes and added-link liveness** — a multi-hop upstream cut/add must ripple EdgeEvents downstream hop-by-hop (generalising plan-item-4 / G-13 upstream traversal to downstream source-set deltas); a liveness proof that a consumer never waits forever for a wave a newly-added link will never carry.
- **Topology-serializing coordinator (JoinBarrier) cell contract** — concrete capture/release/cost design for the seed-12 coordinator.
- **Bridged EdgeEvent frame type and reconnect ordering** — pin the `WireFrame` event type, its ordering vs data and `RegistryAnnounce` frames, and its park/replay behaviour.
- **Floors, cycles, and pre-join-discard vs merge tags** — interaction with open cycle semantics (G-19); document that pre-join discard touches only glitch-free wave completeness and never drops OR-set tags for mergeable cells.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

Confidence **medium**. The core reconciliation — keep the management invocation null-context and put the stamp on an in-band per-link marker whose logical time is a consumer-computed per-source floor — is robust, principle-consistent, and resolves every member pair under one mechanism. The **local** guarantee (consumer-local reconfiguration serialized at the consumer's host) is airtight: prospective floors plus management-preempts-data mean a newly opened link never retroactively invalidates a flushed wave.

Open questions I could not fully close within the fixed decisions:
1. **Added-link liveness** in the fully-distributed case: a glitch-free consumer that adds an inlink expects it for every future wave above the floor, but the link only carries waves its upstream path disseminates; without downstream source-set propagation (gap 2 above) the consumer can stall. The proposed remedy (hop-by-hop EdgeEvents + Candidate C's local-epoch drain as the fallback when no floor can be computed) is sketched, not proven.
2. **Independent concurrent reconfiguration racing with in-flight waves from another source** genuinely yields only convergence, not per-wave glitch-freedom — I treat this as *correct by G-20* (the coordinator cell is the strong-ordering escape hatch), but a reader expecting universal glitch-freedom under arbitrary churn should note this is a deliberate limit, not an oversight.

### I-14 — Wave-source and tag identity: do (sourceId, counter) streams follow the logical cell or the instance, and do counters survive?

> Member pairs: N11×N17, N11×N23, N11×N24, N11×N27, N12×N23, N12×N24, N13×N23, N15×N23, N15×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-20, G-8, G-23 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 9/9 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The wave half as recorded rules: S1/S2 (emission-epoch minting; sourceId per (outlet, epoch) of an instance, never logicalId), the ReBaseline supersession notice for fresh epochs superseding live lanes, S4's origination boundary at Replicable merge re-emiss…
> Reconciled after cross-check: Rule S1 gains the drain-captured adoption clause (T0/T1 promotion preserved-epoch); Rule S5 visibility now conditional on the epoch guard.

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The single mechanism question: `Timestamp(sourceId: UUID, counter: Long)` is one
clock shape put to **two** uses — wave ids (glitch-free per-`(source, counter)`
buffering) and OR-set merge tags (unique-per-add causal metadata) — and the spec
fixes neither the *identity level* of `sourceId` (logical cell vs instance vs
finer) nor the *durability* of `counter`. `20/22 §MessageContext` mints wave ids
"from the emitting outlet's own monotonic counter" (G-20) and `20/24 §Established
pattern` mints tags "cell-locally … unique per add instance," but under the I-2
identity model — one `logicalId` with many live `instanceId`s (replicas 42,
candidates 53) — three things are undefined:

1. **Identity level.** Does `sourceId` name the logical cell (all instances share
   one stream), the instance, or something finer? `10/11 §Identity and persistence`
   (G-8) splits `CellRef(id, instanceId)` but says nothing about what the *wave/tag*
   source keys on. `40/42 §Constraint on everything else` forbids assuming "exactly
   one live instance," so a single per-logical stream is suspect.
2. **Counter durability.** Neither the `Stateful` snapshot half nor the G-25 journal
   proposal (`20/24 §Durability spectrum`) states that outlet counters are captured.
   A recovered source that resets its counter re-mints already-used `(sourceId,
   counter)` pairs — corrupting downstream per-wave buffering and colliding OR-set
   tags (`20/22 §MessageContext` × `20/24 §Durability spectrum`).
3. **Behaviour under multiplication/replacement.** Whether a replica re-emitting a
   gossiped delta preserves the origin wave or originates afresh (`40/42 §What
   replication must mean` × `20/22 §MessageContext`, listed open in 42), whether a
   promoted incarnation inherits its predecessor's source (`50/53 §Mechanical
   decomposition` × `20/22 §Topology versioning`), whether glitch-free completeness
   quantifies over logical or per-instance edges (`20/22 §The glitch-free frontier`),
   and whether tags survive an instance swap identically (`50/53 §G-33` × `20/24`).

**Member pairs** (all TENSION): N11×N17 (counter durability across restart/journal),
N11×N23 (sourceId = instance or logical; counter across re-incarnation), N11×N24
(replica re-emission: preserve origin wave or mint fresh), N11×N27 (promoted
incarnation inherits source or mints fresh; journal-replay reinjection), N12×N23
(frontier over logical or instance edges), N12×N24 (diamond guarantee downstream of a
replicated arm), N13×N23 (is an instance swap a topology event a wave must observe),
N15×N23 (OR-tag sourceId follows instance or logical), N15×N27 (tags survive an
incarnation swap identically or are re-derived).

**Why the spec leaves it open.** G-20 and G-23 are marked decided/resolved *for the
single-instance case*; the shape and its minting rules were written before the G-8
identity split (I-2) put multiple live instances and live swaps on the table. The
per-instance, per-recovery minting discipline is exactly the residue those decisions
deferred.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **G-20 vs per-logical intuition (P4/P6).** The naive fix — make `sourceId` the
  `logicalId` so "the cell" has one stream — needs a *distributed monotonic counter*
  across instances. That is global coordination (violates P4, P6) and contradicts
  G-20's explicit "no global time protocol; convergence not simultaneity across
  sources." Yet per-instance sourceIds "silently fork one logical wave stream," which
  the member pairs flag as a hazard.
- **Two uses, two durability needs, one shape.** Wave counters are *transient*
  propagation state; merge tags are *durable* state that snapshots, migrates, and
  gossips. A single "just persist the counter" rule over-serves waves and couples two
  independent opt-in concerns (glitch-freedom, durability) — but a single "always mint
  fresh" rule must be checked against OR-set/PN correctness where old tags must
  survive verbatim.
- **P2 vs journaling.** Persisting an outlet counter to guarantee no reuse taxes the
  emission path (P2 budgets it at "a volatile read + an enqueue") and makes wave
  correctness depend on a durable host (G-25 unbuilt) — wrong coupling.
- **I-2 already fixed the identity substrate.** I-2 decided full-ref addressing,
  `logicalId` as a grouping/continuity key only, and instanceId minted on
  replica/candidate but preserved on migrate/restart/suspend — and reinforced "each
  instance's outlet is a distinct source → two replicas are two sources → convergence
  not simultaneity." This resolution must be *one level finer* than I-2 (outlets and
  recovery epochs, not just instances) without contradicting it.
- **P1.** Whatever we pick must be a minting discipline on an existing field, not a
  new kernel primitive — meaningful in the single-threaded simulation.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Durable counters (journal the outlet high-water)

Persist each outlet's counter high-water-mark; restore it on recovery; keep `sourceId`
stable (e.g. `sourceId = instanceId`).

- *Semantics*: `(sourceId, counter)` never reused because the counter is durable.
- *Fast-path cost*: writing the high-water on/near every emission — violates P2 unless
  batched, and even batched it couples the emission path to durability.
- *Failure modes*: an in-memory (non-durable) host **cannot** provide it, so wave and
  tag correctness would break on any restart of such a host — coupling two independent
  opt-in concerns (glitch-freedom, durability). Does not by itself answer the
  identity-level question. Rejected as the primary mechanism; retained as an optional
  *optimization* for durable hosts (§4).

##### Candidate B — Epoch source ids (fresh id when counter continuity is unprovable) [recommended]

Never reuse `(sourceId, counter)` by minting a **fresh** `sourceId` whenever an outlet
cannot prove its counter continues monotonically from restored state; preserve merge
tags verbatim as data; re-originate wave envelopes at CRDT-merge outlets.

- *Semantics*: `sourceId` is per-(outlet, emission-epoch) of an *instance*; a fresh
  epoch (fresh id, counter 0) begins on cold start, RESTART, and new-instance spawn;
  the epoch (id + counter) is preserved across suspend/resume and migration (counter
  continuity provable).
- *Fast-path cost*: **zero** — a `sourceId` is minted once per activation (a rare
  operation, P2), and counter increments stay a plain volatile `++`. No journaling.
- *Failure modes*: source-id accretion in OR-set / PN state across many restarts (a
  space cost, deferred to compaction with G-25); a restarted upstream is a *new*
  source to a downstream glitch-free cell, whose stale partial-wave buffers for the
  vanished source must be reclaimed (handled by the relink every restart entails —
  a frontier recompute).
- *Tradeoff*: cheap, decoupled from durability, uniform across both uses; the cost —
  no cross-restart wave continuity — is *semantically honest* (a crashed-and-restarted
  source genuinely is discontinuous).

##### Candidate C — sourceId = logicalId (one stream per logical cell)

Make the wave/tag source the logical cell so all instances/incarnations share one
stream.

- *Semantics*: one wave stream and one tag namespace per `logicalId`.
- *Fast-path cost*: low, but requires a **distributed monotonic counter** across
  instances to stay collision-free and monotone.
- *Failure modes*: two instances minting `(logicalId, n)` for different adds collide —
  corrupting OR-set semantics — and interleave wave counters, breaking per-source
  monotone flush. The only fix is global consensus on the counter (rejected 20/22).
  Fundamentally incompatible with G-20's decentralized minting. Rejected.

**Recommended: Candidate B**, with Candidate A available as an opt-in durable-host
optimization.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **epoch source ids**. `sourceId` is neither the logical cell nor merely the
instance: it names a specific **outlet during one emission epoch** of a specific
instance. `(sourceId, counter)` is made non-reusable *by construction* — either the
counter provably continues (same id) or a fresh id begins a fresh epoch — so neither
use of the clock shape can ever collide. Merge tags carry causality; wave envelopes
carry glitch-free alignment; the two diverge only in *durability* (tags live in state,
wave counters are transient), and both obey one minting rule. The wire shape
`Timestamp(sourceId: UUID, counter: Long)` is **unchanged** (no wire impact, P9).

**Data shapes** (unchanged on the wire):

```
Timestamp(sourceId: UUID, counter: Long)          // unchanged
// Framework-side, per emitting outlet:
Outlet { sourceId: UUID, counter: Long }          // sourceId set at activation (§ Rule S1)
// A "source" = (outlet, emission epoch) of an instance; identified by sourceId.
```

**Rule S1 — Source minting (emission epoch).** An outlet mints a **fresh, collision-free
`sourceId`** (random, like `instanceId`; caller-chosen in deterministic tests) and sets
`counter = 0` at the start of each *emission epoch*. It preserves `sourceId` and
`counter` across an epoch boundary **only** when the framework restores a continuous
counter high-water for that outlet. Epoch boundaries:

> **Reconciled** (post-consistency-check): promotion moved from the unconditional
> fresh-epoch list to the guard-based split below — a COMMIT whose G-33 state transfer
> (T0/T1, I-27) carries each outlet's `OutletWaveState(sourceId, highWater)` inside the
> buffered swap window is *drain-captured exclusive continuation* and preserves the
> epoch (adoption, I-11); every fresh epoch that supersedes a live lane must announce
> itself via the `ReBaseline` notice (I-22).

- *Fresh epoch (new `sourceId`, counter 0):* cold start (first `onActivate`), RESTART
  supervision (restores a checkpoint that cannot prove the live counter high-water —
  `30/31 §Normative rules 5`), new-instance spawn (replica `42`, shadow-phase
  candidate `53`), and a promotion COMMIT **without** state transfer (T2, I-27).
  A fresh epoch that supersedes a live lane MUST be announced via the `ReBaseline`
  notice (I-22), naming the superseded `sourceId`s.
- *Preserved epoch (same `sourceId`, continued counter):* suspend/resume (same instance
  in place), migration (whole-instance move; the counter high-water rides in the
  migration payload beside the `Stateful` snapshot — the drain has already flushed
  in-flight waves, so continuity is trivial to carry), and a promotion COMMIT whose
  T0/T1 state transfer (G-33, I-27) carries each outlet's `OutletWaveState(sourceId,
  highWater)` inside the buffered swap window (I-11) — drain-captured exclusive
  continuation: the candidate adopts the incumbent's source lanes.

Result: `(sourceId, counter)` is never reused; every emission is under a strictly
increasing counter within a never-before-seen-or-continuing source.

**Rule S2 — Source identity level.** `sourceId` is per-(outlet, epoch) of an
*instance* — never the `logicalId`, and finer than a bare `instanceId` (a cell with
several emitting outlets, each with its own G-20 counter, has several source ids).
Distinct instances (replicas, candidates) and distinct epochs (post-restart) have
**disjoint** source ids. There is deliberately no single per-logical wave or tag
stream: cross-instance relationships are *convergence* (waves) or *tag-union* (merge),
never a shared counter. This is exactly I-2's "two replicas are two sources," pushed
one level finer to outlets and recovery epochs.

**Rule S3 — Tag preservation (data, not re-minted).** Merge tags are **data**. A
genuinely new *local* add mints a new tag under the cell's current source epoch
(Rules S1–S2); thereafter the tag travels **verbatim** inside deltas — copied
unchanged by gossip (`42`), by `Stateful.snapshot()`, by `StateMigrating.importFrom`
(G-33, `50/53`), and by state-as-delta-from-empty catch-up (`21`). A cell **MUST NOT**
re-mint tags for state it *received or imported*. Consequences: an instance swap
imports tags identically (downstream dedup unbroken); catch-up replay resends them
identically (idempotent by tag union); `PnCounterCell`'s "private per-instance source
id" is this same discipline — on restart a fresh epoch id opens a fresh PN column,
and pointwise-max merge across the old (durable, in-state) column and the new column
converges correctly without double counting.

**Rule S4 — Wave origination boundary.** Wave envelopes follow `20/22 §MessageContext`
rules 1–2 (origination mints a fresh wave; transparent flow preserves it) with one
clarification for replication: a `Replicable` cell re-emitting an *effective delta
after a CRDT merge* is an **origination point** — it mints a fresh wave from its own
outlet — because gossip convergence is carried by tags (Rule S3), not by wave
alignment. Ordinary transform cells relay waves transparently. Therefore replicas are
independent wave sources (convergence, not simultaneity), and **no source id
circulates around the gossip-mesh cycle** (avoiding the open cycle problem for gossip
traffic). This resolves N11×N24: the wave envelope is re-originated per replica; the
delta's tags are preserved end-to-end.

**Rule S5 — Frontier quantifies over sources.** The glitch-free completeness condition
buffers per `(sourceId, counter)` and therefore quantifies over **physical sources**
(per-outlet-epoch), not logical cells. When a logical upstream has several instances,
its outlets are several sources; the glitch-free cell gets **convergence** across them,
not the diamond guarantee.

> **Reconciled** (post-consistency-check): swap wave-visibility is now conditional on
> the Rule S1 epoch guard rather than unconditional.

A **fresh-epoch succession** (T2 promotion, RESTART) is wave-observable: the
`ReBaseline` notice (I-22) announces the superseded lanes and the frontier recomputes —
the incumbent's source epoch drops, the successor's fresh epoch appears — while the
buffered swap window (traffic-light, `33`) ensures no wave straddles the change. A
**preserved-epoch swap** (T0/T1 adoption, Rule S1) is invisible to versioning: the same
source lane continues monotonically, downstream needs no re-tracking, and the
glitch-free frontier is invariant (I-11, I-13).

**Derived member-pair bindings:**

- **N11×N17 (durability):** outlet counters need **not** be journaled for correctness —
  a fresh epoch on recovery makes reuse impossible. A durable host (G-25) **MAY**
  journal the counter high-water to *preserve* the epoch across RESTART (avoiding
  source churn and keeping wave continuity) — Candidate A as an opt-in optimization,
  never a correctness dependency. In-memory hosts are fully correct via fresh epochs.
- **N11×N23 (instance vs logical):** `sourceId` is per-(outlet, epoch) of an instance
  (Rule S2); same-`sourceId`-across-instances never occurs; per-instance "forking" is
  correct and intended (G-20: convergence across sources), not a bug.
- **N11×N24 (replica re-emission):** origination for the wave envelope, preservation
  for the tags (Rule S4/S3).
- **N11×N27 (promotion / journal replay):** a promoted candidate **adopts** the
  incumbent's source lanes when COMMIT transfers `OutletWaveState` (T0/T1, preserved
  epoch — Rule S1); a T2 candidate mints fresh epochs and announces supersession via
  `ReBaseline`; either way it imports tags verbatim (Rule S3, G-33). Journal-replay
  reinjection is safe:
  journaled invocations replay carrying their *originally recorded* `MessageContext`
  (P9) — i.e. **old ids for old content**, which downstream that did not roll back
  sees as `counter ≤` its high-water for that source and drops (waves) or absorbs
  idempotently (tags); genuinely new post-rollback content is minted under a fresh
  epoch and never collides.
- **N12×N23 (frontier level):** instance edges / physical sources (Rule S5).
- **N12×N24 (diamond over a replicated arm):** the diamond guarantee does **not**
  automatically survive replicating an upstream arm — replicas are distinct frontier
  sources with only convergence promised. To recover it, either subscribe a
  glitch-free consumer to a *single* instance, or insert an explicit **coordinator
  cell** (G-20's named escape hatch) that collapses the replica sources into one wave
  stream. This is a documented consistency change the developer opts into by
  replicating, not a silent glitch.
- **N13×N23 (swap as topology event):** only fresh-epoch successions — announced via
  `ReBaseline`, the frontier recomputes; preserved-epoch (T0/T1 adoption) swaps are
  invisible to versioning; the buffered window guarantees consistency either way
  (Rule S5).
- **N15×N23 (tag identity level):** tags follow the same per-(outlet/cell, epoch)
  source as waves (Rule S2/S3); coexisting instances and re-incarnations mint disjoint
  tags → no OR-set collision.
- **N15×N27 (tags across an incarnation swap):** preserved **identically** via
  `importFrom`/snapshot; re-derivation is forbidden (Rule S3); the catch-up-replay
  fallback resends the same tags idempotently.

**Optional durable-counter optimization (non-normative).** A durable host that already
journals invocations (G-25) MAY additionally persist each outlet's counter high-water
(batched, off the hot path) and, on RESTART, restore `sourceId` + `counter` instead of
minting a fresh epoch. This is a pure optimization (fewer source columns, cross-restart
wave continuity) layered on the always-safe fresh-epoch default; it changes no
downstream-observable correctness because both paths honour "never reuse `(sourceId,
counter)`."

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | satisfied — a minting discipline on an existing field; source minting hooks `onActivate`; meaningful single-threaded; no new primitive. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | satisfied — `sourceId` minted once per activation (rare); emission stays a volatile `counter++` + enqueue; no journaling on the data path. |
| P3 Explicit topology | satisfied — instance swaps and gossip links are explicit relinks; the frontier reads them as topology events; nothing hidden. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | satisfied — no distributed counter, no global clock/lock; convergence across sources is local per-`(source,counter)` buffering. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | satisfied — non-reuse is structural (fresh id or continued counter, never a reused pair); tag preservation is a copy-not-mint rule. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | untouched — sources exist only where an outlet emits; no "just in case" stream. |
| P7 Open, local-first | untouched. |
| P8 Live evolution | satisfied — swap/replica/restart are graph ops; a succession either continues a lane under the drain-captured guard (T0/T1) or begins an announced fresh epoch; nothing assumes a static source set. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | satisfied — `Timestamp` shape unchanged on the wire; no lambdas/handles; source ids are UUIDs. |
| P10 Niche first | satisfied — decentralized minting, convergence-over-simultaneity, and honest discontinuity on recovery are exactly the niche. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves:** reinforced — `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` per emitting
  outlet, refined by an emission epoch; no global coordinator; convergence across
  sources. Consistent.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED:** consistent — no distributed counter or propagation
  lock introduced.
- **Host is the unit of mobility:** consistent — migration carries the outlet counter
  in the whole-instance payload; the epoch is preserved.
- **Suspension = one Buffering primitive:** consistent — suspend/resume preserves the
  epoch; buffered waves survive as before.
- **Location = Local|Remote, one park/replay:** untouched.
- **A snapshot IS a delta:** consistent — tags ride state-as-delta catch-up verbatim
  (Rule S3); no separate snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps minted cell-locally, NOT wave ids:** strongly reinforced
  — tags and waves remain separate *uses* of one shape under one minting rule; they
  diverge only in durability (tags durable in state, wave counters transient).
- **Data push-only / management null context:** consistent — gossip deltas are data
  (carry a wave envelope); management is null-context; Rule S4 is a data-plane rule.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip, NO second sync protocol:** consistent —
  Rule S4 keeps gossip as ordinary dataflow with tag-carried causality; no second
  protocol.
- **Partitioning not a second distribution mechanism:** untouched.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved:** consistent — **no wire change**;
  `Timestamp` shape unchanged.
- **Drain ordering invariant, per-link FIFO:** consistent — per-`(source,counter)`
  monotone flush relies on per-link FIFO; the drain flushes in-flight before the epoch
  boundary at deactivate/activate.
- **Cardinality at link time; Owned/Leased rules:** untouched.
- **CellRef(logicalId, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2):** consistent — builds
  directly on I-2; `sourceId` is finer than `instanceId` and never the `logicalId`;
  the emission-epoch lifecycle parallels I-2's instanceId lifecycle one level down.
- **I-1 (metadata-plane, generic protocols null context):** consistent — waves/tags
  are data-plane; generic protocols carry null context and never mint waves, so this
  resolution does not touch them.
- **Gaps Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved:** consistent — elaborates G-20/G-23/G-8/G-33
  minting residue; reopens none.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/22 §MessageContext:** add Rule S1 (emission-epoch source minting), Rule S2
  (`sourceId` is per-(outlet,epoch) of an instance, never logical), and Rule S4 (the
  origination boundary: `Replicable` merge re-emission originates a fresh wave).
- **20/22 §The glitch-free frontier / §Topology versioning:** state Rule S5 — the
  frontier quantifies over physical sources; a logical upstream with several instances
  yields convergence not the diamond guarantee; an instance swap is a topology event
  the frontier recomputes over; the coordinator-cell escape hatch for
  diamond-over-replica.
- **20/24 §Established pattern:** state Rule S3 — tags are minted under the cell's
  source epoch and preserved verbatim across gossip/snapshot/importFrom/catch-up,
  never re-minted for received/imported state; note `PnCounterCell`'s per-instance
  source id is this discipline and a restart opens a fresh, safe column.
- **20/24 §Durability spectrum (G-25):** state that outlet-counter durability is
  **optional** — the fresh-epoch default is correct on in-memory hosts; a durable host
  MAY journal the high-water to preserve the epoch (the optional optimization).
- **10/11 §Identity and persistence:** cross-reference that `sourceId` is finer than
  `instanceId`; the emission-epoch lifecycle parallels the instanceId lifecycle (I-2).
- **40/42:** state that a replica re-emitting a gossiped delta originates a fresh wave
  while carrying tags verbatim; gossip convergence is tag-based, not wave-based (closes
  the "reuse wave-context or OR-set ids as causal metadata" open item).
- **50/53 §G-33 / §Mechanical decomposition:** state that `importFrom` copies tags
  identically, the candidate mints fresh source epochs for new emissions, and
  journal-replay rollback reinjects old ids only for old (idempotent) content.
- **30/31 §Normative rules 5:** note RESTART mints a fresh source epoch (the spawn-time
  checkpoint lacks the live counter); the source-minting hook lives at `onActivate`.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Source-id / tag compaction under epoch churn.** Frequent restarts accrete source
  columns in OR-set / PN state (and stale source buffers in glitch-free cells);
  compaction — safe reclamation of provably-superseded epochs — is unaddressed and
  ties to G-25 durability.
- **Coordinator cell for diamond-over-replica.** The explicit coordinator that
  collapses replica sources into one wave stream (so a consumer regains the diamond
  guarantee over a replicated arm) is named (G-20 escape hatch) but undesigned.
- **Frontier GC on source churn.** How a glitch-free cell evicts partial-wave buffers
  for a vanished source epoch (a restarted upstream's old `sourceId`); relink-driven
  frontier recompute is the trigger, but the eviction policy for orphaned partial waves
  is unspecified.
- **Durable-counter optimization design.** The journaling-host path that preserves an
  epoch across RESTART (Candidate A) needs a concrete batching discipline that keeps
  the high-water write off the emission hot path, plus the rule for how downstream
  tells intended continuity from a genuine new source.
- **Migration counter-carry.** The concrete migration-payload field carrying the outlet
  counter high-water (vs minting fresh) needs pinning, including whether migration is
  observationally a topology event downstream must causally order.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high.** The mechanism is a minting discipline on an unchanged field,
grounded in already-decided pieces: it builds directly on I-2 (adopted: two replicas
are two sources), honours G-20 (decentralized per-outlet minting, convergence not
simultaneity), and the OR-set / `PnCounterCell` "private per-instance source id" already
*implements* the tag-preservation half in shipped code. The never-reuse-by-fresh-epoch
trick is standard and requires no journaling, so wave correctness is decoupled from the
unbuilt durability layer (G-25). **Open questions:** (1) Rule S4 — treating a
`Replicable` CRDT-merge re-emission as a wave *origination* point — is the most novel
claim and should be validated against the shipped `GlitchFreeCell` × `Replication`
interaction (does any current test place a glitch-free consumer downstream of the mesh
expecting the diamond guarantee?); (2) the frontier-GC and coordinator-cell pieces are
deferred as follow-on gaps rather than resolved here; (3) whether any deployment
genuinely wants cross-restart wave continuity strongly enough to make the durable-counter
optimization non-optional (I argue no — honest discontinuity is the niche-correct
default).

### I-15 — Execution colors as data: where color lives and what validates it across fan-out, wire, replicas, and construction

> Member pairs: N1×N19, N2×N19, N17×N19, N19×N22, N19×N23, N19×N24, N19×N25, N19×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-3 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 3/8 member pairs findings need re-wording while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The normative single-boundary statement (color checked ONLY at admission; a cross-link color mismatch is a cross-host boundary, not an error, and never a link-time check); CellDescriptor.color generation (51 §Code generation and 41 point 2 still list color …

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The three-color model (30/32 §The three colors) classifies **logic** by execution
style — 🟢 Pure / 🔵 Blocking / 🟣 Suspending — and hosts by scheduler color
(🔵 `VirtualThreadScheduler`, 🟣 `CoroutineScheduler`). The one concrete enforcement
that exists today is **spawn validation**: "Explicit markers … exist so spawn can
validate host compatibility; a wrong-color spawn is rejected" (30/32
§Compatibility and coercion). Everything *else* the model touches is unspecified as
a data/enforcement surface.

**The single mechanism question**: *where is color represented as data — on
contracts, refs, links, `GraphSpec` placement metadata, or `WireFrame` — and which
boundary enforces it, uniformly across every composition surface?*

**Member pairs** each hit a different surface of that one question:

- **N1×N19** — a management contract may block on a future (10/12 §Contracts are
  push-only; 30/31 rule 4 blesses 5s waits) but 30/32 forbids blocking in a
  coroutine host: how does a blocking management call execute on a 🟣 host, and how
  does a bounded-intake refusal surface through a push-only contract?
- **N2×N19** — color coerces upstream (30/32), but a **pure** producer whose
  `FanOutlet` feeds subscribers of **both** colors has no defined coercion/placement.
- **N17×N19** — a durable host journals applied invocations (24 §Durability
  spectrum), which is blocking IO 30/32 requires on a virtual thread: what does a
  durable **🟣** host do?
- **N19×N22** — 40/41 point 2 commits generated proxies to "emit … color 30/32,"
  but proxies are still colorless JDK proxies, and color validation for
  spawn/migrate arriving over a **remote** `HostManagementApi`, plus the suspend-call
  continuation mechanics, are unrestated for the wire path.
- **N19×N23** — may two coexisting instances of one logical cell differ in color,
  when color propagates upstream along links that (per G-8 / I-2) bind logical
  identity?
- **N19×N24** — must a logical cell's **replicas** share a color, and are candidate
  hosts color-filtered (42 §Design as implemented is silent)?
- **N19×N25** — `GraphSpec` "replays onto any host" through **one** management inlet
  (51 §Graph construction DSL), yet a `BlockingCell` cannot replay onto a 🟣 host and
  mixed-color graphs are inexpressible in a single-inlet spec.
- **N19×N27** — promotion swaps a candidate behind links bound to logical identity
  (53 §Model), but a candidate whose color marker differs from the active one breaks
  the co-hosting/fusion assumption (30/32 §Compatibility and coercion: color
  propagates upstream to fuse chains).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: 30/32 is written as a *placement* rule (which cell
color may live on which host color) and a *degenerate bridge* note ("every host
intake is an unbounded `(priority, sequence)` queue, so a cross-host send — any
color to any color — is one non-blocking offer"). It never states where color lives
as **data**, so every downstream surface — `WireFrame` (40/41), `GraphSpec` (51),
`CellRef` (11 / I-2), replica placement (42), promotion (53) — inherited the model
without a defined color slot or enforcement point.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path)** vs a color-on-links reading. If color were a
  link/data property, every cross-color send would pay a bridge conversion on the
  hot path — but 30/32 already says a cross-host send is "one non-blocking offer,"
  and P2 budgets the steady state at a volatile read + enqueue.
- **P5 (correctness by construction)** vs runtime color checks. Color is already a
  *type* (`BlockingCell`/`SuspendingCell` markers). The pull is to keep it a
  compile-time/spawn-time structural fact, not a per-message runtime tag.
- **P1 (concurrency-free kernel)** — color is intrinsically about *concurrency
  realization* (threads vs coroutines), the one thing the kernel refuses to model.
  So color must live entirely in the **host** layer and never leak into kernel
  artifacts (links, refs, invocations).
- **Coercion-is-placement (30/32)** vs a pure cell feeding two colors. "Color
  propagates upstream" reads like a data-flow law but is actually a placement SHOULD;
  a pure producer feeding a 🔵 and a 🟣 subscriber cannot be co-hosted with both
  (🔵/🟣 never coexist), so a naïve "adopt the consumer's color" has no answer.
- **I-2's decided identity model** — `logicalId` carries *no* addressing or
  behavioral policy; it is a grouping/continuity key only. Color must therefore
  **not** become a logicalId-level attribute, or it re-introduces exactly the
  logical-level policy I-2 rejected.
- **P8 (live evolution)** vs frozen color. Candidates (53) are different *code* and
  may legitimately change color across incarnations; the model must allow it.
- **The deferred backpressure gap** (30/32 ⚠) sits under three member pairs
  (N1, N2, N17). The resolution must be correct in the current unbounded regime and
  cleanly *locate* where color re-enters once intakes bound — without solving
  backpressure here.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Color as a link / data-flow property (bridges everywhere)

The literal ADR-2 bridge reading: links are typed by `(senderColor, targetColor)`,
`WireFrame` carries a color byte, and every crossing converts.

- *Semantics*: color travels with data; each link/frame is color-aware.
- *Fast-path cost*: a bridge dispatch on **every** cross-color send — contradicts
  30/32's own "one non-blocking offer" and P2.
- *Failure modes*: a pure `FanOutlet` to mixed-color subscribers needs per-subscriber
  bridges; color on the wire bloats the ids-only frame (40/41); it conflates a
  *placement* concern with a *data* concern and forces every surface (links, refs,
  frames) to grow a color slot.
- *Tradeoff*: maximally explicit, but puts color on the hot path and violates P1/P2/P5.
  **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — Color as an identity / `logicalId` attribute

Color is part of the logical cell's identity; all instances share it; refs carry it.

- *Semantics*: "the cell's color" is a logical-level fact.
- *Failure modes*: directly contradicts I-2 (`logicalId` carries no behavioral
  policy) and P8/N19×N27 (candidates may change color); over-constrains replicas of
  *pure* mergeable cells (which can sit on any host); has no answer for a pure cell
  whose "color" depends on placement.
- *Tradeoff*: simple to state, wrong on evolution and identity. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate C — Color as a spawn-admission constraint on logic; links color-blind (recommended)

Color is a **static property of cell logic** (its marker), enforced at exactly one
boundary — the **spawn/activation admission gate** — in every guise it appears
(local spawn, remote spawn, migrate target, replica placement, `GraphSpec` replay,
promotion candidate). Links, refs, waves, `MessageContext`, and data-path
`WireFrame`s carry **no** color. A color mismatch across a link is never an error —
it is merely a cross-host boundary (an enqueue), because 🔵 and 🟣 logic simply
cannot be fused into one host. Host framework operations that touch color (management
await, journal IO) are realized *per scheduler color*, invisibly to callers.

- *Fast-path cost*: unchanged. Same-host links are direct calls (both cells passed
  the same host's gate → same color → color-safe); cross-host links are the existing
  single non-blocking offer (30/32 degenerate bridge).
- *Failure modes*: none of the eight member-pair conflicts survive (see §4); residual
  risk is confined to the already-deferred bounded-intake regime, where color-keyed
  bridges re-enter *at the crossing seam* as rare-path link metadata (§8).
- *Tradeoff*: gives up "color visible on every link/frame" (which the niche never
  needs — cross-color is just cross-host) in exchange for a model where every existing
  surface keeps its color-free meaning and one predicate at one gate covers all eight
  surfaces.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**: color is a static placement constraint on cell logic,
enforced only at the spawn-admission gate; links are color-blind; cross-color =
cross-host. All eight member-pair bindings fall out from one predicate plus seven
rules.
