**Data shapes**

```
enum Color { PURE, BLOCKING, SUSPENDING }        // PURE = unmarked cell
enum HostColor { VIRTUAL_THREAD /*🔵: BLOCKING+PURE*/, COROUTINE /*🟣: SUSPENDING+PURE*/ }

// Generated at compile time (KSP), alongside ownership flags (20/23):
CellDescriptor { color: Color; ... }             // lets a host validate WITHOUT instantiating

// The single admission predicate — the ONLY place color is checked:
fun admits(host: HostColor, cell: Color): Boolean =
    cell == PURE ||
    (host == VIRTUAL_THREAD && cell == BLOCKING) ||
    (host == COROUTINE      && cell == SUSPENDING)
```

Color-as-data lives in **exactly two places**, both off the data path:
(1) the cell's **marker** (a type — `BlockingCell`/`SuspendingCell`; unmarked ⇒ pure),
serialized as part of the cell / the `GraphSpec` `CellFactory` when it crosses a
boundary to be placed; and (2) the **generated `CellDescriptor.color`** (40/41
point 2's "emit … color," 51 §Code generation), which lets a receiving host validate
without instantiating. Color is **absent** from `CellRef`, `PortRef`, `Link`,
`MessageContext`, and the data-path `WireFrame`.

**Rules the model introduces (normative)**

1. **Color is a static property of logic, checked only at admission.** Every
   placement gate — local `spawn(cell)`, remote `spawn`/`migrate` over
   `HostManagementApi`, replica placement (42), `GraphSpec` replay (51), promotion
   candidate placement (53) — evaluates the *same* `admits(hostColor, cellColor)`
   and rejects on mismatch (dead-letter / `LinkResult`-style rejection back to the
   caller, reusing G-26 / G-12 rejection paths). There is no other color check
   anywhere in the system.

2. **Every link is color-safe by construction; color never gates linking.** Two
   colinked cells on the *same* host are necessarily the same host color (both were
   admitted there) → a direct call, color-safe. Two colinked cells on *different*
   hosts communicate by enqueue → color-safe by the degenerate bridge (30/32: "any
   color to any color — is one non-blocking offer"). Therefore a color mismatch
   between linked cells is **not** an error and **not** a link-time check — it simply
   means the link cannot be fused and is realized as a cross-host enqueue.

3. **PURE cells have no logical color; they adopt one only as a per-instance
   placement heuristic.** "Color propagates upstream" (30/32) is a placement SHOULD
   for co-hosting fusible chains (P2), not a data-flow law and not a logical-level
   attribute. A pure producer feeding a 🔵 and a 🟣 subscriber (N2×N19) is placed on
   one host, fuses with the same-colored subscriber, and reaches the other by a
   cross-host enqueue. If both fusions matter, replicate the pure cell (it is pure ⇒
   `admits` on any host, and pure logic has no merge hazard) — one instance per color
   neighbourhood.

4. **Coexisting instances MAY differ in color iff they differ in implementation.**
   Replicas (42) run the *same* implementation ⇒ one marker ⇒ one color (placed on
   color-compatible hosts). Candidate versions (53) are *different* implementations ⇒
   MAY change color. Color is an **instance/placement** attribute, never a
   `logicalId` attribute — consistent with I-2 (logicalId carries no behavioral
   policy). This resolves N19×N23: there is no "the pure cell's color" at the logical
   level to be ambiguous; each instance's color is whatever host it was admitted to.

5. **Replica placement is color-filtered; mergeable cells make it near-vacuous.**
   `Replication` (42) restricts candidate hosts to `admits(host, cellColor)`. Because
   the replicable/mergeable class (tagged set family, `PnCounterCell`) is **pure** —
   it only does tag/counter algebra, no blocking or suspending — its replicas admit
   on *any* host, so the constraint bites only if a marked cell is ever made
   replicable, in which case all its replica hosts must match its single marker color.

6. **Host framework operations that touch color are realized per HostColor,
   invisibly to callers.** The management-await (N1×N19) and durable-host journal IO
   (N17×N19) are **host machinery**, which already exists in two color flavors (the
   scheduler loop: 🔵 drains under `runBlocking`, 🟣 drains as a coroutine). A
   management contract that returns a value is realized with a **blocking `get`** on a
   🔵 host and a **suspend `await`** on a 🟣 host; a durable host's journal writer does
   **blocking file IO** on 🔵 and **suspend/offloaded IO** on 🟣. The *contract* and
   the *durability behavior* are color-agnostic; only their realization is colored,
   exactly as the scheduler loop already is. No color restriction on durable hosts is
   needed, and 30/31 rule 4's "5s blocking wait" is simply the 🔵 realization of a
   color-agnostic await.

7. **Suspend-call continuation mechanics cross the wire exactly as they cross
   in-process.** The trailing `Continuation` is stripped at capture (egress) and a
   fresh one re-supplied at delivery (ingress) — 30/32 §How the colors are realized,
   now stated for the bridge path. Because data contracts are push-only (10/12),
   nothing about the continuation needs to serialize (P9); the far host re-supplies it
   locally per its own color (a 🟣 target calls the suspend fun with a real
   continuation, a 🔵 target falls back to plain invocation). The `WireFrame` gains
   **no** color field.

**Derived bindings (each member pair, resolved under the rules):**

- **N1×N19 (blocking management on a 🟣 host):** Rule 6 — the await is host machinery,
  realized as a suspend on 🟣, a blocking `get` on 🔵; the management *contract* is
  color-agnostic and the caller (holding a proxy / `Deferred`, 40/41 point 5) is
  unaffected. The bounded-intake *refusal* is out of scope here (deferred
  backpressure); its **direction** (rule for §8): refusal surfaces as an
  **upstream metadata-plane notice** on I-1's protocol plane (the same channel that
  already carries suspension notices), never as a data-contract return — keeping data
  push-only.
- **N2×N19 (pure fan-out to two colors):** Rule 3 — place the pure cell once, fuse
  one color, enqueue the other; replicate the pure cell if both fusions matter.
- **N17×N19 (durable 🟣 host):** Rule 6 — the journal writer is host machinery in two
  color flavors; durability composes with either color.
- **N19×N22 (wire & color):** Rules 1 + 7 — color rides *spawn/migrate management
  payloads* (the serialized cell/marker + `CellDescriptor.color`), validated at the
  receiving host's admission gate exactly like local spawn; the data-path `WireFrame`
  stays colorless; continuation mechanics are stripped-at-egress / re-supplied-at-
  ingress. 40/41 point 2's "emit color" = emit `CellDescriptor.color` for the gate,
  not a per-message frame field.
- **N19×N23 (instance color divergence):** Rule 4 — color is per-instance/placement,
  never logicalId; instances may differ iff implementations differ.
- **N19×N24 (replica color):** Rule 5 — replicas share one implementation color; hosts
  are color-filtered; near-vacuous because mergeable cells are pure.
- **N19×N25 (GraphSpec mixed-color replay):** Rule 1 at the replay gate. `GraphSpec`
  spawn steps already carry a `CellFactory` (51), from which `CellDescriptor.color` is
  derivable. A single-inlet replay validates each cell at that one host and **fails
  loudly** on a wrong-color cell (correct — the admission gate is doing its job). For
  mixed-color graphs, spawn steps carry an optional **placement constraint**
  (auto-derived from the cell's color, or an explicit host target); a multi-host
  replay router routes each spawn to an `admits`-compatible host. Placement metadata
  is therefore the cell's own color surfaced for the router — the "color-aware
  placement metadata" 40/41 point 2 / 51 fixed as a direction — not a hand-authored
  field.
- **N19×N27 (promotion across colors):** Rule 4 — a candidate may change color; it is
  placed (rule 1) on a color-compatible host and the swap relinks the incumbent's
  links onto it (I-2 active-swap over full refs). Because links are color-blind
  (rule 2), a color change only turns a fused edge into a cross-host enqueue (or vice
  versa) — a performance change, never a correctness break. The drain window
  (red → transfer → relink → green, 53 §G-33) is unchanged: it is built on the colored
  scheduler and 30/33 already flushes accepted invocations before deactivation and
  parks a suspended task's host until resumed, so color-dependent completion is
  already handled per color with no new mechanism.

**Net effect**: one predicate (`admits`) at one class of boundary (spawn-admission)
covers all eight surfaces; the data hot path never sees color (P2); color stays a
type-level fact surfaced as generated metadata (P5); and the wire, refs, links, and
waves keep their existing color-free shapes (P1/P9). The single unifying insight: a
color mismatch is a **placement** fact, resolved by refusing to co-host — never a
data fact resolved on a link or a frame.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — color lives entirely in the host layer (schedulers, admission gate); kernel artifacts (links, refs, invocations) carry no color; every rule is meaningful single-threaded (the simulation scheduler already issues either color). |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — data path never checks color; same-host links stay direct calls, cross-host stays one non-blocking offer; all color work is on the rare spawn/placement path. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — cross-color communication is a visible cross-host link, not a hidden conversion; color is inspectable via `CellDescriptor`. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Untouched** — no global color coordinator; admission is a local host decision. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — color is a marker type surfaced as generated `CellDescriptor.color`; the admission predicate is total and structural; wrong-color placement fails at the gate. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — replicating a pure cell per color neighbourhood follows expressed interest; nothing colored is placed "just in case." |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — no bearing on boundary security controls. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — candidates may change color across incarnations; the swap places on a compatible host and relinks; nothing assumes fixed color. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — color crosses only as a marker/type + `CellDescriptor.color` in spawn/migrate payloads; no color on data frames; continuations never serialize (stripped at egress). |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — the decentralized niche needs color as a placement constraint, not as ambient per-message metadata; cross-color = cross-host is the niche-appropriate trade. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: color is not on `MessageContext`; waves are unaffected.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent: admission is a local, per-host decision; no global color barrier.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent, reinforced: color constrains which *host* a cell lands on; migration moves a whole host, so a migrated cell's color already matches its (moving) host.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive** — Consistent: the drain/park window is color-realized by the scheduler; no new suspension mechanism for color.
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay** — Consistent: color rides spawn/migrate payloads, not the park/replay path; re-resolution is color-free.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: durability (rule 6) journals invocations + `Stateful` snapshots; no color-specific snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, not waves** — Untouched.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent, sharpened: a returning management contract's await is color-realized (rule 6); push-only data means the continuation never needs a return (rule 7).
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** — Consistent: rule 5 adds only a color filter to candidate-host selection, not a new protocol.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched: partition placement is ordinary placement, hence ordinary color-admission.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: no color field added to the data `WireFrame`; color travels in spawn/migrate payloads.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO** — Consistent: the drain is scheduler-colored and unchanged; color affects only placement, not ordering.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time** — Consistent and parallel: cardinality is a *link-time* check; color is a *spawn-time* check; the two are orthogonal gates.
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased not crossing machines** — Untouched: ownership and color are independent markers.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId (I-2: full-ref addressing, logicalId is grouping/continuity only)** — Consistent, load-bearing: rule 4 keeps color off `logicalId` exactly because I-2 forbids logicalId-level behavioral policy.
- **I-1 metadata plane (bounded protocol set, null context, bypass parking)** — Consistent, reused: the deferred bounded-intake refusal (N1×N19) surfaces as an upstream metadata-plane notice on I-1's plane, not a data return.
- **Gaps/conflicts Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — No resolved item reopened; this elaborates the un-IDed color composition gap and the deferred-backpressure boundary.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **30/32 §Compatibility and coercion** — Add the single-boundary rule: color is
  checked *only* at spawn-admission; state the `admits` predicate; state that a color
  mismatch across a link is a cross-host boundary, not an error (rule 2); reframe
  "color propagates upstream" explicitly as a per-instance placement SHOULD (rule 3).
- **30/32 §How the colors are realized** — Extend the continuation-stripping note to
  the wire/bridge path (rule 7): stripped at egress, re-supplied at ingress; no color
  on the frame.
- **30/31 §Normative rules (rule 4) + §Colors of hosts** — Note that a returning
  management contract's await is color-realized (blocking `get` on 🔵, suspend `await`
  on 🟣); the "5s blocking wait" is the 🔵 realization of a color-agnostic await.
- **24 §Durability spectrum (G-25)** — Add that the durable-host journal writer is
  host machinery in two color flavors; durability composes with either host color;
  no color restriction on durable hosts.
- **40/41 point 2 (generated proxies)** — Clarify "emit … color 30/32" as emitting
  `CellDescriptor.color` for the admission gate, explicitly **not** a per-message
  `WireFrame` field; restate remote spawn/migrate color validation at the receiver's
  gate.
- **51 §Graph construction DSL + §Code generation** — State that spawn steps carry the
  cell's derivable color; single-inlet replay fails loudly on a wrong-color cell;
  mixed-color graphs carry an optional placement constraint (auto-derived from color)
  routed by a multi-host replay driver.
- **42 §Design as implemented** — Add the color filter on candidate-host selection
  (rule 5) and the near-vacuous-because-mergeable-cells-are-pure observation.
- **53 §Model + §G-33** — State that a candidate may change color across incarnations;
  the swap places it on a compatible host and relinks; a color change only re-tiers
  fusion, never breaks the swap.
- **11 §Identity and persistence / cross-ref I-2** — Note that color is an
  instance/placement attribute, never a `logicalId` attribute.
- **90/91** — Give the un-IDed color-composition gap an ID and mark it resolved by
  this design; annotate the deferred-backpressure gap (30/32) as the locus where
  color-keyed bridges re-enter.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Color-keyed bridges under bounded intakes** — When intakes bound (30/32 deferred
  gap), a cross-color enqueue can stall; the four ADR-2 bridges become real at the
  `enqueueHostedInvocation` seam, keyed by `(senderHostColor, targetHostColor)`. The
  target color is discoverable on the rare *linking* path (as link metadata, never a
  frame field). Concrete bridge design + a generative color-crossing test are needed.
- **Backpressure refusal as an upstream metadata-plane notice** — The direction is
  set (a bounded-intake refusal rides I-1's protocol plane upstream, never a data
  return); the notice's descriptor, idempotence, and interaction with the producer's
  outlet are undesigned.
- **`CellDescriptor.color` generation & the placement-constraint shape** — KSP must
  emit `color` per cell type (alongside ownership flags), and the optional
  `GraphSpec` placement constraint (derived color vs explicit host target) plus a
  multi-host replay router are unbuilt.
- **Multi-host / color-aware placement engine** — 30/32 says placement engines SHOULD
  co-host same-colored chains; the actual placement/fusion engine (which host each
  cell of a mixed-color graph lands on, and when a pure cell is replicated per color
  neighbourhood) is undesigned.
- **Remote-spawn color-rejection surface** — The exact rejection channel when a
  wrong-color cell arrives over a remote `HostManagementApi` (dead-letter vs a typed
  `LinkResult`-style rejection back to the caller) needs pinning against G-26/G-12.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high.** The resolution does not invent kernel machinery — it
*classifies* what exists: spawn validation is already the color gate (30/32,
implemented M3.1); the degenerate bridge already makes any cross-host send a single
non-blocking offer; schedulers already come in two color flavors that realize host
machinery differently; and I-2 already established that `logicalId` carries no
behavioral policy. The design draws one bright line — color is a placement constraint
on logic, checked only at admission; links are color-blind — and all eight member
pairs collapse onto it. **Open questions**: (1) the bounded-intake regime is where
color genuinely re-enters as bridges, and while its *location* is pinned, its design
is deferred with backpressure; (2) whether the multi-host `GraphSpec` placement
constraint should be strictly auto-derived from color or also allow explicit host
pinning (I lean auto-derived, with explicit pinning as an opt-in) — deferred to the
placement-engine gap; (3) the exact realization of a 🟣 durable host's non-blocking
journal IO (suspend-native vs offload to a blocking IO dispatcher) is an
implementation choice left to the durability work.

### I-16 — State-request protocol: on-demand pull triggers, answering instance, and snapshot/live interleaving (G-18 residual)

> Member pairs: N3×N9, N3×N15, N3×N24, N9×N21, N9×N22, N9×N24
> Existing gaps touched: G-18, G-13, G-7 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 5/6 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The entire StateRequest protocol: metadata-plane request (depends on I-1's plane, unbuilt for the wire), the single trigger rule (fresh / park-replay / drop keyed on a per-link liveness epoch), the single-wave reply stamp, TagFrontier-incremental replies, p…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The single mechanism question: **design the on-demand state-request protocol** —
"a consumer asking for a recompute or state *without* relinking" (21 §Pull,
⚠ GAP G-18 residual) — as a concrete protocol on the I-1 metadata plane, and
answer the three composition questions the spec leaves open:

1. **Who triggers it and when?** Three trigger contexts pull in different
   directions:
   - *Remote late-joiners* — the M5.4 registry-proxy path "routes cross-peer
     linking around the handshake variant … results are Deferred, rejections
     dead-lettered" (10/13 M5.4 caveat via 41 §Wire point 3), so it is
     "unstated whether and on which side `onLinked` fires for a remote
     subscriber" (N9×N22). Catch-up today "hangs entirely on the … post-install
     `onLinked` hook" (21 §Pull).
   - *Resumed subgraphs* — 34 makes "resume-on-renewed-interest the enforcement
     arm of scheduling" (30/34 §Principle) and parks-not-drops (34 §Decisions 2),
     but whether a resumed subgraph learns what it missed by **park-replay** or
     **pull-on-resume** is unspecified (N9×N21).
   - *Already-linked replica anti-entropy* — 42 defines anti-entropy as
     "the same catch-up protocol as 21's late-join" (42 §Anti-entropy), but
     "catch-up triggers only on link install (`onLinked`)" while partition
     recovery between **already-linked** replicas needs no new link, "so
     partition recovery … has no trigger mechanism" (N9×N24, N3×N24).

2. **Which instance answers** a request addressed to a logical cell, over which
   sub-port (N3×N24).

3. **How the answer interleaves and wave-aligns** with the live tagged delta
   stream sharing the same link — "wave alignment of snapshots waits for the
   request protocol" (21 §Pull; N3×N15).

Why the spec leaves it open: G-18's pull is written only as a *proposal* —
"`RequestState(replyTo)` traveling upstream … answered by a state-as-delta on
the requester's inlet" (21 §Pull) — explicitly "parked on the unbuilt multiplex
state-request protocol (G-13)" (20/24 §Required next steps; 90/91 G-18). The
substrate (I-1's metadata plane) and the identity model (I-2's full-ref
addressing) are now decided; this challenge builds the protocol on them.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 vs a background repair protocol.** The obvious fix for already-linked
  anti-entropy is a periodic digest/Merkle exchange between replicas — but that
  runs "just in case" (violates P6) and is a *second synchronization protocol*,
  which the recorded decision "replication reuses dataflow links and delta
  gossip; there MUST NOT be a second synchronization protocol" (40/42 §2)
  forbids outright.
- **The onLinked trigger is load-bearing but not universal.** Catch-up is
  producer-side push-on-link (`outlet.at(link.to)` from `onLinked`, 21 §Pull).
  The M5.4 remote path may never deliver a `LinkFrom` handshake to the producer
  ("`LinkFrom` is a live object that cannot cross the wire", 41 §Wire point 3),
  so a purely producer-side trigger cannot fire for a remote subscriber, and it
  cannot fire *at all* for an already-linked replica (no new link). One trigger
  cannot cover fresh-local, fresh-remote, resume, and steady-state-drift.
- **Snapshot vs waves (P4, G-20).** A state-as-delta folds *many* waves into one
  value, yet the recorded G-20 model is per-source waves with "convergence, not
  simultaneity". A glitch-free consumer (20/22) groups deltas by wave; an unwaved
  snapshot "waits for the request protocol" (21). Waving it wrong reintroduces a
  glitch; waving it as a global barrier violates P4 (no global barrier).
- **Interleaving with live deltas on the shared link (decided FIFO).** The reply
  travels the *same* link/data-lane as live deltas under the decided invariant
  "per-link FIFO end-to-end" (30/33). The snapshot and the live stream must
  interleave deterministically and the snapshot must be idempotent against a
  live delta that also appears inside it.
- **Suspension is ONE buffering primitive (recorded).** Park/replay already
  recovers missed traffic when the buffer survives; pull must *complete* that
  primitive, not become a rival to it — otherwise "one Buffering primitive at
  two granularities" fractures.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Producer-push-on-link only (status quo, extended)

Keep `onLinked` as the sole trigger; make it fire on both sides of a remote
link; recover already-linked drift by tearing down and re-installing the link
(forcing a fresh `onLinked`).

- *Semantics*: no new protocol; catch-up is always producer-initiated on link
  install.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero new (it is today's path).
- *Failure modes*: cannot fire producer-side for the M5.4 remote registry-proxy
  link (N9×N22); has **no trigger** for already-linked anti-entropy without a
  relink, and a relink is a topology mutation with a fresh handshake/cardinality
  check (P8/P6 churn, and gratuitous per the decided "cardinality enforced at
  link time"); resume would have to relink even when park-replay already holds
  the exact missed messages.
- *Tradeoff*: cheapest, but structurally cannot answer two of the three trigger
  contexts. Rejected.

##### Candidate B — Subscriber-driven pull as the primitive; push-on-link a co-hosted optimization; park-replay for intact buffers (recommended)

One `RequestState` generic protocol on the I-1 metadata plane, issued by the
**subscriber side** whenever a link becomes live in a state where the delta
history across it may be incomplete. Answered by an ordinary state-as-delta on
the requester's data inlet. `onLinked`-push survives as the co-hosted fast path;
park-replay stays the exact recovery when the buffer survived.

- *Semantics*: pull fills exactly the gap park-replay cannot; the two are the
  two arms of the one buffering primitive.
- *Fast-path cost*: none on the steady-state data path — the request is a
  metadata-plane frame emitted only on a link-liveness transition (a rare
  operation, P2). Co-hosted fresh links reduce to today's synchronous unicast.
- *Failure modes*: a mesh-wide reconnect can trigger O(N²) pulls if the frontier
  optimization is unavailable (bounded by debounce, §8); requires every
  delta-serving cell to be `Stateful` (already the M4.2/M4.3 reality).
- *Tradeoff*: one new bounded, event-driven protocol that unifies all three
  trigger contexts and both the interleaving and identity questions. Recommended.

##### Candidate C — Periodic anti-entropy gossip (digest/Merkle exchange)

Replicas periodically exchange compact state digests and pull the diff, in the
classic Dynamo/Cassandra style, running as a background timer independent of
link events.

- *Semantics*: steady-state drift repair without any trigger event.
- *Fast-path cost*: off the data path, but a standing periodic cost per replica
  pair.
- *Failure modes*: it is a **second synchronization protocol** — directly
  contradicts the recorded 40/42 decision — and it runs "just in case" against
  P6; it also needs wall-clock or tick cadence, pressing on the deterministic
  simulation (P1) the way 34 had to route time through host ticks.
- *Tradeoff*: robust but principle-violating; its one genuine advantage
  (repairing silent drift with no event) is not needed because in this model
  drift only arises from a drop, and a drop *is* the event that triggers B's
  pull. Rejected on the recorded decision.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. Pull is a subscriber-driven completion of the one
buffering primitive; the request rides the metadata plane; the reply rides the
data lane as a single waved state-as-delta; every trigger context reduces to one
rule.

##### Data shapes

```kotlin
// Generic protocol on the I-1 metadata plane (dispatch class PORT_PROTOCOL).
// Management-class: null MessageContext, carries no Owned/Leased, bypasses
// data-path parking, idempotent (I-1 rules 2–4). Direction = Upstream.
val StateRequestProtocol = ProtocolId("state-request")

@Contract(management = true)
interface StateRequest {
    // travels UPSTREAM along the established link's metadata plane
    fun requestState(replyTo: PortRef, since: TagFrontier?)
}

// A version vector over MERGE-TAG source ids (24), NOT wave ids — the decided
// separation (20/22, 20/24) is preserved: tags summarize what is materialized,
// waves group propagation.
typealias TagFrontier = Map<SourceId, Counter>   // Timestamp = (SourceId, Counter)
```

The **reply is ordinary data**, not a protocol message: the producer emits
`state-as-delta` on `outlet.at(replyTo)` — the identical mechanism `onLinked`
catch-up already uses (21 §Pull, "unicast its state-as-delta-from-empty to just
that subscriber `outlet.at(link.to)`"). `since == null` ⇒ full state-as-delta-
from-empty; `since` present ⇒ state-as-delta of only the tags with
`counter > since[source]` per source (incremental anti-entropy).

##### Protocol steps

1. **Trigger (subscriber side).** When the subscriber end of a data link becomes
   live in a *history-incomplete* state (the trigger rule below), the framework's
   default data-inlet behavior emits `requestState(replyTo = myInlet.ref,
   since = myTagFrontier())` upstream on that link's metadata plane. `replyTo`
   is the subscriber's own full `PortRef` (I-2: full-ref addressing).
2. **Transport (upstream).** In-host, the request is a direct call into the
   producer port's `ProtocolSupport` (one map lookup, I-1). Cross-host, it is a
   `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame carried on the **reverse bridge path** the link already
   maintains (I-1 rule 6), delivered to the producer's `ProtocolSupport`. It
   does **not** depend on the producer ever observing a `LinkFrom`/`onLinked`
   handshake — this is what dissolves the M5.4 ambiguity (N9×N22).
3. **Answer (producer instance).** The producer instance at the far end of *that
   link* — one full ref, one instance (I-2) — computes state-as-delta from its
   own materialized state (`Stateful.snapshot()`; derived cells re-emit current
   derived state, "never re-execution of history", 21 §Pull), stamps it with a
   single fresh wave `Timestamp(producerOutletSourceId, N)` where `N` is the
   outlet's current counter, and emits it on `outlet.at(replyTo)`.
4. **Interleave (data lane, FIFO).** The reply enters the producer→subscriber
   data lane at a definite position. Everything emitted before it is folded into
   the snapshot; everything after arrives as live deltas with counter `> N`.
   Per-link FIFO (decided, 30/33) makes the snapshot one contiguous unit ahead of
   subsequent live waves — there is no partial-snapshot interleaving on a single
   link.
5. **Merge (subscriber).** The subscriber applies the reply like any delta.
   Overlap with a live delta it already holds dedups by OR-set tag union (24) —
   so the pull is idempotent against concurrent live deltas, and a subscriber
   linked to several mesh replicas (I-2) may pull from each and merge all replies
   by tag union with no double-count.

##### The single trigger rule

`RequestState` is issued **iff the delta history across the link may be
incomplete** — and never when park-replay already holds the exact missed
messages. Three cases, one rule:

| Link transition | Buffer state | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Fresh link** (first install, local or remote) | none existed | subscriber pulls (`since = null` if it has no state yet, else its frontier) |
| **Parked → replayed** (local suspend/resume, buffered migration) | buffer intact, held by `LocationRegistry` | **no pull** — replay is exact (34 park-not-drop; the one buffering primitive) |
| **Dropped → re-resolved** (partition heal, remote reconnect, buffer-losing restart) | buffer gone | subscriber pulls (`since = myTagFrontier()`, incremental) |

The `LocationRegistry` already distinguishes *park* (target temporarily
unlocated, buffer held — 41 §What exists) from *drop* (`unpublishRemotes(sink)`,
41 M5.5). We make that distinction the pull gate via a per-link **liveness
epoch**: incremented on a drop, unchanged across a park. On re-resolution the
registry either **replays the held buffer** (epoch unchanged ⇒ intact ⇒ no
pull) or, finding no buffer for this link (epoch advanced / buffer expired /
never existed), **signals the subscriber inlet to issue `requestState`**. This
makes pull the *completion arm* of the one buffering primitive rather than a
rival protocol.

##### Rules the model introduces (normative)

1. **Pull is subscriber-triggered; push-on-link is an optimization.** The
   authoritative trigger is the subscriber-side liveness transition above.
   Producer-side `onLinked` catch-up (G-22, shipped) is retained purely as the
   **co-hosted / same-side fast path**: when the producer directly observes the
   install, it may pre-empt the request and unicast immediately; the request
   then resolves as a no-op (the subscriber already at frontier). Correctness no
   longer depends on which side sees the install.
2. **The reply is one wave.** A state-as-delta reply is stamped with exactly one
   `Timestamp(producerOutletSourceId, N)`. Its internal merge tags keep their
   original `SourceId`s (CRDT identity); the *wave* is the producer outlet's
   (propagation identity). A glitch-free consumer treats it as one atomic wave
   from that source; a mergeable consumer dedups by tag. This resolves
   "wave alignment of snapshots" (21) without a global barrier (P4) and within
   G-20 per-source waves.
3. **Requests are management-class metadata (I-1).** `StateRequest` carries null
   `MessageContext`, no `Owned`/`Leased`, its own ordering lane and band, and
   bypasses data-path parking — so a request can travel upstream over a link
   whose *data* is parked, which is precisely what must happen to unpark a
   suspended/partitioned branch (I-1 rule 2). It MUST be idempotent: a duplicated
   `requestState` yields a duplicate reply that dedups by tag (rule/§5 above).
4. **Pull requires `Stateful`, single-hop by default.** A cell serving a delta
   outlet answers `requestState` from its own materialized state; it does not
   re-execute or (by default) forward upstream. This is already the shipped
   reality (every data cell/operator is `Stateful`, 24; pure pass-throughs are
   fused away, 21 §Fusion). Transitive/multi-hop forwarding for a genuinely
   stateless cell is an enabled-but-deferred extension (§8), reusing the
   Upstream direction.
5. **Anti-entropy = pull-on-reestablish, incremental by frontier.** Already-
   linked replicas recover by the *drop → re-resolve* arm of the rule: on heal,
   each side pulls the other with its `TagFrontier`; the producer replies with
   only tags beyond the frontier; convergence is restored by tag union. No
   periodic protocol, no relink, no second sync mechanism (40/42). Where a cell
   has no per-source-monotonic tag clock (Map/List, arrival-order limited, 24),
   `since = null` full-state pull is the safe form.
6. **Resume prefers replay, falls back to pull.** A resumed subgraph whose park
   buffer is intact learns what it missed by replay (no pull, rule table row 2);
   only a resume whose buffer was dropped pulls (row 3). This answers the
   park-replay-vs-pull-on-resume question (N9×N21): **both, selected by buffer
   survival**, never both at once.

##### Net effect on the open questions

- *Who/when*: one rule keyed on link-liveness transition + buffer survival,
  covering fresh-local, fresh-remote, resume, and steady-state anti-entropy.
- *Which instance*: the producer instance at the far end of the pulled link (one
  full ref, I-2); mesh-level pull = pull each linked replica, merge by tag.
- *Interleaving/wave*: reply is one waved unit in the FIFO data lane; idempotent
  against concurrent live deltas by tag union.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — request is an ordinary invocation on the metadata plane; reply is an ordinary delta emission; both meaningful in the single-threaded `SimulationController`; no new primitive. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — steady-state data path untouched; a request is emitted only on a rare link-liveness transition; co-hosted case reduces to today's synchronous unicast. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — pull rides an *existing explicit link* and does not relink; `replyTo` is a visible `PortRef`; no hidden mailbox. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global barrier/clock/lock; the snapshot is one per-source wave; convergence is local tag union. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — `StateRequest` is management-class (null context, ownership-free) by the same KSP flags as I-1; pull-requires-`Stateful` is structural; the reply's single-wave stamp is generated. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — pull is event-driven (interest expressed by the link + the drop event), never a periodic "just in case" sweep (why Candidate C is rejected). |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Untouched** — no bearing on boundary controls; requests cross membranes as ordinary metadata frames subject to the same policies. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — recovery needs no relink/topology mutation; anti-entropy composes with a live graph; promotion (I-2) pulls into the candidate via the same path. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `StateRequest` is a `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame (ids-only, contractId/methodId); `TagFrontier` is `Map<SourceId,Counter>` of already-serializable `Timestamp` parts; reply is an existing serializable delta. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — event-driven decentralized anti-entropy for long-lived interest-driven meshes is exactly the niche; a throughput-oriented periodic digest is deliberately declined. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: the reply is one wave minted per
  producer outlet; internal tags keep their sources; convergence not simultaneity.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent: pull is point-to-point over one
  link; no propagation lock.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: a host move that loses the park
  buffer trips the drop arm ⇒ pull; nothing per-cell added.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent,
  reinforced: pull is the *completion arm* of that primitive (buffer gone), not
  a second mechanism; park-replay stays the primary.
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay mechanism** — Consistent: the
  park/drop distinction the registry already draws is the pull gate; re-resolution
  reuses the one registry.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent (core): the reply is state-as-delta;
  no snapshot type introduced.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, NOT wave ids** — Consistent, load-bearing:
  `TagFrontier` is over merge-tag sources; the reply's wave is a separate stamp.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent
  (via I-1): `StateRequest` is management-class push-only (`replyTo` in payload,
  no return), null context.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** —
  Consistent: anti-entropy reuses the data reply path + existing tags/frontier;
  this is precisely why the periodic-digest Candidate C is rejected.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: request is a
  `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame (I-1); no new addressing names on the wire.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent: the reply
  rides the data lane in FIFO (step 4); the request rides the metadata plane
  out-of-band, permitted precisely because it is idempotent (I-1 rule 3).
- **Cardinality enforced at link time, not send time** — Consistent, and a
  virtue: pull recovers *without* a relink, so no cardinality re-check churn.
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased not crossing machines** —
  Consistent: `StateRequest` carries no `Owned`/`Leased` (I-1 rule 4); replies of
  single-writer cells serve *copies* of read state (leader/follower, 42), not the
  exclusive payload.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId → I-2 full-ref** —
  Consistent: the request reaches one instance per link; logical-level pull is
  "pull each linked replica" (I-2 N9 binding), never a logicalId indirection.
- **Gaps/conflicts Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — G-22 (catch-up) stays
  resolved and is *subsumed* as the co-hosted fast path (rule 1), not reopened;
  G-8 (I-2), G-13/I-1 built upon, not re-litigated.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/21 §Pull** — Replace the G-18 residual *proposal* with the built protocol:
  the `StateRequest(replyTo, since)` metadata-plane request, subscriber-side
  trigger rule (fresh / park-replay / drop table), single-wave reply, and the
  statement that `onLinked` push is now the co-hosted fast path, not the sole
  trigger. Remove "wave alignment of snapshots waits for the request protocol" —
  it is resolved (single-wave stamp).
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports / §Directionality** — Register `state-request` as a
  well-known `ProtocolId` with an Upstream `ProtocolDescriptor` (I-1), management-
  class, ownership-free.
- **20/24 §Required next steps** — Mark "on-demand pull without relinking" done;
  note pull requires `Stateful` (already satisfied) and that Map/List get
  full-state pull only (no tag frontier).
- **40/42 §Anti-entropy** — Restate: anti-entropy = pull-on-reestablish gated by
  the drop epoch, incremental by `TagFrontier`; reaffirm no second sync protocol;
  add the O(N²) reconnect debounce note (§8).
- **30/34 §Decisions (suspension/resume)** — State that resume recovers by
  park-replay when the buffer is intact and by pull when it was dropped;
  cross-reference the DEGRADE "post-resume replayed waves as late-join catch-up"
  path as the pull case.
- **41 §Wire / §Addressing** — Note the per-link liveness epoch on re-resolution
  and that the reverse bridge path carries the upstream `StateRequest` frame
  (I-1 rule 6); clarify the M5.4 remote path no longer needs producer-side
  `onLinked` for catch-up.
- **90/91 G-18** — Update to Resolved (build milestone), pointing at this design;
  G-13 "state-request" remaining item closed.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Tag-clock monotonicity for incremental frontier.** Incremental pull assumes
  merge tags are per-source-monotonic counters so `TagFrontier` is a valid
  version vector; the OR-set minting discipline must guarantee this, and Map/List
  must be flagged full-state-pull-only. Needs a stated invariant + test.
- **Buffer-survival detection (park vs drop epoch).** The precise per-link
  liveness-epoch design and the registry cooperation that lets the subscriber
  distinguish an intact park-replay from a lost buffer needs pinning (interacts
  with 41 M5.5 "reconnection beyond park-and-replay is out of scope").
- **Multi-hop / transitive pull for stateless cells.** Single-hop pull assumes
  every delta-serving cell is `Stateful`; forwarding `requestState` upstream
  through a stateless cell (loop prevention, band quantization) is undesigned —
  ties to I-1's "transitive/multi-hop protocol notices" gap.
- **Pull-storm debounce on mesh reconnect.** N mesh peers healing simultaneously
  can trigger O(N²) pulls if the frontier is unavailable (Map/List); a coalescing
  / debounce policy (and whether one peer's pull can satisfy several) is needed.
- **Glitch-free composition of a pulled snapshot with concurrent live sources.**
  Proving the single-wave snapshot composes without glitch in a join that spans
  the pull source and other live sources — extend the 100-seed late-join harness
  (21) with a pull-under-live-traffic control.
- **Recompute-on-demand for non-idempotent / effectful cells.** Pull re-emits
  current state; `CounterCell` (non-idempotent) and `Effectful`/shadow cells (52)
  must not double-count or re-fire on a duplicated reply — a pull-safety marker or
  an explicit "pull-serves-copy-only" rule may be required.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high.** The design adds no kernel machinery: it composes three
already-decided/shipped pieces — the state-as-delta catch-up path (G-22, M4.2),
the I-1 metadata plane (`PORT_PROTOCOL`, upstream generic protocols), and I-2
full-ref addressing — and draws one new line: **pull is the completion arm of
the one buffering primitive, triggered subscriber-side by a link-liveness
transition, gated on whether park-replay's buffer survived.** That single rule
covers all three trigger contexts, and the "reply is one per-source wave in the
FIFO data lane, idempotent by tag" answers both the interleaving and identity
questions using existing invariants.

**Open questions.** (1) The exact liveness-epoch signal distinguishing park from
drop across the M5.5 reconnect boundary is the most load-bearing unresolved
detail (spun to §8). (2) Whether incremental frontier pull is worth its
complexity versus always-full-state-idempotent pull for the mergeable set family,
whose tag sets grow monotonically (compaction is G-25 future work) — full-state
pull may dominate until compaction exists. (3) Multi-hop pull is enabled but
deferred; the niche's fused pipelines may never need it.

### I-17 — Faithful non-perturbing observation: effect classification, suppression scope, and trustworthy judgment (G-32)

> Member pairs: N1×N26, N3×N26, N5×N26, N10×N27, N12×N26, N26×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-32, G-11, G-33 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 5/6 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — Everything membrane-specific: the effect=true contract flag (KSP), downstream-only taps (needs I-1's negotiated protocol capabilities — unbuilt; today a shadow's attention would propagate upstream into production via ProtocolSupport), SCC-closed cuts with o…
> ⚠ Divergence with landed code: Granularity: the landed G-32 mechanism (spec 52 §Live invariants; Shadow.suppress in cell/evolve/Evolution.kt) NoOp-serves EVERY fan-in inlet of an Effectful *cell* as the only suppression mode. The resolution amends this Resolved item: suppression cuts at …

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The evolution pipeline is `synthetic invariants (52) → live shadows (52) → promotion on satisfaction (53)`. Its two load-bearing promises — **observe production without perturbing it** and **judge the candidate faithfully** — are asserted but not mechanized. G-32's shipped core (`Effectful` cell marker + `Shadow.spawn` NoOp-serves effectful inlets, double-fire control, M9.2) is recorded Resolved in `91`, but the observation-fidelity residue is open on five axes, each surfaced by a member pair:

- **The single mechanism question**: *what boundary encloses a live shadow so that it is provably (a) non-perturbing to production in both directions and (b) judged on states that actually occur — and what policy turns invariant verdicts into a promotion decision?*

Member pairs:
- **N1×N26 / N5×N26 — suppression granularity.** Effect classification rides the G-11/G-32 `Effectful` marker; but "`Shadow.spawn` NoOp-serves every fan-in inlet of an `Effectful` cell" (52 §Live invariants) silences the cell's *entire* behavior — including the downstream derived emissions a judge needs. Which port contracts count as effectful is decided only as a cell-level proposal (10/12 §Contracts are push-only — "effect classification … is the `Effectful` cell marker … orthogonal to the contract flag"). The scope of NoOp-serving is unevaluated (10/14 §Standard proxy behaviors).
- **N3×N26 — protocol leakage.** Multiplex ports (I-1) stack upstream generic protocols (attention 30/34, state-request 20/21 G-18, link-management) on the same links a shadow subscribes to. Nothing says whether a read-only shadow may emit upstream protocol traffic that *summons production computation* or inflates its attention/resourcing, nor whether invariants inject sub-port traffic (10/12 §Multiplexed ports and generic protocols, §Directionality of generic protocols).
- **N10×N27 — closed loops.** A shadow of a cell inside a feedback loop is never exercised under its own closed loop (its outputs are suppressed), so it cannot be judged for the dynamics that matter; and a link-swap inside a cycle during the drain window meets G-19's open fixpoint semantics (20/21 §Cycles) and 20/22's open wave-re-entry question (20/22 §Interaction with other parts).
- **N12×N26 — glitch-consistent judgment.** An `InvariantCell` folding a multi-input fan-in is itself glitch-prone; glitch-freedom is opt-in per cell (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom) and 52 never requires wave-consistent invariant evaluation. An invariant across a diamond can fire on an intermediate state no consistent snapshot exhibits — and the same verdict feeds live monitoring and promotion gates (52 §Invariant testing).
- **N26×N27 — promotion policy.** Both docs state the pipeline direction, but the promotion policy — satisfaction threshold, observation window, deciding judge — is undesigned (53 §Model, §Mechanical decomposition; 90/91 §Gaps — process).

Because 52's "Mechanically this needs …" paragraph names *capabilities* (subscribe shadow, suppress side effects, report to promotion) without a boundary that binds them, each capability is decidable in isolation but their composition (non-perturbation + faithfulness) is not.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P6 (interest drives resources) vs non-perturbation.** A shadow *does* express interest — it taps production outlets, which legitimately costs one extra fan-out emission (P6). But the same "interest" channel, the upstream attention/state-request protocols (30/34, 20/21), would make production *reallocate resources and recompute for the shadow's benefit*. Interest-that-observes must be separated from interest-that-summons.
- **G-32 granularity vs judgeability.** The recorded M9.2 mechanism suppresses at *cell* granularity ("every fan-in inlet of an `Effectful` cell"). For a pure terminal sink that is correct. For a cell that is *both* effectful and mid-graph (transforms and emits derived deltas), NoOp-ing its inlets is actively *wrong for judgment* — it deletes exactly the derived output the judge reads. Correct suppression needs finer scope than the shipped decision uses (P5 — the classification must live where it is decidable and surgical).
- **P4 (local, compositional consistency) vs trustworthy verdicts.** 52's harness pattern is "drive to idle, then assert." Live production never goes idle and has no global clock/barrier (P4). A gate invariant folding a fan-in can observe glitches (20/22); cross-*source* joins get convergence, not simultaneity (G-20). So "the candidate satisfied the invariant" has no meaning until we pin *at which consistent evaluation points* a verdict is trusted.
- **G-19 (cycle fixpoint) open vs closed-loop judgment and cycle-swap.** Judging feedback dynamics requires closing the loop; swapping a cell on a live cycle requires wave-re-entry semantics (20/22 §Cycles: "Open") and quiescence (G-19: unbuilt). We must not invent fixpoint semantics here.
- **P1/P8 vs "no new mechanism."** 53's strongest claim: "every deployment primitive is already a kernel/graph primitive … any deployment feature that *would* require a new kernel mechanism should trigger a design review (P1 violation likely)." Whatever we add must reduce to links, proxies, and policy cells — no new kernel primitive.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Status quo: per-cell NoOp (M9.2 as-is)

*Semantics*: a cell carries `Effectful`; `Shadow.spawn` NoOp-serves all its fan-in inlets. Judge with invariant cells on shadow outlets.

*Fast-path cost*: none (NoOp is a served proxy, 10/14).

*Failure modes*: deletes derived emission for mixed effectful/transforming cells (N5×N26); no protocol isolation — shadow attention/state-request leak upstream and perturb production (N3×N26); no loop closure (N10×N27); invariants may fire on glitches (N12×N26); no promotion policy (N26×N27). This is precisely the residue the challenge names.

*Tradeoff*: minimal and shipped, but resolves only the pure-terminal-sink case. Insufficient.

##### Candidate B — Full production-clone sandbox

*Semantics*: replicate all of production into an isolated runtime; run the candidate there against copied inputs; perfect isolation and closed loops.

*Fast-path cost*: N/A (offline).

*Failure modes*: clones the whole graph "just in case" (violates P6, P10 — not incremental/interest-driven); the copy diverges from live production the instant it forks, so it is *synthetic* testing (52 §Invariant testing), not *live* shadowing (52 §Live invariants); enormous, non-decentralized. It answers a different question than "does this candidate behave on *real live* data."

*Tradeoff*: strong isolation, wrong niche. Rejected — it is the synthetic layer, not the shadow layer.

##### Candidate C — The observation membrane (recommended)

*Semantics*: a shadow is a self-contained subgraph of **candidate instances** (full refs, I-2) enclosed by a **directional isolation membrane** (P7 — a boundary control, realized as G-10/43 policy over ordinary links/proxies). The membrane has three isolation rules and one judgment rule:
1. **Ingress (production→shadow)** = fan-out taps that carry data + downstream protocols but **drop all upstream protocols** (via I-1 capability negotiation) — non-perturbing inbound.
2. **Egress-to-world** = **effect-boundary contracts** NoOp-served at *contract* granularity — effect suppression that leaves internal derived computation intact.
3. **Enclosure** = the cut is SCC-closed: feedback loops close on shadow-internal links; only tap edges and effect edges cross the membrane.
4. **Judgment** = gate invariants inside the membrane are glitch-free/convergence-evaluated; a promotion policy (window / threshold / judge, optionally differential vs incumbent) decides the swap.

*Fast-path cost*: production data path untouched (a tap is an extra `Broadcast` fan-out branch, 10/14); NoOp and glitch-free wrappers are off-production; capability negotiation and SCC analysis are rare link-time/spawn-time ops (P2).

*Failure modes*: a candidate whose SCC would re-enter *non-shadowable* production can only be judged open-loop (honest, flagged); cycle-swap still leans on G-19 quiescence (gated, not defined here). No perturbation or judgeability failure survives for the shadowable case (§4).

*Tradeoff*: reuses every existing primitive (fan-out, NoOp, capability negotiation, glitch-free wrapper, policy cell) and adds one contract-classification bit plus one membrane policy object. Recommended.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C — the observation membrane.** A live shadow is a subgraph of candidate instances wrapped by a directional isolation boundary. It is *not* a new kernel mechanism: it is a named configuration of taps, NoOp proxies, capability-restricted links, glitch-free invariant wrappers, and a policy cell — consistent with 53's "every deployment primitive is already a kernel/graph primitive."

##### 4.1 Effect classification — per-contract, cut at the boundary

Refine effect classification from a cell marker to a **contract flag**, decided by the same KSP scan that already emits `@Contract(management)` (G-11, 10/12):

```
@Contract(effect = true)   // a WORLD-TOUCHING BOUNDARY contract:
                           // invoking it changes state outside the graph
                           // (DbWriter.persist, EmailSender.send, Ledger.append)
```

- Effect contracts are a third classification axis, **orthogonal** to `management` (data/management) and to ownership markers. `effect=true` implies the contract is served by a **boundary cell** (10/13, 40/43) — the membrane surface where the graph touches the world.
- **Suppression scope (resolves N1×N26, N5×N26):** the membrane NoOp-serves **exactly those shadow inlets whose contract is `effect=true`** — never a cell's data inlets. Internal cells (whose inlets carry ordinary data contracts: `Propagate`, `SetOps`) run **fully**, so every derived delta a judge needs is still emitted. Effect suppression cuts at the *terminal boundary*, not at the interior. This is the "mock side-effecting boundary cells" pattern of 52 §Invariant testing (synthetic), lifted verbatim to live shadows.
- **The shadow owns its own boundary instances.** The candidate cut includes fresh **shadow instances** of every effect-boundary cell (full refs, I-2); the shadow never links to production's real boundary instances. The tap (data) is the *only* edge from production into the shadow. This is what prevents double-fire structurally (the M9.2 control still passes).
- **Coarse fallback (preserves M9.2):** a cell performing *opaque, non-portable* I/O inside its served logic (not via an `effect=true` contract) cannot be surgically suppressed. It keeps the `Effectful` **cell** marker; in shadow mode it is replaced wholesale by a NoOp/mock instance, and — because its interior effect is un-cuttable — it **terminates judgeability downstream of itself** (the judge cannot see faithful output past an opaque-effect cell). The framework flags this at cut construction. P5 guidance: express effects as `effect=true` boundary contracts so they are shadow-suppressible by construction.

##### 4.2 Protocol isolation — the tap is downstream-only

A shadow tap is an ordinary link with a **restricted negotiated protocol-capability set** (building directly on I-1: `Link.protocolCapabilities = intersection of both ports' declared support`, and "unsupported protocols drop silently"):

```
Tap(from: PortRef /*production outlet*/,
    to:   PortRef /*shadow inlet*/,
    capabilities = DOWNSTREAM_ONLY)   // the membrane-side port declares support
                                      // for NO Upstream-direction protocols
```

- Every generic protocol carries a `direction: Upstream | Downstream` on its `ProtocolDescriptor` (I-1, 10/12 §Directionality). The shadow-inlet port declares support only for `Downstream` protocols. The tap link's negotiated set therefore **excludes all upstream protocols**; a shadow-emitted attention or state-request finds no capability on the tap and **drops at the membrane before crossing into production** (I-1 rule: unsupported protocols drop silently).
- **Resolves N3×N26:** a read-only shadow MUST NOT summon production computation. Attention (30/34) raised by the shadow terminates at the membrane — the shadow rides whatever band production already runs at, never inflating production's resourcing (refines P6: interest-that-observes ≠ interest-that-summons). The on-demand state-request protocol (20/21 G-18) is likewise severed upstream; the shadow initializes **only** through the *downstream* late-join catch-up (`onLinked` → state-as-delta-from-empty, 20/21), which production would serve to any subscriber and which is idempotent by OR-set tags (20/24). Downstream protocols (e.g. suspension notices) may pass — they inform the shadow without perturbing production.
- **Invariants** are ordinary subscriber cells *inside* the membrane; they observe data and may observe downstream protocol traffic, but the same downstream-only rule forbids them injecting upstream protocols. "Do invariants observe sub-port traffic?" — yes, as consumers; "do they perturb via sub-ports?" — no, structurally.

##### 4.3 Enclosure — SCC-closed cuts and closed-loop judgeability

- **The cut MUST be SCC-closed (resolves N10×N27, observation half):** if a candidate cell participates in a feedback cycle, the shadow cut includes the *entire* strongly-connected component as shadow instances, with their internal feedback edges as **shadow→shadow links** (real, not suppressed). The loop then closes *inside* the membrane and is judged for its own dynamics. Only edges leaving the SCC to the world (effect boundaries) or entering it from production (taps) cross the membrane.
- **Open-loop-only detection:** if the candidate's SCC would require a feedback edge back *into* production (the loop passes through non-shadowable production), closing it would perturb production. The membrane detects this at cut construction (the SCC crosses the tap boundary) and marks the shadow **open-loop only** — it may be judged as a transfer function on tapped inputs but the promotion policy MUST NOT claim closed-loop guarantees. Closed-loop validation of such a candidate requires promotion into a **canary/staged** instance (an ordinary active-swap with a small blast radius, 53), not a shadow. Honest limitation, flagged rather than faked.
- **Cycle-swap at promotion (resolves N10×N27, swap half):** promoting a cell on a *live* cycle meets 20/22's open wave-re-entry and G-19's open fixpoint. We do not define re-entry here; we **gate on quiescence**: the buffered swap window (53: red → transfer → relink → green) may relink a cell on an active cycle only once the cycle is **quiesced** (delta magnitude below the G-19 threshold). If G-19 throttling is unavailable, cycle-promotion is deferred/gated rather than attempted. This stays consistent with G-19 being open — we *require* quiescence, we do not *invent* fixpoint semantics.

##### 4.4 Trustworthy judgment — glitch-consistent gate invariants

Distinguish two invariant roles (both are `InvariantCell`s, 52 §Invariant testing):

1. **Monitoring invariants** (exploratory): MAY evaluate eagerly and MAY see glitches; used for signal, never as a gate.
2. **Gate invariants** (promotion-deciding): a verdict is trusted **only at a consistent evaluation point**:
   - **Single common upstream fork (a diamond):** the gate invariant MUST be **glitch-free** — composed with the existing `GlitchFreeCell` per-wave version buffering (20/22 §Local glitch-freedom), so it evaluates once per wave over a consistent snapshot and **cannot fire on a transient glitch** (resolves N12×N26). The requirement is structurally checkable: if a gate invariant's inlet set shares a common upstream fork, glitch-freedom is mandatory.
   - **Independent (cross-source) inputs:** by G-20 there is convergence, not simultaneity, so the gate invariant is a **convergence invariant** evaluated at **quiescence** (the shadow's local idle for that wave family), mirroring the harness's "drive to idle, then assert" (52). No global clock is used — quiescence is local per source family (P4).

A gate violation is therefore trustworthy *by construction*: it corresponds to a wave-consistent snapshot (diamond case) or a converged state (cross-source case), never to a transient no consistent snapshot exhibits.

##### 4.5 Promotion policy — window, threshold, judge, differential

Make the promotion policy a concrete, serializable object consumed by an ordinary judge cell (53 §Trust boundary: "promotion authority is a membrane/policy concern, 43"):

```
PromotionPolicy(
  gates:     Set<InvariantRef>,        // glitch-free / convergence gate invariants (§4.4)
  window:    ObservationWindow,        // observed-wave count AND/OR coverage-stability
  threshold: SatisfactionCriterion,    // e.g. ZERO gate-violations over window
  judge:     CellRef,                  // policy cell; per-runtime authority (43)
  baseline:  Differential? = null      // optional incumbent comparison
)
```

- **Window (P4-safe):** measured in **observed production waves** and/or **coverage stabilization / heuristic saturation** — the exact stopping criteria 52 §Invariant testing already commits to — never wall-clock, never a global barrier. Decentralized and local.
- **Threshold:** strict default = zero gate-violations over the window. Where the incumbent itself violates some invariant, use the **differential** criterion: candidate's violation set ⊆ incumbent's ("no worse than incumbent").
- **Differential shadow (the faithful-judgment core, resolves N26×N27):** spawn incumbent *and* candidate as **parallel shadows tapped from the same production outlets**, both effect-suppressed, both judged by the same gate invariants. Because inputs are identical (same taps) and effects are suppressed on both, the comparison is controlled and faithful. Promote iff the candidate satisfies the threshold **and** is no-worse than the incumbent on the shared gates. This is what "judge faithfully" means concretely, and it reuses I-2's full-ref instance model (two instance sets, one logicalId).
- **Judge = a cell.** The judge is an ordinary policy cell (P1) that subscribes to the gate invariants' `violations` outlets and emits a promote/reject decision; on satisfaction it triggers `Promotion.promote` (the buffered swap, 53/G-33), with rollback by symmetry. Authority is per-runtime policy (single-developer today → federated governance, 53 §Trust boundary, 43).

##### 4.6 The membrane as one object

```
ShadowSpec(
  cut:   Set<CellRef>,   // shadow instances (full refs); SCC-closed; owns its effect boundaries
  taps:  Set<Tap>,       // production outlet → shadow inlet, DOWNSTREAM_ONLY
  policy: PromotionPolicy // gates + window + threshold + judge (+ optional differential)
)
```

`Shadow.spawn` (existing) is generalized to build this: spawn the cut, NoOp-serve every `effect=true` inlet, create downstream-only taps, attach gate invariants, register the judge. All four isolation/judgment properties fall out of one boundary object.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — membrane = taps (links) + NoOp/glitch-free (proxies) + a policy cell; every part meaningful single-threaded (the harness already runs shadows on `SimulationController`). No new kernel primitive (53's own test). |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — production data path untouched; a tap is one extra `Broadcast` branch; NoOp, glitch-free wrapping, capability negotiation, and SCC analysis are off-production, rare-path (spawn/link-time). |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — taps and shadow links are explicit, inspectable objects; the membrane is a visible boundary; no hidden fan (the shadow owns its boundary instances). |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global clock/lock/barrier; window is per-observed-wave/coverage; gate verdicts trusted at local per-wave (glitch-free) or local-quiescence (convergence) points. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — `effect=true` is a compile-time KSP flag; suppression scope is derived from it; downstream-only is a typed capability set; glitch-free-gate requirement is structurally checkable; opaque-effect cells flagged. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied (refined)** — the shadow expresses interest via the tap (legitimate fan-out cost) but MUST NOT summon production via upstream protocols; interest-that-observes is severed from interest-that-summons. |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Satisfied** — the observation membrane *is* the P7 boundary-control instrument (a directional membrane with per-direction policy). |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — shadow/differential/promote/rollback are graph ops over full-ref instances; nothing assumes a static graph. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `ShadowSpec`/`PromotionPolicy`/`Tap` are plain serializable data; taps and invariants use existing wire forms; no lambdas/reflection introduced. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — live, incremental, decentralized shadowing of real production data (not a clone); the honest open-loop/canary distinction is the niche-first trade. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-32 (Resolved M9.2: `Effectful` marker + `Shadow.spawn` NoOp-serves effectful inlets):** ⚠ **CONFLICT (granularity), flagged.** This resolution **amends the suppression granularity** from *cell* to *contract*: the membrane NoOp-serves `effect=true` boundary-contract inlets, not "every fan-in inlet of an `Effectful` cell." Justification: the cell-granularity rule deletes the derived emissions a judge needs for any cell that is both effectful and mid-graph (N5×N26); it is correct only for pure terminal sinks, which remain a special case here. The `Effectful` cell marker is **retained** as the coarse fallback for opaque-effect cells, and the M9.2 double-fire control still passes (the shadow owns its boundary instances). This amends the *mechanism* of an item marked Resolved, so it is flagged per protocol; it resolves the explicitly-named residue rather than reopening G-32's core.
- **G-20 per-source waves (Timestamp(sourceId, counter); convergence not simultaneity):** Consistent, reinforced — gate invariants over cross-source joins are convergence-evaluated at local quiescence, not treated as simultaneous.
- **SID-UP global propagation locks REJECTED:** Consistent — no global barrier; glitch-free gates use the existing local per-wave wrapper; quiescence is local.
- **Host is the unit of mobility:** Consistent — shadow instances are hosted like any cell; migration of a shadow is ordinary.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive (TrafficLight / registry parking):** Consistent — the promotion swap reuses the buffered window (53); cycle-swap gates on quiescence within it; no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local|Remote; one park/replay:** Consistent — taps and shadow links resolve through the existing registry; no new location semantics.
- **A snapshot IS a delta:** Consistent — shadow initialization is `onLinked` state-as-delta-from-empty (20/21); no snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, NOT wave ids:** Consistent — untouched; shadow catch-up idempotence relies on OR-set tags (20/24).
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context:** Consistent — `effect=true` is a third classification axis orthogonal to `management`; effect contracts are push-only data-boundary contracts.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol:** Consistent — the differential shadow is two full-ref instance sets over ordinary taps; no new sync protocol. Builds on I-2.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism:** Untouched.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved:** Consistent — `effect` flag rides the generated `ContractDescriptor` (like `management`); no new wire addressing.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end:** Consistent — the promotion swap uses the buffered drain window unchanged; taps are ordinary FIFO links.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time:** Consistent — taps are ordinary fan-out subscriptions enforced at link time; downstream-only is a capability, not a cardinality change.
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross machines:** Consistent — effect contracts and taps carry ordinary data; unaffected.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind full refs (I-2):** Consistent, depended-upon — shadow instances are full refs; the differential shadow and gate-invariant-to-candidate linking are the "ordinary operation" I-2 established.
- **I-1 metadata plane (protocols ride links, Upstream/Downstream descriptor, capability intersection, unsupported drop):** Consistent, depended-upon — the downstream-only tap is exactly a restricted capability set over I-1's mechanism.
- **Gaps/conflicts Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved:** Honored except the explicit G-32 granularity amendment above, which is the sanctioned way to touch a Resolved item.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **50/52 §Live invariants (production):** rewrite the "Mechanically this needs …" and "(G-32 resolved)" paragraphs to the observation-membrane model: per-contract `effect=true` suppression at the boundary (not per-cell), downstream-only taps, SCC-closed cuts with open-loop detection, glitch-free/convergence gate invariants, and the shadow-owns-its-boundary-instances rule.
- **50/52 §Invariant testing (synthetic):** note that gate invariants over shared-fork fan-ins must be glitch-free and cross-source gates convergence-evaluated at quiescence; monitoring vs gate roles.
- **50/53 §Model / §Mechanical decomposition:** add the `PromotionPolicy` shape (gates/window/threshold/judge/differential), the differential-shadow judging pattern, and the cycle-swap-requires-quiescence rule; update the decomposition table row "Judge" to reference the policy object.
- **10/12 §Contracts are push-only (G-11):** add `effect=true` as a third `@Contract` classification axis (KSP-scanned like `management`), and state that effect classification for shadow mode moves from the `Effectful` cell marker to the effect-contract flag, with the cell marker retained as coarse fallback.
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports / §Directionality:** note the downstream-only tap capability set as the shadow-isolation use of I-1's negotiated capabilities and the Upstream/Downstream descriptor.
- **20/21 §Pull:** state that a shadow initializes only through downstream `onLinked` catch-up; the upstream on-demand state-request protocol is severed at the membrane.
- **20/22 §Local glitch-freedom / §Interaction (cycles):** note that promotion gate invariants reuse `GlitchFreeCell`; cycle-promotion gates on G-19 quiescence pending wave-re-entry resolution.
- **90/91 G-32:** update the Resolved row to reference the observation-membrane refinement (contract-granularity suppression, protocol isolation, SCC enclosure, gate-consistency, promotion policy); flag the granularity amendment.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Effect-contract flag generation & lint:** KSP must emit `effect` on `ContractDescriptor`, and lint/flag cells performing opaque I/O outside `effect=true` boundaries as "shadow-unsafe (coarse-fallback only)." The exact detection of opaque effects is heuristic and needs pinning.
- **Downstream-only capability realization on the wire:** cross-host taps must negotiate a downstream-only set over the bridge (I-1's follow-on cross-host protocol-frame path); a generative test that a shadow-emitted upstream protocol never reaches a remote production peer.
- **SCC analysis for cut construction:** computing the strongly-connected component a candidate participates in, and detecting membrane-crossing feedback (open-loop-only), across hosts and the wire, needs a reverse-topology walk (ties to I-2's promotion-swap reverse index follow-on).
- **Cycle-promotion / G-19 dependency:** the quiescence gate presumes G-19 magnitude throttling; the swap-during-cycle wave-re-entry semantics remain open (20/22 §Cycles).
- **Promotion policy surface:** `ObservationWindow` (observed-wave-count vs coverage-stability vs saturation), `SatisfactionCriterion` grammar, and the differential "no-worse-than-incumbent" comparison over non-total violation orders need a concrete design and generative harness.
- **Judge authority & federated promotion:** who may register a `PromotionPolicy` / trigger a swap under federated governance is a 43 membrane-policy design left open by 53 §Trust boundary.
- **Canary/staged promotion for open-loop-only candidates:** the small-blast-radius active-swap path for candidates whose closed-loop dynamics cannot be shadowed is named here but undesigned.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The resolution is strongly grounded: it reuses shipped primitives (`Shadow.spawn`, NoOp proxies, `GlitchFreeCell`, `onLinked` catch-up, `Promotion.promote` buffered swap, I-1 capability negotiation, I-2 full-ref instances) and adds exactly one classification bit (`effect=true`) plus one membrane/policy object — squarely inside 53's "no new kernel mechanism" test. The five member-pair tensions each dissolve under the single observation-membrane boundary rather than five patches. Confidence is not higher because (1) the G-32 granularity amendment touches a Resolved item (flagged, justified, but a genuine change); (2) closed-loop judgeability has an honest hard limit (open-loop-only + canary) rather than a full solution; and (3) cycle-promotion depends on the still-open G-19 quiescence.

**Open questions:** (a) whether opaque-effect detection can be made correct-by-construction (a marker/effect-region type) rather than heuristic lint; (b) the exact `ObservationWindow`/`SatisfactionCriterion` grammar and how differential comparison orders partial violation sets; (c) whether an open-loop shadow verdict should ever be *sufficient* for promotion or always require a canary stage for cycle-participating candidates.

### I-18 — Wave completeness when an edge will not deliver: absorbed, suspended, restarted, or dead-lettered inputs

> Member pairs: N8×N12, N12×N14, N12×N18, N12×N21, N13×N21
> Existing gaps touched: G-6, G-26 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 2/5 member pairs largely addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The other four causes and the unifying protocol: the Progress watermark (an absorbed-then-quiet arm still stalls a WAITing join — effective-only silence has no positive completeness signal), the typed Stall/Resume family with RESTARTING/DEAD_LETTERED/LOST a…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: a glitch-free join buffers per-wave inputs
"until the input set for that wave is complete on every frontier edge"
(20/22 §Local glitch-freedom, step 2), but the spec never defines how
*completeness* is established for an edge that **will not deliver** a wave-*t*
contribution. Five causes produce a non-delivering edge, and none has a stated
completeness rule:

1. **Absorbed** — effective-only emission means "empty deltas are not emitted"
   (20/21 §Incremental vs complete, rule 2). An upstream arm that has no
   effective change for wave *t* emits nothing, so that frontier edge is
   *silent* for *t* — and silence is locally indistinguishable from
   not-yet-arrived (20/21 §rule 2; 20/22 §Local glitch-freedom).
2. **Suspended** — attention parks one branch of a diamond; 30/34 §Decision 3
   itself flags this open and ships a WAIT/DEGRADE fallback for the *cross-host
   suspension* case only ("a glitch-free join above a remotely suspended branch
   sees an incomplete wave and holds the group").
3. **Restarted** — the glitch-free version buffer is cell state; supervision
   RESTART "restore[s] the spawn-time `Stateful` checkpoint" (30/31 §Normative
   rules 5), silently discarding delivered-but-unflushed per-wave inputs that
   the exactly-once upstream never re-sends — permanently stalling the wave.
4. **Dead-lettered** — an undeliverable contribution is published as
   `DeadLetter` (30/31 §rule 5, G-26) and never reaches the buffer, leaving its
   wave forever incomplete, with no timeout/degrade semantics stated.
5. **Held exclusive payload** — an `Owned`/`Leased` argument can sit
   indefinitely in a version buffer awaiting a wave that may never complete,
   while `Leased` "must be released" (20/23 §The four contracts); 20/23's
   exclusivity-preservation clause covers only the *mobility* Buffering proxy
   ("the Buffering proxy MAY hold them"), not glitch-free version buffers.

A resolution must define **(a)** the *edge-status protocol* — how absorbed,
suspended, and failed edges are advertised — and **(b)** the join's
*wait-vs-degrade-vs-re-scope* semantics, extending the WAIT/DEGRADE direction
30/34 records for suspension to the other four unavailability causes and to
held exclusive payloads.

**Member pairs** all pull on this one axis: N8×N12 (absorption vs completeness),
N12×N14 (held `Owned`/`Leased` in a version buffer), N12×N18 (RESTART discards
buffers; dead-letter leaves a wave incomplete), N12×N21 (30/34's own open
question: advertise incomplete-by-suspension so joins choose wait-vs-degrade),
N13×N21 (whether disinterest-unlinks are versioned topology events that let
joins re-scope).

**Why the spec leaves it open**: 20/22 §Local glitch-freedom states the *goal*
("buffer per-wave inputs until the input set for that wave is complete") but the
shipped static-frontier `GlitchFreeCell` establishes completeness only by
*monotone per-source arrival* — "per-link FIFO makes wave completion monotone
per source" (20/22 §The glitch-free frontier), i.e. a *later* wave on an edge
implicitly closes earlier waves on that edge. That rule has no answer when **no
later wave comes** (absorption-then-quiesce) or when **an open edge stops
advancing** (suspend/restart/dead-letter). 30/34 §Decision 3 supplies WAIT/DEGRADE
for one cause (cross-host suspension) via downstream suspended/resumed notices,
but explicitly notes "notices are single-hop" and does not cover absorption,
