restart, dead-letter, or the exclusive-payload obligation.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **Effective-only emission (20/21) vs the completeness condition (20/22).**
  These two shipped, normative rules are in direct tension: 20/21 says *do not
  emit* for an empty change; 20/22 says *wait until every edge has contributed*.
  Under WAIT-correctness there is no way to reconcile them locally without a
  *positive* completeness signal that is **not** a data delta — silence must be
  made observable, but making it a delta would violate effective-only and
  re-excite cycles.
- **P4 forbids the obvious fix.** A global barrier that advanced every source in
  lockstep would tell each join when a wave is "done everywhere," but that is
  the SID-UP global propagation lock that is REJECTED (20/22; recorded
  decision), and G-20 abolished the global clock such a barrier would need.
- **P2/P6 vs universal progress signalling.** Absorption is the *common* case on
  filter/ref-count arms (20/21's `UnionSetCell` example). A completeness signal
  emitted on every absorbed wave, on every edge, regardless of downstream
  interest, taxes exactly the path P2 budgets at "a volatile read + an enqueue"
  and P6 forbids paying "just in case."
- **P1/determinism vs timeouts.** The intuitive "degrade after a timeout" answer
  needs a clock; the deterministic simulation host reads *scheduling-step ticks
  bound by the host, never wall time* (30/34 §Decision 1). A wall-clock timeout
  is non-deterministic and un-simulatable.
- **Recoverable vs terminal non-delivery need opposite dispositions.** A
  suspended edge *will* resume and re-serve (WAIT is correct — park-not-drop); a
  dead-lettered contribution *is gone* (WAIT stalls forever — the join must
  abandon the wave). The join cannot pick correctly without knowing which.
- **The exclusive-payload obligation adds a liveness deadline** the glitch-free
  buffer was never designed to honour: WAIT is "correct, latency-unbounded"
  (30/34) — but an unbounded hold of a `Leased` payload starves its pool
  (20/23), turning a latency cost into a resource-safety failure.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Local timeout-to-degrade (per-wave timers)

Each glitch-free join arms a per-wave deadline; if a frontier edge has not
delivered wave *t* when the deadline fires, the join drops that edge and
evaluates over the remainder.

- *Semantics*: completeness = "everyone delivered, or the clock ran out."
- *Fast-path cost*: none in steady state; a timer per in-flight wave.
- *Failure modes*: the deadline is a **clock** — non-deterministic, breaking the
  simulation host (30/34 §Decision 1, P1); it cannot distinguish *benign
  absorption* (edge is fine, just had nothing to say) from *failure* (edge is
  gone), so it degrades correct joins on slow-but-healthy arms; and it never
  makes absorption *positive*, so a WAIT join still cannot tell "absorbed" from
  "in flight."
- *Tradeoff*: a coarse liveness backstop, not a semantics. **Rejected as the
  primary mechanism**; survives only as an opt-in, tick-counted last resort
  (§4), the analogue of I-5's hop guard.

##### Candidate B — Positive per-edge watermark + edge-status protocol + join stall policy (recommended)

Make silence *positive*: each frontier edge carries a per-source **watermark**
(highest counter known settled). A real delta advances it (its counter closes
all earlier waves by per-link FIFO monotonicity, exactly as the shipped wrapper
already relies on); an **absorb-ack** advances it with no data when the arm goes
quiet; a later wave subsumes both. Indefinite non-delivery is advertised as a
**Stall(reason, recoverable)** edge-status marker; the join applies a per-edge
**WAIT | DEGRADE | RE-SCOPE** policy. All markers ride the I-1 metadata plane,
gated on downstream glitch-free interest, and extend I-13's `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`
family (edges entering/leaving the frontier) with the *edge not delivering*
case.

- *Semantics*: completeness = every OPEN edge's watermark ≥ *t*; a stuck
  watermark is resolved by policy according to the advertised recoverability.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero for non-glitch-free graphs (interest-gated, P6); in
  active flow real deltas carry the watermark (no extra messages); explicit
  markers fire only at a *quiescence boundary* (an arm absorbs then falls idle
  while a downstream waits) — O(idle transitions), not O(waves).
- *Failure modes*: multi-hop/transitive stalls and deep absorbing chains need
  re-emission (single-hop today, §8); a lost marker needs the Candidate-A
  backstop.
- *Tradeoff*: one protocol family covers all five causes; it is the *minimal*
  extension of the shipped monotone-completion mechanism (adds "positive close
  at quiescence" + "stall policy"). **Recommended.**

##### Candidate C — Pull-on-block (request-watermark upstream)

The join, when blocked on an edge, *pulls*: a `RequestWatermark` travels
upstream (the state-request protocol, I-1/G-18, 20/21), answered with the edge's
current watermark or a catch-up.

- *Semantics*: completeness probed on demand; no proactive markers.
- *Fast-path cost*: cheapest steady state (no absorb-acks at all).
- *Failure modes*: a round-trip per block (latency); must recurse for deep
  chains (the transitive case 30/34 flags open); and a *genuinely failed* edge
  will not answer — distinguishing "slow" from "dead" needs a timeout, dragging
  in Candidate A's clock.
- *Tradeoff*: excellent for a deep, mostly-quiet chain; poor for continuous
  absorption (push-on-quiesce beats a probe-per-block there). **Folded into B**
  as the DEGRADE "is-it-really-stalled" probe and the deep-chain fallback, not
  the base mechanism.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. The five causes collapse to one local view — *a frontier
edge's per-source watermark is not advancing to t* — and the mechanism is: make
absorption advance the watermark positively, advertise indefinite non-delivery
as a typed edge-status, and let the join resolve a stuck watermark by a per-edge
policy keyed on **recoverability**. This *completes* the frontier protocol I-13
began (edges entering/leaving) with the edge *not delivering* case.

##### 4.1 Data shapes — the frontier/completeness protocol

A downstream-directional generic protocol on the **I-1 metadata plane**
(`PORT_PROTOCOL`, null MessageContext, own lane/band, `FanOutBroadcast`),
**gated on a downstream having expressed completeness interest** (a glitch-free
consumer), exactly as I-13 gates `EdgeEvent`. It extends I-13's family:

```
sealed interface FrontierEvent { val link: LinkId; val source: SourceId }

// I-13 (recap): edge enters / leaves the glitch-free frontier
data class EdgeOpen (link, source, floor: Long)  : FrontierEvent  // floor = counter at which L joined
data class EdgeClose(link, source)               : FrontierEvent  // unlink; terminal; drop from frontier

// I-18 additions:
// watermark advance WITHOUT a data delta — "L is settled through counter `thru`, nothing effective"
data class Progress (link, source, thru: Long)   : FrontierEvent  // the absorb-ack / quiescence flush

// L cannot advance past `at` for the foreseeable future
data class Stall    (link, source, at: Long, reason: StallReason) : FrontierEvent
enum class StallReason(val recoverable: Boolean) {
    SUSPENDED    (true),   // attention park (30/34) — upstream will resume
    RESTARTING   (true),   // supervision RESTART of an upstream contributor (30/31)
    DEAD_LETTERED(false),  // an undeliverable contribution (G-26) — the wave value is gone
    LOST         (false),  // an exactly-once input dropped (e.g. this join's own buffer on RESTART)
}

// L recovered; resume with a catch-up baseline that re-floors the edge
data class Resume   (link, source, floor: Long)  : FrontierEvent  // floor from state-as-delta catch-up (21)
```

`Progress`/`Stall`/`Resume` **carry an explicit `thru`/`at`/`floor` counter** in
the per-source wave domain (G-20). They are therefore ordered *by counter value*,
not by lane position: applying them out of order is idempotent
(`watermark := max`), satisfying the I-1 rule-3 reorder/duplication tolerance
that riding the out-of-band metadata lane demands. This is a small **refinement
of I-13**, whose `EdgeOpen` used a *consumer-computed* floor; carrying the
counter explicitly makes the marker lane-independent and safe against a lagging
upstream without relying on in-band FIFO position.

##### 4.2 Join state and the watermark

A glitch-free join holds, per inlink `L` per source `s`:

```
status(L,s)     : OPEN | STALLED(reason) | CLOSED
floor(L,s)      : Long              // pre-floor arrivals discarded (I-13)
watermark(L,s)  : Long              // highest counter known settled on L for s
stallPolicy(L)  : WAIT | DEGRADE    // per-edge, opt-in; default WAIT
```

**Watermark advance** (the core "silence → positive" rule):

- On a **data delta** for wave `(s, c)` on `L`: buffer it; `watermark(L,s) =
  max(watermark, c)`. Per-link FIFO ⇒ every counter `< c` on `L` is already
  settled (delivered earlier *or absorbed*); the gap counters are the absorbed
  waves, correctly counted as "no contribution from `L`."
- On **`Progress(L,s,thru)`**: `watermark(L,s) = max(watermark, thru)`.
- On **`EdgeOpen`/`Resume`**: (re)establish `floor(L,s)`; `watermark := floor`.

**When is `Progress` emitted?** Only when it is *needed to unblock a waiting
downstream*: an upstream feeding a glitch-free frontier advertises a fresh
watermark **at a quiescence boundary** — it processed a wave, emitted no derived
delta, and has no further pending input. In continuous flow the *next* real
delta's counter subsumes all intervening absorbed waves, so **steady state emits
no `Progress` at all**; the marker fires only at the trailing edge of activity,
which is precisely when the join would otherwise stall on an absorbed-then-quiet
arm. Coalescing (`max`) means one marker retires an arbitrary run of absorbed
waves. (Deep/cross-host chains where push-on-quiesce is awkward MAY instead use
Candidate C's `RequestWatermark` pull — §8.)

##### 4.3 Completeness and the stall policy

**Completeness** of wave `(s, t)`:

```
complete(s,t)  ⟺  ∀ inlink L :  status(L,s)=OPEN ∧ floor(L,s) < t  ⟹  watermark(L,s) ≥ t
```

CLOSED edges are excluded (I-13's frontier-shrink); STALLED edges are resolved
by policy below. When `complete(s,t)` holds, the local evaluation barrier fires
once over the buffered `(s,t)` contributions, flushes, and advances the
flush-mark — **unchanged from the shipped wrapper**; I-18 only changes *how a
stuck edge is retired*.

**Stall policy.** If an OPEN `L` has `watermark(L,s) < t` and a `Stall(L,s,at,
reason)` with `at < t` is in force:

- **Recoverable** (`SUSPENDED`, `RESTARTING`):
  - **WAIT** (default): `(s,t)` stays pending; **park-not-drop** (30/34 §Decision
    2, 30/33) — correct, latency-unbounded. On `Resume(L,s,floor)`: re-floor `L`;
    replayed waves `≥ at` are delivered as **late-join catch-up** (20/21),
    idempotent by tags (20/24); completeness resumes. This is 30/34's shipped
    behaviour, now reached through the unified protocol.
  - **DEGRADE** (opt-in per edge): set `status(L,s)=STALLED`; drop `L` from the
    frontier of all pending `(s,·)` waves `≥ at`; evaluate them over the reduced
    set (flagging the emission DEGRADED); on `Resume`, restore `L` and treat its
    catch-up as a fresh baseline. This **reuses the frontier-shrink semantics
    unlink already has** (30/34 §Decision 3, 20/22).
- **Terminal** (`DEAD_LETTERED`, `LOST`):
  - **RE-SCOPE** (the only admissible disposition — WAIT would stall forever):
    advance `watermark(L,s) := t` past the lost wave; the lost `(s,t)`
    contribution on `L` is *abandoned*; the join surfaces a `GlitchViolation`
    (via the opt-in `ErrorReporting`/`CellError` path, 30/31 §rule 5) so the
    loss flows through visible topology to an invariant cell; the wave is then
    evaluated over the reduced set and completeness continues. Re-scope is
    "advance the floor and record the wound" — it keeps the join live at the
    cost of one flagged, provably-lossy wave, rather than deadlocking the whole
    downstream subgraph on an input that will never arrive.

The three dispositions answer the challenge's "wait-vs-degrade-vs-re-scope"
directly: **WAIT** and **DEGRADE** for recoverable stalls (generalising 30/34's
suspension case to restart), **RE-SCOPE** for terminal loss (dead-letter,
exactly-once drop).

##### 4.4 Absorption (cause 1) — resolved by the watermark

An arm that absorbs wave `t` and keeps flowing needs **no marker** — its next
real delta advances the watermark past `t`. An arm that absorbs `t` and *goes
quiet* emits one `Progress(L,s,t)` at its quiescence boundary; the join's wave
`t` completes with "no contribution from `L`." Effective-only emission (20/21) is
**untouched**: no empty *data* delta is ever emitted; `Progress` is a *metadata*
completeness signal, not a data delta, and carries no state. This is WAIT-correct
and needs neither DEGRADE nor re-scope — absorption is *benign* absence, not a
stall.

##### 4.5 Suspension (cause 2) — Stall(SUSPENDED)

A host parking an upstream contributor emits `Stall(L,s,at,SUSPENDED)` downstream
(the "suspended notice" 30/34 already ships, now typed into the family). The join
WAITs (park-not-drop) or DEGRADEs per §4.3; `Resume(L,s,floor)` carries the
post-resume catch-up baseline. **N13×N21 division of labour**: a *disinterest-**unlink*** is I-13's `EdgeClose` (a versioned topology event — the edge leaves
the frontier permanently, re-scoping wave-*t* completeness); a *disinterest-**suspend/park*** is I-18's recoverable `Stall(SUSPENDED)`. The join re-scopes on
unlink and WAIT/DEGRADEs on suspend — the two halves of "attention drops an edge"
land on the two halves of the frontier protocol.

##### 4.6 Restart (cause 3) — transient buffer + re-catch-up

Two sub-cases, both resolved on existing machinery:

- **An upstream contributor restarts.** From the join it presents as
  `Stall(L,s,at,RESTARTING)` (recoverable) followed by `Resume` with a catch-up
  baseline (state-as-delta-from-empty, 20/21 §onLinked). Handled by §4.3's
  recoverable branch — no new mechanism. The waves the upstream "un-emitted" by
  rolling back are subsumed because catch-up serves *current* state idempotently
  (20/24 tags).
- **The join itself restarts.** The glitch-free version buffer is declared
  **transient** — *not* captured by `Stateful.snapshot` (a `@Transient`-style
  structural rule, P5). On RESTART the join restores its durable checkpoint
  (owned state), then **re-runs frontier discovery + re-catch-up**: each frontier
  upstream re-serves state-as-delta-from-empty (the `onLinked` path, 20/21),
  re-flooring every edge at the current wave. The discarded buffered inputs are
  **safe to drop precisely because they were unflushed** — never observed
  downstream — so no downstream sees an inconsistency; the join resumes
  glitch-free at a fresh floor. This is the "RESTART = re-catch-up rather than
  restore-a-stale-buffer" direction I-2 §8 and I-3 §8 already flagged, made
  concrete for the glitch-free buffer. It requires exactly-once upstream to *not*
  re-send: it doesn't — the join rebuilds from *current state*, not from replayed
  history.

##### 4.7 Dead-letter (cause 4) — Stall(DEAD_LETTERED) → re-scope

When a host dead-letters an invocation destined for (or emitted from a frontier
upstream toward) a glitch-free join, it emits `Stall(L,s,at,DEAD_LETTERED)`
alongside the existing `DeadLetter` (30/31 §rule 5, G-26). The contribution is
gone; the join RE-SCOPEs (§4.3 terminal), advancing past the poisoned wave and
surfacing a `GlitchViolation`. Glitch-freedom over that one wave is *impossible*
by construction (the data is lost); the honest disposition is to abandon it
loudly and stay live, not to WAIT forever or silently DEGRADE.

##### 4.8 Held exclusive payloads (cause 5) — link-time rule + policy release

A version buffer holding an exclusive payload for a wave that may never complete:

- **`Frozen` / `Borrowed` snapshot / plain values**: buffer freely — no
  obligation, indefinite hold is safe.
- **`Owned`**: buffering *preserves exclusivity* (20/23: "the Buffering proxy
  MAY hold them") — **allowed**. A stalled wave's held `Owned` is a *liveness*,
  not a *safety*, concern: it is released when the stall policy resolves the wave
  — DEGRADE/RE-SCOPE *drop* the buffered contribution, which is safe because the
  sender already moved-from it (`Owned.take()` is consume-once, 20/23). No
  exclusivity is violated by discarding a consumed `Owned`.
- **`Leased`**: **REFUSED at link time on a glitch-free frontier edge** (P5,
  20/23 §The SPSC link rule enforcement point 1). An unbounded WAIT would hold
  the lease past its mandatory release, starving the pool — a resource-safety
  failure the buffer cannot honour. The producer must `freeze()` first (20/23:
  "freeze or copy first"); `Frozen` is fan-out-safe with no release obligation
  and buffers indefinitely. *Escape hatch*: an edge may instead declare
  `stallPolicy = DEGRADE` with a bounded hold that releases the lease on
  degrade — but the link-time refusal is the default, correct-by-construction
  answer. This extends 20/23's boundary rule ("`Leased` MUST NOT cross machine
  boundaries") to a new boundary: **`Leased` MUST NOT enter an unbounded-WAIT
  glitch-free buffer.**

##### 4.9 Liveness backstop (opt-in)

For malformed graphs or a lost marker (no `Progress`/`Stall`/`Resume` ever
arrives), a join MAY arm a coarse **scheduling-step deadline** — counted in host
ticks, never wall time (30/34 §Decision 1, P1/determinism) — after which a
stuck edge is forced to DEGRADE (recoverable-assumed) or RE-SCOPE. Off by
default; the analogue of I-5's hop guard: it fires only when the protocol has
already failed, and never perturbs a correctly-signalled frontier.

##### 4.10 The load-bearing summary

All five causes reduce to one local predicate — *is this OPEN edge's watermark
advancing to t?* — and one typed answer: **ADVANCE** (delta or `Progress` —
absorption is benign, wave completes), **STALL-RECOVERABLE** (`SUSPENDED`/
`RESTARTING` — WAIT park-not-drop, or DEGRADE-and-restore), **STALL-TERMINAL**
(`DEAD_LETTERED`/`LOST` — RE-SCOPE and surface). One protocol family completes
I-13's frontier events; one stall policy generalises 30/34's WAIT/DEGRADE;
`Owned`/`Leased` obligations are a link-time rule plus policy-driven release.
Nothing global, nothing on the data hot path, no new kernel primitive.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — watermark advance, completeness, and stall policy are per-cell folds over `FrontierEvent`s; RESTART re-catch-up is spawn+link+catch-up; every rule meaningful single-threaded (the shipped `GlitchFreeCell` already runs under `SimulationController`). Tick-counted backstop, never wall time. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — zero for non-glitch-free graphs (interest-gated); steady flow emits no extra markers (real deltas carry the watermark); `Progress` fires only at quiescence boundaries (O(idle transitions)); the data path is untouched. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — edge status rides explicit links on the metadata plane, inspectable; the frontier *is* the current OPEN edge set; stalls and re-scopes are visible events, not hidden decay. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — every join resolves completeness from its own frontier's per-source watermarks; no global clock/lock/barrier; cross-source stays convergence-not-simultaneity (G-20). |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — recoverability is a typed field on `StallReason`; the version buffer is structurally transient; `Leased`-on-glitch-free-edge is refused at link time; `Progress`/`Stall` carry their counter (reorder-idempotent). |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — markers materialise only toward a glitch-free (completeness-interested) downstream; nothing is signalled "just in case"; absorption on an uninterested arm stays free. |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — no bearing on boundary controls. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — the frontier is recomputed under link/unlink (I-13) and now under stall/resume; nothing assumes a static or fully-delivering edge set; RESTART rebuilds by catch-up. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `FrontierEvent`s are ids-only (`LinkId` + `SourceId` + counters); they cross the wire as an I-13-style `WireFrame`/`PORT_PROTOCOL` frame; no lambdas/handles. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — a bounded, interest-gated completeness signal for long-lived incremental dataflow; deliberately not a global progress/coordination protocol. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: watermarks, completeness, and stalls are
  all per `(source, counter)`; markers carry counters in that domain; no global
  coordinator.
- **SID-UP global propagation locks REJECTED** — Consistent: completeness is
  resolved per-join-locally; no global order, lock, or barrier introduced.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent: migration is not a stall (the
  logical edge is invariant, I-13); the parked buffer travels as cell state
  (20/22 §Interaction); only a genuine suspend/restart/fail is a `Stall`.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent:
  WAIT reuses park-not-drop (30/34 §Decision 2); `Stall(SUSPENDED)` is the typed
  form of the notice 30/34 already ships; no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay mechanism** — Consistent:
  cross-host `Stall`/`Resume` are frames on the link's bridge (I-13's
  `WireFrame` EdgeEvent, extended); re-resolution/park/replay unchanged.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: `Resume` and RESTART re-catch-up are
  state-as-delta-from-empty (20/21); no snapshot type introduced.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps minted cell-locally, NOT wave ids** — Consistent:
  watermarks/counters are wave-domain; OR-set tags on catch-up deltas are
  untouched and keep completeness idempotent under replay.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent:
  `FrontierEvent`s are metadata-plane (I-1), null context, management-class,
  push-only; effective-only *data* emission (20/21) is preserved intact.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** —
  Consistent: the watermark is a per-edge *completeness* signal, **not** a
  version vector or anti-entropy digest; it rides existing links; it is not a
  synchronization protocol. Mergeable (replicated) consumers ignore the frontier
  entirely (I-13), so gossip edge churn does not stall completeness.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: `FrontierEvent`
  frames are ids-only under the reserved version byte, joining I-13's EdgeEvent
  frame type.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent and
  *depended upon*: the watermark's monotone-close correctness rests on per-link
  FIFO; markers carry counters so they order by value on the out-of-band lane
  (I-1 rule 3), reconciling I-13's in-band ordering with I-1's separate-lane
  model.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time** — Consistent: the `Leased`-on-glitch-free
  refusal is a link-time check, alongside the SPSC exclusive bit (20/23).
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross machines** —
  Consistent, extended: `Owned` in a glitch-free buffer preserves exclusivity;
  `Leased` is refused at the new glitch-free-buffer boundary (freeze first).
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind full refs (I-2)** — Consistent:
  watermarks key on the full-ref `PortRef` edge; RESTART preserves `instanceId`
  (I-2), so re-catch-up is same-instance; per-instance frontiers.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — G-6 (attention,
  M6) and G-26 (error handling, M3.5/M4.4) stay resolved; this **elaborates**
  their residuals (30/34's single-hop-notice and open WAIT/DEGRADE question;
  G-26's dead-letter as an edge-status). No shipped decision is reversed.

**No CONFLICT flag required.** The one refinement — I-13's *consumer-computed*
floor becomes a *marker-carried* counter for the out-of-band lane — amends a
sibling *resolution* (not a recorded decision) and is called out in §4.1.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/22 §Local glitch-freedom / §The glitch-free frontier** — Add the positive
  completeness rule: an edge's per-source **watermark** advances on a data delta,
  on a `Progress` absorb-ack, or on a later wave; completeness = every OPEN edge
  with floor < *t* has watermark ≥ *t*. State that effective-only silence is
  closed by `Progress` at a quiescence boundary, and that the version buffer is
  **transient** (RESTART re-catch-up, not restore).
- **20/22 §Interaction → Cycles/Suspension** — Add the stall policy
  (WAIT/DEGRADE/RE-SCOPE) and the recoverable-vs-terminal distinction; cross-ref
  I-13 for `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` and this resolution for `Progress`/`Stall`/
  `Resume`.
- **20/21 §Incremental vs complete (rule 2)** — Note that effective-only
  emission is preserved; completeness is carried by a *metadata* `Progress`
  marker, never an empty data delta.
- **30/34 §Decision 3** — Generalise the shipped WAIT/DEGRADE suspension notice
  into the typed `Stall(reason, recoverable)` family; state that restart presents
  as `Stall(RESTARTING)` + `Resume`, and record that notices remain single-hop
  (§8 transitive gap).
- **30/31 §Normative rules 5 (G-26)** — Add: a dead-letter on a glitch-free
  frontier edge emits `Stall(DEAD_LETTERED)`; RESTART of a glitch-free cell drops
  the transient buffer and re-catches-up; a lost `Owned` buffered input surfaces
  a `CellError`.
- **20/23 §The SPSC link rule / §Corollaries** — Add the link-time refusal of
  `Leased` on a glitch-free frontier edge (freeze first), and the rule that a
  stalled wave's held `Owned` is released when the stall policy resolves the wave.
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports / I-1 metadata plane** — Register the
  downstream-directional **completeness** protocol (`FrontierEvent`) beside
  attention (upstream) and link-management; `FanOutBroadcast`, own lane/band,
  counter-ordered.
- **40/41 §Wire layer** — Extend I-13's `EdgeEvent` `WireFrame` type with
  `Progress`/`Stall`/`Resume`; counter-ordered against data frames.
- **90/91 G-6** — Update "Remaining": the WAIT/DEGRADE question is closed for all
  five non-delivery causes; single-hop/transitive notices remain (§8).

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Transitive / multi-hop stall & progress propagation.** 30/34 keeps notices
  single-hop ("a join sees only direct upstream parks, not transitive ones").
  A `Stall`/`Progress` deep in an absorbing chain must re-emit hop-by-hop to
  reach a distant join; the interaction with band-quantized attention and
  loop-prevention (shared with I-4 §8's transitive-notice gap) is open.
- **`Progress` emission trigger precision.** "Quiescence boundary" needs a
  precise definition (processed a wave, no derived delta, no pending input) and a
  proof it fires exactly when a downstream would otherwise block — plus the
  push-on-quiesce vs pull-on-block (Candidate C) choice for deep/cross-host
  chains.
- **RESTART re-catch-up vs mesh re-catch-up.** For a *replicated* glitch-free
  cell, RESTART could re-catch-up from peers rather than upstream frontier
  (I-2 §8, I-3 §8); the trigger boundary and which source serves the baseline
  need pinning.
- **DEGRADE correctness semantics.** Evaluating over a reduced frontier produces
  a *provably-approximate* wave; what "glitch-free" means under DEGRADE, and how
  a downstream invariant distinguishes a DEGRADED emission from a clean one,
  needs a stated contract (flag bit? separate outlet?).
- **Backstop deadline calibration.** The tick-counted liveness deadline (§4.9) is
  a magic number; relating it to frontier depth or making it adaptive is open
  (shared shape with I-5's hop-bound calibration).
- **Generative completeness harness.** A seeded test that injects absorption,
  suspension, restart, dead-letter, and held-`Owned` on frontier edges and
  asserts each join either completes correctly, WAITs and resumes, or re-scopes
  with a surfaced violation — the completeness analogue of the diamond and
  `GlitchFreeSuspensionTest` harnesses.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high** for the recoverable/absorption/exclusive-payload cases,
**medium** for the terminal (dead-letter/lost) case. The core move — make
effective-only silence *positive* with a per-edge watermark, advertise
indefinite non-delivery as a typed recoverable/terminal `Stall`, and resolve a
stuck watermark by a WAIT/DEGRADE/RE-SCOPE policy — is the *minimal* extension of
the already-shipped monotone-per-source completion mechanism (20/22 §The
glitch-free frontier), and it slots directly into I-13's frontier-event family
(edges entering/leaving → edges not delivering) and I-1's metadata plane. The
load-bearing insight is that all five causes are *one* local predicate (is the
watermark advancing?) whose disposition turns on a single typed bit
(recoverable vs terminal), so the mechanism is one protocol and one policy, not
five patches.

Confidence is not higher because: **(1)** the terminal RE-SCOPE case
*abandons data* — glitch-freedom over a dead-lettered wave is impossible, so the
best available answer is "stay live and surface the loss," and whether that
should instead poison the whole downstream (fail-stop) is a policy call a safety-critical
consumer might want; **(2)** transitive/multi-hop stall propagation is enabled
but, as in I-4, not fully specified here; **(3)** the precise "quiescence
boundary" trigger for `Progress` and the DEGRADE approximation contract are spun
out as follow-on gaps. **Open questions**: does a lost `Owned` on RESTART justify
a stronger link-time discipline (refuse `Owned` on glitch-free edges too, not
just `Leased`)?; and should DEGRADE emissions ride a distinct outlet so
invariants never conflate approximate and exact waves?

### I-19 — Partition placement as ordinary placement: a live composite spanning hosts without a second distribution mechanism (G-24)

> Member pairs: N16×N18, N16×N19, N16×N20, N16×N22, N16×N24
> Existing gaps touched: G-24, G-7, G-28 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 1/5 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The whole composition design, contingent on I-8's PartitionedCell: the structural claim (composite is a membrane in the link+registry planes, not a host-hierarchy node), the two-orthogonal-maps separation (routing epoch vs registry location, touched by disj…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: I-8 fixed *what a `PartitionedCell` is* — one
membrane cell, a served key-router proxy on its inlet, a wave-transparent fan-in
merge on its outlet, organelles each owning a disjoint key range, repartition via
per-range Buffering + state-as-delta (res/I-8 §4). I-19 asks the question I-8
deferred: **when the organelles actually sit on different hosts and one migrates,
is suspended, restarts, or refuses traffic under load, does the live composite
reduce to the shipped mobility / supervision / wire primitives, or is there a
missing coordination layer?** G-24 asserts partition placement is "ordinary cell
placement … partitioning must not become a second distribution mechanism"
(20/24 §Partitioned state), but calls this a *proposal sketch* whose composition
"is unevaluated for a live composite spanning hosts."

**Member pairs** all pull on this one placement/mobility axis, each on a different
runtime surface:

- **N16×N20 (mobility)**: do the router's per-partition links park/re-resolve
  through the `LocationRegistry` mid-command-stream, and do the merging outlet's
  per-link FIFO and the drain ordering invariant survive migrating *one* organelle
  of a *live* composite (20/24 §Partitioned state; 30/33 §Stale references; 30/33
  §The drain protocol)?
- **N16×N22 (wire/location)**: how key routing composes with `LocationRegistry`
  park/replay and `Remote` resolution when organelles sit behind bridges or migrate
  mid-stream (20/24 §Partitioned state; 40/41 §What exists; 40/41 §Wire layer).
- **N16×N18 (supervision)**: supervision is per-host and "does not migrate"
  (30/31 §Normative rules 5), so who supervises a partition, what RESTART of one
  key range means for the composite, and what the router does with traffic for a
  SUSPENDed partition are unspecified — even though the host hierarchy that would
  host organelles is now built (G-28 resolved M8.1, 30/31 §Hierarchy of hosts).
- **N16×N19 (colors/backpressure)**: the router funnels *all* command traffic for
  organelles that may sit on differently-colored hosts; with bounded intakes
  deferred (30/32 §Bridges, "degenerate while intakes are unbounded"), there is no
  design for a hot partition refusing traffic without the router stalling every
  other key range — head-of-line blocking at the funnel.
- **N16×N24 (replication)**: 40/42's "volunteering partial responsibility"
  (subscribing peers accepting links for a share of upstream partitions,
  40/42 §Still open) overlaps replication, while G-24 warns partitioning must not
  become a second distribution mechanism.

**Why the spec leaves it open**: 20/24 §Partitioned state is one paragraph that
names "ordinary cell placement (30/33, 40/42)" without evaluating it against the
shipped mobility machinery. Every referenced primitive exists and is verified —
`LocationRegistry` park/replay (30/33; `RemoteAddressingTest`, 50-seed mid-stream
migration), the drain ordering invariant (30/33 §The drain protocol), per-host
supervision (30/31 §Normative rules 5), remote resolution
(`Location = Local|Remote`, 40/41 §Wire layer M5.4) — but none has ever been
exercised *behind a key-router*, because "the M4 exit app never sharded"
(20/24 §Partitioned state; 91 G-24). I-19 is the placement/mobility/supervision
*composition* over I-8's composite; it must not re-derive I-8's routing/merge/wave
design, only evaluate that design under real cross-host placement.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **"Ordinary placement" vs a funnel that concentrates all traffic.** Ordinary
  placement (30/33) moves a cell whose senders re-resolve independently. A
  partitioned composite funnels every command through one router on one host
  context; the naive fear is that this funnel is a serialization point where one
  slow/closed/refusing organelle stalls all key ranges — reintroducing exactly the
  head-of-line coupling that disjoint partitioning exists to avoid, and turning the
  composite into a placement bottleneck (against P2, P10).
- **Per-host supervision that does not migrate (30/31) vs a composite whose
  organelles migrate (P8).** Supervision policy is host-management configuration
  bound to a `(host, ref)` pair and is explicitly dropped when a cell leaves its
  host, dead-lettering parked traffic (30/31 §Normative rules 5). A composite whose
  organelles move under ordinary placement would silently lose their supervision
  policies and any parked traffic on each move — a real friction, not dissolvable by
  citation.
- **The decided "partitioning MUST NOT become a second distribution mechanism"
  (recorded decision; 20/24) vs the pull toward a partition coordinator.** The
  instinctive fix for "who supervises the group, who tracks placement, who sequences
  a group migration" is a per-composite coordinator/supervisor. Any such coordinator
  is a second placement/supervision mechanism, a per-logical-cell singleton the niche
  rejects (P10), and a group barrier over the partition set (against P4).
- **P4 (no global barrier) vs the drain ordering invariant across a merge.** The
  merge fans in N organelle streams; migrating one must preserve per-link FIFO and
  drain ordering (30/33) *without* a cross-partition barrier that would order the
  N streams against each other.
- **Deferred bounded intakes (30/32) vs a concrete head-of-line answer.** Today
  intakes are unbounded, so no organelle can refuse traffic — the head-of-line
  question is *vacuous now and load-bearing later*. The resolution must pin the
  required shape of the future backpressure without building it (P6: nothing "just
  in case").

The load-bearing observations that make it tractable, carried from I-8 and I-2:
**key ranges are disjoint** (so the merge needs no cross-partition ordering), and
**every cross-host edge of the composite is an ordinary registry-backed link**
(so mobility is the shipped park/replay, not a new path). The new insight I-19
adds is the **separation of two orthogonal rare-path maps** (§4).

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — A dedicated partition coordinator (the "missing layer" made explicit)

Introduce a per-composite control cell that owns the organelle set: it tracks each
organelle's placement, supervises them as a group, sequences group migration and
rebalance, and mediates traffic to suspended/restarting partitions.

- *Semantics*: the composite gains a stateful coordinator that is the single source
  of truth for "where the partitions are and how they are supervised."
- *Fast-path cost*: none on steady data (the coordinator is a control plane), but…
- *Failure modes*: it **is** a second distribution/placement mechanism parallel to
  the host + registry — exactly what G-24 forbids; it is a per-logical-cell
  placement/supervision singleton (a coordinator to place, replicate, and fail over —
  the niche rejects this, P10); group operations across it are a barrier over the
  partition set (against P4); it duplicates `supervise`, `replicasOf`, and the
  registry. It also re-answers I-8's identity question badly (a coordinator competing
  with the membrane for who "is" the composite).
- *Tradeoff*: legible group control at the cost of every principle the feature is
  constrained by. **Rejected** — and its rejection *is* the answer to "name the
  missing coordination layer": there isn't one; the responsibilities it would own
  redistribute onto existing primitives (§4).

##### Candidate B — Reduction via two orthogonal maps + a non-blocking funnel (recommended)

The composite is a **purely logical membrane** (identity + epoch-versioned routing
table + merge fan-in) living entirely in the link and registry planes; it adds no
node to the host hierarchy and no placement path. Every cross-host edge is an
ordinary registry-backed link. **Two orthogonal rare-path maps carry the two axes**
— the *routing table* (key → owning organelle **ref**) for OWNERSHIP, and the
*`LocationRegistry`* (ref → location) for PLACEMENT — touched by *disjoint* events
(repartition bumps the routing epoch; migration re-resolves the location), so no
single event perturbs both. Supervision is per-organelle placement *config* the
composite re-applies on (re)placement. The router funnel **never blocks**: a
closed/refusing organelle intake is a per-ref park signal, confining head-of-line
blocking to one key range.

- *Fast-path cost*: unchanged from I-8 — routing is a volatile table read + hash +
  direct call (co-host) or one enqueue (cross-host); migration and supervision run
  only on rare events; the two maps are never consulted together on the data path.
- *Failure modes*: none of the member-pair tensions survive (§4). Residual risk is
  confined to two named composite-local responsibilities (re-supervise-on-migrate;
  the future non-blocking-funnel rule) and one inherited I-8 gap (epoch-consistency
  of the routing table under concurrent organelle migration), all spun out (§8).
- *Tradeoff*: gives up a legible single coordinator in exchange for a design where
  every cross-host aspect reduces to a primitive already shipped and verified.
  **Recommended.**

##### Candidate C — Host-per-partition (make "partition placement" literally host placement)

Place each organelle on its **own host**, so migrating a partition *is* migrating a
host and supervising a partition *is* draining a host — leaning directly on "the host
is the unit of mobility; finer granularity = smaller hosts" (30/33 §The core
decision).

- *Semantics*: each key range gets a dedicated host; group operations become
  host-drain operations; G-28's host hierarchy hosts the organelles directly.
- *Fast-path cost*: identical to B (routing unchanged); a host per key range is
  heavier at rest but hosts are cheap (virtual threads/coroutines, 30/33).
- *Failure modes*: over-provisions hosts for fine partitions; and by itself it does
  *not* remove the supervision-does-not-migrate friction (a host migrating still
  re-establishes its cells' supervision) — it only makes the migration boundary
  coincide with a host boundary.
- *Tradeoff*: elegant alignment with the mobility model, but it is a **placement
  policy, not a rival mechanism**. **Folded into B** as an allowed (and often
  recommended) `placement(partitionId)` choice that makes an organelle's migration a
  whole-host drain — not required, because ordinary same-host organelle migration
  already reduces (§4).

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. The composite of I-8, when its organelles span hosts,
reduces to the shipped primitives under **one structural claim and five rules**.
Nothing here re-opens I-8's routing/merge/wave design; it evaluates that design
under real placement.

##### Structural claim — the composite is a membrane in the link+registry planes, not a host

The `PartitionedCell` is one logical cell (one `logicalId`, I-2) that owns a *link
topology* (router-proxy → organelle inlets; organelle outlets → merge fan-in) and a
*routing table*. It is **not** a host and adds **no** node to the host hierarchy
(30/31 §Hierarchy of hosts, G-28). Organelles are ordinary cells spawned on ordinary
hosts by ordinary `HostManagementApi.spawn` subject to ordinary subtree quotas
(30/31 §Hierarchy of hosts). Therefore "partition placement" is, verbatim, host
placement of ordinary cells; the composite contributes only *logical* structure
(identity + routing + merge). This is the precise sense in which partitioning is not
a second distribution mechanism: **it introduces a third map (keys→cells) that is not
a distribution mechanism at all — the cells it names are distributed by the existing
placement axis and replicated by the existing replication axis.**

##### The two orthogonal maps (the load-bearing separation)

```
// OWNERSHIP axis — the routing table (I-8), held by the served router proxy:
RoutingTable(
    epoch: Long,                          // bumped ONLY on repartition (ownership change)
    ranges: Map<PartitionId, Use<Cmd>>,   // partitionId -> a REGISTRY-BACKED, ref-bound proxy
    owner: (K) -> PartitionId             // = the Serializable partitioner (total function)
)
// each Use<Cmd> is a placement-blind proxy bound to the organelle's FULL REF (I-2),
// resolving location via locate(organelleRef) on every send (40/41 M5.4).

// PLACEMENT axis — the LocationRegistry (40/41), unchanged:
locate(organelleRef): Location = Local(host) | Remote(sink)   // changes ONLY on migration
```

The two maps are touched by **disjoint events**:

- **Repartition** (I-8 Rule 6) changes *which organelle owns a key range* (or swaps
  the partitioner): it mutates `ranges`/`owner`, bumps `epoch`, and drives per-range
  Buffering. It does **not** consult the registry beyond publishing any newly-spawned
  organelle.
- **Migration** (30/33) changes *where an organelle lives*: it re-resolves
  `locate(organelleRef)`. It leaves the routing table **untouched** — the epoch does
  not move, key routing is undisturbed — because the table holds *ref-bound* proxies,
  not locations.

**Migration is invisible to routing; repartition is invisible to the registry.** No
event perturbs both maps, so partition routing and organelle mobility never
interfere. This is the reduction the challenge demands, in one sentence.

##### Rule 1 — Migrating one organelle is ordinary park/replay per link (N16×N20, N16×N22)

An organelle's inlet (fed by the router) and its delta outlet (feeding the merge) are
**ordinary cross-host links** backed by registry proxies. Migrating organelle A runs
the shipped host drain (30/33 §The drain protocol) on A's host:

1. On the **command link** (router → A.inlet): commands A already accepted drain on
   A's old host before A deactivates; commands the router sends after A's intake
   closes hit `IntakeClosedException`, park per-ref in the `LocationRegistry`, and
   replay into A's new location. Per-key FIFO holds because "the accepted batch
   flushes on the old host before the parked batch replays on the new one"
   (30/33 §The drain protocol). The router **keeps forwarding** — a closed A intake
   parks A's keys in the registry, never blocks the funnel (Rule 4), so commands for
   other partitions flow untouched.
2. On the **delta link** (A.outlet → merge): the identical drain invariant applies
   per link; A's pre-closure deltas reach the merge before A's post-re-resolution
   deltas. **Disjointness makes per-link sufficient**: A's `MapDelta` mentions only
   A's keys (I-8 Rule 5), so the merge has no cross-partition ordering obligation to
   violate — no other partition's stream depends on A's ordering, and no barrier is
   introduced (P4). A keeps its instance `sourceId` across migration (I-2: migration
   preserves `instanceId`), so downstream sees a *continuous* per-source wave
   sequence from A — migration causes no wave discontinuity (G-20, I-5 Rule 6).

Thus per-link FIFO and the drain ordering invariant survive migrating one organelle
of a live composite, and they survive *because* disjointness reduces the composite's
ordering obligation to the per-link obligation the drain protocol already guarantees.

##### Rule 2 — Supervision is per-organelle placement config the composite re-applies (N16×N18)

Each organelle is supervised by its host with an ordinary `supervise(organelleRef,
policy)` (30/31 §Normative rules 5). There is **no composite supervisor** — supervision
is per-cell, exactly as for any cell. The composite, as the organelle's logical owner
and spawner, holds `supervisionPolicy(partitionId)` as **placement configuration**,
parallel to I-8's `placement(partitionId)`, and applies it at spawn. Because
supervision "is per-host and does not migrate" (30/31), the composite **re-applies**
`supervise(organelleRef, policy)` on the target host after every (re)placement — one
ordinary management call. This keeps supervision "ordinary placement config," never a
new mechanism. Consequences:

- **RESTART of one key range** (deactivate → activate → restore spawn-time
  checkpoint, 30/31): scoped by construction to A's disjoint range. On re-activation A
  re-emits state-as-delta-from-empty (G-22) into the merge, which forwards it
  idempotently (OR-set tags absorb overlap for a replicated A; a non-replicated A loses
  post-checkpoint deltas — the ordinary RESTART semantics, not a partition problem).
  Other partitions are untouched. Downstream sees A's keys revert then re-converge; no
  composite-level coordination.
- **Traffic for a SUSPENDed partition**: the router forwards the command normally; A's
  host **parks it per-cell in order** under the SUSPEND policy (30/31) until
  `resume(organelleRef)` replays it — the shipped SUSPEND behavior. The router does
  nothing special; per-key FIFO is preserved by the per-cell park; other partitions
  flow (Rule 4).
- **Do not migrate a SUSPENDed organelle**: since a suspended cell leaving its host
  dead-letters its parked traffic (30/31), the composite treats "migrate A" as an
  ordinary *drain* (which flushes accepted traffic and parks new via re-resolution),
  never as moving A while under a SUSPEND supervision policy. If A is supervised
  SUSPEND, the composite `resume`s/drains before migrating. This is a composite-local
  invariant reducing to ordinary drain/resume calls.

##### Rule 3 — Colors reduce to per-host validation; the funnel is color-blind (N16×N19)

Organelles on differently-colored hosts (🔵/🟣) are reached by the router via ordinary
cross-host sends, which are "one non-blocking offer … any color to any color"
(30/32 §Bridges). Color validation is the ordinary spawn/migration check (organelle
color vs host color, 30/32); pure organelles cross colors freely. The router (a served
proxy on the composite's host context) is color-agnostic — it enqueues; the
registry/host handle color. No partition-specific color handling.

##### Rule 4 — The router funnel never blocks; refusal is a per-ref park, not a wait (N16×N19)

**Today** intakes are unbounded (30/32 §Bridges), so no organelle refuses traffic and
head-of-line blocking is *vacuous*: the router's per-key forward is a non-blocking
enqueue or direct call; a closed (migrating/suspended) organelle parks only its keys.
**When bounded intakes / backpressure arrive** (deferred, 30/32 §Bridges GAP), this
rule is normative: the router MUST treat a *refusing* organelle intake identically to
a *closed* one — a per-ref **park signal, never a synchronous wait**. Concretely, a
"full" intake surfaces the same fail-fast the closable intake already surfaces
(`IntakeClosedException`-shaped), the registry parks that key range's commands per-ref,
and the router returns to serve the next command for a different partition. Because the
router runs on the composite host's single consumer, a blocking forward would stall all
ranges; the park-not-wait rule confines head-of-line blocking to the hot partition's
own key range. This adds **no new mechanism** — it pins the shape of the future
backpressure at the `enqueueHostedInvocation` seam (30/32) to reuse the existing
park/re-resolve primitive. Sustained refusal of a hot partition then drives ordinary
attention-based suspension / rebalance (34, I-4; I-8 Rule 6), not a funnel stall.

##### Rule 5 — Replication composes per-organelle; the composite does not distribute (N16×N24)

There are exactly **two pre-existing distribution axes**, and partitioning adds
neither:

- **Placement/mobility** (30/33, 40/41): where a cell lives — host is the unit of
  mobility; `locate` resolves ref→location; park/replay.
- **Replication** (40/42, I-3): how many instances of a logical cell exist — the
  membership-reactive gossip mesh over `replicasOf`.

Each organelle is an ordinary cell: it is placed by axis 1 and, if it is a mergeable
`Replicable` (20/24; I-3 §4.8), replicated by axis 2 via `replicasOf(organelleRef)`,
**independently per partition** — its replica set is just another `replicasOf` of an
ordinary ref (I-3 §4.8). 40/42's "volunteering partial responsibility" (a peer
accepting a *share* of upstream partitions) is precisely a peer spawning local replicas
of *some organelles* and joining *those* organelles' meshes (I-3 §4.7) — nothing about
the composite coordinates it. The composite's routing table stays coherent because the
partitioner is deterministic `Serializable` config replicated with the composite, and
partitionId→organelle-ref resolution is the ordinary registry/`replicasOf` lookup. The
overlap dissolves: **partitioning distributes keys-across-cells (routing table);
replication distributes copies-of-a-cell (mesh); placement distributes cells-across-
machines (registry) — three orthogonal maps, only two of which are distribution, and
partitioning owns the one that isn't.** (The epoch-consistency of the routing table
under *concurrent organelle migration* is I-8's already-named follow-on gap; the
two-orthogonal-maps separation above sharpens it — migration alone never bumps the
epoch — but a concurrent migrate-during-repartition still needs the generative wire
test I-8 spun out.)

##### Net effect

The composite is a membrane in the link+registry planes; organelles are ordinary
placeable, supervisable, migratable, replicable cells; ownership (routing epoch) and
placement (registry location) are orthogonal maps touched by disjoint events; the
funnel never blocks; supervision is placement config the composite re-applies. No new
coordination layer, no second distribution mechanism, no kernel primitive (P1). The
only genuinely new normative content is small and composite-local: **re-supervise on
migration** (Rule 2) and the **non-blocking-funnel rule for future backpressure**
(Rule 4).

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — the composite adds only links, a routing table, and management calls; migration/supervision/restart reduce to the shipped drain + `supervise` + park/replay; meaningful single-threaded. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — routing is a volatile read + hash + direct call / one enqueue (I-8); the two maps are never consulted together on the data path; migration/supervision are rare-path; the funnel never blocks (Rule 4). |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — organelle links, the routing table, and per-organelle supervision are all inspectable; no hidden coordinator or mailbox; the composite is visible link structure. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no partition coordinator, no group barrier; the merge needs no cross-partition ordering (disjointness); migrating one organelle is a per-link drain. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — disjoint ranges make per-link FIFO sufficient; ref-bound proxies make migration structurally invisible to routing; the park-not-wait funnel rule is a structural constraint at the `submit` seam. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — organelles, their replicas, and their links follow interest; sustained refusal drives ordinary attention suspension (Rule 4); nothing placed "just in case." |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Untouched** — boundary controls (membranes, allowlists, 40/43) attach to organelle links as ordinary links; no ambient assumption added. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — organelles migrate/restart/rebalance live; the composite's external identity is stable across placement churn (I-2 membrane); nothing assumes a static placement. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — partitioner/placement/supervision policies are `Serializable` config; routed commands and merged deltas are the shipped `WireFrame`/delta forms; no lambdas/handles on the wire. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — a decentralized keyed shard whose distribution is entirely the existing placement + replication axes; the rejected coordinator (Candidate A) is the niche-first trade. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent: each organelle outlet is a distinct source;
  migration preserves `instanceId`, so a migrating organelle's wave sequence is
  continuous; no wave coordinator over partitions.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent: no group barrier; the merge needs no
  cross-partition ordering.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent and central: organelles migrate as
  their hosts move; Candidate C (host-per-partition) makes this exact; no per-partition
  mobility protocol.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities** — Consistent: SUSPENDed
  partitions park per-cell; migrating organelles park per-ref; repartition parks
  per-range; all the same primitive.
- **Location = Local|Remote; one park/replay** — Consistent and load-bearing: the
  routing table holds ref-bound proxies; migration is pure `locate` re-resolution.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: RESTART/late-join/repartition transfer all use
  state-as-delta-from-empty.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, NOT wave ids** — Consistent: organelles keep cell-local
  OR-set tags; the composite forwards wave context unchanged.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent:
  `supervise`/`spawn`/`migrate` are management calls; command/delta contracts stay
  push-only.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** —
  Consistent: each organelle replicates via the existing mesh (Rule 5); the composite
  only routes.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT become a second distribution mechanism** — Consistent and
  central: the composite adds no host-hierarchy node and no placement path; the routing
  table distributes keys-across-cells, not cells-across-machines (structural claim,
  Rule 5).
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent: routed commands and
  announcements are the shipped `WireFrame` forms; no new wire addressing.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent, exercised:
  migrating one organelle preserves per-link FIFO on both its command and delta links
  (Rule 1).
- **Cardinality enforced at link time; exclusive ownership refuses fan-out** —
  Consistent: I-8's demux-preserves-SPSC (I-8 Rule 2) is unchanged by placement;
  cross-host routed `Owned` degenerates to move-by-serialize at the bridge (20/23).
- **Owned crossing machines = move-by-serialize; Leased not across machines** —
  Consistent: a command routed to a remote organelle obeys the bridge's ownership rule;
  nothing partition-specific.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind logicalId (per I-2: full-ref
  addressing)** — Consistent: the composite carries the external `logicalId`;
  organelles have their own full refs; migration preserves organelle `instanceId`.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — No resolved item
  reopened. G-28 (host hierarchy, resolved M8.1) is *used*, not amended: organelles are
  ordinary cells under ordinary subtree quotas, and the composite is orthogonal to the
  host hierarchy.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/24 §Partitioned state (G-24)** — Extend I-8's replacement text with the live-
  placement composition: the structural claim (membrane in link+registry planes, not a
  host); the two-orthogonal-maps separation (routing epoch vs registry location, touched
  by disjoint events); per-link drain survival under single-organelle migration;
  supervision as re-applied placement config; the non-blocking-funnel rule for future
  backpressure; replication-composes-per-organelle.
- **30/31 §Normative rules 5** — Note that a composite re-applies `supervise(organelle,
  policy)` on organelle (re)placement, since supervision does not migrate; and that a
  composite must not migrate a SUSPENDed organelle without draining/resuming first.
- **30/31 §Hierarchy of hosts** — Note that a `PartitionedCell` adds no host-hierarchy
  node; its organelles are ordinary cells under ordinary subtree quotas; host-per-
  partition is an allowed `placement` policy.
- **30/33 §The drain protocol / §Stale references** — Note that a partitioned
  composite's command and delta links are ordinary registry-backed links; migrating one
  organelle preserves per-link FIFO and drain ordering, and disjointness makes per-link
  sufficient (no cross-partition barrier).
- **30/32 §Bridges (GAP)** — Pin the future bounded-intake rule for the router funnel:
  a refusing organelle intake is a per-ref park signal, never a synchronous wait, so
  head-of-line blocking is confined to one key range.
- **40/41 §Wire layer / §What exists** — Note that the routing table holds ref-bound
  placement-blind proxies, so cross-host key routing is the shipped park/replay +
  `Remote` resolution with no new path.
- **40/42 §Still open** — Mark "volunteering partial responsibility" addressed: a peer
  replicates a share of organelles via the existing per-organelle mesh (Rule 5); no
  partition-specific replication.
- **91 G-24** — Note the live-placement composition resolved (design) on the shipped
  mobility/supervision primitives; build trigger unchanged.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Supervision policy propagation on placement** — the composite re-applies
  `supervise` on each organelle (re)placement; a clean API for "supervision travels with
  placement config" (vs the current per-host, does-not-migrate model, 30/31) would make
  this correct-by-construction rather than composite-local discipline. Interacts with
  the M8.1 hierarchy's deferred "spawn redirection (placement)."
- **Non-blocking router funnel under bounded intakes** — Rule 4 pins the shape but the
  actual backpressure code (a refusing intake surfacing a park signal at
  `enqueueHostedInvocation`, and the router's park-per-ref-then-continue loop) is
  deferred with the 30/32 bounded-intakes gap; needs a generative head-of-line-isolation
  test once intakes can refuse.
- **Routing-table epoch consistency under concurrent organelle migration** — inherited
  from I-8; the two-orthogonal-maps separation shows migration alone never bumps the
  epoch, but a migrate-during-repartition (both maps changing near-simultaneously) needs
  a generative wire test for the stale-epoch re-route (I-8 Rule 6 step 5) racing a
  registry re-resolution.
- **Group placement / rebalance atomicity across hosts** — bulk multi-range rebalance
  (I-8 §8) that also *relocates* organelles couples the ownership and placement axes for
  a window; the triggering policy (load/attention, 34) and its cross-host atomicity are
  undesigned.
- **RESTART within a replicated organelle** — a restarted organelle restoring a stale
  spawn-time checkpoint vs re-catching-up from its partition-mesh peers (I-2 §8, I-3):
  which is correct for a replicated shard needs a rule.
- **Host-per-partition provisioning economics** — when Candidate C's one-host-per-range
  policy is worth its host overhead vs co-hosting several organelles, and how attention
  (34) drives the split/merge of partition hosts, is an economic-layer decision (G-6
  residual).

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The resolution adds no kernel primitive and no coordination
layer: every cross-host aspect of a live partitioned composite reduces to a primitive
already shipped and verified — `LocationRegistry` park/replay (`RemoteAddressingTest`),
the drain ordering invariant (30/33), per-host supervision (30/31), `Remote` resolution
(40/41 M5.4) — and the composition rests on two simple, checkable claims: *the two
rare-path maps (ownership epoch, registry location) are touched by disjoint events*, so
migration and routing never interfere, and *disjoint ranges make per-link FIFO
sufficient*, so migrating one organelle needs no cross-partition barrier. The design
builds directly on I-8 (composite structure), I-2 (full-ref addressing, instanceId
preserved on migration), and I-3 (per-organelle replication). Confidence is not higher
because nothing is built (the harness has never sharded, 20/24) and three interactions
are genuinely unproven: the non-blocking funnel under *actual* bounded intakes (deferred
mechanism), epoch-consistency under concurrent migrate-during-repartition (inherited I-8
gap), and cross-host group-rebalance atomicity — all spun out as follow-on gaps rather
than resolved here.

**Open questions**: (1) whether supervision should be reworked to *travel with the cell*
(amending 30/31's "does not migrate") rather than be re-applied by the composite — the
latter keeps 30/31 untouched but leaves a re-supervise discipline on the composite;
(2) whether host-per-partition (Candidate C) should be the *default* placement policy
(making every partition migration a clean host drain) or an opt-in for large ranges;
(3) the exact fail-fast surface a *full* (vs *closed*) intake presents at
`enqueueHostedInvocation`, deferred to the bounded-intakes work.

### I-20 — Observing, shadowing, and replicating exclusive flows: fan-out refusal vs every multi-consumer feature

> Member pairs: N2×N26, N2×N27, N14×N24, N14×N26, N14×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-21, G-32, G-7 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 4/5 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The whole design: Consume-vs-Observe link roles with the SPSC count narrowed to consumers, FanOutlet.tap + the KSP Borrowed-projection, taps-before-consumer emission order, cross-host tap freeze at the bridge, discharging NoOp sinks for exclusive inlets in …
> ⚠ Divergence with landed code: Shadow.suppress (cell/evolve/Evolution.kt) installs a plain Proxy.noop on every fan-in inlet; for an Owned/Leased-carrying contract that silently drops the payload without take()/release(), contradicting the resolution's discharging-sink rule (rule 7) — the…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The single mechanism question: **how can an Owned/Leased-carrying (exclusive) flow be observed, shadowed, judged, and replicated when the SPSC rule refuses fan-out on exactly those flows** — and where does whatever answer we pick sit relative to the `FanOutlet` funnel and `Broadcast` refusal (20/23 §Implementation)?

The SPSC rule is normative and enforced (M5.6): "a link whose contract carries `Owned` or `Leased` arguments MUST have exactly one downstream consumer … a second link to an `Owned`/`Leased`-carrying outlet is `Rejected`" (20/23 §The SPSC link rule). Every multi-consumer feature in the spec is described as *ordinary fan-out linking*, which collides with that rule:

- **N2 × N26 / N14 × N26** — "attach invariant to subgraph is just linking" and "a late-linked invariant receives catch-up like any subscriber" (50/52 §Invariant testing); a second link on an exclusive outlet is `Rejected`, so exclusive flows are unobservable by invariant cells.
- **N2 × N27 / N14 × N27** — evolution "Feed[s] candidate live inputs | fan-out links, shadow mode" (50/53 §Mechanical decomposition); `OneToOnePort` caps at exactly one counterpart, so a side-by-side candidate on an SPSC flow has no mechanism.
- **N14 × N26 (G-32 hole)** — shadow mode NoOp-serves effectful inlets (50/52 §Live invariants), but a NoOp drop of an `Owned`/`Leased` inlet swallows the consume-once / release obligation (never consumed = leak; never released = pool leak).
- **N14 × N24** — replication "link[s] each replica's delta outlet to every discovered replica's `deltaInlet`" (40/42 §Design as implemented), but 40/42 never mentions `Owned`/`Leased`; G-7 (90/91) is silent on whether exclusive-payload cells are non-replicable or must freeze at the replication boundary.

Why the text leaves it open: 20/23 §SPSC says "one downstream **consumer**" but the enforcement funnel (`FanOutlet.subscribe`) treats *every* attach as a consumer — it has no notion of a non-consuming attachment. 50/52 and 50/53 describe observation/shadowing as generic "links + fan-out" with no exclusive-flow carve-out, and 40/42 was written for the mergeable-set family and never confronts exclusive payloads. Nothing in the spec says whether "observe" and "consume" are the same act.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P5 (correctness by construction) vs P4/P6 observability.** The exclusive bit exists precisely so that sharing is *impossible by construction* (20/23 §Motivation). Any observation path that re-admits a second reader risks re-admitting the aliasing the type system was built to forbid.
- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path).** Exclusive flows are the HFT-inspired hot paths (20/23 §Motivation): in-place mutation of pooled/transferred buffers. A "just copy for observers" answer would silently destroy the fast path the moment anyone attaches an invariant — the observability tax would fall on the most cost-sensitive edge.
- **Prior decision "SPSC enforced at FanOutlet funnel + Broadcast."** Whatever we add must live at that one funnel, not a parallel enforcement path.
- **Prior decision "Owned crossing machine boundaries → move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross."** In-host observation and cross-host observation cannot use the same currency: a `Borrowed` view is invocation-scoped and cannot survive the wire.
- **Prior decision "replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; no second sync protocol."** We cannot invent a replication path for exclusive payloads; the answer must fall out of the existing Frozen-delta path.
- **50/52 "attaching = linking" and catch-up.** Exclusive payloads are consume-once and transient — there is no retained history to replay to a late observer, unlike convergent-state flows.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Uncounted Borrowed observation taps (recommended)

**Semantics.** Split downstream attachments into *consumers* (receive the payload in its declared exclusive form, bear consume-once/release) and *observers/taps* (receive a `Borrowed<T>` projection, invocation-scoped, never retain/mutate/release). The `Borrowed` form is already fan-out-safe (20/23 §The four contracts). The SPSC rule counts consumers only. Taps fire synchronously before the sole consumer; cross-host taps freeze a copy at the bridge. NoOp shadow sinks become discharging; mutable shadow candidates use an explicit copy-fork.

**Fast-path cost.** Zero taps → empty-array volatile read, unchanged. N taps → N extra in-host direct calls before the consumer, only where interest attached (P6). Cross-host observation costs one freeze-copy per observed emission.

**Failure modes.** A misbehaving observer that tries to retain the `Borrowed` view past the invocation — prevented structurally by the invocation-scoped validity already defined for `Borrowed`. Late taps get no catch-up (transient payloads) — real limitation, redirected to observing convergent state.

**Tradeoffs.** Keeps the exclusive fast path zero-cost when unobserved; observation is honest (read-only, cannot become a hidden second consumer). Adds a link-role concept and a KSP-generated Borrowed projection.

##### Candidate B — Mandatory freeze-at-boundary (upgrade the whole flow to Frozen when observed)

**Semantics.** When any observer attaches to an exclusive outlet, the producer `freeze()`s each emission and fans `Frozen<T>` to everyone including the consumer; the consumer must accept `Frozen` (no in-place mutation).

**Fast-path cost.** A freeze-copy allocation on every emission of the observed edge — the exact cost `Owned` exists to avoid.

**Failure modes.** A consumer written for in-place `Owned` mutation cannot accept `Frozen` — type mismatch or forced rewrite. Observability silently changes the pipeline's performance characteristics.

**Tradeoffs.** Simple and fully safe, but defeats P2 for the observed edge. Viable only as an explicit opt-in where the consumer already tolerates `Frozen`.

##### Candidate C — Declare exclusive flows non-observable / non-replicable as a class

**Semantics.** SPSC edges accept no invariants, no shadow, no replication, by fiat.

**Fast-path cost.** None.

**Failure modes.** The HFT hot paths — where invariants (resource bounds, consistency) matter most — become exactly the unverifiable ones, contradicting 50/52's thesis that "invariants cover the space." Blocks evolution of exactly the code most expensive to get wrong.

**Tradeoffs.** Honest and cheap, but a large capability hole. Acceptable only for the narrow Leased-pool-internal case where no external observation is meaningful.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Introduce one structural distinction — consumer vs observer — layered on the existing ownership lattice, plus two obligation rules. Nothing about the exclusive bit or its enforcement location changes; the funnel simply learns to count consumers only.

1. **Two link roles at the outlet.** Every downstream attachment is either a **Consume** link (receives the payload in its declared contract form — Owned/Leased/Frozen/Borrowed — and bears the consume-once/release obligation) or an **Observe** link / **Tap** (receives a `Borrowed<T>` projection, valid only for the emitting invocation, never retains, mutates, or releases). The SPSC rule counts Consume links only.

2. **The Tap primitive.** Add `FanOutlet.tap(observer)` beside `subscribe(consumer)` (equivalently a `LinkRole { Consume, Observe }` on the 10/13 handshake). A tap link's contract is the **Borrowed-projection** of the outlet contract: each payload type `P` carrying `Owned<T>`/`Leased<T>` is projected to `Borrowed<T>`; Frozen/Borrowed/plain payloads project to themselves. KSP generates this projected observer descriptor from the same parameter scan that already emits the exclusive bit, so the projection is checked in types (P5), not by reflection. Add `Owned<T>.borrow(): Borrowed<T>` and `Leased<T>.borrow(): Borrowed<T>` — a read-only view whose validity is the current invocation scope.

3. **Enforcement at the existing funnel.** `FanOutlet.subscribe` splits attachments into a **consumers** list and a **taps** list. The exclusive-bit check `Rejects` a second entry on the consumers list only; taps are always accepted regardless of the bit. This is the same single funnel (M5.6) with the count narrowed to Consume role — the exemption lives exactly where the counting lives.

4. **Emission order.** On emit, `FanOutlet` iterates taps first (delivering `value.borrow()` to each — synchronous, in-host, single-threaded per P1), then delivers the payload to the sole consumer (`Owned.take()` / Leased hand-off). Because `Borrowed` validity ends when each tap invocation returns, no tap view can alias the buffer once the consumer mutates or moves it. Taps fire in emission order, so observers see the same per-link FIFO order as the consumer (drain-ordering invariant preserved). Fast path with zero taps: an empty-array volatile read (unchanged from today). With N taps: N extra direct in-host calls before the consumer call — opt-in per interest (P6), and steady state on an unobserved exclusive edge pays nothing.

5. **Broadcast proxy.** Unchanged for consumers: still refuses `Owned`/`Leased` to more than one consumer. Taps ride as `Borrowed`, which is fan-out-safe, so a `Broadcast` fanning `Borrowed` views to many observers is permitted by the same rule that permits `Frozen` fan-out.

6. **Cross-host taps freeze at the boundary.** A `Borrowed` view cannot cross a machine boundary (its validity window does not survive the wire, and the buffer may be reused). `BridgeEgressCell`, seeing a tap link over an exclusive contract, freezes an immutable copy (`Owned.freeze()` / deep copy) and sends `Frozen<T>` on the observer stream — never `Borrowed`. This reuses the existing send-time boundary rule ("freeze or copy first"; Leased never crosses). In-host observation is zero-copy `Borrowed`; cross-host observation costs one freeze-copy per observed emission, paid only where remote interest exists.

7. **Discharging NoOp sinks (fixes the G-32 hole for exclusive inlets).** `Shadow.spawn`'s NoOp-serve of an `Effectful` inlet must, when the inlet contract carries `Owned`/`Leased`, install a **discharging** server instead of a plain drop: `Owned` → `take()`-and-drop (satisfies consume-once), `Leased` → `release()` (returns the buffer to the pool). Generated from the same exclusive bit. This is installed at the same point `Shadow` currently NoOp-serves effectful inlets.

8. **Copy-fork for mutable shadow candidates.** A shadow / side-by-side candidate that must run the exclusive pipeline itself (mutating an independent input) is a *consumer*, not an observer, and two consumers of one `Owned` is impossible without a copy. Add `Shadow.forkExclusive` at the fork point: it clones the payload to an independent `Owned` so the candidate and the incumbent each hold their own. This is explicitly the one non-zero-copy place in shadow mode, and it is a rare orchestration op (P2 permits rare ops to be expensive). Candidates whose outputs are derivable read-only should instead attach as taps (`Borrowed`) and be judged by invariant cells on their own outlets.

9. **Replication clarification (no new mechanism).** Exclusive payloads (`Owned`/`Leased`) are per-host **pipeline** currency and are never the shared-**state** currency. A replicated cell with an `Owned`/`Leased` data inlet consumes its own local exclusive inputs to advance local state; replicas converge via `Frozen`/mergeable delta gossip exactly as today (40/42) — deltas are effective-only immutable forms, always fan-out-safe. Therefore exclusive-payload cells **are** replicable through their Frozen delta path; only the exclusive edge itself is unshared (it is a local pipeline segment, and an `Owned` value that move-by-serializes is inherently single-location, so "sharing the buffer across replicas" is meaningless by the ownership semantics, not a missing feature).

Net: observation, judging, and cross-host/replication all run on the fan-out-safe forms (`Borrowed` in-host, `Frozen` across boundaries and among replicas); consumption alone runs on the exclusive forms; the funnel counts consumers, not observers. No exclusive value is ever fanned out; every consume-once/release obligation is discharged exactly once.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — taps are ordinary synchronous in-host calls ordered before the consumer; meaningful in single-threaded simulation; the `Borrowed`-before-consume ordering *depends on* single-threadedness. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — zero-tap edge unchanged (empty volatile read); observation cost is opt-in and paid only under interest; freeze-copy only cross-host or on explicit forks (rare ops). |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — tap links are first-class link objects with a declared role; observation is inspectable, not a hidden mailbox. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global lock; invariants remain per-cell opt-in; taps compose like links. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — the tap contract is the KSP-generated `Borrowed` projection; an observer *cannot type-check* as a consumer; consume-once still enforced by `take()`. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — taps, discharging sinks, and forks exist only where an invariant/shadow/replica expresses interest. |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Tension — explain** — uncounted read-only taps let a party observe a sensitive hot flow; who may attach a tap is a membrane/policy question (see §8, follow-on). |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — taps and forks are runtime graph ops; shadow/promotion of exclusive pipelines now has a mechanism. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — cross-boundary observation travels as `Frozen` (wire-registered, 20/23 §Implementation); `Borrowed` stays strictly in-host. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — favors incremental, interest-driven observation of long-lived pipelines over a blanket copy. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **SPSC enforced at FanOutlet funnel + Broadcast** — Consistent; enforcement stays at that funnel, count narrowed to Consume role; Broadcast still refuses exclusive payloads to >1 consumer.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time, not send time; exclusive ownership refuses fan-out** — Consistent; the *consumer* count is still a link-time refusal; taps are a link-time role classification. (Boundary freeze is a send-time check, matching 20/23's existing "boundary rules are send-time checks.")
- **Owned crossing machine boundaries → move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross** — Consistent; cross-host taps freeze/copy at the bridge; `Borrowed` and `Leased` never cross.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; no second sync protocol** — Consistent; exclusive cells replicate via the existing Frozen-delta path; no new protocol.
- **Data contracts push-only; management may return values** — Consistent; tap contracts are push-only `Borrowed` projections.
