- **Drain ordering invariant / per-link FIFO end-to-end** — Consistent; taps fire in emission order before the consumer.
- **Suspension is one Buffering primitive; a parked Owned is still owned by the link** — Consistent; taps do not change parking; the Buffering proxy still holds the single Owned.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Untouched; `StateMigrating.importFrom` unchanged (the discharging-sink fix is orthogonal).
- No CONFLICT flags.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **20/23 §The four contracts / §The SPSC link rule** — add the consumer-vs-observer distinction; state that the "exactly one downstream consumer" count excludes `Borrowed`-projected observation taps; document `Owned/Leased.borrow()` and the cross-boundary freeze rule for taps.
- **20/23 §Implementation (G-21)** — record that `FanOutlet.subscribe` splits consumers/taps and vetoes only a second consumer; `BridgeEgressCell` freezes a copy for cross-host taps.
- **10/12 §Cardinality (rule 2) / §Contracts are push-only** — note that rule-2 fan-out refusal binds Consume links; add the `tap`/`LinkRole` surface and the KSP Borrowed-projection.
- **50/52 §Live invariants (G-32)** — replace "NoOp-serves every fan-in inlet" with the discharging-sink rule for exclusive inlets; note taps as the observation path for exclusive flows and the attach-forward-only catch-up limitation.
- **50/53 §Mechanical decomposition** — split the "Feed candidate live inputs" row into observe-via-tap vs consume-via-copy-fork; add `Shadow.forkExclusive`.
- **40/42 §What replication must mean / §Design as implemented** — add a sentence: exclusive payloads are per-host pipeline currency; replication converges Frozen deltas; exclusive-payload cells are replicable, not a non-replicable class.
- **90/91** — annotate G-7, G-21, G-32 with this resolution; new gap rows per §8.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Borrowed-projection contract generation in KSP** — the derivation of a Borrowed-projected observer descriptor (Owned/Leased → Borrowed, nested/generic payloads), and link-time validation that a tap's contract equals the outlet's projection, needs its own design alongside the exclusive-bit processor.
- **Catch-up semantics for taps on exclusive flows** — transient consume-once payloads have no history to replay to a late tap; spec must state attach-forward-only and redirect history-dependent invariants to convergent state.
- **Copy-fork cost and cloneability contract for exclusive payloads** — `Shadow.forkExclusive` needs a defined copy/duplication capability on `Owned` (and Leased pool duplication) and a failure mode when a payload is not safely cloneable; interacts with phase-3 pooling.
- **Observer authority as a membrane/policy concern** — who may attach an uncounted read-only tap to an exclusive (hot/sensitive) flow, and whether Borrowed/Frozen observation may leak data past a membrane, is a policy gap (ties to 50/53 §Trust boundary, 40/43).

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

Confidence: **medium**. The mechanism is well-grounded — it is essentially a naming and enforcement-splitting of distinctions the ownership lattice already carries (`Borrowed`/`Frozen` fan-out-safe vs `Owned`/`Leased` exclusive), and it keeps enforcement at the one decided funnel. The replication clarification and the discharging-sink fix are direct consequences that require no new machinery.

Open questions: (1) whether the Borrowed-projection should be a compiler-generated contract or a runtime view wrapper (types-first argues generated, but generic payloads may be awkward); (2) exact catch-up story for late taps beyond "observe state instead"; (3) whether `Shadow.forkExclusive`'s clone requirement should force exclusive payloads to declare a copy capability up front (P5) or fail at fork time; (4) tap authority as a membrane control. None of these alter the core mechanism; they refine its edges.

### I-21 — GraphSpec expressiveness: identity-preserving spawn, hierarchy, evolution steps, and remote application

> Member pairs: N7×N25, N22×N25, N23×N25, N24×N25, N25×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-30, G-8, G-9, G-33 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 3/5 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — IdentityBinding (NewInstanceOf/Exact) and the ref-aware CellFactory, the parent field (organelle nesting — G-9 still open), UnlinkStep, spawnBound as the wire form with remote applyTo returning Deferred<ApplyReport>, the ConstructionReport dataflow reply, t…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question.** GraphSpec is deliberately a *thin veneer over the
host protocol*: "No new semantics in the DSL layer, ever: anything the DSL does must
be expressible as management invocations" (`50/51 §Graph construction DSL`). Its step
vocabulary is `spawn`/`connect`, spawn steps carry a `Serializable` `CellFactory`, and
"replay mints fresh cells and refs." Four features stacked above it need words this
vocabulary lacks:

- **Identity-preserving spawn** (N23×N25, N24×N25). Replay "mints fresh cells and
  refs," but G-8 (`10/11 §Identity and persistence`) and `50/53 §Mechanical
  decomposition` require spawning a *specific* logical identity — a new instance or a
  replica of an existing `logicalId`. Whether replay should mint fresh `logicalId`s or
  new `instanceId`s is undefined, and no construction path exists for a same-`logicalId`
  multi-host spawn (`40/42 §What replication must mean here`).
- **Membrane hierarchy** (N7×N25). The DSL may only emit `spawn`/`connect`, but
  organelle composition and selective port exposure have no management-invocation form
  (G-9: "all ports of a spawned cell are reachable by name through the host"; `10/11
  §Hierarchy: organelles`), so GraphSpec "cannot express or preserve membrane
  hierarchy."
- **Evolution orchestration** (N25×N27). Deployments are "incremental graph operations"
  with GraphSpec as the declared declarative path (`50/53 §Model`), but a promotion
  needs buffer → unlink → relink → replay steps plus incarnation-aware spawn — "none of
  which GraphSpec can express and 53 does not say how its orchestration is recorded or
  replayed."
- **Remote application** (N22×N25). `51` claims "link rejections fail construction
  loudly," but a cross-wire `linkTo` returns `LinkResult.Deferred` with the authoritative
  rejection dead-lettered on the target host (`10/13 §Explicit`; M5.4 built no
  synchronous reply channel), and `spawn` takes a *live* `Cell` that cannot cross the
  wire — so how `graph{}`/`applyTo` behaves against a remote management inlet is
  unspecified and the loud-failure claim cannot hold there (`40/41 §Wire layer`).

**Why the spec leaves it open.** G-30 is "Resolved (M4.5)" only for the *local,
fresh-refs, in-process* case: the shipped DSL applies eagerly against a local inlet,
mints fresh refs, and fails loudly because `connect` returns a `LinkResult`
synchronously. Every feature above it was designed *after* the DSL and needs a piece of
vocabulary the DSL froze out — but the freeze ("no new semantics") is itself a load-
bearing decision that must survive. The prerequisite pieces are all *decided*: full-ref
addressing (I-2: `logicalId` is a grouping/continuity key, never a live link target,
one location per full ref); the replication skeleton (I-3: the mesh is built by a
membership-reactive linker from `replicasOf`, not enumerated statically); parent/child
recorded at spawn (G-28/M8.1); `CellFactory` already `Serializable`; management-over-
wire already `Deferred`-wrapped (`40/41` point 5). The challenge is to assemble these
into a vocabulary extension that adds *parameters, not semantics*.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **"No new semantics in the DSL layer, ever" vs four features that want new words.**
  The obvious fix — add `buffer`/`swap`/`replicate`/`expose` step types — is exactly
  what the recorded decision forbids, and it would turn a declarative topology
  description into a scripting language whose control flow (an evolution judge's runtime
  verdict) *cannot be a static step list* at all.
- **P1 / P8 vs recording a feedback-driven procedure.** Evolution's swap is driven by an
  invariant judge whose verdict is only known at runtime (`53 §Model`, `50/52`). A
  declarative spec cannot encode "swap iff the candidate satisfies invariants under live
  data." Trying to make GraphSpec express the swap conflates a *noun* (target topology)
  with a *verb sequence* (a control loop) — a category error.
- **P2 / P4 / M5.4 vs synchronous loud failure across the wire.** Local loud failure
  works because `connect` returns synchronously. The wire deliberately has *no*
  synchronous reply channel (M5.4, `10/13`): a cross-host handshake runs on the target
  and rejections dead-letter there. Restoring synchronous loud failure would rebuild the
  reply channel M5.4 rejected and impose synchronous cross-host coupling (against P2/P4).
- **P9 vs a live `Cell` on the wire.** `spawn(cell: Cell): CellRef` takes a live object;
  a live cell is not serializable. Remote construction must go through the *factory*, not
  the cell — but the DSL's headline method takes a cell.
- **I-2/I-3 vs "a GraphSpec of N replicas."** The naive reading of "construct a replica
  set" is a spec that enumerates N same-`logicalId` spawns and a full mesh of connects.
  That is a *static* replica set (violates P6/P8) and duplicates the I-3 reactive linker.
  GraphSpec must be able to *seed* a same-`logicalId` instance without becoming the
  mesh-maintenance mechanism.
- **P6 / P10.** The extension must not build a general deployment-scripting engine "just
  in case"; the niche needs identity-aware seeding, organelle nesting, and honest remote
  submission — a bounded, known set.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Enrich GraphSpec with imperative step types

Add verbs: `buffer(port)`, `unlink(...)`, `relink(...)`, `replicateAcross(hosts)`,
`expose(port)`, `promote(candidate)`. GraphSpec becomes a deployment script.

- *Semantics*: one DSL expresses construction *and* orchestration.
- *Fast-path cost*: none (construction is rare-path), but irrelevant given the defects.
- *Failure modes*: directly violates "no new semantics in the DSL layer, ever"; a
  judge-driven swap has no static step encoding (the verdict is runtime), so `promote`
  would have to embed policy/logic — smuggling behavior into a data spec (against P9,
  P1); conflates declarative topology with feedback control (against P8); each new verb
  is a new kernel-ish primitive that `53`'s "every deployment primitive is already a
  kernel/graph primitive" explicitly warns against.
- *Tradeoff*: maximally expressive, structurally wrong. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — Pure delegation: freeze GraphSpec, push everything up a layer

Leave GraphSpec exactly as shipped (fresh-ref `spawn`/`connect`); declare identity-
preserving spawn, hierarchy, evolution, and remote application entirely out of scope for
construction.

- *Semantics*: GraphSpec is only ever "replay-as-new-graph" (the M4.5/`52` harness use).
- *Fast-path cost*: none.
- *Failure modes*: under-delivers. The identity gap is not a *layering* problem — it is
  that the spawn step *cannot even name* a replica or candidate as a **noun** today
  (`CellFactory` unconditionally mints a fresh ref). Evolution's candidate spawn (`53`)
  and I-3's seeded replica have *nowhere* to express "spawn this cell under
  `logicalId` X." Remote application (N22) is genuinely broken, not merely unspecified.
  Pure delegation leaves real, decided features with no construction path.
- *Tradeoff*: honors the freeze but strands adopted decisions. **Rejected as
  insufficient.**

##### Candidate C — Parameterize spawn; split declarative construction from imperative orchestration (recommended)

Keep the step vocabulary `spawn`/`connect`/`unlink` and the "lowers to management
invocations" rule. Supply the missing words as **parameters on the existing `spawn`
management invocation** — an *identity binding*, a *parent*, and a *serializable
factory* — none of which is a new kernel semantic. Draw one bright line: **GraphSpec is
declarative topology (nouns); feedback-driven orchestration is imperative (verbs over
time) and lives in an ordinary cell + the invocation journal, not in the step list.**

- *Semantics*: three parameterizations resolve N7/N23/N24 and half of N22; the
  declarative/imperative split resolves N25×N27; a synchronous→asynchronous degradation
  of loud failure resolves the rest of N22.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero — construction is a rare/management path (P2 licenses expensive
  linking/spawn); identity/parent are resolved once at spawn time.
- *Failure modes*: remote loud failure is genuinely weaker (async) than local — disclosed
  and mitigated (§4.4); evolution authors must write an orchestrator cell rather than a
  spec (a usability cost that is *correct* per P1).
- *Tradeoff*: the DSL gains **parameters, not semantics**; every step still lowers to a
  management invocation that already exists (spawn-with-chosen-ref, parent-aware spawn,
  connect, unlink). This is the smallest extension that serves all four features under
  one frame.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**. The litmus that keeps "no new semantics" intact: *every step
must lower to a management invocation the host already accepts; the extension adds
arguments to those invocations, never a new verb.*

##### 4.1 Data shapes (extend `51`; all `Serializable`, P9)

```kotlin
sealed interface Step : Serializable
data class SpawnStep(
    val localName: String,                     // spec-local handle, resolved to a CellRef at apply time
    val factory: CellFactory,                  // the WIRE-crossing construction form (already Serializable)
    val identity: IdentityBinding = IdentityBinding.FreshLogical,
    val parent: String? = null                 // organelle nesting → parent-aware spawn (G-28/M8.1)
) : Step
data class ConnectStep(val from: String, val fromPort: String,
                       val to: String,   val toPort: String) : Step
data class UnlinkStep(val from: String, val fromPort: String,
                      val to: String,   val toPort: String) : Step   // Link.unlink() as a recorded step

// Spawn is parameterized by WHICH ref it should produce — not a new semantic, a choice of ref.
sealed interface IdentityBinding : Serializable {
    object FreshLogical : IdentityBinding                             // mint fresh (logicalId, instanceId) — DEFAULT
    data class NewInstanceOf(val logicalId: LogicalId) : IdentityBinding  // fresh instanceId under a given logicalId
    data class Exact(val ref: CellRef) : IdentityBinding             // materialize a specific full ref
}

// The factory is ref-aware: the host resolves IdentityBinding → a concrete CellRef and hands it in.
fun interface CellFactory : Serializable { fun create(ref: CellRef): Cell }
```

Host management contract (each method already exists or is a pure parameterization):

```kotlin
interface HostManagementApi {
    fun spawn(cell: Cell): CellRef                                    // LOCAL-ONLY (live cell) — unchanged
    fun spawnBound(factory: CellFactory, id: IdentityBinding,
                   parent: CellRef?): CellRef                         // the WIRE form; host mints the ref per id
    fun connect(from: CellRef, fromPort: String,
                to: CellRef,   toPort: String): LinkResult            // unchanged
    fun unlink(from: CellRef, fromPort: String,
               to: CellRef,   toPort: String)                        // unchanged (Link.unlink)
}
```

##### 4.2 Identity-preserving spawn (resolves N23×N25, N24×N25)

`IdentityBinding` is the whole answer to "fresh logicalId vs new instance": **the spawn
step declares it.**

- **`FreshLogical` (default)** — mint a fresh `(logicalId, instanceId)`. This is
  *replay-as-new-graph*: the shipped M4.5 behavior and the `52` generative-harness use,
  unchanged. "Replay mints fresh cells and refs" remains true *by default*.
- **`NewInstanceOf(logicalId)`** — mint a *fresh `instanceId` under a given `logicalId`*.
  This is *identity-preserving spawn*: a candidate version (`53`) or a deliberately
  seeded replica (I-3). Per I-2's instanceId lifecycle rule, minting a new instance of a
  live logical cell is *legal* (the spawn guard keys on the full ref); the host
  constructs `CellRef(logicalId, freshInstanceId)` and passes it to the factory.
- **`Exact(fullRef)`** — materialize a *specific* full ref. Used for deterministic tests
  (caller-chosen `instanceId`, `10/11`), a migration target, and idempotent re-apply.
  Re-applying an `Exact` spawn of a live ref hits the G-16 live-ref spawn guard →
  `Rejected` (a no-op / loud reject), giving idempotent construction for free.

This is **not** new construction semantics: `spawn` already takes a cell carrying *some*
ref (`EchoCell(ref = …)`); the binding only chooses *which* ref, and the host already
mints refs. The distinction the spec "never made" — *replay-as-new-graph* vs
*replay-as-replication* — is now a **per-step parameter**, not two replay mechanisms.

**Replication does not become "a GraphSpec of N replicas."** GraphSpec may *seed* a
same-`logicalId` instance (`NewInstanceOf`), but the ongoing mesh is built by the I-3
membership-reactive `Replication` linker reacting to announcements — *not* by connect
steps enumerating a static mesh. GraphSpec's replication role is bounded to seeding
where an operator or evolution deliberately pre-places an instance; steady-state extent
stays interest-driven (P6/P8). This is why `NewInstanceOf` exists but a
"replicate-across-hosts" *verb* does not.

##### 4.3 Membrane hierarchy (resolves N7×N25)

Hierarchy is recorded and preserved by **two existing mechanisms plus one cell-declared
property** — no new step type:

1. **Organelle nesting = the `parent` field on `SpawnStep`.** It lowers to the *parent-
   aware spawn* the host already records (G-28/M8.1: "parent/child recorded at spawn").
   `spawn("child", parent = organelle) { factory }` is an ordinary parameterized spawn.
2. **Selective exposure = a cell-declared property** (G-9's `exposes` proposal), *not* a
   graph step. Which child ports a container exposes is a static property of the
   container's *type* (P5, correctness-by-construction). It is therefore preserved by
   reconstruction: replaying the same factory rebuilds the same cell with the same
   exposure set. GraphSpec needs no `expose` step.
3. **Connect steps address exposed ports by `(cell, portName)`** as today. An external
   `ConnectStep` to a *non-exposed* child port is `Rejected` at the handshake — the
   membrane veto is the loud-failure surface for hierarchy violations, using the existing
   `onLink` mechanism.

Thus membrane hierarchy is *recorded* (parent on spawn steps), *preserved* (exposure is
type-intrinsic), and *enforced* (non-exposed connects rejected) with the existing
vocabulary. G-9 still owes the concrete `exposes`/`findPort` mechanism (§8), but the DSL
side needs only the `parent` parameter.

##### 4.4 Remote application (resolves N22×N25)

Two defects, two rules.

**(a) Live cell on the wire → factory-based spawn is the wire form.** `spawn(cell: Cell)`
is **local-only**; the *GraphSpec* path uses `spawnBound(factory, identity, parent)` —
and `CellFactory` is already `Serializable`. `applyTo(remoteInlet)` therefore sends the
*factory* (an ordinary serializable management-invocation argument) and the *remote host*
constructs the cell locally. No live cell crosses the wire. Over the wire `spawnBound`
returns `Deferred<CellRef>` — the management-over-wire wrapping already decided in `40/41`
point 5. (`Exact`/`NewInstanceOf` bindings mean the applier can also *predict* the ref
without waiting, since it chose the `logicalId`; only `FreshLogical` truly needs the
`Deferred` reply.)

**(b) Loud failure degrades from synchronous to asynchronous across the wire.** This is
the honest resolution consistent with M5.4:

- **Local application** (`graph{}` eager build, or `applyTo(localInlet)`): **synchronous
  loud failure, unchanged.** `connect` returns a `LinkResult`; first `Rejected` aborts
  construction and throws. `51`'s claim holds *for co-located construction*.
- **Remote application** (`applyTo(remoteInlet)`): construction is *asynchronous
  submission*. It returns `Deferred<ApplyReport>`; per-step rejections surface as **dead
  letters on the target host** (`10/13`: a cross-host `connect` rejection is emitted to
  the target's `deadLetterOutlet`). Optionally, the applier links a **`ConstructionReport`
  outlet** on the target host and subscribes to it: per-step results travel back as
  **ordinary dataflow over an ordinary link** — the same mechanism `RegistryAnnounce`
  uses (M5.4) — never a synchronous cross-wire reply. `ApplyReport` is the eventual fold
  of those results.

The normative statement: **loud failure is synchronous only where construction is co-
located with the target host; across the wire it degrades to asynchronous rejection
reporting (dead letters + optional `ConstructionReport` over an ordinary dataflow link),
never a synchronous cross-wire reply.** This honors M5.4 ("no synchronous reply
channel"), P2 (no synchronous cross-host coupling), and P4 (no barrier), while giving
remote construction an observable, eventually-loud failure path. `51`'s claim is
*scoped*, not abandoned.

##### 4.5 Evolution orchestration (resolves N25×N27)

The category cut: **GraphSpec is declarative topology; the buffer → judge → swap →
replay control loop is imperative and does not belong in the step list.**

- **Declarative part → GraphSpec.** The candidate *subgraph* is an ordinary GraphSpec,
  applied with `NewInstanceOf(incumbentLogicalId)` to spawn the candidate as a new
  instance of the incumbent's logical cell (`53 §Mechanical decomposition`, I-2). The
  *promotion policy* (the judge's invariant criteria) is likewise declarative data.
- **Imperative part → an orchestrator cell.** The buffer/relink/replay procedure is
  driven by the `Promotion` cell that `53` already ships (M9: red → transfer → relink →
  green). It **emits ordinary management invocations over time**: buffer = spawn+connect a
  TrafficLight (`30/33`); relink = `unlink` + `connect`; replay = *automatic* via the
  `onLinked` catch-up (`53 §G-33`, `20/21`). These are exactly "incremental graph
  operations" — emitted by a live cell, which is itself a graph operation (P1/P8).
- **Recording/replay → the invocation journal, not GraphSpec.** `53` asks "how is the
  orchestration recorded or replayed?" The answer is the *second* graphs-as-data form:
  the **ordinary invocation journal** (`20/24` durability; `43 §5` recovery-by-replay).
  The management invocations the orchestrator emits are journaled; **rollback = journal
  reversal** ("same swap, reversed; journaled invocations replay", `53`). A feedback-
  driven swap *cannot* be a static GraphSpec because the judge's verdict is only known at
  runtime — so it is correctly recorded as an *executed history*, not a *declared spec*.

Two graphs-as-data forms, two jobs: **GraphSpec = declarative construction (what
topology); the invocation journal = imperative history (what was done, including
orchestration).** This keeps "no new semantics in the DSL layer": no `buffer`/`swap`/
`promote` step is ever added.

##### 4.6 The load-bearing summary

The missing "words" are supplied three ways, none of which is a new construction
semantic: (1) an **identity binding** and (2) a **parent** as *parameters on the existing
spawn management invocation*, plus (3) **factory-based spawn** as the wire form; and the
imperative features that *looked* like missing vocabulary (evolution's control loop) are
relocated to where they belong — a live orchestrator cell plus the invocation journal —
rather than smuggled into the declarative spec. Remote loud failure is scoped to co-
location and degrades honestly to asynchronous reporting over ordinary dataflow.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — every step lowers to an existing management invocation; orchestration is an ordinary cell emitting spawn/connect/unlink; nothing new below the graph layer. Meaningful single-threaded (the M4.5 DSL + M9 promotion already run under `SimulationController`). |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Untouched** — construction/orchestration are rare/management paths (P2 licenses expensive linking/spawn); identity/parent resolved once at spawn; remote apply adds no synchronous cross-host coupling on any data path. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — parent/child, exposure, and links are all explicit and inspectable; hierarchy is recorded (parent on spawn) not hidden. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — remote apply reports via ordinary dataflow (dead letters / `ConstructionReport`); no global barrier, clock, or synchronous cross-wire reply. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — `IdentityBinding` is a typed sum; exposure is a type-intrinsic property; non-exposed connects and re-applied `Exact` spawns are rejected at the handshake/guard, not by discipline. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — GraphSpec only *seeds* a same-`logicalId` instance; the replica mesh stays interest-driven (I-3 linker); no static replica set, no "replicate just in case." |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Untouched** — bridge policies (`40/43`) apply to remote apply as ordinary links; no ambient trust added. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — orchestration is emitted by a live cell over time; nothing assumes a static graph; the declarative/imperative split is *because* deployment is live. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `Step`/`IdentityBinding`/`CellFactory` are serializable; the wire form is the factory, never a live cell; no lambdas-as-code beyond the already-`Serializable` factory. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — a bounded set of parameters (identity, parent, factory) for a decentralized, evolving, interest-driven system; the general deployment-scripting engine (Candidate A) is the rejected non-niche option. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **"No new semantics in the DSL layer, ever" (`50/51`)** — consistent, *depended upon*:
  the extension adds parameters to existing management invocations; no new verb. The
  imperative control loop is relocated to a cell + journal precisely to keep this true.
- **G-8 / I-2 (full-ref addressing; `logicalId` a grouping/continuity key; instanceId
  lifecycle)** — consistent, depended upon: `IdentityBinding` *is* the construction-side
  surface of I-2's lifecycle rule (mint fresh on `FreshLogical`/`NewInstanceOf`-candidate;
  preserve exact on `Exact`).
- **I-3 (replication skeleton = membership-reactive linker; no static replica set)** —
  consistent: GraphSpec *seeds* `NewInstanceOf`; the mesh stays the linker's job.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol** — consistent:
  `ConstructionReport` rides an ordinary link (like `RegistryAnnounce`); no new reply
  protocol; M5.4's "no synchronous reply channel" is preserved.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — consistent: remote apply targets a host's management
  inlet; migration targets use `Exact` bindings; nothing per-cell added.
- **Suspension = one Buffering primitive (TrafficLight / parking)** — consistent:
  evolution's "buffer" is spawn+connect a TrafficLight, an ordinary graph op, not a step
  type.
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay** — consistent: remote `spawnBound`
  returns `Deferred`; senders park/replay as today.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — consistent: evolution "replay" is the `onLinked`
  state-as-delta catch-up (G-33/G-22); no snapshot type introduced.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — consistent:
  `spawn`/`spawnBound`/`connect` are management (may return `CellRef`/`LinkResult`,
  `Deferred` over wire); construction reporting is dataflow.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — consistent: the factory and
  `IdentityBinding` are serializable arguments to a management invocation; ids-only
  addressing unchanged.
- **Drain ordering / per-link FIFO** — untouched: construction does not alter data
  ordering.
- **Cardinality at link time; SPSC refuses fan-out; Owned→move-by-serialize, Leased not
  crossing machines** — consistent: connect steps still hit the link-time handshake;
  `spawnBound` sends a *factory*, not an `Owned`/`Leased` payload.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind full refs** — consistent, reinforced:
  `IdentityBinding` chooses the full ref a spawn produces; connects bind full refs.
- **Gaps Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — consistent: this *elaborates* G-30's
  residual (identity-aware, hierarchical, remote application) and gives G-9 its DSL-side
  parameter; it reopens nothing.

No CONFLICT flag required. The one refinement is a *scoping*, not a reversal: `51`'s
"link rejections fail construction loudly" is qualified to "*synchronously* loud for co-
located construction; asynchronously reported across the wire" — a precision on a
Resolved item's prose, consistent with the M5.4 decision that item predates.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **50/51 §Graph construction DSL** — state the step vocabulary
  (`SpawnStep`/`ConnectStep`/`UnlinkStep`), the `IdentityBinding` parameter (with
  `FreshLogical` as default = replay-as-new-graph), the `parent` field, factory-based
  `spawnBound` as the wire form, and the scoped loud-failure rule (local synchronous /
  remote asynchronous). Add the litmus: every step lowers to an existing management
  invocation; the DSL gains parameters, not verbs.
- **10/11 §Hierarchy: organelles (G-9)** — record that organelle nesting is the parent-
  aware spawn (G-28/M8.1) surfaced in the DSL; exposure is a type-intrinsic cell property
  preserved by reconstruction; non-exposed external connects are rejected at the
  handshake. (The concrete `exposes`/`findPort` mechanism remains G-9's own residual.)
- **50/53 §Model / §Mechanical decomposition** — draw the declarative/imperative cut:
  the candidate subgraph + promotion policy are declarative (GraphSpec with
  `NewInstanceOf`); the buffer→judge→swap→replay loop is an orchestrator cell emitting
  management invocations; recording/replay is the invocation journal, and rollback is
  journal reversal — *not* GraphSpec steps.
- **40/41 §Wire layer** — add `spawnBound(factory, identity, parent): Deferred<CellRef>`
  as the remote construction form (live-cell `spawn` stays local); the `ConstructionReport`
  outlet as the optional dataflow reply; confirm no synchronous reply channel.
- **40/42 §What replication must mean** — confirm GraphSpec *seeds* a `NewInstanceOf`
  instance; the mesh stays the I-3 reactive linker; no static replica enumeration.
- **90/91 G-30 / G-9** — update G-30's "Resolved (M4.5)" note to cover identity-aware,
  hierarchical, and remote application; cross-reference G-9's DSL-side `parent` parameter.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Concrete `exposes` / `findPort` mechanism (G-9 residual).** This resolution supplies
  the DSL-side `parent` parameter and treats exposure as type-intrinsic, but the actual
  `exposes` declaration and the host `findPort` restriction to exposed ports remain
  undesigned.
- **`ConstructionReport` structured form.** The minimal remote-failure surface is dead-
  letter observation; the structured per-step `ApplyReport` outlet (its contract, how the
  applier links it before the target cells exist, and its interaction with partial apply)
  needs a concrete design.
- **Partial-apply / atomicity of remote application.** When some remote steps reject and
  others succeed, whether `applyTo` leaves a partial graph or compensates (unlink the
  successful prefix) is unspecified; interacts with idempotent re-apply via `Exact` + the
  G-16 guard.
- **Promotion policy as data.** `53`'s judge criteria (which invariants, what threshold)
  as a serializable declarative artifact alongside the candidate GraphSpec — so a
  promotion is fully described by (candidate spec + policy) — is sketched but not
  specified.
- **Rollback-by-journal-reversal semantics.** The precise rule for reversing a journaled
  orchestration (which invocations are invertible, how `unlink`/`connect` reverse, how
  state transfer reverses) needs pinning against `53`/`24`.
- **`NewInstanceOf` collision discipline across hosts.** Two hosts independently seeding a
  `NewInstanceOf(logicalId)` mint independent `instanceId`s (safe per I-2), but a stated
  birthday-bound / caller-chosen-in-tests rule for construction-time minting is owed.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high** for the construction-side extension (identity/parent/factory
parameters and the declarative/imperative split) and **medium** for the remote loud-
failure degradation. The core insight is strongly grounded: the four features do not need
new DSL *semantics* — three of them need *parameters on the existing spawn invocation*
(and the host already accepts chosen refs and recorded parents, G-16/G-28), and the
fourth (evolution) is a feedback-driven procedure that structurally *cannot* be a static
spec and belongs to a live orchestrator cell plus the invocation journal that `53`
already relies on for rollback. The extension keeps "no new semantics in the DSL layer"
literally intact and builds directly on adopted I-2 (identity) and I-3 (replication)
decisions. Confidence is not higher because: (1) the remote loud-failure story trades a
synchronous guarantee for asynchronous reporting — honest to M5.4 but a real weakening
whose `ConstructionReport`/partial-apply details are spun out as gaps; (2) G-9's concrete
exposure mechanism is presumed, not delivered, here. **Open questions:** (a) whether
remote `applyTo` should attempt atomic all-or-nothing application (compensating unlinks
on partial rejection) or accept partial graphs with async reporting — I lean partial +
report, but a transactional membrane could want atomicity; (b) whether the promotion
policy should be folded into GraphSpec-adjacent data so a deployment is one serializable
artifact, or kept as a separate orchestrator input.

### I-22 — Producer rollback contract: RESTART and dead-letter versus state downstream already derived

> Member pairs: N8×N18, N14×N18, N15×N18, N18×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-26, G-33 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 1/4 member pairs findings need re-wording while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The reconciliation core: host-held generation bookkeeping, the ReBaseline(source, supersedes, state, supersede) catch-up mode, the R5 dead-lane filter on convergent consumers, the re-baseline trigger on every RESTART with direction-by-class (push-authoritat…
> ⚠ Divergence with landed code: Landed RESTART (spec 31 rule 5, M3.5) is exactly the bare local rollback the resolution forbids: deactivate → activate → restore the spawn-time Stateful checkpoint, same sourceId with a rolled-back counter (tag/wave aliasing possible), no downstream reconci…
> Reconciled after cross-check: wire Timestamp keeps the opaque per-epoch UUID; generation demoted to host bookkeeping seeding an explicit ReBaseline.supersedes list; R5 fence keys on the list.

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question.** `30/31 §Normative rules` (rule 5, G-26) defines
supervision RESTART as three local steps — *"deactivate → activate → restore the
spawn-time `Stateful` checkpoint"* — and nothing else. But a producer does not exist in
isolation: by the time it faults, downstream cells hold state **derived from every delta
it emitted after spawn**. Restoring the spawn-time checkpoint (for a data cell, *"typically
empty"*, `20/24 §Established pattern`) silently reverts the producer below what its
consumers have already absorbed, and the spec specifies **no reconciliation, re-catch-up,
retransmit, or de-duplication** to close the gap. The three obligations the dataflow layer
rests on all quantify over a stream continuity that rollback breaks:

- **deterministic delta application** (`20/21 §Incremental vs complete` rule 1: `state ×
  delta → state`) and **effective-only emission** (rule 2) presume the producer's state and
  the consumer's derived view stay on one monotone history (N8×N18);
- **tag convergence** (`20/24 §Established pattern` rule 3: OR-set tag-union merge)
  presumes *the set of deltas delivered* — a RESTART-reverted producer and a silently
  dead-lettered delta both violate that premise, and there is *"no retransmit path short of
  relinking"* (N15×N18);
- **consume-once / SPSC exclusivity** (`20/23 §The SPSC link rule`) collides with SUSPEND's
  parked-traffic replay and with dead-letter fan-out (N14×N18).

Four coupled sub-questions, each a member pair, must resolve under **one** contract:

1. **Re-baseline (N8×N18, N15×N18).** After a producer reverts, how do downstream derived
   cells reconcile? Deterministic-application and effective-only emission have no
   re-catch-up semantics; tag convergence has no retransmit path.
2. **Owned/Leased under rollback and replay (N14×N18).** RESTART rolls a cell back *after*
   it consumed `Owned` payloads; SUSPEND parks and replays traffic through a per-host buffer
   that `20/23` never explicitly blesses (only `30/33` drain parking is); dead-lettered
   invocations carrying `Owned`/`Leased` fan out on `deadLetterOutlet` (a `FanOutlet`) with
   **no exclusivity check**.
3. **Tag / wave aliasing (latent, under N15×N18).** RESTART preserves `instanceId`
   (I-2 lifecycle rule) yet resets the cell's state — and with it the outlet's tag/wave
   counter — to the checkpoint. Post-restart emissions then reuse `(sourceId, counter)`
   pairs already minted pre-crash: `Timestamp` tags and G-20 wave ids **alias** across the
   restart boundary. The tag algebra silently breaks.
4. **Checkpoint source under evolution (N18×N27).** RESTART restores *"the spawn-time
   checkpoint"* and *"is per-host and does not migrate"*, while G-33
   `StateMigrating.importFrom` installs *transformed* state inside the promotion swap window
   (`50/53 §G-33`). A post-promotion RESTART of the promoted instance would revert *past*
   the imported state; and *"which policy governs a candidate vs the active incarnation is
   unstated."*

**Why the spec leaves it open.** G-26 (`91`) is marked Resolved, but only for *local fault
isolation* — dead-letter + the three supervision policies. Its RESTART step was written as a
purely local checkpoint restore; the downstream, ownership, tag-hygiene, and evolution
consequences were never designed. I-7 (`res/I-7.md §4 R9`) already observed that *"durability
subsumes RESTART"* and I-2 / I-3 both spun out the follow-on gap *"RESTART within a replicated
logical cell … whether a restarted replica should re-catch-up from its peers … is
undesigned."* I-22 is that carried-forward gap, unified with the derived-state, ownership,
and evolution consequences.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P4 (guarantees opt-in, no global barrier) vs a consistent rollback.** A classic fix —
  coordinate a consistent cut across producer and all consumers, roll them back together — is
  a global barrier (P4 forbids it) and a global coordinator (P1 forbids it). Reconciliation
  must be *local and convergent*: the producer re-establishes continuity on its own links,
  consumers converge by the ordinary tag algebra.
- **"Snapshot IS a delta" + "no second sync protocol" (recorded) vs a bespoke reconcile
  path.** The temptation is a dedicated producer→consumer "resync" protocol. But
  reconciliation must reuse the **one** existing path — `onLinked` catch-up = state-as-delta
  = anti-entropy (`20/21 §Pull`, `40/42`, I-7 R5) — or it violates two recorded decisions.
- **The tag algebra is source-scoped, and that cuts both ways.** OR-set tags carry their
  minting `sourceId` (`20/24`, G-23), which is what lets a rollback be reconciled
  *per source* without disturbing other producers' contributions — but it is also exactly why
  a naïve counter reset **aliases** two distinct operations onto one tag. The same property
  that enables the fix creates the latent bug.
- **P5 (exactly-once by construction) vs replay.** `Owned`/`Leased` are consume-once by
  type (`20/23`). RESTART's rollback, SUSPEND's replay, and dead-letter's fan-out each look
  like a second delivery. The resolution must show none of them actually re-delivers an
  exclusive payload.
- **Rollback is not a legal CRDT operation.** Reverting one replica below its emitted
  frontier, while peers hold the merged result, is precisely what OR-set merge is *not*
  designed to undo. So the answer must depend on the producer's **class** (authoritative
  single-writer vs. mergeable replica): a replica must *not* wipe its contributions from
  healthy peers; a single-writer root *is* the authority on its own reverted state.
- **I-2 says "RESTART preserves instanceId."** Any generation/epoch we add to disambiguate
  emissions must ride *outside* the CellRef, or links break. The fix must be additive to I-2,
  not a contradiction.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Local rollback with no reconciliation (status quo)

RESTART restores the checkpoint and resumes; downstream is left as-is.

- *Semantics*: purely local; `30/31 rule 5` taken literally.
- *Fast-path cost*: none.
- *Failure modes*: **every member pair.** Downstream derived state diverges permanently
  (N8, N15); post-restart tags/waves alias pre-crash ones (sub-question 3); `Owned`
  re-consumption and dead-letter fan-out unaddressed (N14); post-import revert (N18×N27).
  It is the current broken state. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — RESTART completes with a generation-stamped re-baseline over the one catch-up path; direction by cell class; boundary rules for Owned/dead-letter (recommended)

RESTART becomes **restore + re-baseline**. After restoring the *freshest available*
checkpoint the host triggers reconciliation over the existing `onLinked`/catch-up path,
stamped with a bumped per-instance **generation** so nothing aliases. The *direction* of the
re-baseline (authoritative push vs. anti-entropy pull) follows the cell's mutability/
replication class. `Owned`/dead-letter are handled by the boundary rules `20/23` already
states. SUSPEND's park is the one Buffering primitive, exactly-once preserved.

- *Semantics*: reconciliation = *state reconstruction on the producer + one idempotent
  reconcile path downstream*, the same shape as I-7 recovery and I-3 anti-entropy.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero on the steady state. A restarted producer pays a re-baseline (rare,
  P2 budget). Downstream convergent cells pay a one-integer generation comparison that rides
  the tag fold they already perform.
- *Failure modes*: a non-durable, non-replicated root that reverts below its emitted frontier
  genuinely loses post-checkpoint state; the generational supersede makes downstream
  *converge to the producer's reverted state* (producer-authoritative), which is correct for
  a single-writer root but requires durability/replication if *no loss* is the goal (opt-in,
  P4).
- *Tradeoff*: reuses five shipped mechanisms (catch-up, tag algebra, drain/park, boundary
  rules, I-7 recovery) and collapses all four sub-questions into one rule set. The genuinely
  new content is the **generation** field and the **generational supersede**, both additive.

##### Candidate C — RESTART re-derives from the graph, never restores local state (pull-only)

RESTART discards local state entirely and rebuilds by re-subscribing / catch-up from
upstream and peers.

- *Semantics*: the cell is treated as fully reconstructible from its inputs.
- *Fast-path cost*: none (rare path).
- *Failure modes*: works for *derived* cells (a union/filter/count re-catches-up from
  upstream) and *replicated* cells (pull from the mesh), but **fails for source/root cells**
  (no upstream to pull from) and for history-dependent cells whose state is not a function of
  current upstream. Also fails if upstream is itself mid-fault.
- *Tradeoff*: elegant for the derived/replicated case — but that case is exactly the
  *pull-merge* direction of Candidate B. C is therefore not a distinct mechanism; it is B's
  derived/replicated branch. **Folded into B** as the "prefer re-derivation over rollback"
  rule (R3/R4).

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B.** RESTART is redefined as **restore-the-freshest-checkpoint + trigger a
generation-stamped re-baseline over the one catch-up path**, with direction chosen by the
cell's class, and with `Owned`/`Leased`/dead-letter governed by the boundary rules `20/23`
already states. Ten rules; every member pair falls out.

##### Data shapes

> **Reconciled** (post-consistency-check): the wire `Timestamp` keeps its opaque
> per-epoch UUID `sourceId` (I-14 Rule S1); the `(instanceId, outletId, generation)`
> triple is demoted to host-side bookkeeping that seeds an explicit `supersedes` list
> on the `ReBaseline` notice, and the R5 fence keys on that list instead of ordered
> generation comparison — same semantics, no new wire shape.

```
// G-20 Timestamp shape UNCHANGED — sourceId stays an opaque per-epoch UUID (I-14 Rule S1).
Timestamp(sourceId: UUID, counter: Long)                     // wire shape untouched

// Host-side bookkeeping ONLY (never on the wire, outside the Stateful checkpoint):
//   (instanceId, outletId, generation) -> current sourceId UUID
//   generation: per-INSTANCE monotonic recovery counter,
//   - bumped by the host on every RESTART / recovery, BEFORE reactivation
//     (a checkpoint restore can never roll it back);
//   - NOT part of CellRef(id, instanceId) — links bind the CellRef and survive (I-2 honored);
//   - its only observable role is seeding ReBaseline.supersedes below.

// The reconciliation message — an ordinary catch-up delta with a mode.
ReBaseline<D>(
    source: UUID,                // the producer's fresh post-restart sourceId (epoch N)
    supersedes: Set<UUID>,       // this outlet's predecessor sourceIds (host bookkeeping)
    state: D,                    // state-as-delta-from-empty = Stateful.snapshot() (a delta)
    supersede: Boolean           // true = authoritative (single-writer/root); false = merge
)
```

`ReBaseline.state` is exactly the state-as-delta-from-empty the `onLinked` catch-up already
unicasts (`20/21 §Pull`, "a snapshot IS a delta"). It is not a new wire type; it is a
catch-up carrying a `supersede` bit and the producer's current `SourceId`.

##### Recovery protocol (RESTART = restore + re-baseline)

1. **Deactivate → bump generation.** The host deactivates the faulted instance and
   increments its host-held `generation` (R1). `instanceId` is unchanged (I-2).
2. **Restore the freshest available checkpoint** (R3), preferring re-derivation over
   rollback:
   - *durable cell* → I-7 recovery: latest snapshot + suppressed WAL replay (no loss; the
     WAL replay restores the true counter high-water, so no aliasing even before the
     generation bump);
   - *post-import (G-33) cell* → the **imported** state is the baseline (not spawn-time);
   - *replicated (mergeable) cell* → skip local restore; go to step 4 pull-merge from the
     mesh (I-3 anti-entropy);
   - *derived cell with live upstream* → skip local restore; go to step 4 pull-merge from
     upstream (`requestState`, G-18);
   - *plain non-durable root/source* → restore its latest local `Stateful` checkpoint
     (spawn-time in the degenerate case).
3. **Reactivate** (`onActivate`); links are intact (`instanceId` preserved).
4. **Trigger the re-baseline** before resuming live traffic (R2, R4):
   - **push-authoritative** (root / single-writer): emit `ReBaseline(source=Sₙ, state,
     supersede=true)` on each outlet, over the ordinary catch-up path;
   - **pull-merge** (derived / replicated): trigger upstream `requestState` / mesh
     anti-entropy so the producer rebuilds *its own* state by idempotent merge; its own
     downstream then reconciles from its subsequent live deltas (a push- or pull-re-baseline
     per *its* class).
5. **Resume live traffic.** SUSPEND-parked traffic (if any) drains live afterward (R7).

##### Rules the model introduces (normative)

- **R1 — Generation-scoped source identity.** RESTART opens a fresh emission epoch: per
  I-14 Rule S1 the outlet mints a fresh opaque `sourceId` UUID, so post-restart tags and
  waves are distinct from every pre-crash one — **tag and wave aliasing is structurally
  impossible** (sub-question 3 dissolved). The host-held `generation` counter (bumped
  outside the `Stateful` checkpoint on every RESTART/recovery, so a restore can never
  roll it back) is bookkeeping that orders recoveries host-side and seeds
  `ReBaseline.supersedes` with the dead epochs' `sourceId`s. This is the
  mechanically-precise realization of the ADR's original "incarnation" intuition, now
  that I-2 has repurposed `instanceId` for the replica/candidate axis; to avoid
  collision with the retired glossary term it is named **generation**.

- **R2 — RESTART completes with a re-baseline.** RESTART is *restore + re-baseline*, never a
  bare local rollback. The re-baseline is the single reconciliation trigger; it reuses the
  `onLinked` catch-up path verbatim (no second sync protocol).

- **R3 — Checkpoint source is the freshest available; prefer re-derivation over rollback.**
  Durable → I-7 recovery; post-import → imported baseline; replicated/derived → pull-merge
  from mesh/upstream; plain root → local checkpoint. RESTART-to-spawn-empty is only the
  *degenerate* case for a non-durable, non-replicated, upstream-less root (answers N18×N27's
  post-import revert: the imported state *is* the checkpoint).

- **R4 — Two re-baseline modes, chosen by class (P5).** *Push-authoritative* for
  single-writer roots (`supersede=true`); *pull-merge* for mergeable/replicated and derived
  cells (`supersede=false`, ordinary idempotent catch-up). Direction encodes semantics: an
  authority reasserts; a replica/derivation re-absorbs. This is I-3's mutability-class split
  and I-7's input/output split, unified.

- **R5 — Explicit supersession + dead-lane filter (downstream convergent cells).** On
  receiving `ReBaseline(source=S_new, supersedes={S₁..Sₖ}, supersede=true)`, a convergent
  consumer (one that folds OR-set tags): (a) drops every live tag from the listed
  superseded sources that the re-baseline does **not** re-assert; (b) applies `state` by
  ordinary tag-union merge; (c) records `{S₁..Sₖ}` as **dead lanes** and thereafter
  rejects any delta stamped with a dead `sourceId` (a stale pre-restart delta arriving
  late via a longer fan-out path). The explicit list replaces the ordered-generation
  comparison — same fence, no ordering inside the opaque id. Because tags are
  source-scoped, this retracts *only* the reverted producer's lost contribution and
  leaves every other source's tags intact — so it composes with multi-writer merge (an
  element still added by a healthy peer stays present). For `supersede=false`
  (pull-merge) there is no retraction: forward idempotent merge only.

- **R6 — RESTART never replays inputs.** RESTART restores *state*, it does not re-drive the
  invocations that produced it (contrast I-7 suppressed WAL replay, which re-drives with
  outlets NoOp-served but is still state-reconstruction). Therefore a previously-consumed
  `Owned`/`Leased` payload is **never re-delivered**: the state resulting from consuming it is
  whatever the checkpoint holds; any loss is reconciled by the re-baseline. SPSC exactly-once
  is preserved by construction (N14 sub-problem 1 dissolved — there is no second consumption).

- **R7 — SUSPEND's parked buffer is the one Buffering primitive; exactly-once preserved.**
  Per the recorded decision *"Suspension is ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities,"*
  SUSPEND's per-cell park (`30/31 rule 5`) is a *third* granularity of the same primitive and
  inherits `20/23`'s blessing: *"the Buffering proxy MAY hold [Owned]; buffering preserves
  exclusivity."* Each parked `Owned` is held once and replayed **once** to the single
  consumer, never fanned; a suspended cell leaving the host dead-letters its parked traffic
  under R8. This closes N14 sub-problem 2 by *naming* the SUSPEND park as the same blessed
  buffer, not a new one.

- **R8 — Dead-letter applies the `20/23` boundary rules to `Owned`/`Leased`.** The
  `deadLetterOutlet` is a `FanOutlet` (fan-out to observers), so a live `Owned`/`Leased`
  reference MUST NOT enter it. At capture the dead-lettered invocation's payload is
  **frozen/serialized** — the same immutable, fan-out-safe form the wire uses (P9): `Owned`
  degenerates to **move-by-serialize into the dead letter** (the sender's wrapper is consumed
  as the frame is encoded, exactly as `BridgeEgressCell` does), and `Leased` is **released**
  and represented by a redacted marker (a lease cannot outlive its pool). The dead-letter
  outlet then fans a `Frozen`/serialized value, honoring exclusivity by construction. This
  closes N14 sub-problem 3 by treating the dead-letter outlet as the boundary it already is.

- **R9 — Supervision binds the full ref; candidate and active are independent instances.**
  Per I-2, `supervise(ref, policy)`, parked traffic, `resume(ref)`, and dead letters all key
  on the full `CellRef(id, instanceId)`. A candidate and the active instance are distinct
  full refs with **independent** policies — there is no ambiguity about "which policy governs
  candidate vs active" (N18×N27): each instance's own policy governs it. RESTART of the
  promoted instance restores its imported baseline (R3). Because supervision *"is per-host and
  does not migrate,"* promotion/migration onto a new host re-applies the policy as ordinary
  host-management configuration (consistent with *"policies are host-management
  configuration"*).

- **R10 — Re-baseline is the one reconciliation path.** The re-baseline trigger is shared by
  RESTART (R2), relink/`onLinked` (`20/21`), on-demand `requestState` pull (G-18), durable
  recovery (I-7 R5), and mesh anti-entropy (I-3). A dead-letter under **PROPAGATE** (no
  restart) provides *observability* (the `DeadLetter`/`CellError` is emitted, `30/31 rule 5`)
  but **not** automatic retransmission; gap-freedom for a dropped delta is opt-in — via
  durability, replication, or the natural pattern of a recovery/invariant cell that links
  `deadLetterOutlet` and, on observing a `DeadLetter`, issues a `requestState` to the affected
  producer to force a re-baseline. This answers N15's *"no retransmit path short of
  relinking"*: the retransmit path is the re-baseline, triggerable without relinking.

##### Net effect

RESTART stops being a silent local rollback and becomes *restore-the-freshest-state + one
generation-stamped reconcile over the existing catch-up path*. The tag/wave aliasing hole is
closed structurally by the host-held generation (R1). Derived-state divergence is closed by
generational supersede for authoritative roots (R5) and by pull-merge re-catch-up for
replicas/derivations (R4) — the replica case correctly *not* wiping healthy peers. Owned,
SUSPEND-replay, and dead-letter are all resolved by *naming* mechanisms `20/23` already
provides (state-restore-not-input-replay, the one Buffering primitive, the boundary rules).
Evolution is resolved by making the checkpoint source the freshest available and binding
policy per instance.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Untouched** — RESTART, re-baseline, generation bump, and supersede are all host/cell-level; every step meaningful single-threaded (re-baseline is ordinary origination + catch-up; supersede is a per-source tag filter). No kernel primitive added. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied (disclosed tension)** — steady state unchanged. A restarted producer pays a re-baseline (rare, P2 budget). Downstream convergent cells pay one integer `generation` comparison that *rides the OR-set tag fold they already perform* (`20/24`); plain non-convergent cells pay nothing. `generation` widens `SourceId` by one field. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — re-baseline flows over the visible existing links; no hidden multicast; the recovery/invariant cell that triggers retransmit is an explicit link to `deadLetterOutlet`. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — reconciliation is per-source, per-link, convergent; no global cut/barrier/coordinator. No-loss is an *opt-in* stronger guarantee (durable/replicated), best-effort convergence otherwise. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — generation makes aliasing structurally impossible; supersede direction is chosen by mutability *class* (a type property), not runtime discipline; Owned/dead-letter safety is a boundary type rule. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — re-baseline runs only on a real fault/recovery; supersede only where convergent consumers exist; durability/gap-freedom are opt-in, nothing journaled/retransmitted "just in case." |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — orthogonal to boundary security; dead-letter freezing is a payload-form rule, not a trust assumption. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — RESTART keeps `instanceId` so links survive; post-import RESTART restores the imported baseline; candidate/active are independently supervised instances; a restarted graph stays fully mutable. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied, load-bearing** — `ReBaseline` is a catch-up delta (a serializable state-as-delta) plus a bit; dead-letter payloads are frozen via the same serialization; `generation` is a serializable long. No lambdas/handles. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — decentralized, convergent, interest-driven recovery (re-derive from the graph where possible; producer-authoritative reassert otherwise) over a coordinated global rollback. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves (`Timestamp(sourceId, counter)`):** consistent, *refined* —
  `sourceId` gains a `generation`; the `Timestamp` **shape is unchanged**; convergence not
  simultaneity across sources is preserved (each generation of a source is, if anything,
  a further-distinguished source). No wave coordinator added.
- **SID-UP-style global propagation locks REJECTED:** consistent — reconciliation is a local
  push/pull re-baseline, no lock, no barrier; the global-cut alternative was rejected in §2.
- **Host is the unit of mobility; supervision per-host, does not migrate:** consistent —
  R9 keeps supervision per-host and re-applies policy on migration/promotion as management
  config; nothing added to the mobility protocol.
- **Suspension is ONE Buffering primitive at two granularities:** consistent, *extended* —
  R7 names SUSPEND's per-cell park as a third granularity of the *same* primitive, inheriting
  `20/23`'s buffering-preserves-exclusivity blessing; no new suspension mechanism.
- **Location = Local | Remote; one park/replay:** untouched — park/replay keyed by full ref,
  unchanged.
- **A snapshot IS a delta (state-as-delta-from-empty):** strongly consistent — `ReBaseline`
  *is* the snapshot-as-delta the catch-up path already emits; no new snapshot type.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps minted cell-locally and are NOT wave ids:** consistent — tags
  stay cell-local OR-set tags; `generation` scopes the *source* of both tags and waves,
  keeping them "separate uses of one clock shape." Tags and waves remain distinct.
- **Data contracts push-only; management may return; management null context:** consistent —
  `ReBaseline` is push data over the data path; `supervise`/`resume` are management; RESTART
  is a host-management action.
- **Replication reuses dataflow links + delta gossip; NO second synchronization protocol:**
  strongly consistent — the re-baseline *is* the catch-up/anti-entropy path (R2, R10); the
  replicated-cell RESTART re-catches-up from the mesh (R4 pull-merge), reusing I-3's
  anti-entropy. No second protocol.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT become a second distribution mechanism:** untouched — a partition
  is an ordinary cell; its RESTART follows the same contract per its class.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved:** consistent — `generation` is an additive
  field on `SourceId`; `ReBaseline` reuses the catch-up encoding. Bump the reserved version
  byte only if `SourceId` widening is not additively compatible.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end:** consistent — per-link FIFO places
  the re-baseline after all pre-crash deltas on that link; the cross-fan-out late-delta case
  is handled by R5's monotonic-generation filter, not by weakening FIFO.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time; exclusive ownership refuses fan-out:** consistent —
  R8 keeps `Owned`/`Leased` out of the fan-out `deadLetterOutlet` by freezing/serializing at
  capture; the exclusive contract is never fanned.
- **Owned crossing machine boundaries degenerates to move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross
  machine boundaries:** consistent, *reused* — R8 applies exactly this rule at the
  dead-letter boundary (Owned → move-by-serialize into the dead letter; Leased → released).
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation) direction / I-2 "RESTART preserves instanceId":**
  consistent, *additive* — `generation` rides in `SourceId`, **not** in `CellRef`; links bind
  the CellRef and survive RESTART exactly as I-2 requires. I-22 reclaims the ADR's original
  "incarnation" *concept* (a per-instance recovery generation) under the name `generation`,
  distinct from I-2's `instanceId` (the replica/candidate axis). No CONFLICT — I-2 explicitly
  left "RESTART within a replicated logical cell" as a follow-on gap, which this fills.
- **Gaps/conflicts marked Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved:** consistent — this *completes*
  G-26's RESTART step (its downstream/ownership/evolution consequences) and G-33's checkpoint
  interaction; it does not reopen the resolved local fault-isolation core.

No CONFLICT flag required.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **`30/31 §Normative rules` (rule 5, G-26):** redefine RESTART as *restore-freshest +
  generation-bump + re-baseline*, not a bare spawn-checkpoint restore; state R1 (host-held
  generation), R2/R3/R4 (re-baseline and its direction), R6 (state-restore-not-input-replay),
  R7 (SUSPEND park = the one Buffering primitive, exactly-once), R8 (dead-letter freezes
  `Owned`/`Leased`), R9 (policy per full ref; re-apply on migration/promotion).
- **`20/21 §Push / §Pull`:** note that RESTART reuses the `onLinked` catch-up path as its
  re-baseline; add the `supersede` mode; state that deterministic-application and
  effective-only emission are re-established by re-baseline after a producer reverts.
- **`20/24 §Established pattern`:** add the generational-supersede rule (R5) to the tag
  algebra — a convergent consumer folds tags per `(instanceId, outletId, generation)` and
  applies the monotonic-generation filter; state that this composes with multi-writer merge.
- **`20/23 §The SPSC link rule` (corollaries):** state R6 (RESTART restores state, never
  re-consumes an `Owned` payload), extend the buffering-blessing to SUSPEND's per-cell park
  (R7), and add the dead-letter boundary rule (R8) alongside the existing bridge boundary
  rules.
- **`50/53 §G-33`:** state that `StateMigrating.importFrom` re-baselines the instance's
  RESTART checkpoint (imported state becomes the recovery baseline); confirm candidate and
  active are independently supervised full refs (R9).
- **`20/22` (waves) / glossary `00/03`:** record `generation` as a per-instance recovery
  counter distinct from `instanceId`; `SourceId` gains it; `Timestamp` shape unchanged.
- **`91` G-26 / G-33:** annotate with the completed RESTART contract and the residual gaps
  below.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Generation persistence across host failure.** `generation` is host-held outside the
  checkpoint; if the *host* itself fails and restarts, the generation counter must not reset
  below a value already emitted (else post-host-restart tags alias). Needs a rule: derive the
  restart generation from the durable journal high-water (I-7) or from a monotonic host clock;
  for a non-durable host, a fresh random/high generation base.
- **Supersede correctness under concurrent multi-source removes.** R5 retracts a reverted
  source's un-reasserted tags; the interaction with a concurrent *remove* observing those
  same tags (add-wins vs. a superseding retraction) needs a stated precedence and a
  generative convergence test.
- **Re-baseline cost under wide fan-out / large state.** A push-authoritative re-baseline
  unicasts full state-as-delta to every downstream link; for large state or wide fan-out this
  is expensive on a rare path but may still need bounding (diff-against-last-acked, or
  delta-since-generation) — interacts with OR-set tag growth / compaction (I-3, G-25).
- **PROPAGATE-drop gap-freedom pattern.** R10 offers the recovery-cell pattern (observe
  `deadLetterOutlet` → `requestState`) but does not standardize it; a library recovery cell
  and its idempotency contract are undesigned.
- **Choosing the re-baseline direction for hybrid cells.** A cell that is both derived and a
  root of further state (stateful operator over upstream) may need pull-merge for its inputs
  *and* push-authoritative for a locally-owned component; the per-cell direction policy is
  only sketched.
- **Dead-letter payload redaction contract.** R8 freezes/serializes; the exact behavior for a
  non-serializable `Owned` payload, and how much of a `Leased` payload a redacted marker
  should expose for diagnosis, needs a concrete `DeadLetter` envelope spec.
- **Generation and cycle heads (I-5).** A `CycleHead` that RESTARTs bumps its generation
  mid-loop; confirm the head's re-originated waves across a generation boundary interact
  cleanly with in-flight loop waves (likely fine — a new generation is just a further source
  distinction — but assert it).

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The mechanism reuses five shipped/decided pieces — `onLinked`
catch-up (M4.2), the source-scoped OR-set tag algebra (M4.1/G-23), the one Buffering
primitive (recorded), `20/23`'s boundary rules (M5.6), and I-7 recovery — and it slots
cleanly into the adopted resolutions: it is the non-durable generalization of I-7 recovery,
fills the "RESTART within a replicated cell" gap I-2 and I-3 both spun out, and inherits
I-2's full-ref addressing and I-5's per-instance source model. The single load-bearing new
field (`generation`, host-held, outside the checkpoint) closes a *latent correctness hole*
(tag/wave aliasing on counter reset) that none of the prior resolutions addressed, and one
new rule (generational supersede) makes even the lossy rollback converge while composing with
multi-writer merge. Confidence is not higher because three pieces are genuinely new design
rather than reclassification: **generation persistence across host failure** (the host-level
counterpart to the cell-level fix), **supersede-vs-concurrent-remove precedence**, and the
**re-baseline cost bound** for wide fan-out — all spun out as follow-on gaps.

**Open questions:** (1) whether the re-baseline direction should be a declared per-cell policy
or inferred purely from the mutability class (I lean inferred, with a declaration escape hatch
for hybrid cells); (2) whether generational supersede should be *always on* for convergent
consumers or opt-in (I lean always-on, since the generation comparison is cheap and the
aliasing fix is mandatory regardless); (3) whether a non-durable authoritative root that
reverts below its emitted frontier should be *allowed* at all with live convergent consumers,
or flagged at link time as requiring durability/replication for no-loss — a P5 hardening that
could turn the best-effort case into a link-time contract.

### I-23 — Upstream frontier traversal: visibility through delegation and membranes, termination in cycles

> Member pairs: N3×N10, N3×N12, N5×N12, N7×N12
> Existing gaps touched: G-13, G-9, G-10 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 2/4 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **NOT_LANDED** — The whole traversal protocol: DescribeFrontier/FrontierReport on the I-1 metadata plane (unbuilt), epoch + visited-set edge-once termination with CYCLIC flagging (G-19 fixpoint stays open, now with marked back-edges as input), source-and-guarantee vocabular…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The single mechanism question: **when a glitch-free cell (or any upstream metadata
protocol) traverses upstream to learn "which edges/sources feed me," what does the
traversal see — and when does it stop — at a delegation, at a membrane, and around a
cycle?**

20/22 makes the traversal load-bearing but unbuilt. §Local glitch-freedom step 1
requires "on init and on topology change, traverse upstream to discover which
inlets/edges feed it for a given wave"; §The glitch-free frontier says traversal
"stops at the nearest upstream glitch-free cells, whose outputs are already per-wave
consistent"; §Implementation plan step 4 pins the carrier: "Upstream traversal via the
generic management protocol on multiplex ports (12) — 'describe your frontier' is a
management invocation." Steps 1–3 are done; step 4 is not — the shipped wrapper runs on
"the inlet's current link set" (20/22 §The glitch-free frontier, impl note: "Upstream
frontier traversal awaits multiplex ports (G-13); unwaved traffic passes through").

Three constructs leave the traversal's *sight* and *stopping* undefined, and the member
pairs pull on exactly these:

- **Through delegation (N5×N12).** 10/14 §The Link-and-Lease model: "the delegating cell
  is *not* on the per-message path" and "Chains of delegation MUST flatten on
  resolution." A traversal that walks declared cell inlets could either miss the true
  producer (the delegating cell hides it) or stop at a phantom (the delegating cell that
  is not really on the path). 20/22 rule 4 already says "Delegation is not a context
  no-op ... every outlet hop rewrites `sourcePort`" — so waves flow through delegation,
  but what the *frontier query* sees is unstated.
- **At a membrane (N7×N12).** 10/11 §Hierarchy (G-9): "today all ports of a spawned cell
  are reachable by name through the host," with hiding only proposed; 10/11 §Membranes
  (G-10): boundary as authority / causal scope / observability, with no code form for
  the object. Whether a frontier query penetrates a membrane or the membrane answers
  opaquely for its interior is undefined.
- **Around a cycle (N3×N10).** 20/22 §Interaction/Cycles: "wave semantics around cycles
  are unresolved (a cycle re-entering a glitch-free cell with the same wave id must be
  detected)"; 20/21 §Cycles (G-19): fixpoint semantics "an open research item." The
  upstream metadata protocols (frontier-discovery, state-request 21, attention 34) share
  one carrier (12 §Multiplexed ports) but have **no termination rule** on a cyclic graph
  — "two exploratory mechanisms meet with no defined composition."

And **N3×N12 (the carrier itself)**: G-13 is unbuilt, so the dynamic traversal's
composition with the static-frontier approximation is unevaluated.

Two of these are now answered by adopted resolutions and must be built on, not
re-litigated: **I-1** fixes the carrier (frontier-discovery is an *upstream generic
protocol* on the metadata plane — a `PORT_PROTOCOL` dispatch class, null-context,
bypass-parking, direction `Upstream`, its own ordering lane, bridge-aware), and **I-10**
fixes the membrane (Flatten = green/off-path delegation; Mediate = served proxy;
`Remint` membrane "naturally advertises itself as a glitch-free *frontier* ... downstream
glitch-free traversal stops at it"). **I-2** fixes what an edge denotes (full-ref
`PortRef` links; each instance is a distinct wave source). This challenge is the
remaining question those three leave open: the **traversal's semantics and termination
across the three constructs**.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P2 vs a graph walk.** The obvious design — the glitch-free cell reads Link objects
  (P3) and crawls the upstream graph itself — is a *global* read that must reach every
  upstream node, including remote hosts and hidden organelles. That breaks locality (P4)
  and hiding (G-9), and cannot cross the wire without addressing hidden refs (P9/40/41).
  Yet the traversal is rare (init + topology change), so P2 explicitly *permits*
  arbitrary cost there — the constraint is locality/hiding, not cycles-of-CPU.
- **Delegation-flatten is load-bearing both ways.** It gives the flat fast path (P2) and
  erases the pass-through cell — so a traversal defined over the *declared* cell graph
  sees a different topology than the data actually flows over. The frontier must be
  defined over the **resolved** (post-flatten) graph, or it is simply wrong.
- **G-9 hiding vs completeness.** A downstream glitch-free cell needs, per wave source,
  the fan-in multiplicity feeding it (how many inlet edges carry that source). But it
  must learn this **without** being handed a name/ref for any hidden organelle port
  (P5/P7). Frontier knowledge and addressing capability must be decoupled.
- **P4 (no global barrier) vs "collect the whole frontier."** A recursive gather that
  waits for "all upstream replies" is distributed termination detection — a global
  barrier in disguise, and undecidable-in-bounded-time on a cyclic/lossy graph.
- **Cycles: two open items, one must stay open.** Traversal *termination* (does the query
  loop forever?) is this challenge's job. Cyclic-edge *fixpoint semantics* (does a
  glitch-free cell wait for a back-edge wave?) is G-19 / 20/22 §Cycles, explicitly
  flagged open — the resolution must terminate the traversal **without** silently
  resolving fixpoint semantics.
- **P1 reduction.** Whatever the traversal is, it must reduce to cells/ports/links/
  invocations and be meaningful in a single-threaded simulation — not a bespoke
  distributed algorithm.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Keep the static frontier; never traverse (status quo)

*Semantics*: the frontier stays "the inlet's current link set," recomputed on every
completeness check (shipped). No upstream protocol.

*Fast-path cost*: zero beyond today; no termination problem (there is no traversal).

*Failure modes*: cannot see through delegation to the true producer; treats every direct
inlet link as a frontier edge, so it over-buffers glitch-free chains (a glitch-free
upstream cell is redundantly re-tracked) and mis-handles **heterogeneous sources** — an
inlet that carries source X but never Y, waited on for a Y-wave, deadlocks unless the
impl special-cases per-source watermarks. Leaves 20/22 impl step 4 unbuilt and the three
constructs unaddressed.

*Tradeoffs*: correct only in the homogeneous-source case; structurally cannot carry the
challenge. Rejected as the *sole* mechanism — but retained as the **conservative
fallback/bootstrap** frontier in the recommendation.

##### Candidate B — Initiator-driven graph crawl over Link objects

*Semantics*: the glitch-free cell reads the explicit topology (P3), walks upstream Link
by Link, holds a global visited-set, decides stop/continue at each node.

*Fast-path cost*: rare-path, but each crawl is a global read of the upstream cone.

*Failure modes*: requires the initiator to *reach and address* every upstream node —
including hidden organelles (violates G-9) and remote refs behind membranes (violates
P7/P9 and I-10 hiding). Cannot respect membrane authority (a membrane cannot interpose).
Cross-host crawl needs the initiator to hold remote Link objects it has no right to. It
is precisely the global, hiding-piercing walk the architecture forbids.

*Tradeoffs*: conceptually simplest, structurally illegal under hiding + locality.
Rejected.

##### Candidate C — Upstream metadata-plane protocol with terminal-node + visited-set termination and incremental monotone gather (recommended)

*Semantics*: frontier-discovery is the upstream `PORT_PROTOCOL` I-1 already provisions.
Each cell handles a `DescribeFrontier` query **locally**: reply terminally, or forward
upstream with an extended visited-set, re-basing reports at hiding boundaries. Membranes
answer per their I-10 surface mode. Delegation is transparent because the protocol rides
**resolved** (post-flatten) links. Cycles break on already-visited edges. The initiator
never blocks on "all replies" — it accumulates a monotonically growing frontier and
installs each refinement as a **topology version** (20/22 §Topology versioning), falling
back to the Candidate-A conservative frontier until refined.

*Fast-path cost*: none on the data path — the flood rides the metadata plane (off the
data hot path, I-1) and runs only on init/topology-change (P2 rare path). The data path
reads the current completeness map exactly as today.

*Failure modes*: none of the member-pair conflicts survive (§4). Residual risk is
confined to cyclic-edge *fixpoint* treatment (deferred to G-19), per-epoch reply-routing
state lifecycle, and the exact membrane opaque-summary contract (§8) — all bounded.

*Tradeoffs*: gives up a single global picture in exchange for a local, hiding-preserving,
cycle-safe traversal that composes all three upstream protocols under one termination
discipline and reuses machinery already adopted (I-1 carrier, I-10 membrane, 20/22
topology-versioning). Recommended.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**. The load-bearing insight: **the frontier is defined over the
*resolved* dataflow graph and spoken in the vocabulary of wave sources and guarantee
kinds — never cell/port refs.** Because the traversal rides the same resolved links the
data rides, it sees exactly what the data sees (delegation transparent); because it
speaks only sourceIds + guarantee kinds, it never hands out an address to a hidden port
(hiding preserved); because it expands each edge at most once, it terminates on any graph
(cycles safe).

##### Carrier (from I-1, unchanged)

`ProtocolId FRONTIER` on the metadata plane, with descriptor `{ direction = Upstream,
band = management, lane = frontier-lane (its own per-link FIFO), cardinality =
FanInMerge }`. It is management-class: null `MessageContext`, bypasses data-path parking,
idempotent/reorder-tolerant, bridge-aware over the reverse path. The same discipline
governs the sibling upstream protocols `STATE_REQUEST` (21) and multi-hop `ATTENTION`
(34); §"Unified termination" below states the one rule they share.

##### Data shapes

```kotlin
// A resolved dataflow edge (post-flatten). Full-ref per I-2; Link identity per G-12.
data class EdgeId(val from: PortRef, val to: PortRef)   // local dedup key only

// One traversal, minted by the initiator per recomputation (reuses the clock shape).
data class FrontierEpoch(val initiator: CellRef, val counter: Long)

// Upstream query — push-only, null-context, rides FRONTIER lane.
data class DescribeFrontier(
    val epoch: FrontierEpoch,
    val visited: PersistentSet<EdgeId>,   // edges already expanded on this path
)

// Downstream report — pushed back down the path the query came up.
enum class FrontierKind { TERMINAL, TRANSPARENT, CYCLIC, OPAQUE }
data class FrontierReport(
    val epoch: FrontierEpoch,
    val edge: EdgeId,                      // the RECEIVING cell's own inlet edge (re-based)
    val sources: Set<SourceId>,            // wave sources reaching via this edge
    val kind: FrontierKind,
)
```
