### I-26 — When is link time? Cold-phase structure, eager cells (C-7), and what exists on an unactivated port

> Member pairs: N2×N6, N3×N6
> Existing gaps touched: C-7, G-13 · Confidence: high
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 1/2 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The normative layered-port model: the admission-vs-activation split as stated rules (15 rules 1–3 are still absolutes that C-7 contradicts in prose), the port-layer phase table, the admitted-but-unactivated parked-tail rule (no parking window exists between…

#### 1. Challenge restatement

The single mechanism question: **where does "link time" fall relative to the
cell lifecycle phases, and which portion of a port exists in each phase?**

The spec asserts, in three places that were written independently, facts that
only cohere if this question is answered:

- Cardinality, ownership exclusivity, and policies are enforced *"at link time,
  not send time"* (10/12 §Cardinality rule 1; 10/13 §Policies) — but "link
  time" is never located on the COLD → HOT → SUSPENDED timeline.
- The **cold phase** *"forbids port traffic"* yet *"composition operators on a
  cold cell build graph structure"* (10/15 §Cold phase; §Hot phase), and
  **eager cells** (C-7) *"accept subscriptions unhosted"* — so something
  link-shaped happens before activation.
- Lifecycle **rule 2** requires hosts to *"enumerate ports by name without
  running cell logic"* (10/15 §Normative rules), and **rule 3** says
  *"hosting-specific operations require HOT"* — but the handshake (`onLink`
  veto, `serve`/`delegate`) is cell code, and G-13's *"composable sub-port
  handlers may not exist until activation"* (10/12 §Multiplexed ports), leaving
  the behavior of generic protocols (state-request, attention, frontier
  discovery) against a cold or suspended cell **unspecified**.

**Member pairs**:
- **N2 × N6** [TENSION]: cold forbids traffic, yet cold cells build structure
  and eager cells subscribe unhosted, while cardinality is only defined "at
  link time" — the position of link time on the lifecycle is nowhere stated.
- **N3 × N6** [TENSION]: rule 2 wants ports enumerated without running logic,
  but ProtocolId-keyed sub-port handlers may not exist until activation, and
  generic protocols against a cold/suspended cell have no defined behavior.

**Why the spec leaves it open**: "link time" was treated as a single instant,
but a port is not a single thing. G-17 already made *ports themselves* eager
(name registers at construction) while `onActivate` establishes the *served
implementation* — so the port's name/descriptor and its handler come into
existence in **different phases**, and no text says which parts the handshake
needs. C-7 patched this for a hand-picked list of cells ("eager cells") as an
*exception*; the challenge asks for the *rule*.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **Normative rule 1 (no logic in constructors) vs eager cells.** Rule 1 says
  all behavior establishment belongs in `onActivate` so a cold cell is safe to
  create on a machine that will never run it (10/15 rule 1; mobility 30/33). But
  C-7 blesses cells that `serve` in `init`. A single "link time" cannot be both
  strictly-HOT (rule 3) and available-cold (eager) without decomposition.
- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path) vs a pre-activation window.** If a link may be
  admitted before its target is HOT, inbound traffic has nowhere to dispatch
  yet. Any buffering here must reuse an existing primitive or it becomes a new
  mailbox — and P1/P3 reject hidden mailboxes.
- **P5 (correctness by construction) vs "at link time" ambiguity.** Cardinality
  and the SPSC/`Owned` exclusive bit (20/23) are enforced at link time (10/12).
  If "link time" is undefined, so is *when* these become binding — yet they are
  supposed to be structural guarantees, not runtime discipline.
- **Decided drain invariant / one Buffering primitive** (30/33) — a resolution
  must not introduce a *second* parking mechanism; suspension is already "one
  Buffering primitive at two granularities."
- **I-1 metadata plane vs cold cells.** I-1 made generic protocols a bounded,
  bypass-parking metadata plane whose *handlers* live in `ProtocolSupport`.
  Those handlers are behavioral (installed at activation), but their
  *capabilities* are descriptor metadata. Cold/suspended-cell protocol behavior
  sits exactly on that structural/behavioral seam.
- **P8 / P6.** Links must be able to form and re-form live (promotion,
  replication-mesh formation, drain-resume relink) without a global "activate
  everything, then link" barrier, and nothing may park "just in case."

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Link time is strictly HOT (both endpoints must be activated)

*Semantics*: no `Link` may be installed against a cold cell. Cold DSL
composition is pure description; links exist only once both endpoints are
spawned and `onActivate`'d.

*Fast-path cost*: none new; no pre-activation window.

*Failure modes*: contradicts C-7 (eager cells linking unhosted); forbids
admitting a link before a target activates, which replication-mesh formation
(42) and drain-resume relink (30/33 step 6 relinks *and* activates) both need;
forces a global activation-before-link ordering that fights P8 and cannot
pre-validate topology structurally. Rejected — it erases the eager-cell
capability C-7 deliberately kept.

##### Candidate B — Structural admission decoupled from behavioral activation; traffic parks between them (recommended)

*Semantics*: "link time" splits into **admission** (validate + install the
`Link` — reads only the port's structural metadata: descriptor, cardinality,
ownership bit, policies) and **activation** (the handler exists and traffic
dispatches). Admission is phase-independent; activation is the cell's
*handler-establishment time* (`onActivate` for hosted cells, construction for
eager cells). Inbound traffic arriving after admission but before activation
**parks in the same Buffering primitive suspension uses** and replays on
activation. An eager cell is simply one whose handler-establishment time is
construction — a **zero-length** parking window.

*Fast-path cost*: none. Admission is a rare op (P2 budgets linking as
arbitrarily expensive); the hot dispatch path is untouched; the parking window
reuses the shipped primitive.

*Failure modes*: introduces a defined "admitted-but-not-activated" state and
must say what a *stateful* `onLink` veto does before HOT (answer: defer on the
management plane, §4); generic-protocol delivery before handler install must be
made safe (answer: I-1 idempotence → drop-safe, §4).

*Tradeoffs*: turns C-7 from an exception into a rule; unifies the pre-activation
window with suspension parking (a third use of one primitive, not a new one);
keeps every structural guarantee binding from construction. Recommended.

##### Candidate C — Everything-cold: abolish the handler phase (all cells eager)

*Semantics*: require `serve`/`delegate` in the constructor; ports fully live at
construction; drop the COLD/HOT handler distinction.

*Fast-path cost*: none.

*Failure modes*: violates rule 1 (logic in constructors); breaks mobility (a
cold cell must be safe to construct on a host that never runs it, and must not
assume host context); makes `onActivate`'s host-execution-context guarantee
meaningless. Rejected.

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. The unifying statement:

> A port is a **layered artifact**. Its *structural* layers (name, descriptor,
> policy) exist from construction and are immutable; its *behavioral* layer
> (the served handler and protocol sub-handlers) is established at the cell's
> **handler-establishment time**. "Link time" decomposes into **admission**
> (structural, phase-independent) and **activation** (behavioral, gated on
> handler-establishment). Traffic between admission and activation parks in the
> one Buffering primitive suspension already uses. An **eager cell** is a cell
> whose handler-establishment time is *construction* — the parking window is
> zero-length — and that is the rule C-7 was reaching for.

##### The port's layers — what exists in each phase (data shape)

Each `Port` in the per-instance `PortRegistry` (I-2) is:

```
Port {
  name: PortName                       // registry key
  descriptor: PortDescriptor {         // STRUCTURAL — KSP/declaration-derived, immutable, cold-present
     contractId, direction,
     cardinality: FanIn | FanOut | OneToOne,
     exclusiveBit: Bool,               // Owned/Leased (20/23)
     protocolCapabilities: Set<ProtocolId>   // I-1 metadata-plane declared support
  }
  policies: List<LinkPolicy>           // STRUCTURAL — attached at declaration, incl. identity slot
  onLink/onUnlink: hook                // membrane veto (may be structural-only or stateful — see rule 4)
  handler: Served | Delegated | ABSENT // BEHAVIORAL — installed at handler-establishment time
  protocolHandlers: ProtocolSupport    // BEHAVIORAL — installed with the handler
}
```

Which portion exists in each phase (the deliverable the challenge asks for):

| Port sub-part | COLD (constructed) | at ACTIVATION | HOT | SUSPENDED |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| name (registry key) | present | present | present | present |
| descriptor (contract, dir, cardinality, exclusive bit, protocol caps) | present | present | present | present |
| policy set (+ identity slot) | present | present | present | present |
| `onLink` (structural-only) | callable | callable | callable | callable |
| `onLink` (stateful veto) | deferred | becomes callable | callable | callable (mgmt inlet open) |
| handler (serve/delegate) | absent¹ | being installed | present | present, **not dispatching** |
| protocol sub-handlers | absent¹ | being installed | present | bypass-delivered or dropped |
| data-traffic dispatch | **parks** | replay parked → dispatch | dispatch | **parks** |

¹ *Except eager cells: handler and protocol sub-handlers are present at COLD.*

##### Rules the model introduces (normative)

1. **Admission is structural and phase-independent.** The handshake's binding
   checks — declarative `LinkPolicy` predicates, cardinality budget, the
   ownership `exclusiveBit`, contract compatibility `(portName, contractId)`
   (I-2), and `Link.protocolCapabilities` = intersection of both ports'
   declared sets (I-1) — read **only** the structural layers. They therefore
   run in any phase and are binding from construction. This is the precise
   meaning of 10/12's "cardinality enforced at link time": link time is
   **admission time**, and admission needs only the descriptor. The
   ownership exclusive funnel at `FanOutlet.subscribe` (M5.6) is a structural
   check and fires cold too.

2. **Activation is behavioral and per-cell.** Data traffic dispatches only into
   an installed handler. A link admitted against a target whose handler is not
   yet installed is **live topology with a parked tail**: inbound invocations
   park in the Buffering primitive (30/33), in order, with their contexts, and
   replay on activation *before* any post-activation send lands — the same
   accepted-before / delivered-before FIFO discipline the drain protocol uses.
   A cold-admitted-but-unactivated cell is, to the message path, identical to a
   suspended cell.

3. **Handler-establishment time is a declared per-cell property.**
   - *Hosted cell* (default): handler-establishment = `onActivate` (HOT). The
     parking window is the spawn→activate interval (near-atomic on the host
     thread, but defined).
   - *Eager cell* (the C-7 rule): handler-establishment = **construction**;
     `serve`/`delegate` run in `init`; the parking window is zero-length; the
     cell may carry traffic unhosted. An eager cell MUST (per C-7) be pure,
     allocation-free serving, MUST NOT assume host context, and MUST tolerate
     `onActivate` never being called. This is a *declared capability* (an
     `Eager` marker the host/KSP can check), not an ad-hoc exception; default
     guidance stays `onActivate`.

4. **The `onLink` behavioral veto follows the handler clock.** A *structural-only*
   `onLink` (the default; consults only descriptor/policy metadata) completes at
   admission in any phase. A *stateful* `onLink` (consults the cell's hot state)
   requires HOT: an admission request to such a port on a not-yet-hot cell is a
   **management-plane** operation (linking is management-class, I-1) that
   **defers** on the always-open management inlet (30/33) and replays its
   handshake at activation, surfacing `Connected`/`Rejected` then — exactly the
   `LinkResult.Deferred` contract already used cross-host (10/13). Whether an
   `onLink` is structural or stateful is a per-port declaration.

5. **Generic-protocol capability is structural; protocol delivery follows the
   handler clock and is drop-safe before it.** `Link.protocolCapabilities` is
   negotiated at admission from descriptor metadata — available cold, no handler
   needed. But protocol *handlers* (`ProtocolSupport` sub-channels) are
   behavioral, installed with the data handler. A generic protocol arriving at a
   cell whose protocol handler is not yet installed is **dropped**, not parked
   (I-1 rule 2: protocols bypass data-path parking to avoid deadlocking
   catch-up). This is safe **because I-1 rule 3 already mandates every generic
   protocol be idempotent and reorder/duplicate-tolerant**: attention
   re-propagates, a suspension-resume notice replays as late-join catch-up
   (20/21), a state-request is re-issued. Thus "generic protocols against a
   cold/suspended cell" has a defined, safe behavior: *capability negotiation
   succeeds structurally; delivery before handler install drops and the
   protocol's own idempotence covers it.*

6. **Cold DSL composition is deferred admission, not live linking.** The
   `map`/`connect` operators on a cold cell (10/15) record a serializable
   `GraphSpec` (G-30) — a batch of **proposed** links. Proposed links MAY be
   structurally pre-validated cold (descriptors are known, so cardinality/
   ownership/contract mismatches can fail fast at build time), but the
   **binding** admission (`onLink`, the retained `Link` in `port.linking.links`,
   the exclusive funnel) executes when the `GraphSpec` replays onto a host at
   spawn. "Composition builds graph structure" = it builds the *proposed-link
   description*; it is not traffic and does not require a handler — fully
   consistent with "cold forbids port traffic."

##### How each member-pair tension dissolves

- **N2 × N6**: "cold forbids traffic" = no *dispatch* (no handler yet), while
  "cold builds structure" = admission/GraphSpec, and "eager cells subscribe
  unhosted" = zero-length window (rule 3). "Cardinality at link time" = at
  admission, structural, binding from construction (rule 1). All three coexist.
- **N3 × N6**: rule 2 ("enumerate without running logic") is *reinforced* —
  name/descriptor/policy are exactly the structural layers, no logic (rule 1);
  protocol capabilities are descriptor metadata, also enumerable cold (rule 5).
  Generic protocols against cold/suspended cells get the defined drop-safe
  behavior (rule 5). Rule 3 ("hosting ops require HOT") is refined: *traffic
  dispatch* requires HOT; *admission* does not.

##### Net effect

"Link time" is no longer a single instant that must be simultaneously cold and
hot. It is admission (structural, phase-independent, binding from construction)
plus activation (behavioral, per-cell handler-establishment time), with the one
Buffering primitive bridging them. Eager cells are the zero-window case, now a
rule. Every structural guarantee (cardinality, ownership, policy, contract,
protocol capability) is binding the moment the constructor returns; every
behavioral concern (dispatch, protocol handlers, stateful veto) follows the
handler clock; and nothing new is added to the steady-state fast path.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — admission = install a `Link`; activation = install a handler; the window = the existing Buffering primitive. All reduce to link/handler manipulation, meaningful single-threaded. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — admission is a rare op (P2 budgets linking as arbitrarily expensive); hot dispatch is untouched; parking reuses shipped machinery. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — admission records explicit `Link` objects; proposed links are a serializable `GraphSpec`; no hidden mailbox — the parking window is the same inspectable Buffering used for suspension. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — handler-establishment is per cell; parking is local; no global activate-then-link barrier. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — the port's structural/behavioral split is type-level; descriptor/cardinality/ownership/protocol-caps are KSP-generated and binding from construction; eager is a declared marker. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — the parking window exists only when a link (interest) exists; eager is opt-in; nothing parks "just in case" (bound is a follow-on gap). |
| P7 Open / local-first | **Untouched** — no bearing on boundary controls. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — links admit/activate independently; promotion re-admission and drain-resume relink fit; nothing assumes a static or fully-activated graph. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `GraphSpec`/proposed links and `PortDescriptor` are ids-only serializable; no lambdas/handles introduced. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — unifying the pre-activation window with suspend/resume parking directly serves the long-lived, incremental, suspend-heavy niche. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **One Buffering primitive at two granularities (30/33, 10/14)** — Consistent,
  extended: the pre-activation window is a **third use of the same primitive**
  (port suspension, location parking, now admission→activation). No new mailbox.
- **Suspension = TrafficLight (ports) + LocationRegistry parking (location)** —
  Consistent: a cold-admitted-unactivated cell is the suspended case; resume =
  activation clock catching up.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO end-to-end (30/33)** — Consistent:
  parked-then-replay-before-new-sends is exactly the drain discipline; resume
  (step 6) already relinks-then-activates.
- **Cardinality enforced at link time, not send time (10/12, 20/23)** —
  Consistent, **refined wording**: "link time" = "structural admission time,"
  available from construction, binding at install. Still not send-time; the
  intent is preserved and sharpened. Flagged as a refinement, not a CONFLICT.
- **Owned crossing = move-by-serialize; Leased not crossing machines (20/23)** —
  Consistent: the `exclusiveBit` is descriptor metadata; the `FanOutlet.subscribe`
  exclusive funnel is a structural check that fires at admission (cold for eager
  cells too). Unchanged.
- **Management null context; management may return (10/12, 20/22)** —
  Consistent: admission (`connect`) is management-class, so a stateful-`onLink`
  admission to a cold cell defers on the always-open management inlet (rule 4).
- **I-1 metadata plane (link = data unit; protocols = bounded metadata plane,
  bypass parking, idempotent)** — Directly built upon: protocol capabilities are
  structural (descriptor, cold-present); handlers are behavioral; delivery before
  install drops safely precisely because I-1 rule 3 requires idempotence. No
  contradiction; this closes I-1's "protocols against cold/suspended cells."
- **I-2 full-ref addressing; per-instance PortRegistry** — Consistent: admission
  and activation are per instance-port; migration/RESTART preserve `instanceId`
  (handler travels with the whole cell object); promotion re-admits on the
  candidate. All per full ref.
- **G-17 port discovery (eager port registration)** — Consistent and
  generalized: G-17 made *name* eager; this makes the whole *structural layer*
  (descriptor + policy) eager, which is what rule 2 already needs. Stays resolved.
- **G-16 onDeactivate / drain captures state after flush** — Consistent:
  deactivation is the inverse handler clock; parked traffic already flushed.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent: state-request answered by ordinary
  state-as-delta once the handler is up; no snapshot type.
- **CellRef(logicalId, incarnation); links bind full refs (I-2)** — Consistent:
  admission binds full `PortRef`s; no new identity.
- **Gaps/conflicts Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — C-7 is *upgraded* from a
  documented exception to a normative rule (an elaboration, not a reopening);
  G-17/G-16 untouched.

No CONFLICT flag required. The single wording refinement ("link time" =
"admission time") sharpens 10/12 rule 1 without changing its intent.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **10/15 §Cold phase / §Hot phase / §Normative rules** — add the port-layer
  table (§4) and the admission-vs-activation split; restate rule 2 as "the
  *structural* layers (name, descriptor, policy) are discoverable without
  running logic"; restate rule 3 as "*data-traffic dispatch* requires HOT;
  *admission* does not"; define the admitted-but-unactivated state and its
  parking (reusing 30/33).
- **10/15 §⚠ CONFLICT (C-7)** — rewrite as a normative rule: **handler-
  establishment time** is a declared per-cell property; `onActivate` (hosted)
  vs construction (eager); the `Eager` marker and its obligations; zero-length
  window. Move C-7 in 90/91 from "conflict/resolution" to "resolved rule."
- **10/12 §Cardinality (rule 1)** — refine "at link time" → "at structural
  admission (available from construction, binding at link install)."
- **10/13 §Explicit (handshake-based) / §Link lifecycle** — split admission
  (structural, phase-independent) from activation; specify the structural-only
  vs stateful `onLink` distinction and the management-plane deferral of a
  stateful veto to a not-yet-hot cell; add the "parked tail until activation"
  invariant; note `GraphSpec` connect steps are deferred admissions.
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports (G-13) / I-1 plane** — state that
  `protocolCapabilities` are descriptor metadata (cold-present, negotiated at
  admission) while protocol handlers follow the handler clock, and that delivery
  before handler install drops safely under I-1's idempotence rule.
- **30/33 §Port-level buffering** — note the pre-activation window as a third
  use of the one Buffering primitive; frame resume as the activation clock
  catching up to preserved links.
- **50/51 (GraphSpec, G-30)** — connect steps are deferred admissions replayed
  at deployment; optional cold structural pre-validation.
- **90/91** — C-7 upgraded to a rule; add a note that G-13's "protocols against
  cold/suspended cells" is resolved via idempotent drop.

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Stateful-`onLink` classification & deferred-admission semantics** — a
  per-port declaration (or marker) distinguishing structural-only from stateful
  `onLink`; the exact defer/replay/result-surfacing of a management-plane
  admission request to a not-yet-hot cell, and its interaction with the
  cross-host `LinkResult.Deferred` path.
- **`Eager` marker & KSP verification** — a declared capability the compiler/
  host checks (handler established in constructor, pure, allocation-free,
  host-context-free); how unhosted-linking permission is derived from it; what
  the host does if a non-eager cell is linked before spawn.
- **Pre-activation parking bound & interest timeout** — how much inbound traffic
  may park before a target activates, backpressure, and disposition if
  activation never comes (ties to overflow mailbox G-25 and P6 interest-driven
  reclamation).
- **Protocol-drop observability** — dropping a generic protocol against a
  not-yet-hot cell is safe by idempotence but currently silent; whether a
  dropped state-request/attention should be counted, re-driven, or logged, and
  its interaction with single-hop notices (M6).
- **Cold structural pre-validation of `GraphSpec`** — whether cold composition
  eagerly runs cardinality/ownership/contract checks to fail fast at build time
  vs deferring all checks to replay, and how a structurally-invalid `GraphSpec`
  surfaces its error.
- **Admission-before-activation across the wire** — a cross-host link admitted
  (`Deferred`) whose target host has not activated the cell: how the deferred
  handshake result and the pre-activation parking compose with registry
  park/replay (40/41).

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: high.** The resolution classifies behavior that already exists
rather than inventing kernel machinery: G-17 already makes ports eager and
`onActivate` already establishes handlers separately, so the structural/
behavioral split is descriptive; the parking window reuses the shipped Buffering
primitive (30/33) verbatim; the generic-protocol drop-safety is a direct
consequence of I-1's already-decided idempotence rule; and eager cells are the
existing C-7 list, now given a name and obligations. The single moving part —
declaring *handler-establishment time* as a per-cell property with `onActivate`
and construction as its two values — is a small, low-risk addition.

**Open questions**: (1) whether stateful-`onLink` deferral should replay the
whole handshake at activation or is better forbidden outright (require all
`onLink` vetoes to be structural), which would simplify the model at the cost of
membrane expressiveness; (2) whether cold `GraphSpec` composition should
eagerly structurally-validate (fail-fast at build) or stay fully deferred; (3)
the exact backpressure/bound on the pre-activation parking window, deferred to a
follow-on gap because it shares machinery with overflow durability (G-25).

### I-27 — State migration across instances: exportState/importState choreography in the swap drain window (G-33)

> Member pairs: N5×N27, N6×N27, N8×N27, N9×N27, N16×N27, N17×N27, N20×N27, N24×N27
> Existing gaps touched: G-33, G-25 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 8/8 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The contract around the choreography: R3's invariance line + PRECHECK (methodId-superset, merge-semantics equality; 'contract change is not a promotion'), PriorState with schemaVersion, R6 source continuity (candidate adopting OutletWaveState — today downst…
> ⚠ Divergence with landed code: Fallback soundness: current 53 §G-33 presents catch-up fallback as universally available ('cells that don't declare it fall back to upstream catch-up replay'), and the landed fallback is silent — the candidate emits under its own fresh sourceId with no supe…
> Reconciled after cross-check: R6 tier split ratified as the normative guard across the cluster (T0/T1 = preserved epoch; T2 = announced fresh epoch).

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question.** `50/53 §G-33` ships the state-transfer half of
promotion in three sentences: `StateMigrating.importFrom(prior)` on the candidate
consumes the incumbent's `Stateful.snapshot()` *"inside the swap's buffered window
(`Promotion.promote`: red → transfer → relink → green)"*, and cells that don't declare
it *"fall back to upstream catch-up replay — the relink fires `onLinked`, so data cells
re-sync through the ordinary late-join path (21)."* That fixes the *primitive* but leaves
the *composed semantics* open on every side. A resolution must define, under **one**
state-transform contract, all of:

- **Lifecycle ordering (N6×N27)** — where `exportState`/`importState` sit relative to
  `onDeactivate` snapshot capture on incumbent A (`30/33 §The drain protocol` step 3)
  and `onActivate` on candidate B, given that *"re-activation of an already hot cell is
  an error the host rejects"* (`10/15 §Activation`, `§Normative rules 4`).
- **Parked invocations vs an evolved contract (N5×N27, N20×N27)** — parked
  `HostedPortInvocation`s carry `contractId`/`methodId` hashes minted against A's
  contract (`10/14 §Dispatch tiers`; wire is ids-only, `40/41`); replaying them into a B
  *"whose contract evolved — the very case evolution exists for"* has no specified
  semantics (`50/53 §Mechanical decomposition`).
- **Continuation vs re-baseline (N8×N27, N9×N27)** — whether B's outlet continues A's
  delta stream as a deterministic `state × delta → state` continuation for downstream
  (`20/21 §Incremental vs complete`), or downstream must re-baseline through the
  **unwaved** catch-up fallback (`20/21 §Pull`), and how that catch-up orders against the
  swap's replayed buffer (`buffer inlets → relink → replay`, `30/33`).
- **Partitioned unit (N16×N27)** — for a `PartitionedCell` composite whose organelles may
  span hosts (`20/24 §Partitioned state`), what the swap membrane and the export/import
  unit is: whole composite vs per key range.
- **Rollback vs the unbuilt journal (N17×N27)** — 53's rollback row depends on *"journaled
  invocations replay"* (`50/53 §Mechanical decomposition`) and the export/import runs in
  the same drain window that captures G-25 snapshots (`20/24 §Durability spectrum`), but
  the journal is unbuilt.
- **Divergent-schema gossip (N24×N27)** — 53 reuses *"replicated spawn, distinct
  incarnations"* to run candidates side by side, but 42's convergence *"assumes replicas
  share the cell's declared merge semantics"* (`40/42 §What replication must mean here`).

**Why the spec leaves it open.** `50/53 §G-33` is a primitive without a composition
theory; `91 §G-33` records it "Resolved (M9.4)" at exactly that sketch depth. Every
surface it touches — the drain protocol, the ids-only wire, the delta algebra, catch-up,
partitioning, durability, replication — was written before a cross-instance state
transform existed. Four adopted resolutions supply the substrate this challenge assembles
into a state contract:
- **I-11** owns the *link/transaction half* (PRECHECK → PREPARE → COMMIT → RETIRE +
  ROLLBACK; retained-incumbent; non-vetoing commit; wave-domain invisibility) and
  **explicitly delegates the state detail here** — it carries an `OutletWaveState`
  *"migrated as part of `Stateful.snapshot()` / `StateMigrating.importFrom` (G-33)"* but
  does not define the transform.
- **I-2** fixes identity: full-ref addressing; port-sameness is structural `(portName,
  contractId)`; an instance is one live realization; G-33 transfer is instance→instance.
- **I-7** fixes durability: one snapshot serves recovery; `Stateful.snapshot()` is the
  checkpoint; "replay = recovery" reuses catch-up.
- **I-3** fixes replication: the `Replicable` merge-idempotence gate; candidates vs
  replicas; gossip only among identical merge semantics.

I-27 is the *state-transform contract* that ties these together — the export/import half
of the swap I-11 left as a stub.

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P8 (everything evolves) vs P9 (stable wire forms) vs P5 (correctness by
  construction).** Evolution's whole point is that representations change, yet the wire
  addresses methods by a fixed FNV-1a hash of `FQN#name + signature` (`10/14 §Reflection
  budget`), and parked invocations already carry those hashes. A naive "transform
  everything, including in-flight invocations" reintroduces per-version invocation
  rewriting on the wire — exactly what ids-only stability forbids.
- **"A snapshot IS a delta" (recorded) vs a divergent private representation.** The
  interchange between A's and B's private state must be schema-neutral, but the recorded
  decision forbids a separate snapshot type — the transform's middle must be the ordinary
  delta form.
- **G-20 per-source waves vs a mid-stream source change.** A promotion hands downstream a
  new emitting outlet. If B mints a fresh `sourceId`, a glitch-free consumer could strand
  a wave waiting for an A-contribution that never comes; if B *continues* A's counter, we
  are asserting single-active-instance continuity that G-20's "minted per emitting outlet"
  does not literally grant. The catch-up fallback is **unwaved** (`20/21 §Pull`), so its
  interaction with the glitch-free frontier is unevaluated.
- **Exactly-once / non-idempotent merge (`20/23`, `20/24`) vs re-baseline.** A `CounterCell`
  merge is addition — not idempotent. A catch-up re-baseline that serves "current total
  from empty" under a *new* source identity double-counts against A's already-delivered
  total. So "just fall back to catch-up" is not universally sound; the fallback's validity
  is cell-class-dependent.
- **P4 (no global barrier) vs a partitioned composite.** A whole-composite atomic swap
  across host-spanning organelles is a distributed transaction — the barrier P4 and G-20
  forbid.
- **10/15 activation guard.** `onActivate` idempotence is enforced by the host rejecting
  re-activation; B is already hot as a judged shadow, so the transform must *not* be
  expressed as (re-)activation, and A must not deactivate before rollback is impossible.
- **The rollback row cites an unbuilt journal (`50/53`, G-25).** Rollback semantics cannot
  depend on machinery that does not exist.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Bidirectional schema converter (transform state *and* in-flight invocations)

A declared `vOld ↔ vNew` converter translates both the snapshot **and** parked
invocations: parked `HostedPortInvocation`s against A's contract are rewritten to B's
method ids before replay; the snapshot is converted field-by-field.

- *Semantics*: promotion may change any contract; a converter bridges the gap.
- *Fast-path cost*: none in steady state (rare-path), but every parked invocation pays a
  rewrite on the commit path.
- *Failure modes*: invocation rewriting is exactly the ids-are-unstable hazard `40/41`
  bans — a converter keyed on FNV-1a hashes is brittle and non-serializable across builds;
  a converter is a lambda/handle-shaped artifact (P9 tension); it silently turns a swap
  into a general schema-migration engine, contradicting I-11's structural `(portName,
  contractId)` invariance; and it has no answer for divergent *merge semantics* (a
  converter can rewrite a delta but not make an addition idempotent).
- *Tradeoffs*: maximally general, but re-opens settled wire and identity decisions.
  **Rejected** — the generality is unneeded (see Candidate B's invariance line).

##### Candidate B — State-only transform under contract invariance, delta as the interchange *(recommended)*

The swap holds the **port contracts invariant** (I-11 PRECHECK); the *only* thing a
promotion may evolve is **private state representation and cell logic**. `exportState =
Stateful.snapshot()` and `importState = StateMigrating.importFrom(prior)` are the two
halves of a transform whose **middle is the invariant delta contract** ("a snapshot IS a
delta"). Parked invocations carry contract-*interface* ids (shared across
implementations), so PRECHECK guarantees they resolve into B unchanged. Continuation vs
re-baseline is a declared, cell-class-constrained choice; partitioned promotion is
per-organelle; rollback reuses the retained-incumbent snapshot; candidates never gossip.

- *Semantics*: state reconstruction across representations with contracts pinned; every
  member pair falls out of one invariance rule + a three-tier handoff.
- *Fast-path cost*: zero in steady state; the transform, buffered window, and any catch-up
  are rare-path (P2), reusing shipped `Stateful`/`onLinked`/`Buffering`.
- *Failure modes*: a promotion that *must* change a port contract or merge semantics is
  refused as "not a promotion" and pushed to ordinary topology surgery (adapter cell / new
  logical cell) — a deliberate scope cut, not a defect. The unwaved-catch-up glitch case
  and non-idempotent re-baseline are handled by constraining which cells may use the
  fallback.
- *Tradeoffs*: gives up contract-changing promotions in exchange for a transform that
  never touches the wire ids, never needs invocation rewriting, and composes with I-2/I-7/
  I-3/I-11 without contradiction. **Recommended.**

##### Candidate C — Always re-baseline via catch-up (drop the transform)

Abolish `StateMigrating`; every promotion re-baselines downstream through `onLinked`
catch-up; B always starts from its own shadow state.

- *Semantics*: one path — relink fires catch-up, downstream re-syncs.
- *Fast-path cost*: rare-path only.
- *Failure modes*: loses deterministic `state × delta` continuation (`20/21`); the unwaved
  catch-up under a **fresh** `sourceId` double-counts for non-idempotent cells
  (`CounterCell`, `20/24`) and strands glitch-free waves (G-20); cannot handle a cell whose
  recoverable state is *not* reconstructible from its own emitted deltas (hidden internal
  state); forces every stateful promotion through a re-baseline the niche's long-lived
  incremental cells specifically want to avoid.
- *Tradeoffs*: simplest, but wrong for exactly the stateful, incremental, glitch-free cells
  P10 optimizes for. **Rejected as the sole path; retained as the bounded fallback tier in
  Candidate B.**

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate B**. The state-transform contract is: **`exportState`/`importState` are
the two halves of a state transform whose interchange is the invariant delta contract; a
promotion swap holds the port contracts (and their merge semantics) invariant, evolving
only private representation and cell logic.** It is pure orchestration over shipped
primitives (`Stateful.snapshot/restore`, `StateMigrating.importFrom`, `onLinked` catch-up,
`Buffering` replay) — no new kernel mechanism, honoring 50/53's own guardrail.

##### Actors (from I-11)

Incumbent **A** (`rA`, active), candidate **B** (`rB`, a judged live shadow, `52`/G-32).
I-11 owns the transaction; I-27 owns steps 2–3 below (the state handoff) and the ordering
of catch-up and replay.

##### Data shapes (orchestration; no kernel change)

```
// exportState — SHIPPED as Stateful (30/33, 20/24). State-as-delta-from-empty,
// expressed in the INVARIANT outlet delta contract — the schema-neutral interchange.
interface Stateful { fun snapshot(): Delta; fun restore(d: Delta) }

// importState — SHIPPED as StateMigrating (50/53), given a version-aware payload.
interface StateMigrating { fun importFrom(prior: PriorState) }

data class PriorState(
    val snapshot: Delta,                          // predecessor state-as-delta (invariant contract)
    val schemaVersion: Int,                       // predecessor snapshot schema tag (P9 version discipline)
    val outletWaves: Map<PortName, OutletWaveState>,   // I-11 source-identity continuity
)
data class OutletWaveState(val sourceId: UUID, val highWater: Long)   // I-11
```

##### The invariance line (R3) — the load-bearing rule

A promotion swap **holds the port contracts invariant**: the inbound command contract
(`contractId` + the full `methodId` set that could be in flight), the outbound delta
`contractId`, **and the delta's declared merge semantics**. What a promotion MAY evolve:
private state representation, cell logic, and the *snapshot schema*. This strengthens
I-11's structural `(portName, contractId)` PRECHECK to require B's rebindable ports to be
a **methodId-superset** of A's, and merge-semantics equality on any replicated outlet.
A change to a port contract or its merge semantics is **not a promotion** — it is ordinary
topology surgery (insert an adapter cell, or spawn a new logical cell), itself possibly a
shadow-judged evolution of the adapter. This is the clean line P8 needs: *everything can
change at runtime, but the atomic instance-swap changes representation, not contracts.*

Because `contractId = hash(FQN)` and `methodId = hash(FQN#name + signature)` are keyed on
the **shared contract interface**, not the implementation (`10/14 §Reflection budget`),
two implementations of `SetOps` carry *identical* ids; an **additive** contract evolution
(new method, new interface member) keeps every existing methodId resolvable and passes the
superset check; only a **breaking** method change diverges the ids and is refused at
PRECHECK. This is the direct answer to N5×N27/N20×N27 (below).

##### Drain-window choreography (refining I-11 PREPARE→COMMIT→RETIRE)

```
PREPARE (red):
  1. membrane buffers inbound (Buffering, 30/33); in-flight inbound parks in order.
  2. A drains its accepted queue and FLUSHES all rA-sourced waves downstream (30/33 step 2).
     After this no rA wave is in flight — the handoff straddles no wave.
  3. A QUIESCES HOT — it does NOT deactivate.  (R1)

COMMIT (state handoff + relink; non-vetoing):
  4. exportState:  prior = PriorState(A.snapshot(), A.schemaVersion, A.outletWaves)   // pure read (R1)
  5. importState:  one of three tiers (R4), on the ALREADY-HOT B — never onActivate (R2):
        T0  shared snapshot schema  →  B.restore(prior.snapshot)      (identical to migration)
        T1  divergent schema, StateMigrating declared  →  B.importFrom(prior)   (transform)
        T2  neither  →  discard prior; B keeps its shadow state; downstream re-baselines (R6)
     T0/T1 additionally: B ADOPTS prior.outletWaves (sourceId + highWater) — source continuity.
  6. relink outlets then inlets (I-11); onLinked fires per relinked downstream link → catch-up (R7).
  7. green: replay buffered inbound to B; live deltas follow (per-link FIFO after catch-up); delegate/flatten.

RETIRE:
  8. despawn(rA) → onDeactivate(A) runs NOW (10/15).  A's prior.snapshot is retained as the
     rollback checkpoint until a retention horizon (R9).
```

##### Rules the model introduces (normative)

- **R1 — exportState is a pure read, decoupled from deactivation.** `snapshot()` is taken
  at a quiescent inter-invocation boundary (the host is single-consumer, so the window IS
  a clean boundary); it does **not** require or imply `onDeactivate`. In *migration* the
  two coincide (`30/33` step 3) because the instance leaves; in *promotion* the incumbent
  is **retained hot** (I-11) and deactivates only at RETIRE. This dissolves the "ordering
  against onDeactivate" half of N6×N27: export sits *before* deactivation, always.

- **R2 — importState is not activation.** `importFrom`/`restore` runs on the already-hot
  candidate (activated once, at shadow spawn). The host's "re-activation of a hot cell is
  an error" guard (`10/15`, G-16) is **never triggered** because promotion never
  re-activates B and never re-activates A. This dissolves the "ordering against onActivate"
  half of N6×N27: the export/import pair sits strictly *between* the two lifecycle events
  and touches neither.

- **R3 — Contract invariance (above).** The swap holds port contracts + merge semantics
  invariant; evolution changes representation/logic/snapshot-schema only. PRECHECK is
  methodId-superset + merge-sameness. Contract change ⇒ not a promotion ⇒ topology surgery.

- **R4 — Delta is the schema-neutral interchange; three handoff tiers.** Because
  `snapshot()` is state-as-delta-from-empty **in the invariant outlet delta contract**, it
  bridges divergent private representations. `exportState`: A-private → invariant-delta;
  `importState`: invariant-delta(+`schemaVersion`) → B-private. Tiers:
  - **T0 (restore):** B's snapshot schema equals A's ⇒ `B.restore(snapshot)` directly —
    the migration path, no `StateMigrating` needed.
  - **T1 (transform):** schemas differ (e.g. `ShadowPromotionTest`'s v1 `Long` → v2
    `string` state form) ⇒ B declares `StateMigrating.importFrom`, reads the predecessor
    `schemaVersion`, and produces B's state. This is where representation evolution lives.
  - **T2 (catch-up fallback):** B can neither restore nor transform the prior schema ⇒
    discard A's snapshot; B keeps its own shadow state; downstream re-baselines via
    `onLinked` catch-up. Bounded soundness — see R6.

- **R5 — Parked/buffered invocations replay into B unchanged.** They carry contract-
  *interface* ids (shared across implementations, R3), never implementation ids; PRECHECK's
  methodId-superset guarantees B's inlet accepts every in-flight methodId. The "replaying
  A's contract ids into an evolved B" hazard (N5×N27, N20×N27) **cannot arise**: an
  evolution that changes an inbound method id fails PRECHECK and is not a promotion. Parked
  `Owned`/`Leased` payloads retain exclusivity across the window (`30/33`; I-11) and are
  consumed exactly once on replay — the swap adds no re-delivery.

> **Reconciled** (post-consistency-check): R6's tier split is ratified as the normative
> guard across I-11/I-13/I-14/I-22 — T0/T1 = *preserved epoch* per amended I-14 Rule S1
> (drain-captured exclusive continuation, wave-invisible); T2 = *fresh epoch* that MUST
> emit the `ReBaseline` supersession notice (I-22) and is wave-observable (I-14 Rule S5).
> For non-idempotent cells that cannot meet T0/T1, the `supersede=true` retraction path
> of I-22 R5 is the sound alternative to silent double-counting.

- **R6 — Continuation class dictates the handoff tier.** T0/T1 + source continuity (B
  adopts A's `OutletWaveState`) ⇒ **deterministic `state × delta → state` continuation**:
  B continues A's wave lane (same `sourceId`, counter from `highWater`), downstream needs
  **no re-baseline**, and its glitch-free frontier is unbroken (the PREPARE flush left no
  straddling wave). T2 + a **fresh** `sourceId` ⇒ downstream re-baseline, sound **only** for
  cells whose catch-up is idempotent against existing downstream state *under a source-
  identity change*: tag-based OR-sets (`SetCell` family) and complete-value/scalar cells.
  **Cells whose merge is non-idempotent across source identity (`CounterCell`) MUST use
  T0/T1** — a T2 re-baseline under a fresh source would double-count A's already-delivered
  contribution (`20/24 §Established pattern`). This makes N8×N27 a *typed* choice, not a
  free one, and explains why G-33 offers both: transform for stateful/non-idempotent cells,
  catch-up for idempotent ones.

- **R7 — Catch-up orders before live deltas by per-link FIFO; unwaved is safe.** At COMMIT
  the `onLinked` catch-up fires on each relinked *outlet* link; the replayed *inbound*
  buffer produces live deltas that follow on those same outlet links — per-link FIFO
  (`30/31`) orders catch-up-before-live-deltas end-to-end. In T0/T1 the catch-up re-serves
  state downstream already reconstructed from A's stream, so it is a **redundant no-op
  absorbed by tag idempotence** (`20/24`); in T2 it is the actual re-baseline. The catch-up
  being **unwaved** (`20/21 §Pull`) is safe because PREPARE drained A's lane: a glitch-free
  consumer passes the unwaved baseline through, then version-buffers the continuation waves
  (T0/T1, same lane) or the fresh lane's waves (T2, new source) — no wave straddles the
  handoff. This resolves N9×N27's ordering + unwaved concern.

- **R8 — Partitioned unit is per-organelle.** For a `PartitionedCell` (`20/24`; each
  partition an ordinary cell with its own full ref, ordinary placement, possibly host-
  spanning), the swap membrane and the export/import unit are **per partition (per key
  range)**, never the whole composite. Each partition promotes independently — its own
  local, membrane-scoped swap (I-11), its own `importFrom` over its own key-range state.
  The routing-proxy inlet and merging outlet are themselves ordinary cells, promoted
  independently. **No whole-composite atomic transaction** (that would be the distributed
  barrier P4 forbids). Mixed-version partitions coexist safely by R3 (contract invariance),
  and the composite converges partition-by-partition — "partitioning must not become a
  second distribution mechanism." This resolves N16×N27.

- **R9 — Rollback needs no journal in-window; the export snapshot doubles as the
  checkpoint.** In-window rollback is I-11's retained-incumbent re-green: A never left, so
  the buffered inbound's home always exists — **no journal** (this discharges the 50/53
  rollback row's stated dependency on the unbuilt journal for the common case). The single
  `exportState` snapshot serves **two** consumers: `importFrom` (to B) and A's **retained
  rollback checkpoint** (one snapshot, no separate type — "a snapshot IS a delta").
  *Post-retire* rollback (a bad candidate found live after `despawn(rA)`) re-spawns A from
  that retained snapshot as the reverse candidate — which is exactly I-7's journal-restore
  (`Stateful.restore` + WAL suffix). Thus export/import composes with G-25 by *sharing the
  snapshot*, not by adding a second capture in the drain window. This resolves N17×N27; the
  retention horizon for the checkpoint is a follow-on gap (§8), shared with I-11.

- **R10 — Candidates never gossip; only invariant-contract replicas do.** 53's "replicated
  spawn, distinct incarnations" means **shadow coexistence**: B is fed the same live inputs
  as A via ordinary upstream fan-out with B's effectful outlets NoOp-served (`52`/G-32),
  and the judge compares *outputs* — there is **no delta gossip between A and B**. Gossip
  (`40/42`) requires identical merge semantics (I-3's `Replicable` gate); divergent-schema
  candidates fail that gate and MUST NOT be mesh-linked. Conversely, a **rolling promotion
  across a replicated logical cell** (a mesh promoted replica-by-replica) has mixed-version
  replicas gossiping — and that is safe **precisely because R3 holds the delta contract and
  its merge semantics invariant** (the evolution changed private representation, not the
  gossiped delta). This resolves N24×N27: the divergent-schema-gossip case never arises
  (candidates are shadow-fed), and the mixed-version-replica case is sound by invariance.

##### Net effect

The state-transform contract is one coherent mechanism: **`exportState`/`importState` are
the two halves of a state transform bridged by the invariant delta contract; a promotion
holds contracts and merge semantics invariant and evolves only private representation;
export is a pure read before deactivation, import runs on the hot candidate (never
re-activation); continuation vs re-baseline is a typed choice (transform + source
continuity for non-idempotent/stateful cells, catch-up fallback for idempotent ones);
partitioned promotion is per-organelle; rollback reuses the retained snapshot with no
journal; and candidates are shadow-fed, never gossiped.** Every member pair resolves under
it, and every primitive it uses already ships.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — export/import is `snapshot`/`restore`/`importFrom` + `Buffering` replay orchestration; each step is meaningful single-threaded (drain + shadow already run under `SimulationController`). No new kernel primitive (honors 50/53's guardrail). |
| P2 near-zero-cost fast path | **Satisfied** — steady state unchanged; the transform, buffered window, catch-up, and any rollback are rare-path (P2 permits arbitrarily expensive rare ops); the membrane flattens after green. |
| P3 explicit topology | **Satisfied** — the handoff rides explicit relinked links; catch-up is an ordinary `onLinked` unicast; no hidden fan or converter indirection. |
| P4 local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — no global barrier; partitioned promotion is per-organelle local swaps reconciled by convergence; recovery/catch-up are per-instance. |
| P5 correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — contract invariance is a structural PRECHECK (methodId-superset + merge-sameness); the continuation tier is dictated by the cell's delta idempotence class, not by discipline. |
| P6 interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — the candidate exists only because a judged evolution justifies it (`52`/`53`); nothing is transformed or gossiped "just in case." |
| P7 open, local-first | **Untouched** — promotion authority remains a membrane/policy boundary control (I-11, `40/43`); the transform adds no ambient assumption. |
| P8 live evolution | **Satisfied** — this *is* the evolution mechanism; the invariance line (change representation, not contracts) makes the atomic swap's scope precise while contract changes remain possible via topology surgery. |
| P9 serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — `PriorState`/`OutletWaveState` are plain data; the interchange is the ordinary delta form ("snapshot IS a delta"); no invocation rewriting, no lambdas/handles on the wire (Candidate A's converter is rejected on exactly this ground). |
| P10 niche first | **Satisfied** — the transform + source-continuity path serves stateful, incremental, long-lived, glitch-free cells (the niche); the fallback is bounded to where it is sound. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-33 (`importFrom(snapshot)` in the buffered window; non-migrating cells fall back to
  catch-up):** consistent, filled in. Sharpened to three tiers (restore / transform /
  catch-up), a pure-read export decoupled from deactivation, an import that is not
  activation, and a typed continuation-vs-fallback rule. No CONFLICT.
- **G-20 per-source waves (convergence not simultaneity):** consistent with I-11's stated
  refinement — under a single-active-instance handoff (T0/T1) B adopts A's `sourceId` and
  continues the counter; under T2 B mints a fresh source and the PREPARE-drain makes it
  convergence. Flagged (inherited from I-11), not a new CONFLICT.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED:** consistent — no global order; partitioned promotion is
  per-organelle, no coordinator.
- **Host is the unit of mobility:** consistent — a remote candidate is co-located by
  migration before the local swap (I-11); export/import is then in-host.
- **Suspension = one Buffering primitive:** consistent — the red window and replay reuse
  `Buffering`; catch-up reuses `onLinked`.
- **Location = Local|Remote; one park/replay:** consistent — parked invocations key on the
  full ref and replay into B unchanged (R5).
- **A snapshot IS a delta (no separate type):** consistent and load-bearing — the snapshot
  is the schema-neutral interchange *and* the rollback checkpoint (R4, R9).
- **Merge tags cell-local, not waves:** consistent — catch-up idempotence rides tags; the
  transform preserves tag state as part of the snapshot.
- **Data push-only; management null context:** consistent — `importFrom`/`snapshot` are
  management-class lifecycle calls (null context); catch-up is push-only data.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + delta gossip; NO second sync protocol:** consistent —
  R10 keeps candidates shadow-fed (no gossip) and rolling-promotion replicas on ordinary
  gossip under invariant merge semantics; no second protocol.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism:** consistent — R8 promotes
  partitions as ordinary cells, per key range.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved:** consistent and *depended upon* — R5/R3
  keep parked invocations on shared contract-interface ids; Candidate A (invocation
  rewriting) rejected precisely to protect this.
- **Drain ordering invariant / per-link FIFO end-to-end:** consistent and reused — R7
  orders catch-up before live deltas by per-link FIFO; the PREPARE drain preserves
  accepted-before-closure.
- **Cardinality at link time; Owned→move-by-serialize; Leased not crossing machines:**
  consistent — R5 replays `Owned` exactly once; the invariance line keeps cardinality/SPSC
  ports matched at PRECHECK.
- **CellRef(id, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2):** consistent — export/import is
  instance→instance on full refs; `logicalId` is the continuity key.
- **I-11 (swap transaction; retained incumbent; wave invisibility; OutletWaveState):**
  consistent and central — I-27 is the state half I-11 delegated; `OutletWaveState` rides
  `PriorState`.
- **I-7 (durable snapshot = checkpoint; replay reuses catch-up):** consistent — the export
  snapshot doubles as the rollback/recovery checkpoint (R9).
- **I-3 (`Replicable` gate; candidates vs replicas):** consistent — R10 uses the gate to
  forbid divergent-schema gossip.

No new CONFLICT flag; one inherited refinement (G-20 source continuity, from I-11).
