#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Snapshot-schema version negotiation across builds.** R3's methodId-superset assumes the
  shared contract-interface definition is byte-identical at A's and B's builds; two builds
  of the same-FQN interface with different method sets (source-incompatible interface
  evolution) collide on `contractId = hash(FQN)`. A contract-version discipline (the
  reserved wire version byte, `40/41`) guarding `importFrom`'s `schemaVersion` needs
  pinning.
- **Rollback-checkpoint retention horizon.** How long A's `exportState` snapshot is retained
  for post-retire rollback, and its interaction with G-25 durability / OR-set tag growth,
  is open (shared with I-11's "rollback-after-retire" and I-7's compaction gap).
- **`StateMigrating` transform correctness harness.** A generative test that a T1 transform
  `importFrom(vOld.snapshot)` yields a downstream stream identical to the unswapped control
  across representation changes (generalizing `ShadowPromotionTest`), including the
  glitch-free frontier and source-continuity, needs building.
- **Fallback-tier soundness marker.** R6's "T2 only for idempotent-across-source cells" is
  by-convention; a marker/lint (KSP) that refuses T2 for non-idempotent-merge cells (forcing
  T0/T1) would make it correct-by-construction — ties to I-3's `Replicable` gate and I-7's
  determinism marker.
- **Coordinating a partitioned rolling promotion.** R8 promotes partitions independently;
  an orchestration/policy for ordering, monitoring, and aborting a multi-partition rollout
  (and its interaction with the composite's routing-proxy/merging-outlet promotion) is
  undesigned.
- **Hidden-state cells and the transform.** A cell whose recoverable state is *not* fully
  expressible in its invariant delta contract (hidden internal state) cannot be bridged by
  the delta interchange (R4) nor re-baselined by catch-up (R6); such a cell needs a private
  snapshot channel or is declared non-promotable — needs a rule.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The core is strongly compositional and reuses shipped pieces:
`Stateful.snapshot/restore` (M3.3), `StateMigrating.importFrom` (M9.4), `onLinked` catch-up
(M4.2), `Buffering` replay (M3.4), G-32 shadow-serving (M9.2), and I-11's retained-
incumbent transaction. Two ideas carry the resolution: (1) **contract invariance** — a
promotion changes private representation, not port contracts — which collapses the
parked-invocation/evolved-contract cluster (N5, N20) and the divergent-gossip case (N24)
by *exclusion* rather than by machinery; and (2) **the delta form as schema-neutral
interchange** ("snapshot IS a delta"), which makes export/import a transform that never
touches wire ids and never needs a converter. The lifecycle ordering (N6) resolves cleanly
because export is a pure pre-deactivation read and import is not activation. Confidence is
not higher because three pieces are genuinely constrained rather than free: the
continuation-vs-fallback choice is *typed* (R6) and its non-idempotent-cell hazard needs a
lint to be correct-by-construction; the snapshot-schema versioning across builds (§8) is a
real retrofit risk on the ids-only wire; and hidden-state cells sit outside both the
transform and the fallback and need an explicit non-promotable rule.

**Open questions I could not fully close within the fixed decisions:**
1. Whether T2 (catch-up fallback) should be *removed* entirely — pushing every promotion to
   T0/T1 and declaring idempotent cells' transforms trivial `restore`s — for a single
   handoff path, versus keeping the fallback for genuinely representation-incompatible
   idempotent cells. I kept it (bounded by R6) because it costs nothing and serves the
   OR-set family's natural re-sync, but a one-path purist reading is defensible.
2. Whether the invariance line should permit *additive* outlet-contract evolution (new
   delta fields ignored by old downstream) as a promotion, or force even additive changes
   through adapter surgery. I lean permit-additive (methodId-superset already allows it) but
   the downstream-tolerance contract for ignored fields is unpinned.

### I-28 — Boundary security: what a membrane enforces at a crossing — identity, disclosure, and protocol authority (G-29)

> Member pairs: N3×N7, N7×N9, N7×N21, N7×N22, N7×N24, N21×N22
> Existing gaps touched: G-29, G-10, G-6 · Confidence: medium
> Spec drift (judged at `a69186a`): 6/6 member pairs partially addressed by M6–M9 while the analysis ran — see §3.1
> Landed state at `0c09a32` (M11): **PARTIAL** — The policy vocabulary and the flow-time seam: Principal/AuthLevel, the BoundaryPolicy object bound to an I-10 Exposure (I-10 membranes unbuilt, G-10 open), protocolAuthority (minAuth/attention ceiling clamp/per-Principal rate — also blocked on I-1 dispatch …

#### 1. Challenge restatement

**The single mechanism question**: the spec fixes the *posture* (security is boundary
controls, never ambient authority — P7, `40/43 §Posture`) and the *enforcement point*
(bridge cells are ordinary cells, so policies apply to network crossings "with no
special casing" — `40/41 §Transport point 4`), but nothing actually *lives* at the
place reserved for it. `40/43 §The five mechanisms` names authority-at-boundaries,
peer allowlists/encryption, serialization boundaries, isolation, and replay — yet
`40/43 §G-29` records phase-1 as landed (`PeerId` from transport hello → ingress
stamps deliveries → `LinkRequest.identity`/`CurrentPeer`; deny-by-default via
`allowPeers` + ingress admission gate) and flags **authentication of the claimed
name, integrity/signing of replicated deltas, and Sybil resistance for interest
signals as still undefined.** So the question is: **what vocabulary of boundary policy
does a membrane enforce at a crossing, bound to what identity, evaluated at what
seam — and how does that vocabulary answer per-protocol authority, disclosure control,
attention attenuation, and delta integrity under one mechanism rather than four?**

**Member pairs** (all TENSION) pull on distinct facets of the same crossing:
- **N3×N7** — generic protocols crossing a membrane need *per-ProtocolId authority*;
  `40/43` explicitly flags "an attacker claiming attention could summon computation."
  (`10/12 §Multiplexed ports`, `40/43 §G-29`)
- **N7×N9** — every accepted link auto-triggers a full-state catch-up unicast
  (`20/21 §Pull`); may a membrane *deny, scope, or redact* that disclosure?
  (`20/21 §Pull`, `10/11 §Membranes`)
- **N7×N21** — attention is an upstream protocol that *summons computation*; may a
  membrane *veto or attenuate* attention crossing it (Sybil resistance)?
  (`30/34 §Design sketch`, `40/43 §G-29`)
- **N7×N22** — the enforcement point is fixed (bridge = ordinary cell) but *what it
  enforces* (peer identity, link authentication, encryption) is undesigned.
  (`40/41 §Wire`, `40/43 §The five mechanisms`)
- **N7×N24** — an untrusting-but-cooperating replica set needs *integrity/signing of
  replicated deltas* and Sybil resistance, undesigned on both sides.
  (`40/42 §Principles`, `40/43 §Posture`)
- **N21×N22** — attention-over-the-wire is *un-authenticated*; remote interest claims
  have no identity binding. (`30/34 §Design sketch`, `40/41 §Wire`)

**Why the spec leaves it open**: `40/43` is Exploratory — the posture and the five
mechanisms are fixed but "mechanisms undesigned"; phase-1 landed only the identity
*slot* and a peer allowlist. The vocabulary above the allowlist (per-protocol
authority, disclosure scoping, delta integrity, attention attenuation) has "a place to
live" (the membrane, `40/43 §mechanism 2`) but no design. Critically, this challenge is
now the *last* piece over an otherwise-settled substrate: **I-10** gave the membrane a
code form (Flatten/Mediate exposures with link-time `LinkPolicy`, an Invocation-
capturing Mediate proxy); **I-1** gave the three dispatch classes every crossing
carries (`PORT_API` data / `PORT_MANAGEMENT` / `PORT_PROTOCOL` metadata) and made
bridges protocol-aware; **I-4** made attention per-link LWW *level* state (clampable);
**I-2/I-3** made addressing and replication per-instance over full refs. I-28 fills the
one hole those left: **the boundary-policy vocabulary and its binding to identity.**

#### 2. Why this is hard

- **P7 (open, local-first by default) vs correctness for untrusting peers.** Security
  is a *boundary control*, never an ambient property; the common case (a local crossing,
  a cooperating peer) must pay nothing and assume nothing. But an untrusting replica set
  (N7×N24) needs unforgeable identity and signed deltas — real cryptographic cost. The
  mechanism must make strength *opt-in per boundary* without making the open default a
  second-class path.
- **P2 (near-zero-cost fast path) vs per-message authority + signing.** Per-ProtocolId
  authority (N3×N7) and delta integrity (N7×N24) are per-message checks. If they land on
  the in-host data path they violate P2. They must ride only the crossing that already
  pays — the bridge, where serialization already happens (P2's "rare operations may be
  arbitrarily expensive" and "cross-host = enqueue" already concede the wire is the slow
  side).
- **"An attacker claiming attention could summon computation" (`40/43`) vs P6.** Interest
  drives resources (P6) — but if interest is un-authenticated, an adversary manufactures
  interest to summon work (a DoS / resource-exhaustion Sybil). Attention must become a
  *request the boundary may attenuate*, not an entitlement — without a global attention
  coordinator (G-20 spirit, P4).
- **Automatic full-state catch-up (`20/21`) vs disclosure control (N7×N9).** Catch-up is
  *automatic* on every accepted link — exactly the wrong default for a boundary that must
  redact. But it is also load-bearing (late-join correctness, G-18/G-22). The membrane
  must be able to *filter* disclosure without forking the catch-up mechanism.
- **P1 / no-second-protocol.** Whatever security is, it must reduce to
  cells/ports/links/policies (P1) and MUST NOT become a second synchronization or
  membership protocol (recorded decision) — integrity cannot smuggle in acks or version
  vectors.
- **Four facets, one seam.** The four open sub-questions (protocol authority, disclosure,
  attention Sybil, delta integrity) look like four features. The hard part is showing
  they are *one* vocabulary — identity-keyed predicates — evaluated at the seams the
  membrane already owns, not four bespoke subsystems.

#### 3. Candidate mechanisms

##### Candidate A — Capabilities everywhere: every ref is an unforgeable token

*Semantics*: exposing a port hands out an unforgeable capability; holding a `PortRef`
*is* the authority to use it; revocation = rotating the capability. Security is the
addressing model.

*Fast-path cost*: every link/send validates a capability; addressing gains a secret
dimension; `locate`/`connect` become authority checks on the hot path.

*Failure modes*: contradicts P7 (open-by-default becomes closed-by-construction — you
cannot address without a token); contradicts P3/I-2 (refs are `CellRef(id, instanceId)`,
public grouping/continuity keys, *not* secrets); reintroduces per-send authority on the
data path (P2); changes the wire form (ids-only, `40/41`). It also over-solves: the niche
(P10) is cooperating-by-default peers with *boundaries* where trust is scarce, not a
pervasive object-capability OS. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate B — A dedicated security gateway cell distinct from the membrane

*Semantics*: a first-class `SecurityGateway` cell inserted at each trust boundary;
policy, authentication, signing, and disclosure live in it; membranes stay about
structure.

*Fast-path cost*: an extra hop at every guarded crossing; two boundary objects
(membrane + gateway) to keep coherent.

*Failure modes*: directly contradicts `40/41 §Transport point 4` and `40/43 §mechanism
2` — "bridge cells are ordinary cells so policies apply with **no special casing**"; a
dedicated gateway *is* special casing. It duplicates the I-10 Mediate proxy (which
already captures Invocations at the crossing) and the G-29 ingress gate (which already
stamps identity). Two enforcement points invite divergence (a protocol that reaches the
membrane bypassing the gateway). Violates the no-second-mechanism instinct. **Rejected.**

##### Candidate C — Boundary policy as identity-keyed predicates at the membrane's existing seams (recommended)

*Semantics*: security is **not a new object**. It is a `BoundaryPolicy` — a bundle of
**identity-keyed predicates** attached to a membrane `Exposure` (I-10) — evaluated at the
**three seams the boundary already owns**, one per dispatch class (I-1): **admission**
(transport hello / bridge ingress — the G-29 gate), **link-time** (`onLink`/`LinkPolicy`
with `CurrentPeer` — the G-14 slot), and **flow-time** (the I-10 Mediate proxy, which
already captures every Invocation). The *identity* is the authenticated `PeerId` the
ingress already stamps; the *vocabulary* is: peer admission, link authority, per-
ProtocolId authority (attention attenuation among them), disclosure scoping, and delta
integrity. Local crossings carry `LocalTrusted` and every predicate is a no-op (P7 open
default preserved).

*Fast-path cost*: **zero** on the in-host path (LocalTrusted, no policy → the crossing
Flattens as today). Only bridge crossings — already the serialized, slow side — evaluate
predicates, and only where an `Exposure` declares them (P6).

*Failure modes*: none of the six member-pair tensions survive (§4). Residual risk is
confined to the *strength* of authentication (transport-vouched today; cryptographic
later) and the disclosure-projection/signing details, all bounded and phased (§8).

*Tradeoffs*: gives up a uniform per-message security tax (the niche does not want one,
P7/P10) in exchange for a model where every open sub-question is one predicate at one
already-existing seam, riding entirely on landed (G-29 gate, `onLink`, ingress stamp)
and resolved (I-10 membrane, I-1 dispatch classes, I-4 clampable attention) machinery.
**Recommended.**

#### 4. Recommended resolution

Adopt **Candidate C**: a membrane enforces a **`BoundaryPolicy` — identity-keyed
predicates — at three seams, one per I-1 dispatch class.** The load-bearing insight:
**"what a membrane enforces" is not a fourth subsystem; it is the I-10 Mediate proxy and
the G-29 ingress gate, now consulting policy keyed on the authenticated `PeerId` that
ingress already stamps.** Security is where the boundary already is.

##### 4.1 Identity — the thing every predicate keys on

```kotlin
sealed interface Principal {
    object LocalTrusted : Principal                 // in-host / same-registry crossing (today's null identity)
    data class Peer(
        val id: PeerId,                             // transport identity, stamped by ingress (G-29 phase-1)
        val auth: AuthLevel                         // how strongly `id` is vouched for
    ) : Principal
}
enum class AuthLevel { TransportVouched, Authenticated }   // phase-1 = TransportVouched; phase-2 unlocks Authenticated
```

`PeerId` is the value the G-29 hello already carries and ingress already stamps on every
delivery. **Phase-1 (landed)**: the transport connection *vouches* for the name
(`TransportVouched`). **Phase-2 (this resolution's authentication interface, deferred
strength)**: `PeerId` carries (or resolves to) a **public key / DID**; the hello adds a
signed-nonce challenge; a verified peer is `Authenticated`. The *policy vocabulary is
stable across the upgrade* — predicates read `Principal`; only the strength that
`AuthLevel` certifies changes. This is the P7-compatible phasing: open-by-default and
transport-vouched today, self-sovereign-key-authenticated when a boundary demands it —
**no CA, no global identity registry** (P4, P10). Sybil resistance = the *cost* of
minting an `Authenticated` identity plus per-`Principal` quotas (§4.4).

##### 4.2 The policy vocabulary — attached to an I-10 `Exposure`

```kotlin
data class BoundaryPolicy(
    val admission:   PeerPredicate = AllowAll,                 // seam 1: transport hello / ingress
    val linkAuthority: List<LinkPolicy> = emptyList(),         // seam 2: onLink (reuses G-14, I-10 Exposure.policies)
    val protocolAuthority: Map<ProtocolId, ProtocolAuthority> = emptyMap(),  // seam 3: PORT_PROTOCOL
    val disclosure:  DisclosurePolicy = Full,                  // seam 3: PORT_API emission (catch-up + live)
    val integrity:   IntegrityPolicy  = None                   // seam 3: PORT_API inbound (deltas)
)

fun interface PeerPredicate { fun admits(p: Principal): Boolean }   // e.g. allowPeers(a, b) — landed

data class ProtocolAuthority(
    val minAuth: AuthLevel = TransportVouched,     // deny protocol from weaker principals
    val ceiling: AttentionBand? = null,            // ATTENTION: clamp asserted level to this band
    val ratePerWindow: Int? = null                 // frames/window per Principal (anti-Sybil throttle)
)

sealed interface DisclosurePolicy {
    object Full                        : DisclosurePolicy       // serve full state-as-delta (today's default)
    data class Project(val id: ProjectionId) : DisclosurePolicy // named, serializable redaction/scoping (P9)
    object Deny                        : DisclosurePolicy       // no catch-up; link carries no state
}

sealed interface IntegrityPolicy {
    object None                        : IntegrityPolicy
    object RequireSigned               : IntegrityPolicy        // ingress verifies signature before deliver
}
```

`ProjectionId` is a **named registered transform** (exactly like I-4's
`AttentionAggregator` and I-1's protocol descriptors — never a lambda on the wire, P9):
a pure function `Delta → Delta` that redacts/scopes what a boundary discloses.

##### 4.3 The three seams (one per I-1 dispatch class) — normative

Every crossing already carries an I-1 dispatch class. Enforcement is *native to the
class*:

1. **Admission (before any link/traffic)** — `PORT_MANAGEMENT` peering handshake. The
   transport hello / bridge ingress evaluates `admission`: an unlisted/failing
   `Principal` is refused at hello time and its traffic dead-lettered (the **G-29
   ingress admission gate, landed**). This is the coarsest, cheapest gate — a whole peer
   in or out.

2. **Link-time (`onLink`)** — `PORT_MANAGEMENT` link handshake. Any new full-ref link
   (I-2) runs `linkAuthority` (`LinkPolicy`, first-rejection-wins, **G-14 landed**) with
   `CurrentPeer` = the crossing's `Principal` (**G-29 `LinkRequest.identity`, landed**).
   Deny-by-default for privileged ports; migration/RESTART preserve `instanceId` so are
   not rebinds (I-2), promotion *is* a rebind and re-authorizes. This is I-10's "membrane
   surface #1" now identity-aware.

3. **Flow-time (the I-10 Mediate proxy)** — per message, per dispatch class. A boundary
   that declares `protocolAuthority`, `disclosure`, or `integrity` on an `Exposure`
   forces that exposure to **Mediate** (I-10): the Mediate proxy — which already captures
   each Invocation — evaluates:
   - **`PORT_PROTOCOL` (I-1 metadata: attention, suspend-notice, state-request,
     link-mgmt)** → `protocolAuthority[protocolId]`. Below `minAuth` → drop (dead
     letter). Over `ratePerWindow` for this `Principal` → drop/throttle. For **attention**
     specifically, `ceiling` **clamps** the asserted level: because attention is per-link
     LWW *level* state (I-4), clamping is `slot.level = min(asserted, ceiling)` — the
     fold and band-gating are untouched. This is exactly "the membrane attenuates
     attention" (N7×N21) with **no new mechanism**.
   - **`PORT_API` outbound (deltas the boundary emits, including the `onLinked` catch-up
     unicast, `20/21`)** → `disclosure`. `Full` forwards unchanged (today). `Project(id)`
     runs the named projection over each emitted delta — scoping/redacting *both* the
     catch-up state-as-delta *and* the live stream uniformly (a snapshot IS a delta, so
     one filter covers both). `Deny` suppresses catch-up entirely — the link carries no
     state (e.g. an attention-only or management-only peering). This is "the membrane
     denies/scopes/redacts catch-up" (N7×N9).
   - **`PORT_API` inbound (deltas arriving, e.g. replica gossip)** → `integrity`.
     `RequireSigned` makes ingress **verify a signature** over `(contractId, methodId,
     serialized-payload, mintingPeerId, per-source-counter)` using the sender's
     `Authenticated` key *before* delivering to the `deltaInlet`. Failure → dead letter,
     never delivered. Because Replicable merges are commutative/associative/**idempotent**
     (I-3 gate), dropping an unverified delta is safe — no exactly-once dependency; a
     later re-gossiped signed copy converges. The per-source counter defeats replay. This
     is "integrity/signing of replicated deltas" (N7×N24). Signing is **per-emitting-peer**
     (per instance/host key), never per-logical-cell (I-2).

##### 4.4 Rules the model introduces (normative)

1. **Every crossing carries a `Principal`; the boundary is the enforcement point.**
   Local/same-registry crossings are `LocalTrusted`; bridge crossings are `Peer(id, …)`
   stamped by ingress (landed). No traffic is evaluated anywhere but at a membrane —
   there is no ambient check inside a trust domain (P7).

2. **Open by default, opt-in per exposure (P7/P6).** Absent a `BoundaryPolicy`, every
   predicate is its identity/`AllowAll`/`Full`/`None` default and the exposure Flattens
   (I-10) — today's behavior, byte-for-byte. Security cost exists only where a boundary
   declares it, and only on the bridge crossing (P2).

3. **One seam per dispatch class; no fourth subsystem.** Admission gates peers
   (`PORT_MANAGEMENT` peering), link authority gates topology (`PORT_MANAGEMENT` link),
   flow-time gates messages (`PORT_PROTOCOL` authority + `PORT_API` disclosure/integrity).
   Declaring any flow-time predicate forces the exposure to Mediate (I-10); the Mediate
   proxy is the *sole* flow-time enforcement point in both directions (data out, attention
   up, catch-up down, requests up).

4. **Attention is a request, not an entitlement.** A remote `AttentionUpdate` is subject
   to `protocolAuthority[ATTENTION]`: clamped to `ceiling`, rate-limited per `Principal`,
   or refused below `minAuth`. Sybil resistance is therefore *structural*: an
   unauthenticated flood clamps to the floor; authenticated principals are bounded by
   per-`Principal` resource quotas that reuse the **G-28 host-hierarchy quota walk**
   (a remote-driven resource claim is charged to the claiming `Principal`'s budget). No
   global attention coordinator (P4).

5. **Disclosure is a filter on emission, not a new protocol.** Catch-up and live deltas
   pass one `disclosure` transform at the Mediate proxy; `Project` is a named serializable
   projection (P9). Catch-up remains the ordinary `onLinked` state-as-delta (`20/21`,
   G-22) — filtered, not forked.

6. **Integrity is a verify-at-ingress step, not a sync protocol.** `RequireSigned`
   verifies before delivery; failures dead-letter. It adds **no** ack, version vector, or
   round-trip — idempotent merge (I-3) makes drop-and-reconverge the recovery. Replication
   stays "reuses dataflow + gossip; no second sync protocol."

7. **Authentication strength is phased behind a stable vocabulary.** Predicates read
   `Principal`/`AuthLevel`; today all bridge peers are `TransportVouched` and `minAuth`
   defaults let them through; phase-2 self-sovereign keys promote peers to `Authenticated`
   and unlock the predicates (`integrity`, high-`minAuth` protocol authority) that
   transport-vouched identity cannot safely satisfy. Encryption-in-transit stays transport
   config (`wss://`, `40/43`); encryption-at-rest remains a follow-on (§8).

##### 4.5 The load-bearing summary

The four "missing" security features are **one vocabulary of identity-keyed predicates**
evaluated at **three seams the membrane already owns**, keyed on the **`PeerId` ingress
already stamps**. Per-protocol authority = a predicate on the `PORT_PROTOCOL` class at the
Mediate proxy; disclosure = a filter on `PORT_API` emission; attention attenuation = a
clamp on I-4's level slot; delta integrity = a verify on `PORT_API` inbound. Nothing new
lives at the boundary — the boundary's *existing* seams now consult policy. The open
default is untouched; strength is opt-in and phased; the fast path never sees any of it.

#### 5. Principle check (P1–P10)

| Principle | Verdict |
|---|---|
| P1 Concurrency-free kernel | **Satisfied** — predicates are pure checks at existing seams; the Mediate proxy already runs single-threaded in simulation (I-10); no new primitive. |
| P2 Near-zero-cost fast path | **Tension — bounded/accepted** — in-host (`LocalTrusted`) crossings are untouched no-ops. Signing/verify per delta lands only on the bridge (already the serialized slow side; P2 concedes cross-host cost) and only under opt-in `RequireSigned` (P6). No security cost on the volatile-read+enqueue path. |
| P3 Explicit topology | **Satisfied** — policies are declared data on inspectable `Exposure`s; identity is an explicit stamped field; no hidden authority. |
| P4 Local, compositional consistency | **Satisfied** — every check is local to one boundary; allowlists/keys are local; attention quota is a local G-28 walk; no global CA, clock, or coordinator. |
| P5 Correctness by construction | **Satisfied** — `Principal`/`AuthLevel`/`DisclosurePolicy`/`IntegrityPolicy` are types; the dispatch class selects the seam; unverified deltas cannot reach `deltaInlet`. |
| P6 Interest drives resources | **Satisfied** — policy cost is opt-in per exposure; attention attenuation is the direct P6 defense (interest must be paid-for/authenticated to summon work). |
| P7 Open, local-first | **Satisfied — the exemplar** — open + transport-vouched by default; boundary controls opt-in; strength phased in only where trust is scarce. This is P7 made concrete. |
| P8 Live evolution | **Satisfied** — policies rebind like any exposure; revocation = unlink/re-expose (tears down live links, §8); nothing assumes static trust. |
| P9 Serialization-friendly | **Satisfied** — projections and protocol descriptors are named registered transforms; signature is an envelope field; payload stays ids-only; no lambdas/keys-as-code on the wire. |
| P10 Niche first | **Satisfied** — untrusting-but-cooperating decentralized peers with self-sovereign keys and local allowlists, no CA/global identity — exactly the niche; capability-OS (Cand. A) rejected on this ground. |

#### 6. Prior-decision consistency

- **G-20 per-source waves** — Consistent. Security predicates never mint/carry waves;
  attention clamp edits I-4's level slot, not a wave.
- **SID-UP global locks REJECTED** — Consistent. All checks local per boundary; no global
  lock/coordinator; Sybil quota is a local G-28 walk.
- **Host is the unit of mobility** — Consistent. Signing keys are per-host/peer (per
  instance, I-2); a migrating host carries its key; policies travel with the exposure.
- **Suspension = ONE Buffering primitive** — Untouched. Refusals/drops are dead letters,
  not a new suspension.
- **Location = Local\|Remote; one park/replay** — Consistent. `LocalTrusted` vs `Peer`
  mirrors Local vs Remote; enforcement rides the same bridge ingress.
- **A snapshot IS a delta** — Consistent and load-bearing. One `disclosure` filter covers
  catch-up (state-as-delta) and live deltas because they are the same shape.
- **Merge tags are Timestamps, not wave ids** — Untouched. The integrity per-source
  counter is a *third* monotonic-counter use (like I-4's `version`), distinct from tags
  and waves.
- **Data push-only; management may return; management null context** — Consistent.
  Admission/link authority are `PORT_MANAGEMENT`; disclosure/integrity are on push-only
  `PORT_API`; protocol authority on `PORT_PROTOCOL` (I-1). No amendment.
- **Replication reuses dataflow + gossip; NO second sync protocol** — Consistent.
  Integrity is a verify-at-ingress step; idempotent merge (I-3) makes drop-and-reconverge
  the recovery; no ack/version-vector protocol added.
- **Partitioning MUST NOT be a second distribution mechanism** — Untouched. A partition
  organelle's exposure carries the same `BoundaryPolicy` vocabulary; no new dimension.
- **Wire form ids-only, version byte reserved** — Consistent. Signature/`PeerId`/counter
  are envelope fields; contract/method stay hashed ids; a strong-identity `PeerId` (key)
  is a value, not names.
- **Drain ordering invariant; per-link FIFO** — Consistent. Dropped (unauthorized/
  unverified) messages dead-letter without entering the data lane; accepted traffic keeps
  per-link FIFO.
- **Cardinality at link time; SPSC refuses fan-out** — Consistent. Security is orthogonal
  to cardinality; the Mediate proxy is a single consumer face (I-10 counts SPSC once).
- **Owned→move-by-serialize; Leased MUST NOT cross machines** — Consistent. Signing an
  `Owned` delta is move-by-serialize plus a signature envelope field; no new crossing rule.
- **CellRef(id, instanceId); links bind full refs (I-2)** — Consistent. `PeerId` is
  transport identity, orthogonal to `CellRef`; signing is per-instance/per-peer, never
  per-logicalId.
- **I-10 membrane / I-1 dispatch classes / I-4 attention / I-3 replication** — Built upon,
  not re-litigated: the Mediate proxy is the flow-time seam, the dispatch classes select
  the seam, attention clamp edits the level slot, idempotent merge makes integrity-drop
  safe.
- **Gaps/conflicts Resolved in 90/91 stay resolved** — G-29 phase-1 is **extended**, not
  reopened; the ingress gate and `LinkRequest.identity` are reused as seams 1–2. No
  resolved item reversed.

No CONFLICT flag required. Phase-2 cryptographic authentication is a *new design*
(deferred, §8), not a contradiction of the landed transport-vouched phase-1.

#### 7. Spec impact

- **40/43 §The five mechanisms / §G-29** — Deliver the vocabulary above mechanism 2:
  `BoundaryPolicy` (admission / linkAuthority / protocolAuthority / disclosure / integrity)
  bound to `Principal`; the three-seams-per-dispatch-class model; the phased
  authentication interface (`AuthLevel`); state that per-protocol authority, disclosure,
  attention attenuation, and delta integrity are one identity-keyed predicate vocabulary.
  Update "Still undefined" to: authentication *strength* (phase-2 keys/DIDs) and
  encryption-at-rest remain; the rest specified here.
- **10/11 §Membranes and policies (with I-10)** — Add that a membrane `Exposure` carries a
  `BoundaryPolicy`; declaring a flow-time predicate forces Mediate; the Mediate proxy is
  the flow-time enforcement point.
- **10/12 §Multiplexed ports (with I-1)** — Note a generic protocol crossing a membrane is
  subject to `protocolAuthority[protocolId]`; attention carries a boundary `ceiling`/rate.
- **20/21 §Pull** — Note catch-up emission passes the membrane's `disclosure`
  (Full/Project/Deny); catch-up is filtered, not forked.
- **30/34 §Design sketch / §header** — Resolve "an attacker claiming attention could
  summon computation": attention crossing a membrane is attenuated (clamp/rate/`minAuth`);
  Sybil resistance = authentication cost + per-`Principal` G-28 quota.
- **40/42 §Principles** — Note untrusting-but-cooperating replicas may declare
  `IntegrityPolicy.RequireSigned`; verify-at-ingress; idempotent merge makes drop safe;
  signing per-emitting-peer.
- **40/41 §Wire / §Transport** — Note the ingress stamps `Principal`; frames may carry a
  signature/counter envelope field under `RequireSigned`; identity strength phased.
- **90/91 §G-29** — Update: boundary-policy vocabulary + three seams + attention
  attenuation + disclosure + delta-integrity *specified*; cryptographic authentication and
  encryption-at-rest remain (§8).

#### 8. Follow-on gaps

- **Cryptographic peer authentication (phase-2).** Key/DID format, the hello
  challenge-response, key distribution and rotation, and how `Authenticated` is certified
  without a CA — the load-bearing deferred piece that upgrades `TransportVouched`.
- **Delta signature scheme.** Exact signed tuple, per-source replay counter semantics,
  verification cost/batching on the bridge path, and interaction with move-by-serialize
  `Owned` deltas.
- **Disclosure projection language.** How a `ProjectionId` transform is declared,
  registered, and kept serialization-friendly (named, not a lambda) — parallel to I-4's
  aggregators; whether projections compose across nested/transitive membranes.
- **Attention/interest Sybil economics.** The per-`Principal` resource budget that bounds
  authenticated interest claims (ties to the deferred G-6 economic layer and the G-28
  quota walk); what "cost to mint an identity" concretely is.
- **Capability revocation as a boundary control.** Whether exposing a port hands an
  unforgeable capability, and how revocation (unlink/re-expose, removing an allowlist
  entry) tears down *live* links, not just refuses new ones.
- **Encryption at rest.** Still undefined in `40/43`; for durable journals (G-25) and
  parked/overflow state, distinct from `wss://` in-transit.
- **Transitive / multi-hop trust and disclosure.** When a peer relays disclosed state to a
  third party, whether disclosure and integrity policies compose across hops or must be
  re-declared at each membrane (relates to I-10's nested-exposure gap).
- **Management-plane authority across membranes.** Who may drive `PORT_MANAGEMENT`
  (spawn/connect/despawn, promotion swap) across a bridge; the authority model for remote
  graph mutation beyond peer admission.

#### 9. Confidence & open questions

**Confidence: medium-high.** The mechanism composes cleanly on landed machinery (the G-29
ingress gate, `onLink`/`LinkPolicy` with `CurrentPeer`, the ingress identity stamp) and on
adopted resolutions (I-10's Mediate proxy as the flow-time seam, I-1's dispatch classes
selecting the seam, I-4's clampable attention level, I-3's idempotent merge making
integrity-drop safe). It resolves all six member pairs under one vocabulary — identity-
keyed predicates at three seams — without a new subsystem, a second protocol, or any
in-host cost (P1/P2/P7). Confidence is not higher because the *strong* guarantees
(unforgeable identity, delta integrity, Sybil economics) rest on **phase-2 cryptographic
authentication**, which this resolution fixes an *interface* for but deliberately defers
the design of (§8) — the transport-vouched present is honest but weak.

**Open questions**: (1) whether `Authenticated` should be self-sovereign keys/DIDs (my
lean, P10) or admit an optional web-of-trust, without ever mandating a CA; (2) whether
disclosure `Project` should compose automatically across nested membranes or require
re-declaration at each level (the safe default is re-declare); (3) whether delta signing
should be mandatory for any cross-machine replica set or strictly opt-in (I chose opt-in
per P7, but a "sign by default across machines" posture is arguable for the untrusting
niche); (4) the precise per-`Principal` quota that turns attention attenuation into a real
Sybil bound, which needs the deferred economic layer.

## 7. Deferred challenges

None. All 28 consolidated challenges received a resolution; the 28-challenge
cap was reached exactly, with no overflow.
